passages.name: SP: Charlotte x Mariel A - Begining
passages.content:
Charlotte: ...
Charlotte adjusted her gear, fixing it in place.

With tightened straps, her hand lowered down to 
pat one of her Lockhart developed handguns in its 
holster.
Charlotte: ...
A small exhale accompanied the motion, and her 
tense posture relaxed a little.
Charlotte: ...
But with the relaxation, she saw her ears adjust in 
the mirror looking back at her.
Charlotte: ...
She breathed in.

And out...
Charlotte: ...
Mariel: ...and then you'll need to use the power cell 
directly on the chest.

It will...
Medic: Right... Yeah...
Mariel was explaining a potentially life saving 
procedure that she had refined.
Mariel: ...so you have to be precise. It can be the 
difference maker.

While I am gone, you will need to-
Footsteps interrupted her, and Mariel turned.
Mariel: ...?
Charlotte: ...
Mariel: ...
Mariel turned back to the Lockhart based medic.
Mariel: And while I am gone, remember... we all do our 
part to help each other thrive.

The city is still reeling, so never forget how much of 
a difference every action you can take can be.
Medic: R- Right... No pressure then.
Mariel: Good luck while you're in charge.
The medic pumped herself up as she headed off to 
work.

Charlotte's footsteps accompanied her effort to find 
her way to Mariel's side.
Charlotte: Are you ready?
Mariel: Yeah... So it's time then?
Charlotte: Yeah.
Both of the sisters turned towards the camp 
exit. 

They faced it, and they tried to control their 
breathing.

They closed their eyes...
And took breaths slowly but surely.

In and out, preparing the self for the moment to 
come.

And... their eyes opened.
Mariel: It's that time.
Charlotte: Yeah.

Time to say goodbye.
Bells rang across the Covenant church grounds.

And with it, the large wooden doors of the building 
creaked open.
Charlotte: ...
The two sisters turned to each other and...
Mariel: ...
Charlotte: ...
Mariel: Even with the rubble around... this city still feels 
nostalgic.
Charlotte: Yeah, like home.
Mariel nodded in agreement, and Charlotte let her 
take the lead as they made their way to their next 
destination.
Mariel: ...?
The faint sound of a bark could be heard, so Mariel 
turned into an alleyway.
Mariel: ...?!
...only to see a coyote scampering away.
Charlotte: An opportunist species, right? We should be... 
more...
Charlotte: Sis...?
Mariel: ...
Mariel had started to approach an even fainter 
sound.

The sound of a small, injured bird.

Bellowing what little sound it could into chirps of 
pain.
Mariel: ...
Charlotte turned towards the alley entrance to try 
to call for help, but she was met with the 
lowering sun instead.
Charlotte: That time already...

It's not that long until-
Mariel: *Puff*!
Mariel slapped her cheeks a little and jumped into 
action.

Quickly pulling out some of her supplies, she 
kneeled down around the small bird.
Charlotte: ...not that long... until... sunset...
Charlotte finished her sentence, but the words 
trailed off to a whisper as she did.
Charlotte: ...
She stepped to the side, and she chose to wait.
Mariel: ...
...

.........

....................

.................................
Bird: ...

*Chirp chirp*...!
Mariel: *Giggle*

I'm happy you're better too, little guy.
Bird: *Chirp*~
The bird tweeted melodically.

But soon enough it flapped its wings and took off.
Mariel: Be safe, will you?
Mariel rose to her feet and turned towards 
Charlotte.
Charlotte: ...
Mariel: ...
With a smile and nod each, the two were back on 
their way.
Mariel: ...and then, Charlotte looked like she was about to 
cry.
Charlotte: I- I wasn't...! It was a harrowing experience!
Charlotte: You never had a secret like mine, so...
Mariel: But it was adorable.

I could just imagine how Mom would've reacted.
Mariel: How she is reacting...
Charlotte: ...
Charlotte: Yeah.
The two turned their heads to the precipice of the 
hill.

A place where two stones stuck out of the ground.

Two stones with names on them.

Two gravestones.
Charlotte: I'm sure they're watching and have enjoyed our 
shenanigans.
Charlotte: Our stupid little choices. All that immaturity.

It must have looked so silly looking at it from afar.
Mariel: I can just imagine their faces through it all.
The two laughed softly together.

But their faces shifted to one more serious.
Charlotte: ...

And there's something we wanted to tell you.

I don't know how you two would react, but... this 
isn't an ask, either.
Mariel: Yeah. We came to a decision. Together.
Charlotte: Lockhart needs to change.
Mariel: It has so much potential.

The city has some great people. People that can 
do great things as a people.
Charlotte: I think... No, we think you both would've liked 
them, if you had the chance to truly know that 
city.
Charlotte's ears twitched a little with a sense of joy.
Mariel: We want to create a city that works for the city 
itself. For its people.
Charlotte: And we know it won't be easy. Many will oppose it.
Mariel: Many of those in power won't want to give that 
up.

They'll fight it to the bitter end.

...
Mariel: But... so will we. It'll work out. We know it will.
Charlotte: If we fight for the people, we fight for the city 
itself.

It's a source of power and motivation that can 
never have its flame extinguished.

What we seek... What we seek is inevitable.

No matter what roadblocks we encounter... no 
matter what barrier must overcome...
Charlotte: Lockhart will have a shining future.
Mariel: I can't wait to see it one day.

And for us to show it to you, Mom and Dad.
Charlotte: ...
Mariel: ...
The two turned to each other with smiles on their 
faces before rising to their feet.

Approaching the gravestones, they both put their 
hands tenderly on them.
Charlotte: Goodbye, and...
Mariel: ...and until we meet again.
Charlotte: Yeah.
The two turned, and they started their descent 
along the hill.

The two gravestones stayed there in the setting 
sun as though giving farewells as well.

And to their side... 

...sat a smaller, third stone among the grassy 
hillside.

A third gravestone.
Bird: *Chirp*
A familiar tweeting sound passed along the sight of 
the setting sun.

And a small bird landed on this third gravestone.

One it nestled itself upon.

As both greeted the night together.
passages.content_zh:
夏洛特：…
夏洛特調整了她的裝備，將其固定到位。

隨著帶子的收緊，她的手下降到
拍拍她的一把洛克哈特開發的手槍
皮套。
夏洛特：…
伴隨著這個動作，她輕輕地呼了一口氣，然後她
緊張的姿勢放鬆了一些。
夏洛特：…
但隨著放鬆，她發現自己的耳朵適應了
鏡子回頭看著她。
夏洛特：…
她吸了一口氣。

然後出來...
夏洛特：…
Mariel：……然後你需要使用電池
直接在胸部。

它會...
醫生：對……是啊……
馬裡爾正在解釋一種可能挽救生命的方法
她改進的程序。
Mariel：……所以你必須精確。它可以是
差異製造者。

當我不在的時候，你需要—
腳步聲打斷了她，馬瑞爾轉過身來。
瑪麗埃爾：……？
夏洛特：…
瑪麗埃爾：…
馬裡爾轉向洛哈特的醫生。
Mariel：當我離開時，請記住...我們都在做我們的事情
幫助彼此成長的一部分。

這座城市仍然搖搖欲墜，所以永遠不要忘記有多少
你採取的每一個行動都可以帶來改變。
軍醫：R- 好的...那就沒有壓力了。
Mariel：祝你在負責期間一切順利。
醫護人員在前往醫院時給自己打了氣。 
工作。

夏洛特的腳步伴隨著她努力尋找
她走到瑪麗埃爾身邊。
夏洛特：你準備好了嗎？
Mariel：是的……那麼現在是時候了嗎？
夏洛特：是的。
姊妹倆轉身朝營地走去
退出。 

他們面對它，並試圖控制自己的情緒
呼吸。

他們閉上了眼睛…
然後緩慢而堅定地呼吸。

進進出出，為當下的自我做好準備
來吧。

然後……他們的眼睛睜開了。
瑪麗埃爾：就是那個時候了。
夏洛特：是的。

是時候說再見了。
鐘聲響徹聖約教堂。

隨之而來的是建築物的大木門
嘎吱嘎吱地打開了。
夏洛特：…
兩姊妹面面相覷，然後…
瑪麗埃爾：…
夏洛特：…
Mariel：即使周圍都是瓦礫……這座城市仍然給人感覺
懷舊的。
夏洛特：是的，就像家一樣。
馬裡爾點頭同意

passages.name: SP: CharlottexRowan C - First
passages.content:
Charlotte: Hmm~...
Charlotte rose the glass to her lips, taking in the 
crisp smell of the tea.
Charlotte: Ah... Just the right amount of sweet.
Charlotte: You really have always known how to pick them, 
Kara.
Kara: I thought you would enjoy this
blend.

Did you happen to see the daily special for our 
snack? It has a strawberry on top.
Charlotte: This is starting to feel like that time from freshman 
year.
Charlotte: Or... Uh... my freshman year, I mean. When we 
went to a place with a strawberry dessert.
Kara: I do remember such a place.
Charlotte: Was that a strawberry cake then, too? Just 
thinking about the taste is so nostalgic~
Charlotte’s beaming smile met a waitress delivering 
three slices of the strawberry cake.
Kara: I do not believe you actually were able to sample 
the cake that day.
Charlotte: What? Of course I did.
Charlotte: I can still remember the kick of the strawberry’s 
flavor.
Kara: Then perhaps you went back another day?
Charlotte: Oh, I wouldn’t do that to you.
Kara: I would describe it as the only possibility.
Charlotte: Why is it so hard for you to believe? Wasn’t that a 
fun day for you, too?
Kara: ...
Kara adjusted herself and more directly faced 
Charlotte.
Kara: Well... The odd thing about that day...
Kara: Do you remember our outing when you got lost 
and I had to arrange for you to be picked up?
Charlotte: Y- Yeah... I was a freshman and got lost in a big 
new city.
Charlotte: W- What... What are you getting at?
Kara: It was the very same outing.
Charlotte: I- I...
Kara: Such a memory would be hard to form, no?
Charlotte: We went back later...? Or maybe another shop had 
a...?
Kara: None of the above are applicable to our outings.

In fact, this shop itself is a recently opened branch 
of that same little café. It is a specialty offering.
Charlotte: I...
Charlotte: S- Sorry...
Kara: No need to apologize.

More than anything, I am delighted to see the 
mysterious ways memories can work.
Charlotte: Still...
Rowan: If you wish to replicate the happy memory, I would 
be delighted to assist.
Charlotte: ...
Charlotte’s neck creaked a foreboding screech as it 
turned.

And turned to place her eyes squarely on the third 
part of this group.
Rowan: They say the strawberry shouldn’t taken lightly for 
one’s figure.
Charlotte: ...
Rowan: Or... so I am told?
Kara: Haha... I can imagine some girls feeling self-
conscious over it.
Charlotte: ...
Another creaking sound.

Charlotte’s eyeline slowly turned away from the 
thing to her side.

Before her now was... Kara, again.
Charlotte: Well, it wouldn’t be the first time I did something 
stupid.
Charlotte: Remember that time I accidentally negotiated a 
trade deal in the middle of a class?
Kara: I do. It caused quite a stir at the contract signing 
when the story was told.
Charlotte: Imagine trying to tell someone about how you 
wrote out tariff rates on a napkin. I doubt 
even you’ve had to do that before, Kara.
Kara: Haha, I might have to think on that, yes.
Rowan: I do not believe I’ve heard this one before, actually.

Who was it with?
Charlotte: ...
Kara: One of the city states from the East Auran Alliance, 
should I recall it correctly.
Rowan: Ah... Yes, there was that one boy in the academy 
at the time.
Kara: Charlotte, am I remembering correctly?
Charlotte: ...
Kara: Charlotte?
Charlotte: ...
Charlotte took in a deep breath, and then exhaled.
Charlotte: Yeah, something like that.
Charlotte: Kara, how about that time we went to that one 
sweets store just outside of-
Rowan: Ah, sweets once more.

Such an interesting topic...
Rowan was inching his hand and body over to pilfer 
the still uneaten strawberry atop Charlotte’s cake.
Charlotte: Or... there was that time we went to that 
restaurant...
Kara: You may need to be more specific.
Charlotte: Well, there was... was that...
Charlotte’s eyes were jumping to Rowan’s 
presence.

To his hand inching towards her plate as he acted 
like he wasn’t noticed.
Charlotte: That time... that...

...
Closer and closer...

Until...
Charlotte: ...!
Rowan: ...?!
Charlotte: Get your damn hands away from my cake!
Kara: *Sigh*...
Rowan: You merely needed to say...
Charlotte: And could you shut up for once?! Stop acting like 
you’re Alexei.
Rowan: Ah... That may be... difficult?
Kara: My friend, we have been over this topic before.
Charlotte: You’re not Alexei, so you can’t just have my food!
Rowan: Wait... Does that not imply that I could have the 
berry should I be labeled as ‘Alexei’?

Kara! We must make haste to a courtroom to keep 
this verbal contract valid!
Charlotte: I wouldn’t give it to him either!
Charlotte swiped the strawberry up and quickly 
dumped the entirely thing into her mouth.
Charlotte: *Violently, Audibly Chewing*...!
Rowan: Ah... No recompense from a judge could replace 
this empty feeling I have...!
Charlotte: I... I jwust nweed two...

...

AWAHWAHAW...!
Charlotte jumped to her feet and stormed away 
from the scene, still smashing the strawberry into 
nothingness within her mouth.
Rowan: ...
Kara: It is a shame she hasn’t come to terms with it.
Rowan: Such is the state of things.

Her path is her path, and I am not one to judge it 
regardless of my position within.
Rowan: I am sure everything will work out in the end, at 
the pace most appropriate.
Kara: Hmm...?

So you choose the path where you have no actions 
to take or effort to exert?
Rowan: Ah...
Rowan: Haha... There may be some... indisputable truth to 
that.
Rowan lowered his finger to take a dollop of icing 
off Charlotte’s mostly untouched slice of cake.
Rowan: Could one truly blame me? When it offers an extra 
serving of aftermeal sweets as so?
The icing covered finger slid betwixt his lips.
Rowan: Ah... As deliciously chosen as ever, my ever lovely 
Lady Kara.
Charlotte: ...

Say that again.
Charlotte was staring daggers at a member of the 
Crows.
Crow: Uh... w- well... Like I said, we exceeded our 
operations budget by about 5% this month.

And... uh... Yeah. Still just that.
Charlotte felt around for her holstered fire arm. 

Half ready to shoot the messenger.
Charlotte: How... dare you...
Crow: W- What...?
Charlotte: ...!
Charlotte breathed in deeply.
Rowan: ...!?
Rowan: Ah...
Rowan winced from the sharp pain in his ears.
Rowan: That was...?
His head turned around the corner to see Charlotte 
yelling at a member of the Nightless Crows.
Rowan: Haha... I imagine Norde will be hearing about this 
soon enough.
Rowan: Is the stress getting to her?
Rowan: Is it... related to... me?
Rowan sighed a dramatic sigh. One that acted like 
it wanted to be heard.
Rowan: Alas, no savior to my rescue.
Rowan: ...
He continued to observe Charlotte.
Charlotte: ...and ANOTHER thing...!
Rowan: It doesn’t truly matter who she believes I am, does 
it? I cannot say that I care.
Rowan: Ah... I have an idea.

Oh... happy day.

Happy days to come, for her and me~
passages.content_zh:
Charlotte: 嗯~...
夏洛特將玻璃杯湊到唇邊，吸入了茶的清爽香氣。
Charlotte: 啊... 甜度恰到好處。
Charlotte: 妳真的總是知道該怎麼挑選，卡拉。
Kara: 我想妳會喜歡這個
混合茶。

妳有沒有看到我們點心的每日特餐？上面有一顆草莓。
Charlotte: 這開始感覺像大一那次了。
Charlotte: 或者... 嗯... 我大一的時候，我的意思是。我們去了一個有草莓甜點的地方。
Kara: 我確實記得有這麼一個地方。
Charlotte: 那時也是草莓蛋糕嗎？光是想到那個味道就覺得好懷念~
夏洛特燦爛的笑容迎向了送來三塊草莓蛋糕的女服務生。
Kara: 我不認為妳那天真的有吃到蛋糕。
Charlotte: 什麼？我當然有吃到。
Charlotte: 我還記得草莓的味道刺激。
Kara: 那也許妳是改天又去了？
Charlotte: 喔，我不會對妳做那種事。
Kara: 我會說這是唯一的可能性。
Charlotte: 為什麼妳這麼難相信？那天對妳來說不也是開心的一天嗎？
Kara: ...
卡拉調整了一下姿勢，更直接地面對夏洛特。
Kara: 嗯... 那天最奇怪的事情是...
Kara: 妳還記得我們出去玩，妳迷路了，我必須安排人來接妳嗎？
Charlotte: 呃- 嗯... 我當時是大一新生，在一個新的大城市裡迷路了。
Charlotte: 呃- 呃... 妳想說什麼？
Kara: 就是同一次出遊。
Charlotte: 我- 我...
Kara: 這樣的記憶很難形成，不是嗎？
Charlotte: 我們之後又去了...? 或者也許另一家店有...?
Kara: 以上皆不適用於我們的出遊。

事實上，這家店本身就是最近才開張的那家小咖啡館的分店。這是一種特色產品。
Charlotte: 我...
Charlotte: 對- 對不起...
Kara: 不用道歉。

最重要的是，我很高興看到記憶運作的神秘方式。
Charlotte: 還是...
Rowan: 如果妳想複

passages.name: SP: PupxCharlotte C - First
passages.content:
I gritted my teeth. I forced myself to continue 
walking.

My arms felt as though they were on fire.

But I wouldn’t dare admit that aloud.
Pup: (Especially... with HER around...)
Charlotte: What’s wrong? Do you need some help?
Charlotte had turned around to see me carrying the 
shopping bags.
Charlotte: ...
Charlotte: Ah... Let me check something.
With a smirk, Charlotte pulled a bag and lifted it up 
over her shoulder.
Pup: Hey... I’m fine, you don’t need to...
Charlotte: Could’ve fooled me, with all that grunting and 
wheezing.
Pup: I’m just... a bit winded. I did sword training in the 
morning.
Charlotte: And I did some shooting practice.
Charlotte: Ever try to use a bow that can penetrate armor? 
Think of the draw weight that needs.
Pup: I am well aware. I grew up around a band of 
mercenaries, remember?
Charlotte: One would think a mercenary kid would understand 
physical limits better.
Pup: It’s... You know it’s only...
Pup: It’s the curse. It’s been hitting me harder than 
normal today...
Pup: Not that you deserve that much of an explanation.
Charlotte: ...
With a huff, I had closed my eyes and turned my 
head away to prepare myself for another teasing 
blow.
Charlotte: Then you’ll be fine resting for a bit.
Charlotte: While I... uh...
She cleared her throat.
Charlotte: ...answer the call of nature...
With hastened, muffled words hidden behind the 
distraction of a beaming smile... 

The ever delightful princess gingerly ducked around 
a corner towards a nearby shop.
Pup: S- Sure... I’ll...
She exited my sight.
Pup: I’ll watch your bags.

...

...............
Pup: *SIGH*...!
I collapsed against the alley wall with my 
exasperated exhale.
Pup: Thank the Goddess... My arms felt like they were 
about to fall off.
Slinking further down into a sitting position, my 
eyelids felt heavy.

I left them drift closed.
Pup: Maybe just...

(...a little... nap...)
Thug: ...look what we have here...
My eyes creeped open and the light was obscured 
by several silhouettes.

Silhouettes of...
Pup: (People)

(Young adults)

(Young men)

(Thugs)

...
Pup: ...!
I jumped to my feet.
Pup: E- Excuse me? Who are...?
As my senses came back to me, I found myself 
surrounded by a group of five men around my age.
Thug: What’s a pretty girl like you doing all alone here?
Pup: Girl?
The thug raised his eyebrow, and his friends behind 
him also chuckled.
Pup: W- Wait? Me!? I’m no girl!
Thug: Ha! Funny one.
The entire group laughed along, unclear if they 
found it funny or were following the guy’s lead.
Thug: Come on, now. No way someone as cute as you 
could be a guy.

You’ll have to try harder than that to get rid of me, 
babe~
He pressed closer, and his size became imposing.
Pup: (The Goddess’s underpants... have I shrunk that 
much? Was I always this... this...)
Pup: ...?!
The thug had slammed his hand against the wall 
inches from my face.

He leaned in, and the whole ordeal had 
shocked me.
Pup: Hah! I’m not “your babe”, you creep!
Thug: How about we start with introductions? 
Your name?
He smiled that creepy smile, and I felt like punching 
him.
Pup: (My arms still feel...)
Pup: (If it was just him, I could, but...)
My eyes scanned the full group of five blocking all 
my exit paths.
Pup: Anton. Anton Baranov.
Thug: Pft... Pretty masculine name for a pretty thing like 
yourself, no?
Pup: Almost like it’s a name for a guy. 
Like I told you, moron.
Thug: Eh? Well... I guess you are a bit disheveled for a 
chick...
Thug: Eh? Well... I guess you are a bit flat chested for a 
chick...
He paused, scanning me lecherously.
Thug: Heh. Never been with a tomboy before...
He started twirling a finger in the air, before 
leaning in and sniffing.
Thug: Hm... Lilac? What a nice smell.
I closed my eyes.
Pup: (This isn’t happening...!)
A hand cupped my cheek.
Pup: G- Get away from me!
I went for a kick to the groin...!

But...
Thug: Been there, done that.
He closed his knees to trap my leg before it could 
make contact.
Thug Grunt: Haha! Boss got them moves!

Ladykiller there!
Thug: Heh. Yeah. That ain’t gonna work on me, babe.
Charlotte: Then how about this!?
Thug: Argh!
A shopping bag came crashing down hard over his 
head.
Pup: (An opening!)
I dived forward through a gap between the men!

With a somersault and springing myself to my feet, 
I was away from the wall.
Pup: Charlotte?!
Charlotte: ...
She winked at me as she started to spin another 
bag into a mini-tornado.
Charlotte: Now who’s next, you filthy shit-eating perverts!?
So a thug brilliant volunteered as he lunged at her.
Like a flail, the bag smashed down onto his head.
Thug Grunt: The hell’s sort of arm does that chick got?!
The lead thug rubbed his head and stood up.
Thug: That’s assault, you bitch! I could call the guard on 
your for that!
Charlotte: Oh do try.

Gonna have to get past my friend ‘La Tornade’ 
here first, though.
She brandished the high momentum and spinning 
bag at the thug.
Thug: Oh, ya gonna take on all five of us with just two of 
you bitches?
Charlotte: ...
With her smirk withering just a touch, Charlotte’s 
eyes shifted to me.
Pup: (She’s not confident about our odds, either...)
Both us knew we couldn’t just brute force way out 
of this.
Pup: (I got to try something... I got to try...)
I closed my eyes in concentration. 
Searching for an answer.

Anything I could just say to help.

Then a memory popped into my head.
Rowan: ...
And it all clicked into place.
Pup: Ha...
Pup: Hahaha...
Pup: HAHAHA!
Thug: What the...? W- What’s so funny?!
Pup: The absurdity of it!

To think... you’d fall for my very first trap!
Thug: T- Trap?!
Pup: You’d have to be blind to not see the reports...
Pup: “Group of thugs harass young women”
Pup: You’re infamous in the wrong places to be 
infamous.
I saw the group’s lead take a step back.
Pup: Did you really expect to find a noblewoman 
defenseless and alone? With no protection in the 
wings?
Thug Grunt: A- A noble?! B- Boss, should we really be doin’ 
this?!
Thug: S- Shut it! Don’t let her fool you so easily, boys. 
She ain’t no noble.

Just look at her.
Pup: Such hope you’ve given... to something so easy to 
prove.
I reached into my equipment and pulled out...!

My locket!
Thug Grunt: Shit... Is that an heirloom?
It may have been a trick of the light, but the locket 
almost looked like it was glowing.

Like it was prepared to protect me.
Thug: Noble bitches or not, ya still fucking assaulted us. 
You got no proof we did shit.
Pup: Haha... So we bow down to a simple ‘word against 
word’ with the guard?

Oh, I wonder, I wonder... whose word they would 
believe?
I plastered the haughtiest look I could on my face, 
all the while jingling the locket for emphasis.
Thug: ...
Pup: ...
Thug: FUCK!

Run boys! We’ve been had!
The gang of thugs sprinted down the alley and 
disappeared around a bend.
Pup: ...
Pup: GAHH!!!
The tension released from my body and my heart 
stopped pounding as hard.
Charlotte: Actually a brilliant play there from our little pup.
Pup: What? Oh that?
Pup: I just... made that up.
Charlotte: It was actually a pretty convincing argument.

Maybe a tad melodramatic, but it was better than I 
could’ve come up with on the spot. And I’m an 
actual noble.
Pup: Oh, that’s... not entirely true.
Pup: You have very convincing... fists...
Charlotte: ...
Pup: ...
Both: *Laughing*...!
Charlotte: I suppose so. Maybe I should try them out more 
often?
Pup: On... uninformed targets, of course.
Charlotte: Guess we’ll chalk this one up as a team effort.
Pup: I mean... I would’ve clobbered them too if it wasn’t 
for this curse...
Charlotte: I’m sure you would’ve.
As I locked eyes with Charlotte, she looked like she 
looked at me wistfully.

There wasn’t any condescension in her tone, 
for once.
Charlotte: Don’t worry. I’ll protect you if any others show up.
She put a hand on my shoulder reassuringly.
Pup: ...
And retracted it just as swiftly.
Charlotte: A- As I would do for anyone.

I just hate those damned handsy creeps, you 
know?

You even get them in court events and fancy 
parties.
Pup: Ah, yeah. I can imagine.
Pup: Though, maybe we should get going before any 
witnesses actually do call the guards.
passages.content_zh:
我咬牙切齒。我強迫自己繼續
步行。

我的手臂感覺好像著火了。

但我不敢大聲承認這一點。
Pup：（特別是……有她在身邊……）
夏洛特：怎麼了？您需要協助嗎？
夏洛特轉過身來看到我拿著
購物袋。
夏洛特：…
夏洛特：啊……讓我檢查一下。
夏綠蒂壞笑一聲，拉起一個袋子，將它舉了起來。 
在她的肩膀上。
Pup：嘿…我很好，你不用…
夏洛特：我可能會被這些咕噥聲和
喘息。
Pup：我只是……有點氣喘吁籲。我在訓練劍
早上。
夏洛特：我做了一些射擊練習。
夏洛特：試過使用可以穿透盔甲的弓嗎？ 
想想所需的拉力。
小狗：我很清楚。我是在一群樂團的陪伴下長大的
僱傭兵，還記得嗎？
夏洛特：人們會認為一個僱傭兵的孩子會理解
物理限制更好。
Pup：這是…你知道這只是…
小狗：這是詛咒。這對我的打擊比
今天正常...
Pup：並不是說你值得那麼多解釋。
夏洛特：…
我氣呼呼地閉上眼睛，轉過身去
走開，為另一次戲弄做好準備
吹。
夏洛特：那你休息一下就好了。
夏洛特：雖然我…呃…
她清了清喉嚨。
夏綠蒂：……響應大自然的召喚…
隱藏在背後的匆忙、低沉的話語
燦爛的笑容分散了注意力…

永遠可愛的公主小心翼翼地躲開
一個轉角處通往附近的一家商店。
小狗：當然…我會…
她退出了我的視線。
小狗：我會看管你的包包的。

…

............
小狗：*嘆氣*...！
我癱倒在巷子的牆上
惱怒地呼氣。
小狗：感謝女神…我的手臂感覺就像是
快要掉下來了。
進一步下滑到坐姿，我的
眼皮感覺沉重。

我讓它們漸漸關閉。
小狗：也許只是…

（……稍微……小睡一下……）
暴徒：……看看我們這裡有什麼…
我的眼睛慢慢睜開，光線被遮住了
由幾個剪影。

S

passages.name: SP: NordexJenny C - First
passages.content:
Norde: That would get them killed.
Pup: Well... Hmm...
Pup: What if I... grease the ground?
Norde: Wouldn’t that assume you have a jar of grease on 
hand at any given moment?
Norde and I had been discussing tactics. 

Between us was a board meant to represent a 
battlefield. One with tiles representing enemies, 
allies, terrain, and objectives.
I had, at multiple occasions, slipped up and referred 
to it as a game in front of Norde.
Norde: ...
Norde was not amused.
Pup: You know, Rowan might.
Pup: Carry around a jar of grease, I mean.
Norde just rose an eyebrow.
Norde: Then you gamble on luck alone.
Pup: Okay... fine.
Pup: How about I skirt the enemy’s range with the 
tank?
Norde: Without getting into the logistics of measuring 
that...

Let’s assume you can bait attacks. It would still be 
inefficient.

What if that gives time for reinforcements to arrive? 
Or we wear out our troops?
Norde: More importantly, you are giving the prerogative to 
the enemy to execute their own strategies.

Ambushes, group rushes...
Pup: I get it...
Pup: Then how about sending our strongest ally in to 
wear down the enemy?

When they’re weak, we can send in reinforcements 
to finish them off.
Norde: That’s... slightly more efficient. 
Only slightly, though.
Norde: At least you’re taking the initiative in the battle.
Norde: But mercenaries with no real hands on experience 
against trained units will rust.

Our troops need experience or they will never 
grow. We need real fighting experience for real
mercenaries.
Pup: ...

Dad could’ve taken them out by himself, though.
Norde: And heroes like that are rare. They even can die...

Sometimes even the best of us meet tragic ends 
without support.
Pup: ...
Pup: Did you... have to say it like that?
Norde: It... is what it is.
And then suddenly a red hair girl popped into 
their perception.
Jenny: Oh, are you moving figurines around this board?
Jenny: Are you playing a...
Jenny: ...a- a game...?
Pup: ...
Norde: ...
Jenny: I’ll... come back later...
Without moving any muscles above her hip, Jenny 
scurried back to the tent door with a crab walk.

Step by slow step, she shuffled deftly through the 
tent entrance.
Norde: *Sigh*... I need to take a break.
Pup: ...

(Yeah, I could use a breather, too.)
We left soon after, leaving the tactics figurines on 
the table.
Norde: Have you cooled off as well?
Pup: ...Yeah.
Norde: One must accept the realities of war. Especially 
when others’ lives are in our hands.
As we went to enter the tent, the red-haired girl 
exited the tent.

Our situation distracted us too much to notice who 
it was beyond the hair color.
Norde: To review the scenario we were discussing... 
Bandits here, forest here, and your units here.

How do you proceed?
Pup: ...
Pup: Nothing?
Norde: Wrong.

What sort of answer is that?
Pup: Did you look at the board?
Norde: ...
Norde: The board?
The figurines were positioned in such a way that I 
had basically won against Norde’s troops. I didn’t 
even need to move them.
Norde: You didn’t move these before we left?
Pup: No...
Norde: ...

After?
Pup: No!

Did you move them?
Norde: Why would I do that?
Pup: Why would I?!
I gave Norde a stink-eye, but it was paid no mind.
Norde: Hmm... Perhaps...?
Norde’s feet were soon moving and out of the 
tent.
Soon enough, Norde returned with a red haired girl 
being pulled along.
Jenny: I- I don’t wanna be corrupted~...!
Pup: Norde, what are you doing...?
Norde: VIP retrieval.

A good skill for a mercenary.
Pup: Sure, I’ll just... write that down...
Jenny: C- Compliments won’t make me want you to 
corrupt me more, you know!
Norde: I am not doing... whatever that is. I do not even 
know what it means.
Jenny: Then how do you know you’re not doing it?
Norde: ...!
Jenny: S- Scary...
Pup: Tell me about it...
Norde pulled Jenny up from her prone position and 
to her feet.
Norde: Did you move the figurines?
Jenny: Oh! I’m sorry! I didn’t realize they were important!
Norde: Show us what you did.
Jenny: I... I just thought it was a game. So I moved the 
blue pieces so they could win.
Norde: Show us... what you... did...
Jenny: Y- Yes! Sorry!
Jenny scurried over the table with the figurines. I 
had moved them to our previous positions again.
Jenny: It wasn’t much. Just a simple idea.
Jenny: Just capitalize on your units’ movement range and 
set them up in terrain that’s most appropriate to
their class.
Move this guy here... and this one here... and... 
voila!
We both peeked over Jenny’s shoulders to look at 
the endeavor.
Pup: ...
Pup: You didn’t need grease?
Jenny: No? Do you bring grease everywhere?
Pup: No.

...

I’ll be right back.
I ducked out of the tent and left the two behind.
Norde: An excellent demonstration...
Jenny: “Jenny”
Norde: Yes, an excellent demonstration, Jenny.
Norde: Pup would do well to learn from you.

Dividing one’s units to cover more ground is 
important.
Jenny: Uh...
Norde: Do you have something to add?
Jenny: Just that... Well...
Norde: It is fine.
Jenny: Okay. Then if I may...

Dividing a squad for completion speed can work in 
some scenarios, but not others.

Imagine you are in the middle of the night or in a 
heavy mist.

Spreading out when visibility is not in your favor can 
let an archer or mage pick off allies from a blind 
spot.
Jenny: Turtling to avoid casualties can be more efficient, at 
times.
Norde: A fair point. I may have spoken too generally.
Norde: But... consider this scenario: You are inside a 
fortress.
Norde: Visibility is also going to be limited with the twisting
corridors.

How do you make sure you have looted the place 
in as timely a manner as possible?
Jenny: I’ll admit I have a bit of a bias there. My luck with 
chests is... bad.
Jenny: With that being said, I would check if they’re 
trapped or not before looting.
Jenny: And before that, shouldn’t you secure the place 
first?
Jenny: A dead friend is heavier than any piles of gold we 
can carry.
Norde: ...
Norde: Right. Of course that’s right...
Jenny: Ah, no need to feel gloomy~ I’m sure every tactic 
is valid to a scenario out there.
Pup: I’m back!
And I was holding a jar of grease.
Pup: I got Rowan’s grease!
Norde: ...
Jenny: Like... grease. I’m... sure there’s a good place to 
use that as a tactic.
Jenny: Everything can be a good tactic if placed well.
Norde: Goddess... I feel like I am being talked down to.
Pup: Any tactic? What about broken weapons?
Jenny: Why are you... going into battle with broken 
weapons?
Pup: Uh... So I cannot harm the enemy? The battle lasts 
longer and...
Pup: That’d be good for... “real fighting experience for 
real mercenaries”?
Norde: You know I didn’t mean it like that.

That sounds incredibly inefficient and... put 
bluntly... stupid.
Norde: You couldn’t guard with half a blade.
Jenny: Are your battles THAT long?!
Jenny: I can’t say I have experience with broken weapons 
during battle.

Maybe that was the demon lord’s influence?
Norde: As much as we maintain weapons, they will 
eventually break with enough wear and tear.
Pup: Yeah...
Pup: Wait... “Demon Lord”?!

You mean like Zened the...
I went to point upwards to the sky, but...
Pup: Wait, it’s the middle of the day.
So I... pointed to the ground?
Pup: Like Zened the Moon?! THE Zened?! THE Moon?!
Jenny: Uh... I don’t think she was quite as round as the 
moon, I guess?
Pup: (SHE...?!)
Jenny: But the demon lord I did escape... I just barely 
managed to. By getting sent here... somehow...?
Pup: H- Hey, Norde... What do you... you...
I turned to a Norde that had a dour look of 
contemplation.

Mumbling... Scenarios to counter Jenny’s tactics... 
state of our weapons... Etc.
Jenny: Is Norde okay?
Pup: Norde will probably be... “fine”.
Pup: Eventually...
Jenny: Oh... is there nothing I can do?
Pup: Probably not.
Pup: Oh, but maybe there is one thing you could help 
with.
Jenny: Really?
Pup: Right, so this is important since many things could 
go wrong if we don’t do this.

...

Do not tell Rowan I stole his jar of grease.
passages.content_zh:
Norde：那會害死他們的。
小狗：嗯……嗯……
小狗：如果我…在地上塗油怎麼辦？
Norde：那不是假設你身上有一罐油脂嗎？ 
在任何特定時刻手？
諾德和我一直在討論戰術。 

我們之間有一個委員會，代表一個
戰場。一張代表敵人的瓷磚，
盟友、地形和目標。
我曾多次疏失並轉介
將其視為 Norde 面前的一場遊戲。
諾德：…
諾德並沒有被逗樂。
Pup：你知道，Rowan 可能會。
小狗：我是說，隨身攜帶一罐油脂。
諾德只是揚起一邊眉毛。
Norde：那你就只能賭運氣了。
小狗：好吧……好吧。
Pup：我用
坦克？
Norde：無需進入測量流程
那...

假設您可以誘餌攻擊。仍然會是
效率低。

如果這給了增援部隊到達的時間呢？ 
還是我們的部隊疲憊不堪？
Norde：更重要的是，你賦予了特權
敵人執行自己的策略。

伏擊、集體衝鋒…
小狗：我明白了...
Pup：那麼派我們最強大的盟友去怎麼樣？ 
削弱敵人？

當他們虛弱時，我們可以派出援軍
來結束他們。
Norde：這……稍微更有效率。 
不過只有一點點。
Norde：至少你在戰鬥中佔據了主動。
Norde：但是沒有真正實務經驗的傭兵
對抗訓練有素的單位會生鏽。

我們的部隊需要經驗，否則他們永遠不會
成長。我們需要真實的戰鬥經驗
僱傭兵。
小狗：…

不過，爸爸可以自己把它們拿出來。
Norde：像這樣的英雄很少見。他們甚至可以死...

有時，即使是我們中最好的人也會遭遇悲慘的結局
沒有支援。
小狗：…
Pup：你……一定要這麼說嗎？
Norde：這……就是這樣。
然後突然一個紅髮女孩闖了進來
他們的看法。
珍妮：哦，你在這塊板上移動小雕像嗎？
珍妮：你在玩...
珍妮：……一個－－遊戲……？
小狗：…
諾德：…
珍妮：我……稍後再回來

passages.name: SP: Pup x Otisl B - Begining
passages.content:
*Chop*!
Pup: I- I... I can’t believe I’m doing this.
*Chop*!
Otis: Ya have a problem with it, lad?
*Chop*!
Otis: Don’t see much differentiation between this n’ 
what ya normally do.
*Chop*!
Pup: It just... feels wrong.
*Chop*!
Norde: ...!

Stop talking...

...and more...

...more wood-chopping.
A split log fell to the ground around 
everyone’s feet.
Norde: Wood won’t chop itself.
The passing remark came and went as Norde exited 
and left hearing range to continue rounds.
Otis: I still don’t see any problem in handlin’ our wood 
together.

I see you handle wood with other folk all the time.
Otis: Unless... you’re a laddy-lass that prefers to handle 
their wood alone?
Pup: ...This.
Pup: *Sigh*... This is what I was referring to.

Do you really still need to be so... unnecessarily 
dirty all the time?
Otis: Heh, just teasing ya a bit lassyloo.

Nothin’ wrong with two laddies handlin’ some 
mornin’ wood.
Pup: Just because it’s the morning doesn’t make this 
“morning wood”.
Otis: Alas, laddy-lass! I never knew.
Otis: I must retrieve my ‘mourning’ wood to cope with 
this stroke of crisis.
Pup: *Sigh*... Sometimes I just wanna...
Pup: Hmm...

(Two people... two lads... conflict...)
Pup: A duel?
Otis: Eh? I don’t know what ya was taught, but take 
your morning wood at your own pace.

A competition may turn it sour.
Pup: A duel in combat. If I win, then you stop all this 
vulgar stuff around me.
Otis: Eh? I guess I haven’t done one in ages. 

People get scared at beating a small girl or gettin’ 
beat by one.
Otis: So what’s your ante?
Pup: Uh...
Pup: One week’s salary! I’ll give you a week of my salary!
Otis: That’s ya prize pool?

Give me an hour an’ I’ll have more loot than that on 
me own.
Otis: Three months.
Pup: U- Uh... Two weeks...
Otis: Oh so confident, aren’t ya laddylass?
Pup: One month!
Otis: Deal.
Otis: Call it a week. In one week at high noon.
Otis: Get the grumpy fiend to officiate.
Pup: Deal...!
One Week Later
Pup: ...!
I twirled a sword as I stood in the impromptu 
dueling ring.
Pup: ...
I breathed in with my weapon ready to strike.

And...
Norde: ...
Pup: ...
Pup: Where is he?!
Pup: It’s almost high noon already...
Pup: (And I’m starting to really... need to go the 
bathroom?)
Norde: I have places to be. Why am I even here?
Pup: To officiate the duel.
Norde: ...
Fellow Crow: Norde. I have a message from Otis.
The Crow whispered into Norde’s ear.
Norde: Thank you for the message.

Let's see what it says...
Norde turned my way.
Norde: I am leaving. Otis cannot participate and has 
requested a postponement.
Pup: So I... I won?
Norde: It doesn’t-
Norde: ...

Sure.
Norde left as quickly as possible.
Pup: Yes! Victory!

(No more vulgar shit from that fucking crap mouth 
of his!)

(I can’t wait to rub his shit eating grin in this!)
After looking around for some time, no one had a 
good idea for where Otis was.

But as I passed through a nearby building, that’s 
when I saw him.

Walking slouched with his hands on his stomach.
Otis: Urgh...
Pup: Hey... So... About the duel...
Pup: It’s my win. You were given a forfeit.
Pup: Oh... What was that? Right. Cat’s got your tongue.

You can’t say your innuendos anymore~
Otis: Shove it up your end-o, you noisy twat!
Pup: ...
Pup: Sheesh... No need to get that angry.
Pup: Getting into sore loser territory there.
Otis: Just leave, Pup. I... have important matters to 
attend to.
Pup: Really? That’s your big excuse after all this?
Pup: Aren’t you the “do whatever I want” territory’s 
local nobility?
Otis: Sure, yeah. Normally...

Not today... Since today...

...rains crimson.
Otis: Now leave!
Pup: ...Huh? What are you-
Pup: Ugh...
A stomach cramp hit me.
Pup: (Okay... yeah... so the meat was expired...)
Pup: Be... right back.
Pup: (Bathroom, bathroom, bathroom!)

...!
Pup: Phew...!
Pup: ...
Pup: (What? Is... nothing... happening?)
Pup: (Though upfront, something is wet?)

...
Pup: ...?!
I nearly jumped from the seat.
Pup: B- Blood?! Why?!
Pup: *Sniff*... W- Why...?

(Is that... a tear?!)
I thought it had to be some evil magical attack.

I tried to think of any time we encountered magic 
like this and...
Pup: (Ugh! C- Cramp! Getting... worse...!)

(Is this the curse somehow, too?!)
Pup: (Why...)

(Why am I not...? I don't feel normal...)

(Like I’m... broken...)
Pup: *Sniff*
Otis: ...
*Knock knock*
Otis: *Clears throat*

Lassie-lad. I’ve noticed you’ve been in the toilet for 
over an hour.
Otis: Figured I should check on ya...
Pup: *Sniff*
Pup: That’s...
Pup: That’s uncharacteristically... nice of you.
Otis: Ya sound quite the mess for someone that’d won a 
duel today.
Pup: I- I don’t know what’s happening anymore...

Terrible stomachaches... Then I sat down and just 
had... blood... from... yeah...
Otis: Hmm...
Otis: Heh. That’s a wickedly awful sense of humor.
Pup: Huh?
Otis: That damned Oathbreaker sword whatcha’ma’callit.
Otis: Got the nerve to make us have our periods on the 
same day.
Otis: *Sigh*...
I could hear an exasperated Otis loudly lean against 
the bathroom’s door.
Pup: Period...?

(Oh... Goddess... I didn’t even think of... of that...)
Otis: Normal me woulda bragged about liking something 
long n’ sturdy to pierce me...
Otis: But I just “lost” my joke making privileges.
Pup: I, for one, can’t wait to bury my long thick sword 
into Wolf’s behind after he caused all this.
Otis: Heh. Careful what you ask for, laddy-lass.

But do keep makin’ ‘em jokes for the both of us. I 
love it.
Pup: I just...
Pup: Don’t worry about the duel results... I can get why 
you were a no show.
Pup: I think there’s a long and hard day ahead of us for 
when we do actually duel...
Otis: Eh? Well, we gotta long and hard day ahead of us 
after I win the duel.
Pup: Ahaha... Things to look forward to.
passages.content_zh:
*劈*！
Pup: 我...我...我真不敢相信我在做這個。
*劈*！
Otis: 你有問題嗎，小子？
*劈*！
Otis: 看不出這跟你平常做的事情有什麼區別。
*劈*！
Pup: 只是...感覺不太對。
*劈*！
Norde: ...！

別說話...

...多劈一點...

...多劈點木頭。
一塊劈開的木頭落在大家腳邊。
Norde: 木頭不會自己劈。
Norde隨口說了一句，然後離開了，走出了聽力範圍，繼續巡邏。
Otis: 我還是不覺得我們一起處理木頭有什麼問題。

我經常看到你和其他人一起處理木頭。
Otis: 除非...你是個小姑娘，喜歡自己處理木頭？
Pup: ...這個。
Pup: *嘆氣*...我指的就是這個。

你真的還需要一直這麼...沒必要地齷齪嗎？
Otis: 呵呵，只是逗你一下，小妞。

兩個小伙子一起處理早上的木頭沒什麼不對。
Pup: 只是因為是早上，並不代表這是「早上的木頭」。
Otis: 哎呀，小姑娘！我從來不知道。
Otis: 我必須找回我的「哀悼」木頭來應對這場危機。
Pup: *嘆氣*...有時候我只想...
Pup: 嗯...

（兩個人...兩個小伙子...衝突...）
Pup: 決鬥？
Otis: 蛤？我不知道你學了什麼，但按你自己的節奏來處理你的早上的木頭。

比賽可能會讓它變質。
Pup: 一場戰鬥決鬥。如果我贏了，你就停止在我身邊說這些粗俗的東西。
Otis: 蛤？我想我已經很久沒做過了。

人們害怕打敗一個小女孩，或者被一個小女孩打敗。
Otis: 那麼你的賭注是什麼？
Pup: 呃...
Pup: 一個星期的薪水！我給你一個星期的薪水！
Otis: 這就是你的獎金池？

給我一個小時，我就會有比那更多的戰利品。
Otis: 三個月。
Pup: 嗚...兩個星期...
Otis: 喔，這麼有自信，不是嗎，小妞？
Pup: 一個月！
Otis: 成交。
Otis: 就定在一周後。一周後正午。
Otis: 讓那個脾氣暴躁的傢伙來主持。
Pup: 成交...！
一周後
Pup: ...！
我站在原地，轉動著一把劍。

passages.name: SP: Satia x Otis B - Begining
passages.content:
Guard A: *Yawn*... Zzzzzzzz......
Guard B: Come on, man. Stay awake. I’m not your damned 
alarm.
Guard A: ...then... don’t wake... me...
Guard B: All ya fuckin’ gotta do is look pretty and make a 
show of it. I’m not getting fired cause you’re that
lazy!
Guard A: Then get fired for... waking up the dead... Dealer’s 
choice.
Guard B: What the HELL are ya on about?!
Guard A: I dunno... Got like four hours of sleep... Your 
shrieks are like gunshots...

This herb I’m runnin’ on only helps so much.
Guard B: Goddess’s underpants, I get the damned druggie!
Guard A: Well if it’ll shut you up... Shit ain’t doing anything 
for me.

No night vision... Just makes the ground look like 
the best bed you could get... and...

...and... makes everythin’ smell like vinegar.
Guard B: Of for fuck’s sake, I...!

I...

Vinegar? I smell vinegar too.
The guard spun around, and he started blinking 
rapidly.
Guard B: My eyes... The hell’s wrong with them?!
Guard A: Heh. Someone picklin’ around here?
Guard B: No you dumbass! We gotta check inside. It’s comin’ 
from within!
Grabbing the other guard, the two made their way 
to the entrance.
Guard A: Ugh... Whatever...
Guard A: *Cough cough*! What the hell?!
A miasma of gas seeped out from the cracks of the 
sliding heavy door.
Guard B: R- Run... We... gotta...
Guard A: The... hell... I feel... Ugh...!
Otis: By the Goddess with a dick on the side... I knew 
this stuff was good, but not THAT good!
Satia: Focus.
As Otis snickered his head off, Satia went to 
inspect one of the fainted men.
Otis: Have some fun, Momma. Whatcha even need to 
focus on?
Satia: ...still breathing. Hmm...
Otis: Careful with your pretty face around that 
concoction.

Back in the day, these damned fungi ruined so 
many of the trade shipments that I was itchin’ to 
get sold.
Otis: One time a lad of mine thought burnin’ the shit 
would be good enough to save some of the 
product.
Otis: T’is not his brightest idea... as the result of this 
merry jaunt do show.
Satia: And they are 100% likely to live?
Satia: Your bet does depend on it.
Otis: Heheh...
Satia: It’s your ass on the line.
Otis: Not yours, Momma?
Satia: Just... get inside.
In order to finish preparations, Otis stepped away 
from Satia and did a final inventory of the fungi 
bombs.
Otis: Eh... Would’ve been cheaper to do it the normal 
way. Might not even break even with this...
Otis, as he did inventory, started to eye Satia’s 
bum.
Otis: Heh. Somethings money can’t buy.
Otis: Now go, my Murder of Crows!

Grab the loot and smash the rest! Ahahahaha!
Crow: Ugh... of course he makes up a name.
The Nightless Crows broke in through the open 
door to find a won battle with smoldering 
remains and knocked out guards.
The fungi bombs had spread effectively and didn’t 
leave one person left to resist.
Otis: Argh! Rum this bad is barely worth drinkin’, let alone 
sellin’...
Otis: ...but still fun to break!
Satia: ...”Galzus Trading Company”...
Satia looked at the box’s logo with little hiding her
disgust. She raised her weapon, and...
Satia: It’s like a shell of its former self.

Not even a shell company for horrid deeds... Just 
ruined to the core even with their products.
Satia: In a sense, your skullduggery tonight is almost an 
admirable goal.
Otis: “Almost”? That hurts, Momma.
Satia: Don’t call me that.
Otis: Got it twice. Don’t blame me goin’ for triplets.
Satia: Well, you should go for triplets of tearing down 
these 'rotten to the core' companies.
Otis: Ya know, I did make it a point to go after ‘em with 
my pirate fellas.
Satia: *Sigh*...
Otis: Eh!? I did, though. Had a shit list knifed to a galley 
wall and everythin’!
Otis: The shite those bastards put me through as soon 
as I wasn’t a long dicked merchant anymore? Fuck 
‘em.
Satia: Well... you’re not the only one with bad memories 
of noble merchants like this.
Satia: ...
Otis: ...
Otis stood there as Satia lost herself in the bottle 
smashing. He was content to let her have that 
moment.
Some time passed between each shattering glass.
Crow: ...and that’s all the valuables we could snag. Not all 
that much.
Otis: Ay... Part of the business but sad when it happens 
all the same.
Otis: Let’s get before the guards catch on. Ain’t got 
shrooms left for them.
Crow: Speaking of the mushroom bombs, there was 
one that didn’t go off.
Otis: Eh? Nice. Might be the most worthwhile thing 
here.
Satia: They seem like they’d be useful for the future, 
too.
Otis: Oh? Happy with ‘em?

Not in my normal wheelhouse to get, but I’ll be 
sure to keep my fluffy little ears out for ‘em.
The group headed out, and Otis followed Satia as 
she fled from the scene.

And as they did, Otis decided to speak up.
Otis: And... listen, Satia.
Otis: I respect ya keeping stuff close to your bosom. But 
if ya ever need to speak with someone...
As Satia was about to round a corner, she stopped 
and the others stopped with her.
Satia: ...
Satia: Hmph.
Satia turned liked a knife through the crowd of 
fleeing Crows.
Satia: Why, Otis! Look at you.

Trying to double dip on a bet, are you~?

I thought you wanted to get in my pants, not dig 
into my life story.
Otis: Eh?!
Satia: You are quite ‘ballsy’ for a lass... especially after 
such a middling success!
Otis: Ay! After what you gave me to work with, anyone 
would’a considered that a success!

None of them lot died and we got some loot from 
it!
Otis leaned in as he shifted to offense.
Otis: And if ya seriously wanna make me choose?
Otis: Of course I’d want to know if the carpet matches 
that smooth, silky, pin-like-peach drapes!
Satia: W- What? You of all people should know that 
peaches aren’t pink...
Satia: And unlike you, I know how to use a razor...
Satia: And for constructive purposes over destructive 
ones, at that.
Otis: Eh? Then teach me. Ya can wrap your arms 
around me and...
Satia: Very funny. Such a jester you are, nekolyn~
Otis: You know that I love it when you get all hot and 
bothered.
Satia: Mayhap you should drop that pack of fungal brain 
rot.

With the curse, can you really risk what’s left?
Otis: Pft! If anythin’ the curse has made me smarter! 

So smart that I may be a bonafide genie-us!
Satia: ...
Satia: Are you just trying to hurt me now?
Otis: Heheh~ Consider it foreplay for tonight.

I’ve left many a girl with tears as the night brought 
on the morn’~
Satia: I meant that you were hurting my brain. Was yours 
not enough rot for us both?
Satia: And why would you take that as a compliment?!
Otis grabbed his petite belly and laughed a full 
sounding laugh.
Otis: Don’t worry, lassie!

You’ll be takin’ that and more by the time I’m done 
with-
Otis: Argh! The shrooms!?
Otis’s eyes scrambled as he watched the fungi 
bomb pack slip through his fingers.
Otis: *Cough cough cough*!
Satia: *Cough cough*...

Otis, you... stupid... dammit...! *Cough*...!
Crow: ...

Did they forget we were here?

...

*Sigh*... Come on guys.

Guards might still show up soon. Let’s drag ‘em 
outta here...
passages.content_zh:
守衛 A: *呵欠*... Zzzzzzzz......
守衛 B: 拜託，老兄。清醒點。我他媽的不是你的鬧鐘。
守衛 A: ...那就...別...吵醒...我...
守衛 B: 你他媽的只要看起來像樣，做做樣子就好。我可不想因為你這懶鬼被開除！
守衛 A: 那就因為...吵醒死人...被開除吧... 隨便你。
守衛 B: 你他媽的到底在說什麼鬼話？！
守衛 A: 我不知道... 大概只睡了四個小時... 你的尖叫聲就像槍聲...

我現在靠的這玩意兒也只能幫這麼多了。
守衛 B: 女神內褲啊，我真是受夠這該死的癮君子了！
守衛 A: 好吧，如果這樣能讓你閉嘴... 這玩意兒對我一點用都沒有。

沒有夜視能力... 只會讓地面看起來像是你能找到最好的床... 而且...

...而且... 讓所有東西聞起來都像醋。
守衛 B: 真是他媽的，我...！

我...

醋？我也聞到醋味了。
守衛轉過身，開始快速眨眼。
守衛 B: 我的眼睛... 到底怎麼了？！
守衛 A: 嘿嘿。有人在這裡醃東西嗎？
守衛 B: 你這蠢貨！我們得檢查裡面。是從裡面傳出來的！
抓住另一個守衛，兩人朝入口走去。
守衛 A: 呃... 隨便啦...
守衛 A: *咳嗽 咳嗽*！ 搞什麼鬼？！
一股毒氣從厚重滑動門的縫隙中滲出。
守衛 B: 跑... 快... 我們... 得...
守衛 A: 我... 感覺... 糟... 呃...！
奧提斯: 以長著雞巴的女神之名... 我知道這玩意兒很棒，但沒想到這麼棒！
莎提亞: 專心點。
當奧提斯咯咯地笑個不停時，莎提亞去檢查其中一個昏倒的人。
奧提斯: 開心點，老媽。你到底需要專心什麼？
莎提亞: ...還有呼吸。嗯...
奧提斯: 小心你的漂亮臉蛋，別靠那玩意兒太近。

想當年，這些該死的真菌毀了這麼多貿易貨物，我早就想把它們賣掉了。
奧提斯: 有一次，我的一個小夥子認為燒掉這些東西就足以拯救一些產品。
奧提斯: 這不是他最聰明的想法... 這次愉快的旅行的結果證明了這一點。
莎提亞: 然後呢

passages.name: SP: Pup x CHarlotte B - Begining
passages.content:
Pup: HIYYAA!!!
My sword bounced awkwardly off the dummy’s 
shield, leaving me wide open for a nonexistent 
counterattack.
Pup: *Sigh*...
Pup: Okay, let’s try that again...
I sized up my target and swung with a little more 
caution this time.
And so repeated the result.
Pup: Ugh... The hell is wrong with me?
I readied my sword for the third time.
Pup: ...
Pup: ...!
I raised my sword for the follow-through!
Pup: ...!
Pup: ...
Pup: *Sigh*...

(This doesn’t feel right. I’m only getting worse 
results.)
It had been a few hours of this endeavor, and I 
didn’t have much to show for it.

Besides a thoroughly chipped sword.
Pup: Hmm...
A memory popped into my head.
Ivan: Stubborn persistence isn’t always the answer. 
Sometimes it's just not meant to be.

If you try another approach, it could be insightful 
on what went wrong, at the very minimum.
Pup: (You’re right. That’s almost definitely right.)
I let the damaged sword fall unceremoniously into 
the dirt as I started walking towards the side of 
the training area.
The corner of my eye caught a blur of blonde hair 
in my vision. It turned away from me quickly.
Pup: Hm...?
The figure started fiddling with the gun holstered 
on her hip as if pretending to ignore me.
Pup: ...
Pup: ...Charlotte?
And the princess previously known as a blonde blur 
hesitantly turned her head towards me.
Charlotte: O- Oh... Hello... I didn’t see you there.
She had looked up with a seeming feigned 
confusion, and a tint of blush was waning 
from her visage.
Pup: (She’s not sick, is she?)
Pup: Are you feeling okay?
Charlotte: What? Of course... Why would you even ask that?
Pup: Well, you’re... uh...
Pup: ...acting a bit strangely...?
Charlotte: H- How so?!
Pup: Because... you “didn’t see me” as I was making a 
lot of noise while training...?
Charlotte: D- Don’t think so highly of yourself. You’re not as 
fascinating as you think.
Pup: ...
I blinked a few times. I didn’t know how to process 
that as a response to what I said.
Pup: Uh... How long were you standing there?
Charlotte: Not important.
She cleared her throat as she turned to her side 
and avoided eye contact.
Charlotte: You see, I came here to follow up on that tutoring 
I mentioned.
Pup: “Tutoring”...? Oh, do you mean that thing about 
nobility?
Charlotte: Sort of. I had a thought that it’d be good to go 
beyond just that.

We can go over the art of diplomacy itself: rhetoric, 
elocution, and so on.
Pup: ...
I found myself blinking in silence again.
Pup: Are we... speaking the same language? You didn’t 
just make those words up, did you?
Charlotte: Oho... So we’ve strained the limits of your feeble 
vocabulary, have we?
Pup: Charlotte...
Pup: (She’s acting like I’m some barbarian...)
Charlotte: Let me just start from the basics. In simpler terms...

I want to teach you to make more sense in 
debates and act more like a dignified, educated 
noble.
Charlotte: But maybe that was misguided.
Charlotte: If you’re too busy whacking hunks of metal with 
other hunks of metal, I’ll be on my way.
Charlotte pointed her pistol at the dummy and 
peered down the sights with a confident smirk.
Pup: This all coming from “La Tornade”?
Charlotte: ...
She lowered the gun and looked down with a 
crestfallen expression.
Charlotte: You remember that from last time, then...
Charlotte: Heh... I guess you’re right...
Pup: ...

(That’s... Crap. Did I say something too 
insensitive?)
Pup: You know... I was... I was just looking for a change 
of pace anyways.
Charlotte: ...
Charlotte looked over at me without any words 
spoken, but I could see a variety of emotions 
alternating on her face.
Pup: So sure. Let’s do this training. It might give me a 
new perspective.
Charlotte: ...
Charlotte: I...
Charlotte: *Clears throat*... Then maybe we should relocate 
to my quarters.
Charlotte: It’d be a more fitting venue.
Charlotte: In conclusion, you’re going to have to learn to rely 
more on wits and eloquence than theatrics.
Pup: But why?
Charlotte: Because it fits your personality better.
Charlotte: Persuasion is born from authenticity.
Charlotte: That’ll be the case whether its a sleezy noble telling 
a lie or you advocating for something you’re
passionate about.
Pup: What’s wrong with what I did before? Those 
alleyway thugs seemed perfectly well persuaded.
Charlotte: That was more of a matter of “right time, right 
place” for tricking some uneducated common folk.
Charlotte: With noble education, someone could’ve poked 
enough holes in it to see through it.
Pup: I... guess that makes sense.
Charlotte: Besides... I could tell you were channeling...
Charlotte: ...THAT thing...
Rowan: ...
Charlotte: There’s more to charisma than simple flamboyance.
Charlotte: Presenting a logical argument, for one.
Charlotte: And even if you don’t have a clear logic to give, 
just present it in a compelling way.
Charlotte: Like simply being nice could lead the other person 
to being agreeable.
Pup: I’m not sure I follow...
Charlotte: Ah, of course not.
Charlotte: Here, let’s start by working through some 
roleplaying scenarios and you’ll see what I mean.
Pup: And... that’s why it’d be a bad idea to attack us. 
You’d lose too many men.
Charlotte: But why should I care if I’d lose too many men? It 
means I win.
Pup: Uh... Well...
Charlotte: Try to meet the other person halfway. Avoid things 
like... intimidating them like a brute, for example.
Pup: So avoid what-
I stopped myself before the key word there.

“You”... “...what you’d do...”
Charlotte: ...
She sat there bracing herself with an expectant 
look on her face.
Pup: So... avoid what I’d normally do as a mercenary.
Charlotte: ...
Charlotte: Hah... Yeah. Something like that.
Pup: So, Lady Charlotte. You may be able to take the 
land. But you cannot hold it.

The amount of troops you’d lose would make it 
neigh impossible to hold it against a rebellious
populace.
If it really is the resources you want, it would be 
more productive to work with us, the 
local government, instead.
Charlotte: A rocky start to it, but I think you aced the landing.
Charlotte: Keep practicing, and you could be pretty good at 
this.
Pup: Thanks... I think.
Pup: (More little jabs here and there. Why can’t she just 
say I did well?)
Ironically, after the training I had just drilled into 
me, my instinct was that I should avoid a 
response to her that was too direct.
Pup: I do feel like I’m starting to understand now. I get 
what you were praising in it.
Charlotte: As per the bylaws of Lockhart, I am always right 
after all.
Pup: It’s also a relief to not need to rely on acting like 
Rowan either.
Pup: Better to be true to what strengths I have.
Charlotte: Indeed. Every noble man or woman must discover 
their own form of elegance.
As she said as much, a thought came to mind.
Pup: So... how did you discover yours?
Charlotte: ...
Charlotte: ...
Charlotte breathed in a deep, lengthy breath.
Charlotte: I didn’t.
And she exhaled.
Charlotte: As an heir to a city state’s leadership group... I had 
it all forced onto me.
Charlotte: And one day I realized I was sick of it.

All the faux charm, all the fake diplomacy worn like 
a mask to cover up selfish manipulations...
Charlotte: I wasn’t true to myself. I eventually threw a lot of 
it away.
Charlotte: And even now, I’m still trying to search for the 
approaches that fit me like a glove.
Charlotte: Like... I’ll let myself snap in anger a little more 
than I ever could have imagined before.

Let the Goddess’s judgement deal with the 
enemies I make, haha~
Pup: If you hated it so much, then why pass it along to 
me?
Charlotte: Because I saw someone who might resonate with 
it?
Charlotte: And... maybe I just didn’t want those years of high 
society crap I went through to go to waste?
Pup: Ah, so that’s the plan. I suffer in your place?
Charlotte: Don’t act like you didn’t enjoy it.
Pup: It... should come in useful. I won't need to 
resort to strong arming as much.
Charlotte: Aggression may not win you many allies, but it helps 
set boundaries.

Now you can try to use the best of both worlds? 
You don’t need to live up to being some 
tough as nails mercenary all the time.
Pup: ...

(I wonder if I could...)
Pup: You know... 

Maybe I could return the favor?
Pup: My father taught me a lot about intimidation 
techniques he had picked up over time.
Charlotte: Sure, why not?
Pup: Uh... so...
Pup: One was the idea that you could use their 
imagination against them.

Make a vague threat to make their mind go wild.
Charlotte: Like “you don’t want to know what I’ll do to you” 
or something?
Pup: Haha, not quite.
Pup: That comes off like you’re trying too hard.

“You have to be subtle. Lead them to the 
conclusion as if it was their own idea.”
Charlotte: That... makes a lot of sense. I’d never really 
thought about it like that.
Pup: Too many words can be bad. Since you want them 
to fill in the blanks with what THEY fear the most.

It can be like an animal feeling. It’s instinct.
Pup: Like there was this one time we were 
outnumbered 5 to 1.

The bandit leader approached my father, so he 
stared his down for a good 10 seconds before 
finally saying...
Pup: ...*whispering*...
Charlotte: ...
She had turned a bit pale.
Charlotte: I wanna try! And whatever else you’ve got!
Pup: Uh... W- Well..
Pup: Sure. Let me just set a scene for you...
passages.content_zh:
小狗：嘿呀！ ！ ！
我的劍從假人的劍上笨拙地彈開
盾牌，讓我對不存在的事物敞開大門
反擊。
小狗：*嘆氣*...
小狗：好吧，我們再試一次…
我估量了目標並加大了揮桿力度
這次要小心。
如此重複了結果。
Pup：呃……我到底哪裡出了問題？
我第三次準備好我的劍。
小狗：…
小狗：……！
我舉起劍進行後續！
小狗：……！
小狗：…
小狗：*嘆氣*...

（這感覺不對。我只會變得更糟
結果。 ）
這個努力花了幾個小時，我
沒有什麼可展示的。

除了一把徹底破損的劍之外。
小狗：嗯…
一段記憶突然浮現在我的腦海裡。
伊凡：頑固的堅持並不總是答案。 
有時候，事情本來就不是這樣的。

如果你嘗試另一種方法，它可能會很有洞察力
至少是出了什麼問題。
Pup：（你是對的。這幾乎肯定是對的。）
我讓破損的劍毫不客氣地掉進
當我開始朝旁邊走去時，泥土
訓練區。
我的眼角瞥見一抹金髮
在我的視野中。它很快就轉身離開了我。
小狗：嗯……？
那人影開始擺弄槍套裡的槍
放在她的臀部，好像假裝無視我。
小狗：…
小狗：……夏洛特？
和以前被稱為金髮模糊的公主
猶豫地把頭轉向我。
夏洛特：哦-哦...你好...我沒在那裡看到你。
她抬起頭，表情似乎是假裝的
混亂，紅暈漸漸褪去
從她的面容來看。
小狗：（她沒生病吧？）
小狗：你感覺還好吧？
夏洛特：什麼？當然……你為什麼要問這個？
小狗：嗯，你是……呃……
Pup：……表現有點奇怪……？
夏洛特：什——怎麼會這樣？ ！
Pup：因為…當我在做一個東西時，你“沒有看到我”
訓練時噪音很大...？
夏洛特：D-別把自己看得太高了。你並不像
正如你所想的那樣令人著迷。
小狗：…
我眨了幾下眼睛。我不知道如何處理
這是對我所說內容的回應。
小狗：呃...多久了

passages.name: SP: Reagynx Flynn C - First
passages.content:
Norde: And then you’ll check on the armament.
Flynn: Right.
Flynn was listening to Norde’s lecture outside the 
supply tent.
Norde: We keep a logbook of our stockpile in the tent, so 
be sure to review previous days as well 
for discrepancies.
Flynn: R- Right...
Reagyn: Hm?
Reagyn exited from the tent as the lecture went 
on.
Norde: If we’re missing anything, be sure to make note of 
what’s missing so we can track down whoever 
forgot to return theirs.
Flynn: And that would be...?
Norde: Here.
Norde had taken out the stock records 
to demonstrate.
Flynn: Ah, that’s what you meant.
Reagyn: Hm...
Reagyn was peeking in to look as well.
Reagyn: It’d be better to note who the offender is, too.
The group halted.
Norde: ...
Flynn: Oh, sis... Greetings.
Reagyn: My lord.
Norde: Is there something you need?
Reagyn: It is natural that I am to assist my lord, no?
Flynn: Well, I’m not... not yet...

We’re just going over the Nightless Crow procedure 
for doing rounds, really.
Norde: ...
Norde turned back to Flynn.
Norde: Once you’ve confirmed the stock’s inventory, you’ll 
need to check the status of the weapons.

Check for cracks, chips, sharpness, and the like. We 
require maintenance when it...
Flynn: Okay, so when-
Reagyn: What? That’s irresponsibly dangerous to let your 
equipment deteriorate that much.

Do you mean to get those you are given charge of 
killed?!
Norde: I do not think you understand the investment that 
comes with keeping equipment pristine for an 
active fighting force.
Flynn: Sister, I do think-
Reagyn: What sort of excuse is that? What sort of example 
are you setting for the people your serve?
Flynn: Sis, please just-
Norde: Do you wish to dedicate your time and money to 
make up the difference then?
Reagyn: ...!?
Reagyn: ...
Reagyn: ...!
Reagyn was unable to respond, and the frustration 
showed on her face.
Flynn: ...?!
Flynn just stared his sister’s way as he was left 
speechless by Reagyn’s speechlessness.
Norde: Then, Flynn, let’s move to discussing emergency 
procedures.

If we’re ambushed, or a nearby village is struck by a 
bandit raid, our armory tent is setup so we can
retreat quickly.
We’ll have a regroup point picked when we setup 
camp and-
Reagyn: You’d let the villagers die?!
Norde: Even if we wanted to, we’d still need to regroup.
Reagyn: Then design your weapon storage to allow for a 
quick counteroffensive.
Flynn: Uh... guys...?
Norde: We cannot commit to that for every time a similar 
situation arises.
Flynn: Uh... I just wanted to learn the procedure so I 
could start...
Reagyn: So is that how you mercenaries operate? You’d 
abandon others?
Flynn: ...
As Flynn failed to get a word in, he looked down to 
the box of supplies Norde had brought.

It was a kit meant for helping conduct the rounds 
that Flynn was being taught.
Flynn: So the first step was...
He reached down and picked it up...
Norde: ...
Reagyn: ...!
..and walked away without either of the other two 
noticing.
Flynn: That should be everything on the supply list.
Flynn worked his way step by step through the trail 
back to camp.
Reagyn: I believe it’d be prudent to get more flour.
Flynn: S- Sis...!?
Reagyn: I believe the camp’s menu has been more focused 
on baked goods lately.
Flynn: Right... Yeah, that makes sense...

And... We’re not too far out of town...

...
Flynn: There we go. All done.
Flynn placed the steel helmet down on the ground 
after he finished removing scratches and polishing 
it.
Reagyn: Done?
Flynn: Ah...?!
Reagyn’s head had suddenly popped in through the 
tent opening.
Reagyn: The armorer at the Coslett household always said 
you should be able to see yourself in them.
Flynn: Yes. That does sound familiar...
The two stayed quiet as Reagyn seemed to wait 
for Flynn.
Flynn: ...
And so he reached out to pick up the helmet 
again.
Flynn: Hragh!
The log split in two and fell to the ground.
Reagyn: My lord.

...

I believe the split there was off-center. 
It won’t stack well.

When we were taught this before, there was one 
technique that helped keep it more consistent.
Reagyn began to move into position 
to demonstrate.
Flynn: It’s not... that bad.
Reagyn: Hm... I still think it isn’t ideal.
Flynn: Right. Of course it is.
Flynn moved to place another log in a position to 
cut.
Flynn: Then...

Hragh!
Flynn: ...........!
Flynn: Agh...
The axe swung and kicked the edge of the log. It 
cut, but it was so off center that it was more 
damaging than not.
...

........

..............
Reagyn: *Sigh*...
Flynn: Yes, of course. I’m sorry I didn’t listen, sister.
Flynn: It all comes so naturally to you... of course you’d 
know best.
Reagyn: ...

I think you can be a great lord. I think there’s so 
much good you could do.

I just think you need just a little more of a push 
here and there.

Little adjustments could go a long way in making 
things better for everyone involved.

My lord. I mean no disrespect. I only mean to help 
you be the best you that you can be.
Flynn: Right... It’d be bad if a lord couldn’t chop a log...

Couldn’t swing a sword... cast a spell...
Flynn: ...
Flynn picked up his axe and positioned it like he 
was going to do a horizontal swing.
Flynn: Couldn’t...!
The axe smashed into the side of the log.
Flynn: Ah...!?
Flynn lost his grip on the axe and it, along with the 
log it stuck itself within, went flying off to the side 
of the scene.
Flynn: *Sigh*...

It’d be bad if a lord couldn’t do anything right...
He slumped to the ground with an exhausted 
exhale.
Reagyn: ...

Yes, that would be bad.

People depend on their lords.
Flynn: ...

Can I be alone?
Reagyn: My lord, I think that we shouldn’t-
Flynn: Please.

I just...
Flynn: I just need a second to regroup on my own.
Reagyn: I...
Reagyn: ...

Of course, my lord.

If there is any assistance you need, I will be sure to 
be at the ready to help.
Reagyn dismissed herself respectfully and began 
walking back towards camp proper.
Flynn: *Sigh*... It’s always the same, isn’t it?
Flynn leaned back and laid on the ground as he 
looked towards the sky.
Flynn: Haha... If I wilt so easily now, how will I fare as a 
Lord?
Flynn: Dammit...
passages.content_zh:
Norde：然後你會檢查武器。
弗林：對。
弗林正在外面聽諾德的講座
供應帳篷。
Norde：我們在帳篷裡保留了一份庫存日誌，所以
一定要回顧一下前幾天的情況
對於差異。
弗林：對——對…
雷金：嗯？
講座進行時，雷金走出帳篷
上。
Norde：如果我們遺漏了什麼，請務必記下
丟失了什麼，以便我們可以追蹤到任何人
忘了歸還他們的。
弗林：那會是……？
諾德：這裡。
Norde 已取出庫存記錄
來展示。
弗林：啊，這就是你的意思。
雷金：嗯…
雷金也在偷看。
雷金：最好也記下罪犯是誰。
一行人停了下來。
諾德：…
弗林：噢，姊姊……你好。
雷金：陛下。
諾德：你需要什麼東西嗎？
雷金：我協助主人是理所當然的，不是嗎？
Flynn：嗯，我還沒有……還沒有……

我們只是回顧一下不夜烏鴉的程序
確實是為了巡視。
諾德：…
諾德轉身面向弗林。
Norde：一旦您確認了庫存，您就會
需要檢查武器的狀態。

檢查是否有裂痕、缺口、銳利度等。我們
需要維護時，...
Flynn：好吧，那麼當-
雷金：什麼？讓你的
設備惡化到這種程度。

你的意思是要讓那些由你負責的人
殺了？ ！
Norde：我認為你不了解這種投資
配備保持設備原始狀態
積極的戰鬥力。
弗林：姐姐，我確實認為──
雷金：那是什麼藉口？什麼樣的例子
你是為你所服務的人設定的嗎？
Flynn：姐姐，請-
Norde：您願意投入時間和金錢嗎
那麼補差價嗎？
雷金：……！ ？
雷金：…
雷金：……！
雷金無法回應，沮喪之情溢於言表。 
表現在她的臉上。
弗林：……？ ！
當弗林被留下時，他只是盯著妹妹的方向
雷金的無言以對讓我無言以對。
Norde：那麼，Flynn，我們開始討論吧

passages.name: SP: Pup x Norde B - Begining
passages.content:
Pup: A letter for Norde?
Crow: Yeppers. Dropped off just recently.

Wasn't the typical sort of delivery person either, so
be careful with it.

Could've come from a sketchy source over a friendly
one.
Pup: Norde doesn't have friends, just associates.
Crow: Uh... Sure. Just giving you a heads up.
My fellow Nightless Crow bid his farewell before
heading off.
Pup: (A letter for Norde?)
Pup: (It's not like an arrest warrant or something...?)
Pup: ...
Pup: (No, it couldn't actually be from a friend...?! Could
it...?)
A sense of morbid curiosity washed over me.
I had to know.
Norde: A letter?
Pup: It was handed off to one of our guys earlier today.
Pup: You... uh... expecting some correspondence from a
friend?
Norde: Hmm...

Unlikely.
Norde: Not many would claim me as a friend, I suspect. More
often it would be an acquaintance.
Pup: That's what I said!
Norde: ...
Pup: A- As a joke...?
Norde: Please just hand it over.
Norde reached out to grab the envelope, but I 
pulled it away.
Pup: Ah...! Ah ah ah! Not quite!
Norde: What are you doing?
Pup: Playing the hand I was dealt.
Pup: I wanna know the contents.
Pup: You just said it wouldn't be a friend, so I can't be
anything too intimate to share, right?
Pup: You're going to kill me with curiosity if you don't, at
this rate.
Norde: *Sigh*...
Norde: It is safe to assume you'd read it yourself anyways if
I refused?
Pup: Oh, no.
Pup: I'd get an audience, too.
Norde: ...
Norde: Very well.
Pup: Great, now we can-
Pup: Ah!
As my guard fell, Norde snatched the envelope 
from me.
Pup: W- Wait, this wasn't the deal...?
Norde: Do not worry. I will read it out loud.
The sound of paper filled the silence as he opened 
the letter.
Norde: 'Dear Mr. North, we hope you are doing well...'

'It has been some time since we've seen you, and 
we hope our previous letters had arrived safely...'
Norde: 'We are-'...'We are'....
Norde stumbled on the line a few times as a 
surprised expression overtook his face.
Pup: Huh? Why'd you stop? Who is the letter from?
Norde: ...
Norde: It is from a group of children I once saved from a 
life threatening situation.

...
Norde: I believe I'll need to take a leave of absence soon.
Pup: That... was a out of left field.
Norde: Often times... peace is earned through heroics...
'happily ever afters' are beyond the grasp of most.
Norde: Even for vulnerable children.
Pup: ...Then I'll come, too.
Norde: You do not need to. This is my responsibility.
Pup: I insist in every way I can.
Pup: After all, what's the point of trying to get strong if
you can't use that strength when the need 
presents itself?
Norde: ...
Norde: Indeed.
Paralogue Unlocked: "Beauty or Beast"
passages.content_zh:
Pup：給諾德的一封信？
烏鴉：是的。最近剛掉下來。

也不是典型的送貨員，所以
小心一點。

可能來自粗略的來源，而不是友好的來源
一。
Pup：諾德沒有朋友，只有同事。
烏鴉：呃……當然。只是給你一個提示。
我的不夜鴉同胞曾經告別過
出發。
Pup：（給諾德的一封信？）
Pup：（這不像是逮捕令什麼的…？）
小狗：…
Pup：（不，這不可能是朋友送來的…？！可能
它...？ ）
一種病態的好奇心席捲了我。
我必須知道。
諾德：一封信？
Pup：今天早些時候它被交給了我們的一個人。
Pup：你……呃……期待某個人的來信
朋友？
諾德：嗯…

不太可能。
Norde：我懷疑沒有多少人會認我為朋友。更多
通常是個熟人。
小狗：我就是這麼說的！
諾德：…
小狗：A-開個玩笑…？
Norde：請把它交給我。
諾德伸手抓信封，但我
把它拉開。
小狗：啊……！啊啊啊！不完全是！
諾德：你在做什麼？
Pup：玩我拿到的牌。
小狗：我想知道內容。
Pup：你剛剛說它不會是朋友，所以我不能
任何太親密的事情都無法分享，對嗎？
Pup：如果你不這麼做的話，你就會因為好奇而殺了我
這個速度。
諾德：*嘆氣*...
Norde：無論如何，可以肯定地假設您自己會閱讀它，如果
我拒絕了？
小狗：哦，不。
Pup：我也會有觀眾的。
諾德：…
諾德：很好。
Pup：太好了，現在我們可以──
小狗：啊！
當我失去警戒時，諾德搶走了信封
從我這裡。
Pup：等等——等等，這不是交易……？
諾德：別擔心。我會大聲唸出來。
當他打開時，紙張的聲音充滿了寂靜
這封信。
諾德：“親愛的諾斯先生，我們希望您一切順利……”

「我們已經有一段時間沒有見到你了，而且
我們希望我們之前的信件已經安全到達...”
諾德：「我們是—」...「我們是」...
諾德（Norde）作為一名
他的臉上露出驚訝的表情。
小狗：啊？為什麼停下來？誰是萊特

passages.name: SP: PupxReagyn C - Story
passages.content:
Pup: Oh... shit! I'm late, aren't I?!
Bursting out of my tent, I almost tripped 
over myself.
Pup: Of course Rowan had to schedule a sparring 
match for an inane time...
I had been busy with logistical prep for the Crows.
More specifically... I had been having our logistical
needs drilled into me by Norde.
Reagyn: ...?!
An orange blur rose from the corner of my vision to
encapsulate all the sight in front of me.
Reagyn: Sir... Or ma'am? I... Anton?
Pup: O- Oh... Hey. 'Pup' is fine.
Pup: ("Sir"...? I thought she hated my guts?)
Reagyn: Such seems... inappropriate for one acting as a
provisional leader, but if you insist.
Reagyn stood back and cleared her throat.
Reagyn: Then, Pup. I have a report that is important for the
group's leadership to be aware of.

Since I have started working within this system, I 
have made notes of a handful of startling poor 
practices being used.
Reagyn pulled out a notebook. One that was 
spilling out clusters of notes at its edges.
Pup: That's a "handful"?
Reagyn: In particular, the logistical side is lacking.
Pup: (Wait, more logistics?!)
Pup: W- Why not ask Norde? Norde has been our
logistical expert for... a time?
Reagyn: I did.

Norde mentioned that you "should act like a leader 
and listen to the feedback".
Pup: Oh, such a jokester.
Pup: I'm more the "lead the charge into battle" type of
leader.
Reagyn: If the problem is a lack of experience, then we better
get started now.
Pup: (Shit... this is gonna take forever, isn't it?)
Pup: I'm actually organizing sparring matches right this
moment... so how about we resume this wonderful 
talk after?
Reagyn: Hmm... I WAS wanting to check on the quality and
organization of training...
Reagyn: Though... Wait, I had that paperwork deadline
looming, too. When was that...?
Pup: Ah shucks. Sounds like you're busy! We'll have to
reschedule!
With a hop and a skip, I had jumped past 
and escaped.
Crow: That's it, you have him cornered!
Another Crow: Don't let yourself be beaten!
Crow: Yeah! This is what we're talking about!
Rowan: Well, well, well... Is our indomitable Pup all bark and
no bite?
Pup: Since when did you have a jab like that in your
skillset?
Rowan: You mistake my comment for critique.
Rowan: We can howl to the moon together. It would be a...
passionate way to see off the sun~
Pup: Tsk!

(I can't block his magic, so... I need to stay light on
my feet to evade)
I readied my sword with a sidestep prepared.
Pup: Rragh!!!
And so Rowan fell to the ground.
Rowan: Urk! I have been bested...
Pup: (Wait, he went down easily...?!)
Reagyn: A lively activity, isn't it?
Reagyn stepped into the scene, and the audience 
of Crows started to scatter.
Pup: Ah...!?
For my part, I swiftly threw a blanket over Rowan.
Pup: Well, we try to keep morale up.
Pup: I thought you were busy...
Reagyn: I made it work. Enough so to watch your "sparring
match", it seems.
Pup: Why say it like that?
Reagyn: *Sigh* ... I wonder.
Reagyn: I believe this transitions well into the conversation I
wished to have earlier.

First off, I have noticed how you lack a morning roll
call or a roll call of any sort.
Pup: "Roll call"?
Reagyn: It's a process to take attendance, assign tasks, and
document completion of said task.

For example, what if someone had deserted the 
regiment?
Pup: Then they don't get paid.
Reagyn: And what about food? How do you if know your 
supplies will be sufficient for the number of soldiers?
Pup: Oh, stuff like that?
Pup: We do take a count every once in a while for stuff like
that.
Reagyn: Which leads me to the topic of food organization... 
or the lack thereof.
Reagyn: The percent of forgotten food... or even rotting 
food... that I've made note of is problematic.
Pup: Wait, are YOU of all people saying we shouldn't eat
food when it's fresh?
Reagyn: With better logistics and numbers to back up 
decision making, you can buy and distribute food 
with less waste.
As of now, you're just hemorrhaging money.
Reagyn tried to soothe an oncoming headache.
Reagyn: Perhaps we should talk about the sparring matches while
we're here?
Pup: Ha... Out of everything, I know I can do this well.
Reagyn: Then...

How are you organizing and scheduling them?

How are you planning for balancing of matches and
development of skillsets?
Reagyn: And how are you setting up security control to avoid
injuries?
Pup: "Balancing of matches"?
Reagyn: With a magic user vs a weapon wielder, the latter 
has the advantage in close range combat.

Isn't that right?
Tsk.
A disgruntled voice was heard from 
below the blanket.
Reagyn: And, as noted, the security protocols for the 
audience is entirely lacking.
Pup: F- For the audience?
Pup: Just don't stand in front of the sharp stick and you
should be fine. We are all proper mercs, for the
Goddess's sake.
As I finished my sentence, Reagyn already 
had a finger pointed at a nearby tree.
One flickering with embers from a fiery 
attack that Rowan had made.
Reagyn: Would you like me to elaborate?
Pup: P- Point taken...
Reagyn: And maybe worst of all... Bless the Goddess...
Reagyn: There's the gambling.
Pup: Gambling? What?
Reagyn: So you are not aware. Or at least claim not to be?

I wonder...
Reagyn's foot stomped down hard onto the nearby
blanket.
...!?
Pup: H- Hey! Be careful!
Reagyn: How much did you make?
The playful voice was directed at a blanketed lump
below. A lump that had been foiled in its slow 
moving getaway.
...
Reagyn: Ah, what do we have here?
Reagyn reached down to the edge of 
the blanket and...
Reagyn: A bag of coins? How fortuitous.
Reagyn: Surely no one would ever miss it. Doubly so a blanket.
...!
Reagyn: How much?
...
A head stuck out from the blanket.
Rowan: Uh... 103 gold pieces? Give or take?
Reagyn: Then there you have-
Rowan jumped to his feet and grabbed the bag.
Rowan: Uh...
Rowan: I mean... BLEH!
Rowan fell down underneath the blanket again.
Pup: B- B- B- But...?!
Reagyn: *Sigh* ...
Reagyn: I'd guess that he threw the match on the final 
move after betting against himself.
Rowan: Your words wound me.
Reagyn: Would you dispute it?
Rowan: No, you are correct.
Rowan: But the words do still wound me.
And without any subtlety, the blanket rolled away 
from the scene at a brisk pace.
Pup: I...
Reagyn: *Sigh* ... If you allow these temptations to occur
undisturbed, it'll never be a fair match.
Pup: ...
Pup: F- Fine... I... guess you have a point.
Pup: Let's... imagine all your complaints are based in
fact...
Pup: Just imagining it... not saying they are...
Pup: But... what would be your recommendations, then?
Reagyn: Well, I would start with...
passages.content_zh:
Pup: 喔... 糟了！我遲到了，對吧？！
我衝出帳篷，差點絆倒自己。
Pup: 羅文當然得把比武安排在這種無聊的時間...
我一直忙著鴉團的後勤準備。
更具體地說... 我一直在被諾德灌輸我們的後勤
需求。
Reagyn: ...?!
一道橘色的模糊身影從我視線的角落升起，
包覆了我眼前所有的景象。
Reagyn: 先生... 還是女士？我... 安東？
Pup: 喔- 喔... 嗨。「小不點」就好。
Pup: （「先生」...？我還以為她恨死我了？）
Reagyn: 對於一個代理領導者來說，這似乎... 不太合適，但如果您堅持。
Reagyn 退後一步，清了清嗓子。
Reagyn: 那麼，小不點。我有一份報告，對於
團體的領導層來說很重要。

自從我開始在這個系統中工作以來，我
注意到了一些令人震驚的不良
做法。
Reagyn 拿出一個筆記本。邊緣
溢出了成堆的筆記。
Pup: 這叫「一些」？
Reagyn: 特別是，後勤方面很缺乏。
Pup: （等等，又是後勤？！）
Pup: 為- 為什麼不問諾德？諾德一直是我們的
後勤專家... 一段時間了？
Reagyn: 我問過了。

諾德說你「應該像個領導者一樣
聽取回饋」。
Pup: 喔，真是個愛開玩笑的人。
Pup: 我更像是「帶頭衝鋒陷陣」型的
領導者。
Reagyn: 如果問題是缺乏經驗，那我們最好
現在就開始。
Pup: （糟了... 這會花很長時間，不是嗎？）
Pup: 我現在正在組織比武... 所以不如我們
之後再繼續這場精彩的
談話？
Reagyn: 嗯... 我正想檢查訓練的品質和
組織...
Reagyn: 不過... 等等，我還有那份迫在眉睫的
文件截止日期。那是什麼時候...?
Pup: 哎呀，聽起來妳很忙！我們得
改期了！
我一蹦一跳地跳過去
逃走了。
鴉兵: 就是這樣，你把他逼到角落了！
另一個鴉兵: 別讓自己被打敗了！
鴉兵: 沒錯！這

passages.name: SP: ReagynxFlynn B - Begining
passages.content:
Flynn: Hmm...
Flynn: Yeah. Yeah, that should work.
Flynn: It's a good edge.
Flynn flipped his dagger in his grip.
The shine of the newly sharpened blade glittered in 
the fiery flicker of the tent's lighting.
Flynn: Haha...
Perhaps a bit recklessly, Flynn started to play 
with his weapon via casually going through 
training drills.
Reagyn: My lord.
Flynn: Oh...! H- Hey, sis...
Flynn quickly ended his playful endeavor.
Reagyn: I have a...

...?

Ah, had you completed a sharpening routine?
Flynn: I did. I think it came out well.
Flynn offered the dagger up for her inspection.
Reagyn: ...

It's good. Nothing I can see being problematic with 
it.
Flynn: Right? I thought its the best result I've gotten in a
while.
Reagyn: I'd agree, though I'm not an expert.
Reagyn: How long did it take?
Flynn: Ah...! W- Well...
Flynn briefly admitted to it taking notably longer 
than normal.
Flynn: B- But... you gotta develop the skill, then speed it
up... right?
Reagyn: I agree.
Flynn: I just... I just have to build on this. 

"A good heir to noble seat is one that's always 
learning"... as we were taught.

...right?
Reagyn: I said I agreed, no?

Keep up the good work at progressing.
Reagyn raised her hand with something in it.
Reagyn: A letter was delivered to the camp.
Flynn: Sure...
He took the envelope and Reagyn began to leave.
Flynn: ...

Hey... Reagyn...

What's... your time on that task now?

How long does it take you for blade maintenance?
Reagyn: ...
Reagyn: *Sigh*
Flynn: Right... I thought so.
Flynn: Hey... sis... Do you...?

Do you ever think... that maybe you'd... you'd be a
better...
Flynn's words trailed off.
A silence came over them both until Reagyn turned 
to Flynn.
Reagyn: I have. I think I would be an excellent heir to our
family's title.
Flynn: Oh...

Yeah, you have always been a natural at all this...
Reagyn: But I also cannot. I am not the heir. You are.

The choice was made long ago.
Flynn: I mean... If you really feel that way...

We could just do something to make you heir.
Flynn: If you're worried about reputation, I'm sure we 
could think of a plan to-
Reagyn: That...! How underhanded...

I thought you had moved past that.
Flynn: B- But...! If we're just smart about it...!
Reagyn: The choice was made long ago, brother.
Reagyn: *Sigh*

...
Reagyn: Is this really what you want to waste your worries on?
Flynn: I... guess... not...
Another silence fell over the two.
Reagyn: Flynn. I do sincerely believe you'll be a great lord.

Do not let your stumbles determine your motivation 
for getting there.
Reagyn turned and, with a hint of hesitation, exited
the tent.
Flynn: ...
...leaving Flynn alone with his thoughts.
Flynn: Yeah... She's right. As usual... she's...
Trailing off, Flynn looked at the letter he had been
handed.
Opening it, he read the first line.
Flynn: Ah...!

R- Reagyn! You need to see this!
He scampered out of the tent after his sister.
passages.content_zh:
弗林：嗯…
弗林：是的。是的，那應該有效。
Flynn：這是一個很好的優勢。
弗林翻轉了手中的匕首。
新磨利的刀刃閃閃發光
帳篷裡閃爍的燈光
弗林：哈哈…
也許有點魯莽，弗林開始演奏
用他的武器隨意穿過
訓練演習。
雷金：陛下。
弗林：噢……！嘿，嘿，姐姐…
弗林很快就結束了他的頑皮努力。
雷金：我有一個…

……？

啊，你完成磨刀程序了嗎？
弗林：我做到了。我認為結果很好。
弗林把匕首遞給她檢查。
雷金：…

很好。我認為沒有什麼問題
它。
弗林：對嗎？我認為這是我在一次比賽中獲得的最佳成績
同時。
Reagyn：我同意，儘管我不是專家。
雷金：花了多久時間？
弗林：啊……！呃——嗯……
弗林簡短地承認需要更長的時間
比正常情況下。
Flynn：但-但是...你必須培養技能，然後加快速度
起來……對嗎？
雷金：我同意。
Flynn：我只是……我必須在此基礎上再接再厲。 

「一個好的貴族席位繼承人總是
學習”...正如我們被教導的。

……正確的？
Reagyn：我說我同意了，不是嗎？

保持良好的工作進展。
雷金舉起手，手裡拿著什麼東西。
雷金：一封信已送到營地。
弗林：當然…
他接過信封，雷金開始離開。
弗林：…

嘿...雷吉恩...

現在……你有什麼時間來完成這項任務？

刀片維護需要多長時間？
雷金：…
雷金：*嘆息*
Flynn：對……我也是這麼想的。
Flynn：嘿……姊姊……你……嗎？

你有沒有想過...也許你會...你會變成一個
更好...
弗林的話音落了下去。
他們兩人都陷入了沉默，直到雷金轉過身來。 
到弗林。
雷金：我有。我想我會成為我們的優秀繼承人
家庭的頭銜。
弗林：噢…

是的，你在這一切上一直都很自然......
Reagyn：但我也不能。我不是繼承人。你是。

這個選擇很久以前就做出了。
Flynn：我的意思是…如果你真的有這樣的感覺…

我們可以做點什麼
