passages.name: SP: PupxReagyn B - New Event
passages.content:
Pup: *Breathes in* ...
Pup: Ahhh........
The warmth of the sun shined down onto 
my relaxed visage.
Pup: Always nice to hear the birds chirping away under 
an inviting sun...

And along with that...
I held a piece of parchment up to that same sun.
Pup: ...I finished the count of ALL the mercenaries in 
camp now.

...
Pup: Finally... How is one person supposed to do this every
day, anyways?
Pup: But at least I can finally sit and relax...
I turned towards my tent.
And what met me was a set of judgmental eyes.
Reagyn: Hello, "leader"... Or was "Pup" the one that'd do?
Pup: Good, uh... afternoon, Reagyn.
Reagyn: I was hoping for a follow-up on my proposals.
Pup: Well... you see... I am busy since...
I looked around for who else was here.
Pup: Because... uh... Norde!
Norde: ...
Pup: Eh... I mean... Rowan!
Luckily for me, Rowan was passing by.
Pup: (At least one good thing came from counting everyone
here.)
Rowan: Fancy meeting you two ladies... or two... uh...

...well, meeting a Pup and a Reagyn, at least. 
Always a pleasure.
Rowan: Did you finish that task you were-
Pup: Actually, I was meaning to talk to you about that!
Pup: I have not finished and am busy with it, so can you
help me do it... right... over... far away from here.
Rowan: Ah... I see where this is going.
Rowan lowered his voice and whispered in my ear.
Rowan: Well, I have been feeling a bit... thirsty.

I hope you don't mind... sharing your "goods" with 
me for a week or so.
Pup: Rowan. I don't have any. I'm too young to-
Rowan: Ha! When has that ever stopped you?
Pup: ...Always.
Rowan: Exactly! Now, I expect it to be delivered to my tent by
midnight.
Pup: ...?!

(He's joking, right? Right?)
Rowan: And, but of course, such a task would take the WHOLE
day.
Rowan had swiftly shifted from whispers into 
something akin to someone projecting to an 
audience.
Rowan: The task includes such endeavors to keep one 
busy... doing... stuff. Manly stuff... and Pup stuff.
Pup: Really? That last part?
Reagyn: *Sigh* ... Understood.
Reagyn: Please contact me when you are available to talk, then.
And with that, Reagyn turned on her heel and left.
Pup: *Exhale* ...
Pup: And then my father deflected the swing of steel by 
that brute of a man!
I stood up to rally the crowd.
Pup: He attacked and attacked but could barely make 
him bleed!
Pup: It was then that the beast did the dastardly deed,
using a handful of sand from his pocket to blind our
brave leader!
Pup: But he evaded all of his blows! He managed to 
defeat him without sight!
A clamor of cheers came from pockets of the 
crowd.
After the noise settled down a bit, but before I was
ready to continue, a familiar voice spoke.
Reagyn: I think I've heard this one before. A crusades tale,
correct?
Pup: Uh... I don't know... I just heard it from my father.
Reagyn: So the tale went, he had regained his sight after 
the battle due to well maintained organization.

He was able to get back and get quality care 
despite the impairment.

If it was a crusade, then is it safe to assume he was 
a part of that logistical effort before the event?
Pup: ...
Pup: Are you trying to insinuate something?
Reagyn: No, no... I think you are doing your best.
Reagyn: But examples of quality can serve as a vision to strive
towards, no?
Pup: ...
The remark stung. Maybe it shouldn't have, but the
topic would probably never be a simple one to me.
Pup: ...
I slowed my breathing, as I didn't want to let it
distract me from the situation in front of me.
I had been wanting to undermine Reagyn's naggy 
attitude for some time, and this felt like my golden 
chance.
Pup: (Just be classy and thorough. Don't be so easy to 
push around.)

It isn't as though the camp is... poorly 
administrated.
Pup: We're just working with the resources we have. Money
and all.
Pup: You're used to working with nobles, right?

Trying to cater to a diverse group's likes and dislikes
from equipment to food isn't simple.
Reagyn: Is that so? Then is the recent food rationing part of
some dietary plan?
Pup: ...What?
Reagyn: I... I do not mean to offend.
Reagyn: I want to understand what you're approach 
here really is. 

i want to see what I'm missing.
Pup: Reagyn...
Pup: ...

...maybe we should talk in a more quiet place 
where we can... hear each other better.
Reagyn affirmed the idea and we slipped 
away from the nightly festivities.
Norde: ...
Norde: The observation wasn't wrong.

Ivan ran a tighter ship around here.
Norde: Who's to blame for that change, though...
Norde paused in indecision for a second.
And then returned to eating.
Pup: This is probably far away enough...

Reagyn, I want to be diplomatic about this, but...
Pup: ...you might even be giving the Goddess a 
headache at this point.
Reagyn: I... simply want to make this work.
Reagyn: What we do is important, after all.
Pup: Right... Then with that in mind...
Pup: You know the food shortage is because I was trying to
follow your guidelines, right?
Pup: We're doing matches by your ruleset, too...
Pup: Should you really be grilling me like that when we're
doing things by YOUR book?
Reagyn: I don't see it happening like that.
Reagyn: Maybe... a fundamental understanding is lacking?
Pup: Excuse me?
Reagyn: How about we review the basics from step one? How do
you perform a roll call?
Pup: Eh? Just walk around and count the heads. Simple.
Reagyn: Wait, but couldn't that lead to misses or redundancy?
You'd get an incorrect count.
Reagyn: ...

Have we been purchasing food on that basis?
Pup: Y- Yeah...
Pup: It's not like I go everywhere only once, you know?
Reagyn: ...

Next topic.

What's the current process for practice weapon
maintenance?
Pup: Same as any other weapon.
Reagyn: Meaning... the practice weapons are just real weapons?
Pup: Yeah... when they get too worn down in battle, we move
them to be used for practice.
Reagyn: That poses a number of issues with people 
restraining themselves in practice...

If they don't hold back, the injuries could be
deadly... but the practice is significantly less
effective if they do.
Reagyn: ...

Did we ever address the gambling issue on those
sparring matches?
Pup: You do realize we didn't have these major problems
before your "recommendations"?
Reagyn: ...

So that is your conclusion. That this is my fault?
Reagyn: Of all conclusions to come to...
Pup: Speaking of. You nag a lot for someone doing so 
little yourself.

I tried your ideas and you still give me shit for not
doing them PERFECTLY.
Pup: *Inhale* ...  *Exhale* ...
Pup: I... understand that you just want to help and
appreciate the sentiment.

But they're not working out. Unless you want to
implement them yourself, then...
Reagyn: Okay.

It was foolish of me to expect you to understand
the standards without the foundational education.

A good leader or teacher can be as much by 
providing an example.
Reagyn nodded and started heading back to camp.
Pup: ...

That worked?
I was soon alone again.
Pup: ...Really?
Pup: (Honestly, I just suggested Reagyn do it because 
that's how Rowan normally gets out of it.)

(Maybe... Is he onto something?)
Pup: (Actually...)

(Maybe I can "accidentally" leave some things
unfinished and she can "correct" that?)

...
Pup: (Maybe Rowan is rubbing off on me?)
Pup: ...
Pup: Eww...
passages.content_zh:
小狗：*吸氣*...
小狗：啊啊啊…
溫暖的陽光灑落在身上
我輕鬆的面容。
小狗：總是很高興聽到鳥兒在下面嘰嘰喳喳地叫
誘人的陽光...

同時...
我把一張羊皮紙舉到同一個陽光下。
Pup：……我已經清點完所有傭兵了
現在紮營。

…
Pup：終於……一個人該如何做到這一點？
無論如何，一天？
Pup：但至少我終於可以坐下來放鬆了…
我轉身走向我的帳篷。
映入我眼簾的是一雙充滿批判的目光。
Reagyn：你好，「領導者」…或「Pup」就是那個會做的人？
Pup：好，呃……下午，Reagyn。
Reagyn：我希望我的建議能得到後續落實。
Pup：嗯……你看……我很忙，因為……
我環顧四周看看還有誰在這裡。
Pup：因為……呃……諾德！
諾德：…
Pup：呃……我是說……羅文！
對我來說幸運的是，羅文正好路過。
小狗：（統計每個人的數量至少帶來了一件好事
在這裡。 ）
羅文：很高興認識你們兩位女士……或者兩位……呃……

……好吧，至少會見一隻小狗和一隻雷吉恩。 
總是一種樂趣。
Rowan：你完成那個任務了嗎——
Pup：其實我正想跟你談談這個呢！
Pup：我還沒做完呢，正忙呢，你也可以嗎？
幫我做吧……對……在……遠離這裡的地方。
Rowan：啊...我明白這是怎麼回事了。
羅文壓低了聲音，在我耳邊低聲說。
羅文：嗯，我覺得有點……渴。

我希望你不介意...與人分享你的“商品”
我一個星期左右。
小狗：羅文。我沒有。我太年輕了，不能-
羅文：哈！這什麼時候曾經阻止過你？
小狗：……總是。
羅文：沒錯！現在，我希望它能在
午夜。
小狗：……？ ！

（他是在開玩笑吧？對吧？）
羅文：而且，當然，這樣的任務需要整個過程
一天。
羅文很快就從竊竊私語變成了
類似於某人投射到
觀眾。
羅文：這項任務包括努力維持一個
忙著……做……事。男子氣概的東西......還有小狗的東西。
小狗：真的嗎？最後一部分？
雷金：*嘆息*。

passages.name: SP: Pup x Charlotte A - Begining
passages.content:
I focused on the locket pinched between my fingers.
Pup: ...!
A curtain of crimson flames enveloped the dummy, 
then disappeared.
Pup: *Pant*...
Pup: *Exhale*...
Charlotte: I knew you'd eventually move on from pounding 
steel mindlessly.
Charlotte entered the training area with a 
smug grin.
Pup: Is "La Tornade" offering to help me refine my
technique?
Pup: Perhaps she could fan these flames with some of 
her legendary hot air?
Charlotte: ...
Pup: ...
Pup: Haha...
Charlotte: Hah... I see you've been doing your readings.
Charlotte: That line is similar to one of Sir Rangar's famous
retorts in that volume I recommended.
Pup: Huh? Really? 

I guess I just internalized that one into my
repertoire without realizing?
Charlotte: Trisyllabic words? Who are you and what have you 
done with Pup!?
My heart fluttered with humor and one other 
tingling feeling I couldn't quite identify.
Pup: Yeah. Sometimes I don't even recognize myself in 
the mirror.
Charlotte: ...Well... Speaking of changes, would you mind 
speaking privately in your tent?
Charlotte: Wow, you've really started to build up a collection of
books.
Charlotte: It suits you.
Charlotte glanced around at my small collection of
half-open tomes and scribbled notes.
Pup: Well, we can only carry so much once we move.
I picked up a loose book and put it on a small pile.
Pup: So what did you want to see me for? Another mutual
lesson?
Charlotte: No, actually. It's more of a personal matter.
I breathed a sigh of relief.
Pup: I'm glad. You've grown beyond my meager tutelage.
Charlotte: Likewise. Which leads me to my next point: I need 
some replacement parts for my revolver.
Charlotte: It's a prototype weapon, so the parts are hard to 
come by. Especially if I want to avoid getting undue
attention.
Pup: If you want extra muscle for a back alley deal, then...
Charlotte: Trust me, I'll bring plenty of muscle all on my own.
Charlotte: What I'd to rely on is your brain.
Pup: ...?
Charlotte: I think we compliment the other's skillset very well.
With knowledge on brains and brawn to make the 
two work well together.
A... tactical alliance, if you would.
Pup: (Is that what it is? Just a tactical alliance?)
My face twitched a little from the thought, though 
I couldn't get myself to actually disagree with it.
Pup: How could I possibly say no after all we've been
through together?
Charlotte: Thank you! Then get ready and we'll meet at...
Pup: So this is the place?
Charlotte nodded as I slipped inside the warehouse.
Charlotte: You there? "Fist"?
Fist: Ah, you must be my buyer. Let's-
Charlotte: Oh, goddess. It's you!
Fist: Huh... Wait, C- Charlotte?!
Pup: What's going on?
Charlotte: I've told you about... 'handsy' nobles before, right?
It didn't take much for me to put two 
and two together.
Fist: Heheh. I didn't realize we were back on speaking 
terms. You must have missed me.
Charlotte: Don't flatter yourself. You do want my business, right?
Fist: Hmm... Do I?

No. No, I don't think I do.

I think I have a new offer. One exclusive for our 
dear Lady Charlotte.
Charlotte: Well, fuck off.
Charlotte turned to start heading towards 
the door.
Fist: Grgh! I don't think so, princess.
Charlotte: Don't you dare call me th-
Fist raised his hand to snap, and several men 
entered from the shadows.
Fist: You know, if it wasn't for that foul temperament of
yours, you might not be in this position in the first
place.
Despite those barbaric ears of yours, you could at
least pretend to be of good breeding when 
addressing a gentleman.
Charlotte: Is this... Is this about those rejections I gave you?!
Still?!
Charlotte: If you had taken them like the proud man you pretend to
be, maybe it wouldn't have been so humiliating.
Fist: Y- You pinned me to a table in front of everyone!
Charlotte: YOU tried to grab my butt!
Even some of the thugs snickered at that.
Fist: S- Shut it! Stop laughing!
His eyes spun from person to person, 
settling on me.
Fist: Wait. Who the hell are you?

So you've become so arrogant as to drag your 
chambermaid instead of a proper rugged guard?
Pup: No. I'm not a chamermaid. I'm...
Charlotte and I glanced at each other.
Pup: I'm a frie-
Charlotte: Comrade-in-arms.
Fist: Huh?
Pup: I'm... I'm a friend.

Not yours, though.
I motioned towards the guards.
Pup: You two are... I'm still making up my mind on that. 
I hope he's paying you enough to deal with this.
Fist: This... This explains everything. The rejections, 
your lack of ladylike qualities...

You were always just into women, weren't you?!
Charlotte: Yeah... THAT'S why a girl would reject you...
Fist: You actually think this girl can be strong? That she
can protect you with that sword?
Charlotte: First of all, dipshit, I don't need protection.
Charlotte: Secondly, you don't know who you're talking 
about. She's stronger than you'll ever be without 
even needing to lift that sword.
Charlotte cocked her head as if realizing 
something for the first time.
Charlotte: Maybe... Maybe that's why I like her so much.
Charlotte grabbed my hand and squeezed it, 
causing my heart to soar. I was completely 
stunned.
Pup: U- Uh...?!
Fist: Grh... You know, even now the Empire has people 
that would gladly see you delivered in a body bag, 
yeah?
Fist motioned to his men.
Fist: Any last words?
Charlotte: ...Just three.

Duel me, coward.
Fist: Hah! You can't be serious.
Charlotte: After all these years... can your 'oh-so-manly' ego
really live with needing to outnumber me to win?
Fist: You...!
He paused with a slight twitch to his eye.
Fist: F- Fine! What are the terms, then?
Charlotte: You win, I'll honor your years old marriage proposal.

We win, we go free. With my parts.
Fist: Heh. Deal.
Fist gestured, and the hired thugs formed a sort of
ring to act as an arena.
Pup: Good luck...
Fist: She'll need it.

Last chance, princess. Are you sure you wanna do 
this?
Charlotte: Never been surer of anything in my life.
Fist: ...
Charlotte: ...
They were off!
Fist came at her, but his stance was sloppy.
Charlotte took advantage immediately, out 
maneuvering him and going completely on the 
offensive by turning his power against him.
Fist didn't even land a blow.
He fell to the floor after less than a minute, bloody
and bruised.
Charlotte: I win.
Fist: Ughh... how is this... even possible?
Fist: Dammit...! Men! Shoot them both!
Pup: (Not even going to hesitate, are you?!)
I turned to the thugs that were on the verge of 
moving, and I decided to act on an observation I 
made before.
Pup: Wait! "Fist" isn't your real name, obviously...

You're Thileous Sork, right? Of the Sork 
family name?
Pup: The same 'Sork' family that's lost a lot of trade
agreements in Lockhart over the past few years?
Fist: W- What?! What does that matter?! You think I care?!
Pup: I think they'd care.
I turned to the thugs, who had tilted their heads in 
my direction.
Pup: I really do hope he paid you guys enough to deal with
this.
Pup: Or rather... already paid you.
Pup: I imagine that's most of what he has left.
Fist: ...?!
Pup: This man has nothing to pay you with except a few
shoddy firearms.

He already botched the trade he needed to get 
you the rest of your pay.
Pup: All over a personal dispute he can't even win.
Charlotte: I guess that does technically mean you're working 
for me?
Pup: Assuming they WANT to get paid.
I tilted my head to the hired help, and slightly
reached out my hand in an inviting manner.
Pup: How about it? We came here expecting to pay 
that money anyways.
Thug 1: Fuck... he did say half up front for me. You?
Thug 2: Yeah, same...
Pup: And an awful lot of silence from him on the topic so
far.
Fist: W- Wait, no. That doesn't mean I can't...!
The thugs lowered their weapons.
Thug 1: I'm gonna go guard outside... ma'am.
He nodded at Charlotte and myself before 
leaving. 

The others nodded in agreement as they
followed him.
Fist: Y- You can't just...! You fucking...!
Charlotte: I think that's enough out of you.
Fist continued to spout obscenities until Charlotte
knocked him out with a pistol whip.
Charlotte: Happy to do business with you.
Charlotte: That was amazing~
With parts in hand and a few kind words from our 
new hired hand friends, we were on the road back 
to camp by sunrise.
Charlotte: So tell me, how did you know who he was?
Pup: One of the books you have me had a 'genealogy of
Lockhart' section.
Charlotte: *Sigh*... That does sound like Lockhart.

Where people get to be featured in an
academic book because they financed 
its publication.
Pup: Between that and hearing about rumors in my 
time as a mercenary... His 'escapades' are well 
documented.
Charlotte: Color me impressed. I never would have connected 
those dots like that, and I've known him for years.
Pup: I don't think I could have pulled it off without you 
making him look like a fool first.
Charlotte: Ah... well, let's not give me too much credit.
Charlotte: I just… reacted when I realized you were dealing 
with all this nastiness on my account.
I bit my lip, debating if I should voice the thoughts
that were burning in my head.
Pup: Well, that's not what really bothered me about it...
Charlotte: Really? Then why do you look so pale?
Pup: ...
Pup: Did you mean what you said back there?
Charlotte: Hm? I said a lot of stuff.
Pup: What you said about...
My mouth started to move, but the word didn't 
want to come out immediately.
Pup: Do you really see me as a... strong person?
Charlotte: I- I don't know... There are many different kinds of
strength.
Charlotte: Do you see me as a mindless brute?
Pup: Of course not. You've got so much more to you, and I
like that side of you.
Charlotte: Well... then there's your answer.
There was a tense silence. My heart was pounding 
again.
Pup: But I mean, you still don't actually... you know...
right?
Charlotte looked a bit hurt.
Charlotte: Don't... what?
Pup: What I mean is, I know you wanted to do this 
training because you felt sorry for me.
Pup: I shouldn't have expected anything.
Pup: It's just that even though you're... 
and I'm... I still felt a sort of...
Charlotte: ...
Charlotte: ...
Charlotte: Hmph...
As my eyeline dodged the scene forming in 
front of me, she leaned in.
Pup: ...?!
Pup: (S- Soft?!)
Her lips pressed to mine.
I was frozen, not knowing what to do.
Then I felt her hands on my lower back and behind 
my head, pulling me deeper into the kiss.
I started to act on instinct in return.
Seconds later, when we were both breathless, 
we pulled apart.
Charlotte: *Clear throat*
Charlotte: For someone who has come such a long way so 
quickly, you can act really dumb.

And that's what all these insecurities are. Dumb.
She stepped back and fixed her outfit.
Charlotte: Now, let's continue this later.
Charlotte: I'm exhausted...
As Charlotte headed off, I caught the faint hint of a
blush forming on her face.
I watched her head back, and I saw her pace 
slowly change from a composed one to a rushed 
one.
Pup: ...

What just happened?
She had already made a habit of odd actions 
like this.
What I wasn't sure about...
Pup: (Was that a genuine moment of vulnerability?)

...
I raised my hand to feel the lingering imprint of her
on my own lips.
Pup: (Could have it meant... No... It... couldn't...?)
Pup: Hmm...
I turned my gaze to the sea as my thoughts 
jumbled themselves within indecision.
Pup: (Well, she was right about one thing.)
Pup: I am so... very... very... dumb...

Ahaha.... haha...
passages.content_zh:
我專注於手指間捏著的墜盒。
Pup: ...！
一道緋紅色的火焰幕簾吞噬了假人，
然後消失了。
Pup: *喘氣*...
Pup: *呼氣*...
夏洛特：我就知道你最終會擺脫毫無意義地敲打
鋼鐵的行為。
夏洛特帶著
一臉得意的笑容走進了訓練場。
Pup: 「龍捲風」要來幫我精進
技巧了嗎？
Pup: 也許她可以用她傳說中的熱空氣來煽動這些火焰？
夏洛特：...
Pup: ...
Pup: 哈哈...
夏洛特：哈... 我看你一直在讀書。
夏洛特：那句話很像朗格爵士在你推薦的那本書中的一句著名
反駁。
Pup: 蛤？真的嗎？

我想我只是在不知不覺中把那句話內化到我的
詞彙庫裡了？
夏洛特：三個音節的詞？你是誰？你對Pup做了什麼！？
我的心因幽默和另一種
難以名狀的刺痛感而顫動。
Pup: 是啊。有時候我甚至在鏡子裡都認不出自己。
夏洛特：...嗯... 說到變化，你介意
在你的帳篷裡私下談談嗎？
夏洛特：哇，你真的開始收集
書籍了。
夏洛特：很適合你。
夏洛特環顧四周，看著我那小堆
半開的書和潦草的筆記。
Pup: 嗯，我們搬家的時候只能帶這麼多。
我拿起一本散落的書，把它放在一小堆上。
Pup: 所以你想找我做什麼？另一次互相
學習？
夏洛特：不，實際上。這更像是一件私事。
我鬆了一口氣。
Pup: 我很高興。你已經超越了我微薄的教導。
夏洛特：我也是。這引出了我的下一個重點：我需要
一些左輪手槍的替換零件。
夏洛特：這是一種原型武器，所以零件很難
找到。特別是如果我想避免引起不必要的
注意。
Pup: 如果你需要額外的人手來進行黑市交易，那麼...
夏洛特：相信我，我自己就能帶來足夠的人手。
夏洛特：我想要依靠的是你的腦袋。
Pup: ...？
夏洛特：我認為我們互補彼此的技能

passages.name: SP: Pup x Reagyn A - Begining
passages.content:
Reagyn: ...and you just have to shove that thing there...
Reagyn: Is there a problem? It's not about force, it's about
technique.
Reagyn: Come on, let me show you how it's done.
Reagyn gently moved my hands in a rhythmic 
pattern. I noticed an elegance to the motion.
The pen she guided in my hand moved like a 
dancer on a ballroom floor.
Graceful, no hesitation, no error.
Reagyn: And if you follow this specific pattern you will be
able to shave some seconds on each signature.

Trust me, these few seconds will accumulate to 
minutes or sometimes hours in the long run.
Pup: ...Right. Yeah, you're right.
I looked towards the written words...
"...or your family line may end unceremoniously 
rather than flourish alongside ours."
Pup: ...
Reagyn: Hm...?
Pup: It's... graceful.
Reagyn: ...

Indeed. One must show respect and decorum.

And they must show that respect to their 
adversaries and, more importantly, to their 
own kin.
Reagyn: If one's noble leader cannot act with such 
confidence in their purpose, then how can one 
expect the people you lead to follow suit?
Pup: Yeah, I... I guess that makes sense.
Pup: (Reagyn really knows the theory on this all inside 
and out.)
Reagyn: Why don't you give it a try? This time you can do it 
by yourself.
I grabbed the pen, carefully dipped it into the ink 
and carefully moved it onto the paper.
Reagyn: ...
I carefully looked at Reagyn for approval.
I knew that if I took too long or made a mistake,
Reagyn would end up covering for me and do the 
whole thing without my input.
Pup: (I don't really wanna do this... but I do feel like I
should try.)
However...
*Splat*
Pup: ...?! No...
In a moment of hesitation, my nervous twitch 
knocked over the inkwell.
Reagyn: Quick! Pup, grab those cloths! We got to clean 
this spat of ink before it bleeds to other 
parchments!
Pup: *Exhale* ...
Pup: I think... only one piece of paper got ruined?
Reagyn: Luckily so...
Reagyn: Pup, why don't you go ahead and finish the other 
task? The one in the armory.
Pup: U- Uh... Yeah. I can do that.
Pup: I am... sorry, you know? I didn't mean to do that.
Reagyn: No need to worry. I'm sure you'll-
Pup: -get it next time... Yeah. I know.
It wasn't the first time that was said.
The reminder of it did manage to annoy me.
She was being nice. This was even what I 
wanted: To get out of doing the chore.
Reagyn: Yes... As you and I have said before.
Pup: I do mean it. I really do.
Pup: (I was... actually sort of trying this time. Sort
of...)
Reagyn: ...

Of course you do. I understand.

Just make sure the weapons task is done as I told 
you.
Pup: (I feel a little guilty about that.
She has been very helpful lately...)
Pup: (On the bright side, I can trust that Reagyn will do
the paperwork well.)
Pup: (She didn't seem... too mad. Not happy, but I've 
seen angrier.)
I turned to start walking away from the tent.
Pup: (Besides, everything will work out if it's Reagyn 
doing it. The paperwork will be done in record 
time!)
(The whole "mother hawk" over my shoulder thing 
was a waste of both our times. There are better 
things for us to do.)
I stopped walking.
Pup: (Wait, what was I doing now? Something with 
the... weapons?)
I shook my head and scampered off to do my task.
Stepping away from the armory tent, 
and I smacked my hands to get off 
the dust.
Pup: All good.
Pup: The weapons are in a way better state since 
Reagyn started to take care of the logistics around 
here.
Pup: (Reminds me of how Dad used to run things...)
Norde: ...........
Norde: ...weapons.
Pup: Ah!
I stepped back in a bit of a shock.
Norde was standing over mty shoulder with a stern,
annoyed look.
Norde: Pup, do you have the weapons specifications 
ready? I told you weeks ago today was the 
deadline.
Pup: Weapon specifications...?
Pup: (Oh, shoot! The thing I was supposed to do was 
not to check on the weapons, but order new 
ones!)
Pup: Right... the weapons specs... I had them ready. 
Yep... Right over... in my tent.

Ready to send... at any given moment... The 
weapon specs...
Norde: Just make sure to send them by the end of the day.
With a familiar disappointed look, Norde turned 
around and left.
Pup: (Shoot! Writing them will take days...  I need...)

(I need...!)
Pup: (...Reagyn!)
STAGE DIRECTION> FADE MUSIC SLOWLY, 
RUNNING SE
Pup: *Pant* ... R-...  *Pant* ... Reagyn!
Reagyn: ...
Pup: R- Reagyn?!
Reagyn: ...And done.
Reagyn put the pen down as I hunched over just 
within the tent flaps.
Reagyn: You forgot to do something again, didn't you?
Pup: H- How did you... I mean... of course not...
Reagyn: The way you blush and stutter says otherwise...
Reagyn: It's something related to sending the weapon 
specs to the blacksmith, isn't it?
I nodded.
Reagyn: Did you forget where you put them, or...
Pup: A little closer to... "or"...
Reagyn: *Sigh* ... Forgotten, then?
Pup: N- Not 100% forgotten... but...
Pup: Would you be upset if I told you that I did?
Reagyn: More... disappointed than upset. I can't get mad 
with that-
Reagyn: ...
Reagyn shook the thought away.
Reagyn: I guess we're at a crossroads then.
Reagyn: You won't be a great leader of anything if you 
don't own up to your mistakes.

And we can't fix it if I don't understand the 
situation in detail.
Reagyn: Explain to me what happened in as much detail as 
you can.
Pup: Fine... then... I... accidentally... maybe a little on
purpose... then again... forgot to write out the
weapons specs.
Reagyn: ..."on purpose"?
Pup: Well... there was a small blunder... and you helped.

Then another blunder you helped with again... 
and...
Reagyn: I see where this is going... leading up to this
impossible, multi-day task.

If we don't do them, it may cause the death of 
multiple allies in an upcoming battle.
Reagyn had started pacing with a slight huff.
Reagyn: You know what, let's talk about this "you purposely
forget to do things so I do them for you" part.

To be that irresponsible! And to wait this long to 
tell me.

Did it not occur to you the consequences of your 
own actions!? Were you not ashamed a little bit 
about it?
Pup: I mean... yeah, a little.
Pup: But you really are great at this.
Pup: You're more graceful and assertive when doing it. 
I'm best with a sword in my hand.
Reagyn: It's a bit too late to sweet talk your way out of 
this, missy!
Reagyn: You lied. You know what they do to liars in some
countries?
Reagyn: They cut their tongues! Sometimes they cut their 
hands, or even sometimes your eyes.
Pup: *Gulp* ...!
Less Reagyn's words, but the dominating aura 
around the words pushed me back on my heels.
Reagyn: Of course, I can go easy on you... I can make you 
carry all the weapons from to the top of a 
mountain...
Reagyn: Or maybe some mental punishment would be best. 
Some 'deep end' training for your womanhood?

I've heard about this new "bikini" outfit making its
way out of Lockhart in the past months.
Pup: "B- Bikini"? What is...
Reagyn: Don't worry about it. I have a better idea for your
punishment~
Pup: ...?!
I flinched, closing my eyes as I expected a strong
slap.
Pup: ...
............
*Bonk*
Pup: ...Huh? Did you... Did you just softly "bonk" me 
with a book?
Reagyn: Maybe that way you'll grow a little smarter.
Reagyn: Why didn't you just ask me to help?
Pup: I... thought you'd be angry...
Pup: Each time I let you do the work, it was
done better and the risk you getting angrier
got bigger and bigger...
Pup: I'm not good at these sorts of things... I thought 
you were helping me out of pity...
Reagyn: It's not pity. I grew up helping Flynn out. It's 
second nature to me.

I couldn't be the heir to my family, but I was well
positioned to be Flynn's right hand, including the
struggles there.
Reagyn: And in this moment, I am helping you be a better
leader, so we can return to our paths as quickly as
possible.
Pup: You...  want to leave as quickly as possible?
Reagyn: I- I mean... I wouldn't say it like that.

There are some benefits of being here... lack of
cleanliness notwithstanding.
Reagyn's face had turned away.
Reagyn: But anyways, we have a task we need to fulfill as
urgently as possible.
Pup: No, you were right... It'd take days to do it.
Reagyn: It's going to take days if you do it or I do it...

...separately. 

But together...
Pup: You think? 

Well... If you believe we can, then we can.
Pup: You tell me what to do and I will do my best in 
order to do so!
Reagyn: First, I need you to go to the training grounds and
gather up these details.

Write them up and bring them here. I'll start 
writing the requisition forms.
Pup: Got it!
I started to run off to the training grounds.
But then...
My face planted itself into the group as I tripped on a
nearby tree root.
Pup: ...
Without another word, I stood back up.
...and continued sprinting.
Reagyn: ...
Reagyn: PFFT!!!

Haha! Haha... I... Haha...
Reagyn: *Sigh*...

You're lucky you're cute.
passages.content_zh:
Reagyn：……你只需要把那個東西推到那裡…
雷金：有問題嗎？這不是力量的問題，而是
技術。
Reagyn：來吧，讓我向你展示它是如何完成的。
Reagyn 有節奏地輕輕地移動我的雙手
模式。我注意到這個動作很優雅。
她引導在我手中的筆像一支筆一樣移動
舞廳地板上的舞者。
優雅，沒有猶豫，沒有錯誤。
Reagyn：如果你遵循這個特定的模式，你就會
能夠在每個簽名上節省幾秒鐘。

相信我，這幾秒鐘將會累積到
從長遠來看，幾分鐘甚至幾小時。
小狗：……對。是的，你是對的。
我看向上面寫著的字…
「……否則你的家族可能會毫不客氣地結束
而不是與我們一起繁榮。 」
小狗：…
雷金：嗯……？
小狗：它……很優雅。
雷金：…

確實如此。一個人必須表現出尊重和禮節。

他們必須尊重他們的
對手，更重要的是，他們
自己的親人。
雷金：如果一個人的高貴領袖不能採取這樣的行動
對自己的目的充滿信心，那麼如何才能
期望你領導的人效法嗎？
Pup：是的，我……我想這是有道理的。
Pup：（Reagyn 真的很了解這裡面的理論
並出去。 ）
雷金：為什麼不嘗試呢？這次你可以做到
靠你自己。
我抓起筆，小心翼翼地將它浸入墨水中
並小心地將它移到紙上。
雷金：…
我仔細地看著雷金尋求認可。
我知道如果我花了太長時間或犯了一個錯誤
雷金最終會替我做掩護
整件事情沒有我的參與。
Pup：（我真的不想這麼做……但我確實覺得我
應該嘗試。 ）
然而...
*啪啪*
小狗：……？ ！不...
猶豫的一瞬間，我的神經抽搐了
打翻了墨水池。
雷金：快點！小狗，抓住那些布！我們必須清潔
這滴墨水在流到其他墨水之前
羊皮紙！
小狗：*吐氣*...
Pup：我想……只有一張紙被毀了？
雷金：幸運的是…
Reagyn：小狗，為什麼不繼續完成另一個呢？ 
任務？ ar 中的那個

passages.name: SP: Tatiana x Jakson C - Story
passages.content:
Tatiana: Ah... what a long battle.
Tatiana emptied her backpack, leaving a pile of 
armor sitting on a ground cloth.
Tatiana: Should make sure none of these are too banged 
up, then...?
Tatiana: *YAWN*

Eh... It's fine. Probably... I'll just...
She slumped with weary eyes that were becoming 
more difficult to keep open.
Tatiana: ...just take a...

...little...

...nap...
.........
Tatiana: ...?!?!
Tatiana: Wha' was...? Where am.. I...?
She blinked a few times.
Tatiana: Oh right... 

*Yawn*

...my armor.
With a few more blinks, her awakening mind forced 
her neck to creak her head towards the left.
Tatiana: ...
Tatiana: What the...?!
From her armor set, the cuirass and leg-guards 
were missing.
Tatiana: T- Thieves...?
A few angrier blinks directed her attention to 
nearby the incomplete armor set.
Tatiana: Footprints?

...

...Amateurs.
The footprints, while aged and indistinct, led her to 
a bonfire where Nightless Crows were carousing 
loudly.
Crow: Heresh to our victoreh! ... *hic* ...
The Crow toasted a mug of beer, nearly spilling the
contents.
Tatiana: All right, you drunken louts. Which one of you stole 
my armor?
Crow: Eh...?
Tatiana: Of for the fuckin' Goddess's sake... Why are you 
not even wearing shoes?!
The group of drunken Crows burst forth in laughs 
and snickers.
Tatiana: Is your imminent demise really that funny?
Other Crow: Should we tell 'er?
Tatiana: ...
Her stare was accompanied by the foreboding 
sound of cracking knuckles.
Tatiana: Five... four... three...
Crow: Aight! I'll tell ya...

'Tis the same feller that... *hic* ... nipped me 
shoes.

'Sides, we aint havin' enough legs to make off with 
yer armor... hehe...
Tatiana: Legs? Are you actually making a pass at me right now?
The Crow flailed about in a poor attempt to what
appeared to be a shrug.
And the remaining Crows burst into laughter around
them.
Tatiana: You're lucky I'm too busy catching a thief to teach 
you dogs a lesson.
Tatiana glared at them before walking off.
Crow: Ah, wait... He went...
The Crow pointed to the armory tent.
Crow: ...that-away-I-thin'...?
The Crow blinked, and the flap of the tent's 
opening was already flapping from an entrant.
Tatiana: ...

Well, I can't exactly say I'm surprised...
The tent was a mess of knocked over weapons and 
armor stands.
Tatiana: So whoever took my armor stole from here too...
Tatiana knelt to inspect the pile of metal.
Tatiana: ...?! Is that...?!
There was a leather boot partially buried by some 
armor pieces.
Tatiana reached for it.
Tatiana: ...............
Tatiana: Gross...
It was wet with a weird substance.
Tatiana: Almost like a dog slobbered on it.
Tatiana: Well, at least it's obvious what happened.
Tatiana: The same thief stole my armor, the Crow's boot, 
and from here.

They were interrupted by Jakson, who latched 
onto the perp, ripping the boot off.
Tatiana: Only question is... where is Jakson now?
Tatiana stopped in front of Jakson's miniature 
doggy-tent.
The canine was nowhere to be seen.
Tatiana: Did the thief come here, too?
There were no human footprints, only pawprints 
leading away from the scene.
Tatiana began to follow them.
Tatiana: Ugh...?!
Tatiana: O- Ow...
She looked down to see what she'd 
stubbed her toe on.
It was a pauldron covered in slobber.
Tatiana: Huh? That's... wait...

.....................
The lightbulb illuminated above her head.
Tatiana: Oh, that mangy mutt!
Tatiana's cuirass and leg-guards lay in the middle of
the clearing at the end of the pawprint trail.
Tatiana: Found you!
Tatiana: Now come home to mama...
Tatiana extended her hand, summoning the armor 
to her with a magical grip.
Tatiana: ...?
Instead, the armor sprouted four furry legs that 
began running around in circles.
Tatiana: ...This night just will not end, will it?
Jakson: *Playful bark*!
Tatiana: Playtime's over.
She invoked her magic, attempting to summon the 
armor to her body.
It twitched slightly but remained firmly in place.
Jakson: *Bark feigning innocence* ...!
The canine planted his feet, resisting her pull.
Tatiana: Ugh... You...!
Tatiana's veins bulged as she fought to control the
armor with all her willpower.
Tatiana: I am vengeance! I am a knight! I am...
Tatiana: *Sigh*... completely at an impasse.
Tatiana relaxed, releasing her magical grip.
Jakson: *Snickering pants*...
Jakson wiggled through the armor, emerging his 
head from the top of the cuirass.
Tatiana: Tricked you!
Tatiana flung out her hand, propelling a gauntlet to
move across the grass and grab for the armor.
Jakson leaped, discarding his spoils as he chomped 
down on the gauntlet in midair.
Tatiana: Tsk...! You little...!
Jakson landed, pinning the gauntlet on the ground.
Tatiana: What are you doing with that? Knock it off!
Jakson dragged the gauntlet with him to the 
cuirass, put it on, and then wedged himself inside 
the armor again.
Jakson: *Defiant bark*
He stomped awkwardly with his gauntleted paw as 
he made his way over to the discarded leg-guards.
Jakson: *Annoyed whine*...
Tatiana: Oi, come now. My armor isn't that loud.
The canine slammed his gauntleted paw repeatedly 
into the leg-guards, making loud clanging noises.
Tatiana: Uh... I guess... point taken.
Jakson: *Happy bark*!
Tatiana: Oh boy... this is as bad as the time with 
the pickled...
Tatiana: ...
Tatiana: Wait, why am I even comparing it... 
The mutt is a mutt, not a human.
The absurdity of the situation suddenly struck her.
Tatiana: ...
Tatiana: Heh...
Tatiana: Heh... hehehe... bwahaha!
Jakson: *Jovial bark*!
Tatiana: I guess I could see how you'd find it fun to play 
with. I like it myself.

You know, I've got an idea for a little agreement 
we could come to on that.
Jakson: *Curious whine*...?
Crow: Alright so... hic... what I got ta do ta get me shoes
back again?
Tatiana: Just go over there and attack my armor. I'm testing
some... improvements.
Crow: Ya gunna do your magic watchamit to make it moove?
Tatiana: Nope. I put my heirloom down over there, if you're
curious. Can't use my magic.
Crow: Er... okay, I guess...
The Crow stumbled over to his sword.
Crow: CCCHHHHAAAAaarrrgggee...!
But the armor started flying towards him.
Crow: AARGHH!!!???

I- It's possessed!
A low, keening howl reverberated from the armor.
Crow: B- Banshee! Banshee!
The crow dropped his weapon and sprinted away in
terror.
Tatiana: Bwahaha!!
Other Crow: Pft...! Oi, ya think he soiled himself?
The other Crows shared the laugh with Tatiana.
Meanwhile, Jakson poked his head from the armor 
once the crow was out of sight.
Jakson: *Triumphant bark*!
passages.content_zh:
塔蒂亞娜：啊... 好漫長的一場戰鬥。
塔蒂亞娜清空了她的背包，留下一堆
盔甲放在一塊地布上。
塔蒂亞娜：應該確認一下這些有沒有損壞太嚴重，然後...?
塔蒂亞娜：*打呵欠*

呃... 沒事啦。大概... 我就...
她疲憊地癱倒，眼睛越來越難以睜開。
塔蒂亞娜：...就稍微...

...小睡...

...一下...
.........
塔蒂亞娜：...?!?!
塔蒂亞娜：剛才...？我在哪裡...？
她眨了幾次眼睛。
塔蒂亞娜：喔對...

*打呵欠*

...我的盔甲。
又眨了幾次眼，清醒過來的思緒迫使
她的脖子發出嘎吱聲，將頭轉向左邊。
塔蒂亞娜：...
塔蒂亞娜：搞什麼...?!
從她的盔甲套裝中，胸甲和護腿
不見了。
塔蒂亞娜：小...小偷...?
幾次更憤怒的眨眼將她的注意力引導到
附近不完整的盔甲套裝。
塔蒂亞娜：腳印？

...

...業餘的。
腳印雖然年代久遠且模糊不清，但引導她到
一堆營火旁，那裡無眠烏鴉們正大聲喧鬧
著。
烏鴉：敬我們的勝利！ ... *嗝* ...
烏鴉敬了一杯啤酒，差點灑了出來。
塔蒂亞娜：好了，你們這些醉鬼。你們之中誰偷了
我的盔甲？
烏鴉：呃...?
塔蒂亞娜：看在該死的女神份上... 你們為什麼
甚至沒穿鞋？！
這群醉醺醺的烏鴉爆發出大笑
和竊笑。
塔蒂亞娜：你們即將到來的末日真的那麼好笑嗎？
另一隻烏鴉：我們該告訴她嗎？
塔蒂亞娜：...
她的凝視伴隨著不祥的
指關節爆裂聲。
塔蒂亞娜：五...四...三...
烏鴉：好啦！我告訴妳...

是同一個傢伙... *嗝* ... 偷了我的
鞋子。

而且，我們沒有足夠的腿來搬走
妳的盔甲... 呵呵...
塔蒂亞娜：腿？你現在實際上是在調戲我嗎？
烏鴉笨拙地揮舞著，試圖做出
看起來像是聳肩的動作。
剩下的烏鴉們圍繞著他們爆發出笑聲。
塔蒂亞娜：你們很幸運，我正忙著抓小偷，沒空教訓
你們這些狗東西。
塔蒂亞娜瞪了他們一眼，然後走開了。
烏鴉：啊，等等...

passages.name: SP: CastelxNorde C - Story
passages.content:
Norde: You know as well as I do that the price you're 
asking is excessive.
Merchant: Well, that's the only offer you're getting. Take it or
leave it.
Norde: ...
Norde: You understand that I'll be taking my business
elsewhere?

My bulk purchase business.
Merchant: ...
Norde: ...
The shopkeep's glare lingered on Norde's scales and
pointed ears.
Merchant: And what a terrible loss it is, too.
Norde: ...
Norde detected sarcasm in the man's voice.
Norde: Aye. Indeed so.
With just a hint of a lingering antagonistic glance,
Norde turned away from the stall and disappeared 
into the crowd.
Merchant: Tsk. Damn lizard.
Norde: Patience, Norde. Patience.
Norde had almost left the market when 
a strange sight appeared.
Norde: That should be about everything...

Hm...?
There was a flash of violet eyes as a feminine figure
in a bulky cloak flipped a hood over their head.
Norde: Is that...?
Norde: ...
Norde: Perhaps I should ensure nothing goes wrong...?
Norde followed the figure to a stall that had just
opened up in an isolated corner.
They had stopped and began peering at the titles
displayed on the carts.
Bookseller: Hello ma'am. What can I do for you today?
Castel: *Sigh* ...
Castel: Don't mind me. I'm just browsing for now.
Castel adjusted his hood and robe to better ensure 
his appearance was obscured as much as possible.
Bookseller: If you're sure. Just... let me know if I can help
and... get you on your way.
Castel stared at the titles on display for several
minutes.
People soon began to point and whisper. A small 
crowd formed to gawk at the shady figure.
Bookseller: Listen ma'am, I hate to turn away a paying 
customer, but you're starting to scare away my 
other customers.
If you're not going to buy anything, then I'm going 
to have to ask you to leave.
Castel: Er... I suppose I am actually looking for a couple of
things...
He rattled off a list of academic-sounding texts.
Bookseller: Ah, what luck! I do happen to have one of those 
left in stock.
The bookseller hurriedly grabbed the book and 
turned back to Castel.
Bookseller: You have excellent taste, miss.

This is actually one of my favorites. The binding is
superb and...
The bookseller got close to Castel, entering his
personal space with said book.
Castel: ...?!
Castel backed away.
Castel: I can see that very well from here, thank you.
Bookseller: Nonsense! How can you get that smell of a good 
book if not from up close?
Castel: ...
Castel: ...
Castel: Oooooh, you're right. That is quite nice.
Bookseller: ...?
Castel: And a first edition? Exquisite.
Just then, a strong breeze kicked up and slipped 
the hood from Castel's head.
Castel: Ah...?!
Bookseller: B- By the Goddess...?!
Castel: I- uh...
Castel tried to yank the hood back up, but the 
wind was too strong.
The crowd from the nearby merchant stall started 
to gasp audibly.
Villager 1: W- What do you think she is?
Villager 2: Some sort of... dark spirit?
Villager 1: I- it looks like a m- monster!
Castel: What? Of all the things...?!
Castel: Clearly I am a 'Shade'! Have you imbeciles never 
seen a summoner's-
Norde: *Sigh* ...
Norde ran up to Castel and grabbed his arm.
Norde: Not here. Not now.
Castel: But... But I...!
Norde: We're leaving.

Quickly now.
A proper crowd was starting to form in the market.
Norde pulled Castel into a sprint and the two swiftly
exited the scene.
Despite Castel's grumblings, the two were able to 
make it back to camp without more than stares 
directed their way.
Castel: What is with those... Argh!
Castel: How can they not at least recognize a shade?! Do 
they not even know what they are?!
Norde: I actually do doubt many would be aware in a small
village like that.
Castel: What? Shades, especially summoned ones, 
are all too common.
Norde: In academia, noble spaces, affluent districts... yes.
Norde: This place, though?
Castel: ...
Castel: Then... I can explain it. I could explain my situation,
even.

You didn't need to drag me away from the scene.
Norde: They wouldn't have understood.
Norde: ...and you were causing a scene.
Castel: It wasn't that bad.
Norde: Trust me. I know how quickly those situations can 
go sideways.
Castel: Hmm...
Norde: Moreover, what do you suppose the reaction would 
be even among those that did recognize what a 
shade was?
Castel: ...

I... may have not gotten to considering that step, 
yet.
Norde: Exactly.
Norde approached the active campfire in the camp.
Only a scattered few other Crows were out and 
about, so Norde took a seat next to it.
Norde: Something bad could've happened because of it.
Castel: Are you saying... perhaps... as a person who 
appears as a shade...
Castel: You are suggesting the idea that an innocent 
person may be unfairly castigated?
Castel shuffled over in a slight huff, sitting across
from Norde.
Castel: Do I not have the right to freely conduct business 
in a town square?
Norde: That is not the issue here.
Castel: Then enlighten me.
Norde: The issue is that people like you and I can't always
get what we want.
Norde: It's unfortunate, but it's the reality we live in.
Norde: If you refuse to adapt to it, then you will create
trouble for yourself.
Castel: So... what? Your solution is to just give up, then?
Norde: ...
Norde: It's not 'giving up'. It's called being realistic.
Norde: Even beyond myself, I've never wanted to pull the 
Crows or Ivan into trouble of my own making.
Castel: Hmph. I can see that further conversation is 
completely pointless.
Castel: I'll do things my way, thank you very much.
Castel pushed himself to his feet as he started to 
make his way from the campfire.
Norde: *Sigh*... Wait.
Castel: ...
Norde: Hard to let that one pass, as one of the people
responsible for the Crows.
Norde: Explain what your way is.
Castel: ...
Norde: I am willing to hear you out.

But more importantly...
Norde turned his head towards Castel.
Norde: I won't let the Crows be drawn into that sort of
trouble.

You decision will affect all of us, regardless of
specifics.

You are a part of this team, too.
Castel: Hmm... Well...
Castel: Given sufficient rhetorical acumen, my hypothesis is
that anyone could be persuaded.
Castel: They can be persuaded to see that people in a 
situation like my own, shade or not, are not so far 
removed from what they see as "a real person".
Castel: The same can be applied to homlyns and non-
homlyns, I'll note.
Norde: So your answer is to meet suspicions with an 
academic debate.

Do you think that'd actually work?
Castel: ...In truth, I cannot say.
Castel: I do know that giving up before even trying is
illogical.
Castel: The steps we have taken forward are largely by 
those who didn't take "impossible" as an answer.
Norde: ...

I can understand the desire.
Norde: Nor am I inherently opposed to the attempt.
Norde rose to meet Castel's gaze.
Norde: All I'm saying is that we should approach this with a
greater level of caution.
Castel: "We"?
Norde: We are a team, after all. You have joined the 
Crows for this mission, and your problems are our 
problems.
Norde: So solving your problems is solving our problems, as
well.
Castel: Hmph. Tis' true that great discoveries were seldom 
made alone.
Castel: Very well. I'll be looking forward to our partnership.
passages.content_zh:
Norde：你跟我一樣清楚你的價格
要求太過分了。
商人：嗯，這是你得到的唯一報價。拿走或
離開它。
諾德：…
Norde：你明白我會繼續我的生意
其他地方？

我的大量採購業務。
商家：...
諾德：…
店主的目光停留在諾德的鱗片上，
尖耳朵。
商人：這也是多麼可怕的損失。
諾德：…
諾德聽出了男人聲音中的諷刺。
諾德：是的。確實如此。
只是帶著一絲揮之不去的敵對目光，
諾德轉身離開攤位，消失了
進入人群。
商家：嘖。該死的蜥蜴。
諾德：耐心點，諾德。耐心。
當 Norde 幾乎退出市場時
奇怪的景像出現了。
Norde：這應該是關於一切的......

嗯……？
紫羅蘭色的眼眸閃爍著女性般的身影
穿著一件厚重的斗篷，把兜帽翻到了他們的頭上。
諾德：那是……？
諾德：…
Norde：也許我應該確保不會有任何問題…？
諾德跟著人影來到了一個剛開幕的攤位。
開在一個偏僻的角落。
他們停下來開始盯著標題
顯示在購物車上。
書商：您好，女士。今天我能為您做什麼？
卡斯特：*嘆氣*...
卡斯特爾：別介意我。我現在只是瀏覽一下。
卡斯特調整了他的兜帽和長袍，以更好地確保
他的容貌被盡可能地遮掩起來。
書商：如果你確定的話。只是...如果我能幫忙請告訴我
並且...帶您上路。
卡斯特盯著展示的標題看了好幾眼
分鐘。
人們很快就開始指指點點，竊竊私語。一個小
人群聚集在一起，呆呆地看著那個陰暗的身影。
書商：聽著，女士，我討厭拒絕付費的人
顧客，但你開始嚇跑我的
其他客戶。
如果你不打算買任何東西，那我就走了
不得不請你離開。
Castel：呃……我想我其實是在尋找幾個
東西...
他滔滔不絕地列出了一系列聽起來很學術的文章。
書商：啊，運氣真好！我碰巧有其中之一
剩餘庫存。
書商趕緊

passages.name: SP: RowanxCharlotte B - New Event
passages.content:
So the sun hit its apex.
The beat of the Goddess's light shone down upon 
her realm.
The oppressive aura of the day fed into the daily 
lives of all those around.
After all, the agreed upon time had come.
This would be a day that lived in the shadows of 
fame and infamy.
It would be a decisive day for two nations and the
world around them.
Shadows blanketed the inside of the tent.
A sole table sat within the dim light at its center.
Feminine Voice?: So you're ready?
Masculine Voice?: Indeed I am.
One of the voices stepped from the shadows.
Charlotte: You better take this seriously.
She was flanked by two people, dressed in 
traditional Lockhart military garb.
Rowan: I will do my utmost.
He was also flanked by two people. They were 
dressed in Imperial military styles.
Rowan: Ladies first?
Charlotte: Hmm...
Charlotte was hesitant, but she soon took her seat.
Rowan soon followed her lead and sat across 
from her.
Rowan: Now then. You know that I called you here. 
As for the why...

Beyond the conflict we are embroiled within, we 
both seek the empire's withdraw from Lockhart.

This meeting is meant to establish expectations and
initial plans for a post-conflict world for the both of
us.
Do you agree to this goal, with we as 
representatives of Nolvanus and Lockhart?
Charlotte: Mmm...
The room was met with silence as Rowan sat 
waiting for her to confirm.
Charlotte: Calling yourself a representative of the empire is a
bit...
She glared harder at Rowan.
Rowan: Then... what would manifest your trust in that
sentiment?
Charlotte: Do the shit you're claiming to want to do.
Rowan: Perfect.
Charlotte: Huh...?
Rowan: Your condition is a simple matter of fixing the 
empire.

Something I've already the motivation to do.

Now, shall we establish an ideal path forward for 
our two great states of people?
Charlotte: Mmm...!
Rowan: ...
Rowan waited patiently with a very serious look 
across his face.
Charlotte: *Sigh*... Fine. You already set this up, I guess.
Rowan: Then, on the topic of...
The two sat and worked through political issues like
borders, reparations, and trade routes.
Much of the conversation delved down a rabbit 
hole of "what if"s, but not all.
Charlotte: Isn't that just giving the Empire what it wanted 
when it invaded?
Rowan: Yes, but if we can end the war with the Republic, 
then Lockhart doing so wouldn't be dangerous.

Taking a side in that war was what your 
government was avoiding, no?

Working with the empire or republic more closely 
would just be business, rather than an act of war.
Charlotte: Hmm... Maybe.

You know, since when did you get an actual feel 
for this political stuff?
Rowan: I've had my share of it hammered into me in my youth.
Rowan: I take it you don't disagree, though?
Charlotte: Mmm...
Charlotte stewed in her seat.
The conversation continued on, until...
Rowan: And that would settle that topic quite effectively.
Charlotte: In a sense...
Rowan: As for the next topic...
Rowan hung on those words as the atmosphere 
of the room settled into the silence.
.........
Rowan: Shall we have a cup of tea?

This dreariness has quite of subtle aroma to it, but
tea would be all the nicer, no?
Charlotte: *Sigh*...
Rowan's tone shifted from the more serious one he 
had taken into the more lighthearted one he 
typically used.
Charlotte: Only a matter of time.
Armored Guard: Uh... are we gonna be here much longer?
Within the armor...
Pup: It's... not the easiest to breath in this thing, you
know. Or hear. Or see anything going on.
Pup: Sort of getting stuffy, too...
Armored Guard 2: Y- Yeah. This isn't what I was expecting when you
asked.
In the other armor.
Mariel: I'm getting... a little... sweaty in here...
Crow: Argh... I just wanted to eat my breakfast in peace.
Charlotte: Did you rope in... all of...
Charlotte: *Sigh*...
Charlotte: Alexei...!
She turned to Rowan.
Rowan: Oh?
Rowan: That'll do.
Rowan reached out to grab her hand.
Charlotte: Ah, what?
Charlotte: W- Wait, what are you-?!
Rowan: Negotiations, my dear! Negotiations!
Charlotte: I didn't say you could-
Rowan pulled Charlotte out of the tent.
Pup: I couldn't hear that clearly. Are we done?
Pup: ...
Armored Guard: ...Hello?
Charlotte: What are we doing here?
Rowan: This location will work.
The two stopped at the apex of a small, grassy hill.
Charlotte: Work for what?
Rowan: As I said: Negotiations.
Charlotte: Hmm.........
Rowan: Now, at the top of this fair hill, we need to... 
lay down.
Charlotte: If you try to do something...

...

Fine, but I'm keeping my hand on my gun in case 
you do anything... funny.
Rowan: If it helps you relax, then I embrace that choice~
Charlotte: So what do you wanna negotiate now that we-
Rowan: Shh.
Charlotte: What...?
Charlotte: ...
Charlotte laid back along with Rowan.
Rowan: Ah...
Rowan started to relax his eyes and stare out into 
the sky.
Charlotte, on the other hand...
Charlotte: Hmm...
Kept moving her eyes towards Rowan as though 
expecting something more to happen.
As though expecting this "negotiation" to start in
earnest.
Charlotte: Rowan, aren't we-
Rowan: Shh... At the right time.
Charlotte, bewildered still, laid back again.
Charlotte: Hmm...
Rowan: ...
Charlotte: ...
Rowan: ...
Charlotte: ...
Rowan: ...
...............
Both of the two had entered a zen like calm.
Relaxing.
In the warmth of the sun.
Pup: ...?

There you two are.
Charlotte: Ah...?!
Charlotte jumped to her feet with her gun ready to 
be drawn.
Charlotte: W- What are you doing here?!
Pup: I was just trying to figure out where you guys 
went. It's been an hour.
Charlotte: Huh?!
Rowan: Ah... good morning~
Charlotte: It isn't morning.
Rowan: It's morning somewhere.
Charlotte: And you! Did you just waste an hour of mine...!?

Argh! I should...! I should...!
In a huff, Charlotte stomped away.
Mariel: *Pant* ... Wait... for...
Mariel: Huh...?! Sis? Where are you...?
Rowan: Hmm...
Pup: I'm... just confused, now.

She seemed pretty mad... I thought you guys 
were discussing Lockhart and the Empire.
Pup: What was that about? Did it not go well?
Rowan: ...

I would call it...
Rowan: ...progress.
passages.content_zh:
於是太陽來到了頂點。
女神的光芒照耀在
她的國度之上。
白日那令人壓迫的氣息，融入了
周遭所有人的日常生活中。
畢竟，約定的時間已經到來。
這將會是個活在名聲與惡名陰影之下的日子。
這將會是對兩個國家，以及
他們周遭世界來說，決定性的一天。
陰影籠罩著帳篷內部。
一張孤零零的桌子，位於其中心那昏暗的光線中。
女性聲音？：妳準備好了嗎？
男性聲音？：我確實準備好了。
其中一個聲音從陰影中走了出來。
夏洛特：你最好認真對待這件事。
她身旁站著兩個人，穿著傳統的洛克哈特軍裝。
羅文：我會盡我所能。
他身旁也站著兩個人。他們穿著帝國軍裝。
羅文：女士優先？
夏洛特：嗯...
夏洛特有些猶豫，但她很快就入座了。
羅文也很快跟著她的腳步，坐在她對面。
羅文：那麼。妳知道我為何邀請妳來這裡。
至於原因...

除了我們身陷其中的衝突之外，我們
都尋求帝國從洛克哈特撤兵。

這次會議旨在為我們雙方建立衝突後世界的
期望和初步計畫。
妳是否同意這個目標，我們作為
諾爾瓦努斯和洛克哈特的代表？
夏洛特：嗯...
房間陷入沉默，羅文坐著等待她確認。
夏洛特：自稱是帝國的代表，有點...
她更用力地瞪著羅文。
羅文：那麼...什麼能體現妳對這種
說法的信任？
夏洛特：做你聲稱想做的事情。
羅文：完美。
夏洛特：蛤...？
羅文：妳的條件只是一個簡單的修復
帝國的問題。

這也是我已經有動力去做的事情。

現在，我們是否應該為
我們兩個偉大的國家的人民，建立一個理想的前進道路？
夏洛特：嗯...！
羅文：...
羅文耐心地等待著，臉上帶著非常嚴肅的表情。
夏洛特：*嘆氣*...好吧。我想你已經安排好了。
羅文：那麼，關於這件事...

passages.name: SP: Castel x Pup C - Story
passages.content:
Castel: Hmm....

What if I use that spell in order to...?
In a cozy corner of the encampment, Castel
flipped through an academic text.
Castel: Hmm... but then I would have to shift that to, 
wait... that won't work...
Castel: Hmm...

If my hypothesis is correct, that may be a good first
step.
Castel: Could the curse stabilize long enough to apply a
procedure properly?
Castel: ...
Castel leaned back in his seat.
Castel: Wait... that's it...?!
Pup: Mmm...  *munch* ...

(Such tender and plump meat. I wonder what the 
chickens in the area eat?)
I looked over to the cook tent's interior to see who
was tasked with it today.
Pup: (I wonder if they know how they got the meat this
tender?)
As I was about to get up to ask...
Castel: Pup. I need you to undress and follow me.
Pup: ...
I stopped chewing.
I blinked back at the person that had suddenly 
appeared in front of me, but the distraction from 
the meat didn't go away.
So I started chewing again.
Pup: Insh… thash order?
I could barely talk with my mouth full of chicken.
Pup: *Gulp*
Castel: Order? Order is irrelevant.
Castel: Though, undressing as we travel could save time...
Pup: ...
Pup: W- What about I follow you... THEN I undress...?
Castel: If you must, but do please not dawdle, then.
I stood up, but Castel noticed something I was
carrying.
Castel: Are you... bringing the chicken into the lab?
Pup: ...
I looked at the "lab" and saw a tent.
Pup: Ywou mhen da tent?
I talked while munching on another piece 
of chicken.
Castel: Whatever you wish to call it, it is unhygienic to 
bring half eaten food into a place of research.
Pup: Aww...
Pup: Uh... Let me just... What to do with it...?
Jakson: *Hungrily licks lips* ...
I had just entered the lab's door, but Castel 
stopped me before I could.
Castel: Clothes off.
Pup: Ah...
While I hesitated for a second, the next few 
seconds after that were spent staring at Castel.
Castel: ...
Pup: (It'll... probably... be fine...?)
Pup: ...
Castel: ...
Pup: *Sigh*...
Pup: Give it to me straight, doc... how bad is the damage?
Castel: Hmm...
Castel: From 1 to 10... maybe a 5...
Pup: That doesn't sound... too bad...?
Castel: With a 10 being so large that they break your spine 
and you could not walk anymore.
Castel: Hmph. A 5 is not terrible, indeed.
Pup: Break my spine? W- We're talking about these 
things on my chest, right?
Castel: Naturally.
Pup: If that's a 10, then what's a 0 or 1?
Castel: It is simply a scale derived from my own
observations... Men being, of course... a zero.
Pup: That'd imply that you've seen a 10?

What unlucky soul got that fate?
Castel: I cannot disclose that information. Research
confidentiality.
Pup: R- Right...
I fidgeted around as the imagined image flickered 
in my mind's eye.
Pup: So... what are we doing here?
Castel: I hypothesize that in order for your body to 
become a man, it first off must be more manly.
Pup: Oh! So this is about transforming back to a man?
Pup: Wait... "become a man" and "be more manly"... 
aren't those the same thing?
Castel: Not quite.
Castel: If we try to revert the entire process at once, 
there's a high rate of failure. Therefore...
Pup: Make... small changes first?
Castel: Precisely!
Castel: Starting with...!
I looked down towards our previous topic of
conversation.
Pup: (Boobs...)
Castel: Your gaze surmises correctly.
Castel: With that consent, I will start immediately.
Pup: A- Ah... Umm...
I was at a loss for words. I did not know what 
Castel was about to do.
A way to fight the curse was tempting, but I had a 
bad feeling about this.
Castel: Hands on top of your head.

Grab your hair and don't let it go, unless you want 
to resemble a nekolyn.
Castel created a green light from his hands. I could
sense a warm sensation on my chest.
And...
Pup: I think it's actually working this time?!
The weight I felt on my chest was noticeably
decreasing.
Pup: Wow...
As it went along, I let my mind drift.
Pup: (On the bright side, if this is done quickly enough, I
can go back and eat the chicken legs... if they're
still there.)
Castel: Almost... there...

...
Castel: And... done.
Castel slowly stepped back.
Castel: From a 5 down to a 1.
Castel: Can you do some stretches? Anything hurt?
My breasts went down a significant level. My chest 
was almost flat.
There were still small mounds of flesh, but nothing
that couldn't be hidden if I wanted to.
Pup: Nope. I feel pretty light! My shoulders won't feel as
stiff anymore!
Castel: Excellent. Then we can continue with another
transformation at a later date.
Castel: Once your body reacclimates and stabilizes with the
"new" change, of course.
Pup: Thanks, Castel! You've really outdone yourself.
As I dressed back up again, I could feel that my 
pants were a bit tighter than I remembered.
Pup: (Weird... Maybe I ate too much?)
After finishing dressing, I headed out and about the
Nightless Crows campsite.
Crow: Is that ye olde leader over there?
Another Crow: Hm? No, couldn't be. Not with that... cake.
Pup: Hm...? Cake?

...
Pup: (It's been forever since I had cake...)
Pup: (Though... maybe I should avoid sweets for a while...)
As I walked through camp, I could feel something
swaying on my rear.
Pup: Weird.
And suddenly.
*RIIPPPP* ...!
Pup: Ah... W- What the-?!
I felt a sudden breeze along my rear.
As I checked what had happened, the sight behind 
me showed a mountainous trek.
Pup: (I- Is that my ass?! It's huge!)
As I touched the cheeks, they felt like big and 
fluffy marshmallows. They were like melon sized 
cushions.
Pup: (I- I need to go back to Castel!)
*RIP* ...!
The breeze became more distinct.
Pup: P- Pants...! My tent is close by...!
Pup: ...?
The sight inside was one of dread and silence.
It was as though a death in a family had taken place.
Pup: ...nothing fits...
My gaze drifted towards my bed.
...where someone, likely as a prank, had left a skirt.
Pup: ...
Pup: C- Castel...!?
Pup: Castel!
I stuck my head into Castel's tent with my 
whispered yells.
.........
Nothing.
Pup: Where did he...?

(At a time like this?! I'm gonna kill him!)
Castel: Hmm... An 8, maybe?
Pup: Ah...?!
I spun to find Castel closely observing my butt.
Emphasis on "closely".
Castel: Hmm...
Castel: Hypotheses are made to be tested.
Pup: Undo it...!
I leaned in towards him to whisper exasperatedly 
as to not draw more attention.
Castel: You say that, but with data from this, we could...
Pup: ...!
Castel: *Sigh* ... Very well. That should theoretically be
possible.
Castel raised himself to a standing position.
Castel: You will have to remove the... new apparel before
entering.
Pup: Just fix it!
And my angry whisper ushered us both within to 
live for another day.
And to live for another experiment.

如果我的假設是正確的，那可能是個好的開始

passages.name: SP- SatiaxTatiana C - New Event
passages.content:
Tatiana: Hmm?
Tatiana leaned down with her eyes on her pants.
Tatiana: A... hole? 

Dammit.
She shuffled along across the camp.
Tatiana: Oi. Doily girl. We got any thread and needle sets in
that stash back there?
Mariel: Oh, Tatiana...? You mean for that hole in your 
pants? That might be hard to get done.
Mariel: Thread is good for stitching wounds when blue 
magic isn't plentiful, after all.
Mariel: We've gone through so much in our recent 
battles... could you perhaps find another source?
Tatiana: Oi. Crow friend. We got any thread and needle sets 
in that stash back there?
Crow: 'fraid not. Been going through a lot of supplies in 
the recent battles.

Thread is good for stitching wounds when blue 
magic ain't plentiful, after all.

You'll have to supply your own unless it's an
emergency.
Tatiana: Tsk. That's my luck, alright...
Tatiana: If that changes, let me know, 'kay?
As Tatiana began to walk off, a head popped 
around the corner.
One that overheard the conversation.
Satia: Oh? Hello, Tatiana... You were looking for thread?
Tatiana: Ai. My trousers finally ripped, so I need to close up
the hole in it.
Tatiana: A few threads and a minute of work and it'd be 
done, but supplies are low.
Satia: Well, if that's all, then I have a patch and bobby 
pins that you can have.

It won't be as stable as proper needlework, but it
should last until we can get more thread.
Tatiana: A patch can work. Where'd you have it?
Satia: Back at my quarters. Just follow me~
Satia turned, beckoning Tatiana to follow.
The two entered Satia's personal tent.
Satia: One moment.
Satia moved to her bag.
Rifling through it for a moment, she pulled out the
patch.
Satia: Here it is~
Tatiana: Thanks, that should-
Tatiana: ...Wait.
Tatiana looked closer at it. It had a flowery design.
Specifically, it was a Peony patch. 
Prominently purple, too.
Tatiana: ...
Satia: Is something wrong?
Tatiana: It's... not... really my style.

Ya know... fancy flower patterns might give off the
wrong impression...
Tatiana: Like... I'm a noble or somethin'
She shivered a bit.
Satia: Aw, don't be like that. Flowers are something 
everyone can have.
Satia: Did you know there's a 'language of flowers'? Each 
can have different meanings.
Satia: This one means prosperity and fortune.
Tatiana: Well... hmm...
She fidgeted, seemingly hesitant to take a stance
either way at first.
Tatiana: Nah...
She shook her head.
Tatiana: Appreciate the thought, but think I'll go without for
now.
She left, leaving Satia alone.
Satia stood there and watched her leave with a
thoughtful gaze.
Satia: Not a fan of flowers, perhaps...?

It could've worked... But maybe something else 
instead.
Some time later.
Satia: Alright, so we have the list for the food, the plates
for replacing broken armor, medical supplies...
Tatiana, having been keeping her ears perked for 
any tell of someone going to town, stepped 
forward into Satia's view.
Tatiana: And the stuff I mentioned?
Satia: Of course, of course. We can spend some more on 
that in exchange for your help here.
Tatiana: Good deal, thanks!
Satia: Even for an order this size, this is a long fulfillment
time...
Satia: We've some free time now. Did you want to go window
shop? Perhaps we can find what you need?
Tatiana: Yeah, that works. I have a couple things to do in town
anyways.
The two walked through the crowded 
streets together.
Satia's gaze went up and down the shop stalls and
windows.
Tatiana's gaze... drifted towards the money 
pouches in the crowd.
Tatiana: Hmm...
Tatiana slowly weaved through the crowd, and 
approached someone of higher standing, with a 
fat money pouch jingling, when...
Satia: Tatiana, I have something for you to look at. 
Where'd you go?
The voice bellowed through the crowd, drawing 
most of its gazes.
The mark was included in that, and they stepped 
away from the suspicious looking Tatiana.
Tatiana: Dammit, why now...?
Tatiana moved her feeet back over to Satia,
if just to see what it was about.
Satia stood in front of a tailor's shop, looking
through the materials, with something in 
one hand.
Satia: It looks nice, doesn't it?
Satia held up a green ribbon; not quite Tatiana's 
hair color, but close.
Tatiana: That's... really not my kind of thing, either.
Satia: Is there something wrong with it?
Tatiana: That's something someone who has too much 
money and not enough sense would buy. No 
practical use.
Satia: Looking cute is a practical use, no?
Tatiana: Ya know what I mean.
Tatiana: *Sigh*... You find what you were looking for?
Satia: I have. What about yourself?
Tatiana: They... ran out of stock before I could snatch it.
Satia: Well, if you're done browsing, we can always head 
back to the shop.

It shouldn't be too much longer before they're 
ready, anyways.
Tatiana: I still have something more to do, so go ahead. I'll
catch up once I'm done.
Tatiana proceeded to quickly walk down the street 
and right past Satia.
Satia watched as Tatiana turned a corner and out 
of sight.
Satia: Hmm...
So Satia followed.
And then peeked around the corner.
And then saw the slight magical aura.
And it be around Tatiana's Armored Bandit armor.
Satia: Hmm...
From the alley, Tatiana slipped silently in the 
hulking armor, the crowds none the wiser.
Satia continued to follow, observing some of 
Tatiana's actions, tracking her by the 
strangely deft footsteps of the armor.
Footsteps that... shifted.
Satia: She's...?
Satia peeked around the corner to see the armor 
enter an alleyway, so she followed.
And as she turned her head again, she saw Tatiana 
with a small bag.
Tatiana: Here.
The arm extended to a small family that the armor
towered over.
Family's Father: Oh, thank you so much.
They unfurled the bag, and started 
taking food from it.
Child: *Munch*...
Family's Mother: I don't know how you managed it, but thank you. I 
won't ask questions.
As Tatiana began to turn to leave...
Satia: She'll spot me...!
Satia ducked back into the crowd, retreating at the
last opportunity and losing Tatiana's trail.
Tatiana and Satia had regrouped, packing the 
supplies and lugging them back to camp.
It was a quiet trip, all things considered.
Tatiana: Between all the mess in the town, I forgot the one
reason I actually went over there. Dammit.
She whispered under her breath.
Satia: If you need to run back, I can wait, or assist as
needed.
Tatiana: Ah... n- no.
Tatiana: It's just ma pants. Doesn't matter. I'll just get
somethin' for it next time.
Satia: Hmm... Alright. Do you want me to give you a 
heads up when the next group goes out on a 
supply run?
Tatiana: That'd actually be great. Thank you.
The rest of the day came and went, as though a
footnote.
Tatiana had yet to fully process what had 
happened. She had yet to wind down for the day.
And in that state, she entered her room to find...
...a needle, a spool of thread... as well as a small
patch and a note.
Tatiana: Huh...?
Tatiana's eyes dotted across the page.
It was from Satia.
Satia: "It's not exactly what you were looking for, but I
think these should cover up the damage without 
making it worse."
Satia: "Give it a shot. You can always rip it off later, after
all."
Tatiana looked back down at the patch.
It wasn't extravagant or flashy, but it did have a
slight and subtle pattern around it's border,
reminiscent of flowers.
Tatiana: ...
Tatiana: *Sigh*... Didn't I tell you it ain't my style...

.........
Tatiana: Ah... Oh well.
The next day.
Charlotte: Thank you. I'll just head out now.
Crow: Sure, and-

Hm?
The Crow looked over Charlotte's shoulder, seeing...
Tatiana: ...
The two looked on as she passed.
Crow: She seems chipper.
Charlotte: Did she? I just noticed the patch on her pants.
Charlotte: Had a little embroidered pattern on it.
Crow: Huh? How did you notice that sort of detail?
Charlotte: I'm a regular eagle eye~
Charlotte: Though, mostly...

I didn't expect her to enjoy tailoring designs like
that.
passages.content_zh:
Tatiana: 嗯？
Tatiana 彎下腰，眼睛盯著她的褲子。
Tatiana: 一個... 洞？

可惡。
她拖著腳步走過營地。
Tatiana: 喂。蕾絲邊女孩。我們後面的儲藏裡有針線組嗎？
Mariel: 哦，Tatiana...? 你是指你褲子上的那個洞嗎？可能不太容易弄好。
Mariel: 畢竟，藍色魔法不夠用的時候，線可以用來縫合傷口。
Mariel: 我們最近的戰鬥消耗了很多... 你能不能找找其他來源？
Tatiana: 喂。烏鴉朋友。我們後面的儲藏裡有針線組嗎？
Crow: 恐怕沒有。最近的戰鬥消耗了很多物資。

畢竟，藍色魔法不夠用的時候，線可以用來縫合傷口。

除非是緊急情況，否則你得自己準備。
Tatiana: 嘖。這就是我的運氣，好吧...
Tatiana: 如果有變動，記得告訴我，好嗎？
當 Tatiana 開始走開時，一個頭從角落探了出來。
一個聽到了對話的人。
Satia: 哦？你好，Tatiana... 你在找線嗎？
Tatiana: 嗯。我的褲子終於破了，所以我需要把洞補起來。
Tatiana: 幾根線和一分鐘的工作就能搞定，但物資不足。
Satia: 嗯，如果只是這樣，那我有一些補丁和髮夾可以給你。

它不會像正規的針線活那麼牢固，但應該可以撐到我們能拿到更多線的時候。
Tatiana: 補丁也可以。你在哪裡拿到的？
Satia: 在我的房間裡。跟我來～
Satia 轉身，示意 Tatiana 跟隨。
兩人進入了 Satia 的私人帳篷。
Satia: 稍等一下。
Satia 走到她的包旁。
翻找了一會兒，她拿出補丁。
Satia: 在這裡～
Tatiana: 謝謝，這應該-
Tatiana: ...等等。
Tatiana 更仔細地看了看。它有一個花卉設計。
特別是，它是一個牡丹補丁。
而且是顯眼的紫色。
Tatiana: ...
Satia: 有什麼不對嗎？
Tatiana: 這... 不是... 我的風格。

你知道... 花俏的花紋可能會給人錯誤的印象...

passages.name: SP- JudexCastell C - New Event
passages.content:
Castel: Oh Goddess... may the light guide my magic and 
make it true! Eucrasia!
Castel: Oh goddess, may the light smite my enemies with 
the one true light! Rime!
.........
Castel: Tsk... it did not work...
Far into the depths of a makeshift lab lay a 
certain... researcher.

Not technically a shade, but 
not technically a human either.
His experiments to return to human form had 
guided him into very different paths, and this 
is but one of them.
Castel: Oh goddess, may the light smite my enemies with 
the one true light! Rime!
The cold air surrounding a piece of raw rat meat 
began to condense and encase the meat.
Soon after, ice crystals began to form, starting from
the wettest parts of the cut and ending on the 
driest parts of the bone.
Castel: Oh Goddess... may the light guide my magic and 
make it true! Eucrasia!
The frozen piece of meat began to thaw, but as it 
did so, it began to crumble.
It fell apart into meat crystals, and those
transitioned to bloody game meat once 
more after the magic faded.
Castel: Tsk... Even if I reverse the order... the results are
similar enough.
Castel: Therefore it might be safe to discard the order as a
variable.

But if that is not it... then what could it be? Maybe
in Experiment 119, I can-
Castel: .........
Castel looked down into an empty bucket, now filled
with game meat blood instead of any usable meat.
Castel: I need to go to the provisions tent again.

Inefficient waste of time, but I can hypothesize 
while walking...
Castel hoisted his empty bucket and started 
walking towards the cafeteria.
Castel: There are no spells that will transform me, especially
permanently, to my original form.
Castel: Weaving multiple spells together should be a faster 
way of reaching the wanted result...

Perhaps with shorter and safer spells...?
Over crafting a new spell to make it quicker.
The bucket clattered around, creating a 
contrasting sight between the elegant 
shade and the bloodied metal.
Castel: *Sigh*... it is good that Lady Stewart agreed to 
fund my jaunts into food preservation.

Magically sustaining hunted meat is fascinating as a
topic...
Castel: ...and also offers insight I can use for my own
preservation. To be a human once more.
Pup: Morning Castel, what do you have...
I found my eyes staring into a bucket.
One that was a bloody mess within.
Pup: .........
...and decided some things are better off not 
known.
Castel: Combining spells seems to be a challenge no one 
has truly been able to decipher.
Castel: There have been tales of the old days where the 
ancient delivered spells in combination, but...
Castel: ...no record of the how exists.
Pup: ...

(Is he... talking to me? No, he's gotta be talking to
the air.)
With an unsettling feeling from the sights and 
sounds, I stepped away cautiously, and left Castel 
to his fixation.
Castel: From the spells available to me, I have narrowed 
down the two most likely to yield the result I want, 
Rime and Eucrasia.
 One to freeze the meat, and the other to 
preserve it without major damage to the tissue...

Hmmm...
Castel: One of my current hypotheses is that the speed of
casting might be affecting the outcome of the 
desired result.
Therefore the speed of casting needs to be 
reduced... 

But speeding up the incantation or prayer has led 
to... tongue-twisting results.
Castel stepped into the dining tent.
Castel: Cook. I require more 'experimental' meat.
Cook: Again!? Couldn't you use your fancy firework magic 
and capture a pigeon or rat?
Castel: First of all, changing the ingredients of the
experiment might alter the result.
Castel: It would be best to remain consistent.
Castel: But I will take fault... I assumed the experiment 
would have yielded results by now.
Cook: Ugh... fine. I'll prep you another batch.

But you should ask the boss to organize some sort 
of hunting party if you continue at this rate.
The cook's cutting knife struck down 
onto the wooden board.
Cook: This is gonna take a sec, though, since I just 
finished a big order of pasta for a guy.

Go grab a snack or somethin' in the meantime.
Castel: I don't-
*Grrroooowwlllll*
Castel: Hmm... lack of sustenance might lead to a lack of
focus.
Castel: Fine, I'll take some of that.
Castel picked up some of the stuffed pasta, 
put it in a bowl...
...and sat in a corner of the room as he continued 
mumbling to themselves about potential course
corrections on their current experiments.
Jude: Cook, is that pasta ready?
Cook: Yeah, someone took the first bite though. But 
there is plenty more from where that came from.

Gotta say, I never would have imagined stuffing 
pasta this way.
Jude: That's how the book said to cook it. Just adapted 
to our provisions.

Nothing too extraordinary.
Cook: You are underselling yourself a lot, man.

Just look at that... lady... over there. She has been 
staring at the table, taking a few bites,
and repeating. 
It is clear she has been enjoying it a lot.
Jude: If you say so.
Jude grabbed a bowl of pasta, poured some sauce, 
and sat near the full-mouthed mumbling shade.
Jude: ...
Castel: Bush if I cansh...
*Gulp*
Castel: There was one teaching from the Covenant about 
magical chants...
Castel grabbed another spoonful of pasta and ate it.
Jude: *Chews quietly*...
Castel could feel a slightly uninterested gaze upon
him.
It wasn't intense, but it was there.
Jude: ...
Castel: If I... then...
*Gulp*
Castel: May I... help... you?
The mercenary looked around as if expecting Castel 
to be talking to someone else.
Then he realized the shade was talking to him.
Jude: Hmmm...
Jude: Don't think so...
Castel: Very well. Good.
Castel continued to mumble to himself, but every 
time he took a bite out of the pasta, Jude 
directed his gaze toward them.
Castel: ...
Castel: Look... if you are not going to inquire about
something, can I ask you to stop staring?
Castel: I understand this... form... is a bit distracting to
all you simple-minded mercenaries, but I am 
trying to do important research here.
Jude: *Munch*... 

I can give you the recipe book on the pasta.

No research needed.
Castel: Pasta...?! I...
Castel: I'll have you know I am just waiting for my 
ingredients to be ready.

I also require sustenance. Otherwise I may not be 
able to focus while I experiment.
Jude: Hmm...
Jude's usual disinterested gaze looked ever 
so slightly brighter at the words Castel used.
Castel: I am not talking about how to make food, you simpleton.
Castel: I refer to highly important research for maintaining
and preserving food for long periods of time.
Castel: We are talking about magic that can revolutionize 
the logistics of warfare!
Jude: Preserving food...? So... spices?
Jude: I can recommend salt. It preserves the food and
improves the taste.
Castel: Magic. MAGIC...! Not... simple salt!
Castel: Salt can be an expensive resource.
Castel: If I get this correct, even novice mages might be 
able to cast it.
Jude: Noted...  *Munch*...

What've you tried?
Castel: *Sigh*... I am not expecting a simple mercenary 
like you to understand.
Jude: *Munch*...

"Knowledge can come from the most unexpected 
of sources"
Castel: ...Isn't that from "Bartholomew, A theoretical view
into the advances of culture"?
Jude: *Munch*...
Castel: Was that not just a cooking book in disguise?
Jude: ...Perhaps.
Castel: I know you mercs are only good for fighting and eating.
Jude: *Sigh*...

Have it your way.
Jude's disinterested gaze returned, as he turned to
focus on his meal.
Castel: Now... if only I was able to cast things a bit
quicker...

I should be able to get the desired result, but 
nothing has worked so far...
As Castel mumbled out loud, the 
mercenary interjected.
Jude: Why bother praying between castings?
Castel: Because heirlooms are her blessings...?
Castel: Though... not praying to the goddess...
Castel: I have heard the hypothesis that that was the
difference between eastern and western magic.

But there has been no consistent results, from the 
few papers people have written...
Castel: Not that heretical propositions are often taken
seriously...
Castel: W- Wait a minute...!
Castel's hands slammed down onto the table.
Castel: I should not listen to some brute whose only 
purpose is to eat, sleep and fight!
Castel: Besides, that would be heretical! A sin!

Using the goddess's power without her approval 
would be blasphemous!
