passages.name: SP: BennetxLiebra C - Story
passages.content:
Bennett: ...
Bennett's eyes fluttered open at the light of dawn.
Bennett: Hmm...
But she just laid there in bewilderment.
Pup: You're awake?
Bennett: Probably. Hard to tell these days.
Pup: Uh... You seem pretty awake?
Bennett: That's the golden question, isn't it?
Pup: ...There was a question?
Bennett: Hey, you ever have weird dreams?
Bennett rolled up into a sitting position.
Pup: No.
Pup: Or... wait...
Pup: Argh... Doesn't everyone have weird dreams sometimes?
Bennett: Sure, but what if they just... stopped?
Pup: That'd be a good thing, right? If they're weird 
enough to call weird in the first place, then it'd 
mean...
Bennett: Yeah, it should be.
Pup: Right, then I'll just...
I grabbed the item I originally entered to 
acquire and made my way out, 
leaving Bennett alone again.
Bennett: Yeah, it should be a good thing.

...
Bennett: But... why do I keep seeing... that hallucination?
The camera panned over.
Liebra: ...
Liebra: ...
Bennett: I need some air.
Bennett pushed herself to her feet and exited the 
tent.
Liebra: Hmm...
Liebra: How amusing.
This went on for several weeks.
Each time Bennett saw Liebra, she rationalized it as 
a hallucination brought out by this or that.
It was only a matter of time before it drained away 
at her mental well-being.
Bennett: ...
Bennett: ...sleep...!
The night dragged on after a recent perceived
hallucination kept Bennett's heart racing.
Bennett: ...
But this didn't last forever, and eventually...
zzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzz.........
Liebra: Hmm...
Liebra: ...
Bennett wasn't sure who or what she was, and her 
head felt like it was about to burst apart at the 
seams.
The dark around swayed with the pain. It coursed
through her essence as she started to feel the 
world around once more.
And that pushed her eyes open once more.
Bennett: Five... more... minutes...
Liebra: Nostalgic, isn't it?
Bennett: Hm...?
Bennett: Ah...?!

This dream again?! I thought it had stopped?!
Liebra: And it had. Consider this a recreation.
Bennett: A... what? A recreation?
Liebra: Indeed. Much as we are.
Bennett: I...
Bennett: I think I lost the plot on that one. 
What do you mean?
Liebra: Alas, in this state we lack the connection we once 
did, so I cannot simply know your thoughts 
intuitively.
Is it safe to assume you have not explored the 
nature of our existence here?
Bennett: I mean... I was curious, but I've woken up in a 
strange world before.
Bennett: Really I've just been trying to stay alive and keep 
my wits about me.

While looking for Penny, Cal, Harper, and the rest, 
of course.
Liebra: Then shall I elucidate to you the nature of our 
beings here?
Bennett: ...

You're... being surprisingly open.
Liebra: You and I play no notable role in the story here, so
I've no reason to hold back.
Liebra: Though if that changes, I will certainly let you know.
Bennett: Yeah, that feels about right.
Bennett: Then, your explanation?
Liebra: As I said, we are recreations.

Bodies given thought and form from a basis of 
dormant memories.
Liebra: It appears that this is the basis of several magics
here in this time.

To draw upon the memories to give form and 
power to a machination of the caster.
Liebra: And this includes the summoning magic that 
created both of us.
Bennett: You make it sound... like we're not real.
Liebra: We are not.
Bennett: Hmm... I feel pretty real.
Liebra: As do I. To the point of incredulity.
Liebra: Even for the human lives I have lived, they were 
never in the form of my self image as a Will as this 
is.
Bennett: So... you really were walking around the camp as...
that?
Liebra: And I see you can imagine the intrigue I've had on 
the subject.
Liebra: The core thesis is, though, that we are indeed "not
real". Not the originals, at least.
Liebra: With memories picked from the soil itself, we are 
more akin to computers running old code.
Liebra: Our story is in a different place and time, seen to its
finale by our originals.
Bennett: This is... a lot to take in.
Liebra: In a sense, there's even no guarantee any of those
created by summoning were ever real in the first 
place.
After all, artificial memories are just as malleable as
our own.

Books, moving pictures, games... They very well 
could be sources for these summonings, as well, if 
the summoner stumbles upon it.
Bennett: And now we've got existential crises as a side dish.
Liebra: *Chuckles*...
Liebra: If it helps, I do think that doesn't apply to us, if
simply because we were both summoned 
independently of one another.
Liebra: And even moreso because the underlying nature of 
the world matches my understanding of it, still.
Bennett: Mmm... I should be more upset over this.
Bennett: *Sigh*... maybe I'm just dulled to the idea of not
feeling like my old self?
Bennett: Or maybe I'm just happy you're being open about 
it?
Liebra: Hmm... While I came to some conclusions via my
knowledge of the world, much of what I learned is 
what I learned while here.
Bennett: Yeah, yeah. And I was too busy just trying to stay
alive to figure it out.
Liebra: You were too busy worrying about others, like your
friends from our original struggle.
Liebra: As you often have.
Bennett: Hmm...
Bennett: So... does us being memories mean this is... the
future?
Liebra: Not necessarily.
Liebra: "Memories are timeless"
Liebra: It was a lesson often drilled into my head in a past
life.
Bennett: That's... quite a phrase. What does it even mean?
Liebra: It means that memories have a tendency to slip 
into different parts of history.
Liebra: In Aldania, there were professions designated as
"oracles".
Liebra: Their job was to connect with Daega that could 
give hints and prophecy of the future by way of 
their recollections.
Bennett: Uh... "Aldania"...? "Daega"...?

That's a lot proper nouns to dump onto me.
Liebra: Ah yes... I suppose you haven't gotten to that 
point.
Liebra: *Chuckle*... In due time, then.
Liebra: The ultimate point is that there is no guarantee of
where or when we are, relative to our experiences.
Liebra: It may well be the future. 
Or the distant past. 
Or "other".
Bennett: Like this could be just another "other world" like 
the expanse was?
Liebra: Hmm... I wonder.
The discussion ended up pausing at that point.
It was enough time for some more morbid 
thoughts to bubble up in Bennett's head.
Bennett: You know... with how you talk about it all... Does 
this mean we ended up dying, after all?

These memories would be... from like where we fell 
in the expanse?
Liebra: An easy enough theory to test.
Liebra: Bennett Morrison, what is the last thing you 
remember?
Bennett: Hmm... Good question.
Bennett: I think... we were headed off to try to rescue Mia 
and help the students at a school?
Bennett: Though it's all admittedly a bit... muddled, when I
think about it too hard.
Liebra: Then right before the beginning of the end...
Bennett: Wait, do you remember more?
Liebra: Yes.

My memories go well beyond.
Bennett: So what ended up happening?
Liebra: That I cannot say with certainty. My memories stop
before the grand finale.
Liebra: No need to fret, though. I can confirm it was
entertaining all the same to that point, as well.
Bennett: You know that's not the important part.
Liebra: I will admit, being denied the finale and closure of it
does leave a bitter taste in mouth.
Liebra: Though perhaps all the more reason to stay alive 
here and watch the Pup's journey to its end?
Bennett: I guess...
Bennett: ...it is sort of comforting to see that you're still
like this even now.
Liebra: Then what say you? Shall you join me?
Liebra: In this reprieve of an epilogue we've been granted,
shall we watch over the new protagonists in their
struggle until the last page?
Bennett: Well... I've honestly never thought about it like
that...
Bennett: ...
Bennett: Will you actually explain to me how all this crap
works, for once?
Bennett: If so, then... sure. At this point I think I'd be up
for that.
Liebra: Then, to "The End" of one more adventure...
Liebra: ...together.
Bennett: Yeah...

...together.

周圍的黑暗隨著疼痛而搖曳。它的路線

世界再一次。

貝內特：五…更多…分鐘…
Liebra：很懷舊，不是嗎？
貝內特：嗯……？

又做這個夢了？ ！我以為停了？ ！

貝內特：一個……什麼？

本內特: 大概吧。最近很難分辨。
小狗: 呃... 你看起來很清醒？
本內特: 這才是最關鍵的問題，不是嗎？
小狗: ...有問題嗎？
本內特: 嘿，你曾經做過奇怪的夢嗎？
本內特坐起身來。
小狗: 沒有。
小狗: 或者... 等等...
小狗: 呃... 難道不是每個人偶爾都會做奇怪的夢嗎？
本內特: 當然，但如果它們就... 停止了呢？
小狗: 那應該是件好事吧？如果它們夠奇怪，
一開始就被稱作奇怪，那就意味著...
本內特: 是啊，應該是這樣。
小狗: 對，那我先...
我拿走了我原本進來要拿的物品，
然後走了出去，再次留下本內特獨自一人。
本內特: 是啊，這應該是件好事。

...
本內特: 但是... 為什麼我一直看到... 那個幻覺？
鏡頭轉向。
莉布拉: ...
莉布拉: ...
本內特: 我需要呼吸一些空氣。
本內特撐起身子，走出了帳篷。
莉布拉: 嗯...
莉布拉: 真有趣。
場景指示> 淡入黑幕背景
場景指示> 等待 90 幀
這種情況持續了幾個星期。
每次本內特看到莉布拉，她都將其合理化為
由這個或那個引起的幻覺。
這只是時間問題，它會慢慢耗盡
她的精神健康。
場景指示> 等待 90 幀
場景指示> 淡入背景 營地內部 (傍晚)
場景指示> 非常緩慢地淡出音樂
場景指示> 等待 30 幀
本內特: ...
本內特: ...睡覺...！
在最近一次感知到的
幻覺讓本內特的心跳加速後，夜晚變得漫長。
本內特: ...
但這種情況並沒有永遠持續下去，最終...
zzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzz...

passages.name: SP: PupxCastel B - New Event
passages.content:
Pup: Uhh...?!
Norde: Keep your eyes forward. I'm your opponent today.
Pup: B- But...?!
Pup: Argh! Why?!
Norde: Have YOU met an enemy that would be merciful 
in this scenario? Focus.
Pup: B- But what if Castel comes to start another
experiment?
Norde: *Sigh*... Look... You were the one that asked me 
to help you train.
Pup: Honestly? It... gave me a good excuse to appear 
busy.
Norde: *Sigh*... Sir, why me...?
Castel: Pup!
Pup: Oh shi-
Castel: Pup, I have rerun some calculations from my initial
hypothesis, and I think that the next experiment 
will be more fruitful than the last.
Pup: Ehh... ahh... I am currently busy... sparring with...
Norde.
With a blade stabbing into the ground with a thud,
Norde's eyes trained themselves on me.
Norde: ...
Pup: ...Right?
Norde: ...
And I was on my back.

Norde had swiftly brought down a heavy
blow that I barely blocked.
Pup: O- Ow...
Castel: Hmm... a bruised body might yield an unexpected 
outcome in the experimental results.
Pup: So... we can... ow... do this another day, right?
Castel: Hmm... No, I don't think so.
Castel: There's an argument to be made that it can make the
Blue magic act faster and be more effective.
Castel: I may have to adjust some numbers, but...
Norde: Happy to help.
Norde raised the axe up to strike.
Pup: Oh fuck...!
Pup: Aghh~ That was close...!
The deliberate movements had made it more
predictable, so I was able to dodge.
Pup: You know... Castel...
I turned towards Castel as I got to my feet.
Pup: What makes you think this time it'll work?
Castel: I AM a professional, you know?
Castel: I started small and have built to this stage of the
experiment.
Pup: (Small to... large...)
Pup: (That brings some feelings of deja vu...)
Norde: Keep your eyes locked on your opponent, Anton.
Pup: ...?!
Norde: ...Huh?
Pup: B- But... what about last time...?! With the
shrinking... a- and the... b- butt stuff?!
Norde's swing had been dodged.
Castel: Research is a matter of progress. To fail last time
paves the path forward for this time to succeed.
Pup: How about the time when you did the opposite?

My back hurt due to the size of the melons 
attached to my chest!
Castel: It was a learning experience for both of us. 
Datasets must be thorough to prove effective for 
predictive experimentation.
Pup: How about the time you made my hair shorter?
Norde: Hm? I thought you couldn't cut it?
Castel: That is the issue we developed the experiment to 
deal with, indeed.
Pup: But it back grew out within a matter of days... and 
it left me starved and malnourished.
Castel: By that point, it was... within expectation. And
enlightening.
Castel: Using what we have learned from those 
experiments, I believe I have found the next step.
Pup: "Step" is different than "solution"...
Castel: Only time and test runs may tell us if they are one 
and the same here.
Pup: I- I... don't know...
Norde: *Sigh*... so this can offer... what? A greater 
control over this curse?
Castel: Indeed. Of all people you'd understand the desire.
Perhaps you'd like to act as a lab assistant in-
Norde: Don't... just don't...
Pup: ...
Pup: Fine...
Castel: Excellent. You know where I have my mobile lab 
setup, then?
Pup: Unfortunately...
Pup: You really do make the most of what you're given.
Castel: Thank you.
Castel: Though I imagine it looks more impressive than it
really is.
Pup: So... what's next?

Are you going to make my hair longer to see if my 
chest grows smaller?

Or maybe a tonic that shortens my hair, but makes 
my lips plumper?
Pup: Ah.... Wait... To note, don't take those as
suggestions...
Castel: Every new thought helps.
Castel: *Clears throat*... Anyways, the procedure should 
be simple this time so long as you have some
imagination.
Pup: Are you asking? Is this an insult?
Castel: An actual question. Experiments have shown that 
some people can't imagine things when someone 
tells them to.
For this specific experiment, it is important that you
know how to visualize within your mind's eye.

Can you?
Pup: Uh... yes? If you tell me to imagine a red apple...
I'll picture a red apple...
Castel: This technique comes from a certain cosmetic 
medical technique originating in Rabaneau.

It involved picturing yourself as something specific.
It will guide the magic to change you in that 
specific way.
Pup: So... if I think of myself as an apple, I will
transform into an apple!?
Castel: Hmm... If it makes you think more precisely, let's 
just assume it will.
Pup: Got it! ...so do not think of red, juicy apples...
Pup: Damn, shouldn't have eaten one just before training...
Castel: Focus, Baranov. I want you to picture yourself as a
man.
Pup: Well... am I?
Castel: If you wish control over this, then those remnants 
of your previous self image may be your best shot.
Pup: Argh... what do you want out of me?! All you're 
doing is stressing me out more with this all...!
Pup: But... I am a man?
Castel: Is that what you think?
Pup: Just because... I'm like... like...
Pup: I am me. I'm a guy inside. A man. No matter what
happens.
Castel: The emotional reaction seems a bit unnecessary... I
might have "struck a nerve".
Castel: Anyway, continue those thoughts. I will cast some
spells, and I will tell you when I am done.

So close your eyes. Picture yourself as a man.
Pup: (Think of all the stories we were told when we 
were young. Of heroes and legends...)

(Think of how strong and powerful they were. 
How able they were able to guide everyone to a 
better fate...)
Pup: (Think on... uh... how they're... uh... pretty buff?
Yeah. Strong guys with a manly chest.)

(Reminds me of that training I just did... and the
apples before...)

(Those apples... remind me my breasts...)

(They felt different from apples... The nipples on 
one hand... pretty hard to ignore... They rub on
EVERYTHING!)
Pup: (Wait...)
I realized my train of thought had gotten 
distracted. My idle, wandering thoughts had taken 
over just enough to...
Castel: Pup... Wake up...
Castel: ...How are you feeling? Any different...? You don't
physically seem different.
Pup: I feel... good?
I checked other parts of my body.
My breasts were the size they were before. My hair 
and rear were as well.
Everything in check. Everything normal for a girl.
Pup: ...
Pup: (Wait...)

I am a b- b-... girrrlll...!
Castel: Excuse me? Yes, you are a girl as it stands...?
Pup: Wait, no. Castel, you're misunderstanding. I am...
like... girl...!
Castel: Less like and more are. But yes. You are "like" a girl.
We are trying to control that process.
Castel: Has the spell messed with you mentally?
Pup: It totally, like, did! I can't get it out of my head!
It's like a tick or somethin'!
Pup: It's all like, getting harder to think that I was a
girl, I mean b- b- ...girl!
Pup: Please, like, do something!
Castel: Huh... What a perplexing side effect. I certainly
didn't anticipate this result...
Castel: You... were picturing yourself as a man?
Pup: Like, yeah! I was thinking of burly men, and then I
imagine my bouncing boobies...
Pup: ...and how, like, good they felt when they rubbed
against, like my bra, and my cute clothes...
Castel: So you ignored the instructions.
Pup: It's not, like, it was my fault or anything...
Castel: Well, it wasn't MY fault. This was supposed to be...

...
Castel: No... no... it was my fault... I did not account for
human error and the subject's incompatibility to
comprehend the task at hand.
Pup: I am now totally lost...
Castel: Lessons have been learned.
Castel: Perhaps this is reason to go back to the drawing 
board, though.
Pup: Wait... are we, like, done?
Castel: I am afraid so.
Pup: You can't, like, leave me like this! Everyone will
totally laugh at me!
Castel: I can't do anything at the current time.

There may be an option if you truly want to be a 
man. To control this curse...
Pup: I, like, totally want to!
Castel: ...
Pup: Like, j- just watch me!
I stormed off from the lab... angrily skipping.
Luckily enough, I returned to normal a couple days
after that.

passages.name: SP: Pup x Castel A - Begining
passages.content:
Castel: Hmm... All my past attempts have ended in 
failure...
Castel: What am I missing...?

Think, Castel. There is something you are missing...
Castel: I have eliminated the obvious and unconventional, 
so I guess the only thing left to try is...
Pup: Hmm...
I found myself deep in thought as I stood naked in
front of a mirror.
I was at a point where I had decided to give being 
a girl a sincere try, and my habits were shifting 
due to it.
Charlotte had slowly worn me down to take care 
of myself a bit more...

...from a feminine perspective.
I can't say I was a fan at first... but the results had
me intrigued.
Uncomfortable as bras could be, that sensation of
intrigue outpaced it.
Pup: ...
Pup: ...Bouncy...?
Castel: Mister and/or Miss Baranov, I found a new 
experiment that might help your predicament.
Pup: Argh...!
And so, Castel nonchalantly opened the door to 
the changing room, and I caught my breath.
Castel: Hmmm...? Unwarranted reaction, I feel.
Castel mentioned as much after a brief glance at 
both of our bodies.
Pup: Castel, how many times have I told you to knock 
on the door!?
Castel: 13 times, with this time, it would be 14.
Castel: Are you experimenting with something? It isn't as
though we aren't both female at this point.
Pup: What? No! Is just that... I am not a fan of... 
someone seeing my naked body...

Or at least, after the last time... Charlotte lectured
me... so... so much...
Castel: Noted.
Castel: Anyway, I have come to the realization about our
experiments so far-
Pup: Castel. Still naked.
Castel: I don't mind. For the experiments, I believe-
Pup: Out.
I shouted as I pushed Castel out the door with a 
hip check, due to my preoccupied hands.
*Slam*...!
Castel: ...
Shut out of the room, Castel touched his own 
breasts.
Castel: Hmm... So our shared situation isn't enough to 
allow that comfortability... 

I may need to look more into that later.
Pup: Hmm...

(If I go out right now... Castel might pull me aside
for more of those experiments...)
Pup: (What if I just... slip out the window...?)
Pup: Foundation, lipstick, powder, eye shadow...
Pup: Or was it powder, foundation, eyeshadow, 
lipstick...
Pup: *Sigh*... How do girls do this every day...?
Pup: (Actually, have I even ever seen Charlotte with all
this on...?)
Pup: (Might as well try something... Maybe the lipstick...?)
Castel: Mister and/or Miss Baranov! About the other day's
experiment...
Castel, as usual, surprised me while I was trying to
apply lipstick.
The surprise created a red line that perfectly
delineated my jaw.
Pup: ...

Castel. Knock.
Castel: Must we? Time is such a valuable resource...
Castel: Anyways. What I was trying to say the other day 
was about the experiments...
Castel: I found a way to transform us back to being males.
Pup: ...

(I... He... what...?)
I had to shake my head.
Pup: Castel... I'm a girl. A woman.
Castel: And I believe to have the key to control that.
Pup: Like talking to a brick wall.
Pup: Hmm...
I grabbed a powder puff from the makeup set.
Pup: Sorry, gotta run!
Castel: Ugh...!
Castel: ...
Castel looked at their powder face in the mirror.
His face, unusually white, looked more so like a
clown than a proper lady.
Castel: Such an enigma... Is it worth research itself? No, I
have this experiment to finish.
Castel never gave up. He kept trying and trying to
convince me into performing an experiment.
Castel: Mister and/or Miss Baranov. May I-
Pup: Castel! I'm bathing...!
Castel: One can multi-task...?!
At the most inopportune times...
Castel: Mister and/or Miss Baranov. May-
Pup: Biam Beabing (I am eating)!
Castel: That doesn't need to stop us. If we just have you
strip-
All I could do was run away at times...
Castel: Mister and/or Miss-
A sword narrowly missed Castel.
Pup: How do I not look busy...?!
Until one day when I was about to go to sleep...
Castel: Mister and/or Miss Baranov. You seem a bit more 
relaxed at this moment. Perhaps I can proceed with 
the experiment.
Pup: ...
Pup: *Sigh*... Guess I have to do this...
Castel: Truly? Excellent. I brought the equipment with me, 
so it will just be-
Pup: Not the experiment. I decided to be clear with 
you.

Castel...
I swiveled myself to face Castel sincerely and
directly.
Pup: I want to live as a woman.
Pup: Or... the best shot I can do at it.
Pup: A lot has happened. A lot I had no say in. I just...
Just give me this, okay?
Castel: Then... I am too late to fix my mistakes...?
Pup: Wait, no. It's not your fault.
Despite this, Castel began to mumble to himself.
Castel: ...failure...
Pup: (Was that... directed at me...?)
Pup: ...

I may not know how to act as a man or woman any 
more, but I am by no means a failure.

You have experimented with me like a guinea pig 
since I met you. My body has changed into things 
beyond my understanding.
I have given you try after try, and you call me a
failure!?
Castel: Heheh...
Pup: ...You're... You're laughing now?!
Castel: Miss Baranov... you fail to understand that you have
been my number one priority since I have joined 
your band of mercenaries.
Day in and out I have experimented with myself.

Formulated theories, read on research and applied 
my knowledge into simply executing experiments 
for you.
Castel: But I understand.
Castel: I understand I may come across as little more than 
an annoyance that comes up at the most 
inopportune times. 
A failure...
Castel: I suspect the depth of my effort does not come 
across to your perception.
We both sat there in silence.
Castel: Perhaps I should stop... perhaps I should leave all
together.

It is not like my lab won't accept me back with this
form... perhaps...
We both stood in front of one another, 
an exasperated smile forming on our lips.
Our bodies, shaped beyond recognition due 
extreme circumstances inflicted on our bodies.

For better and for worse, respectively for each.
Both our eyes had puffy black marks, indicating our
lack of sleep. It seemed that we were both tired.
Pup: That's... I didn't mean it like that...
Pup: Look... I'm sorry...

I've taken for granted how much effort you've put 
in for my sake.
Castel: I apologize, as well.

I allowed myself to become unprofessional.
Castel: If you feel comfortable in your current body... I will
stop asking you to perform experiments.

It isn't as though I've a lack of options to satiate 
my curiosity these days.
Castel relaxed further and started to stare off into
nothing.
Castel: I myself can only claim indifference to my form on 
my best days.

The feminine elements feel alien to me, and the 
non-human ones even more.
Castel: I thought, even through a brave face, you felt the
same.

That was the source of my insistence and drive.
Pup: I...
Pup: Yeah... It was scary.
Pup: The weight on my chest is still something I am 
getting used to.
Pup: But it was the change that was scary.
Not the end result, in the end.
Pup: For a time it seemed like that whenever I got used  
to them, they just got bigger again...
A silence fell onto us again.
Pup: Say... Castel...

If you are still open to experiments, I do have one
request.

I still want to keep trying to be a woman... but 
what if we find a way to control it?
Pup: I don't know how big my breasts are going to grow 
to, or if my mind and body will change any further.
Pup: So... what if that was the focus? And we drop the 
idea of me, at least, changing back.
Castel: Hmm... a refined control over a pure reversion?
Pup: I mean... assuming it's even an option on the table.

Is it? Is it possible?
Castel: Perhaps. Do not get your hopes up.
Castel: Then again, maybe your new mindset can work miracles in
this.
Castel: If there is one thing I've learned over our efforts...

...it is that the first step of making this line of 
research work... is the subject truly wanting it.
Pup: Maybe it'll work, then?
Castel: It might take a lot of tries... and a lot of time.
Pup: If you're like this for it, I'll gladly follow you in
that pursuit this time.

I am the one asking now, after all.
Castel: Well, then the first step is to schedule time for our
efforts.
Pup: I might be... a bit busy lately.
Pup: Oh, wait... I still need to eat most days.
Pup: Maybe over a meal?

...
Pup: ...Oh, wait... Uh...
Castel: It does sound apt to approach it as such. Less
miscommunication, for one.
Castel: And I feel as though I know one half of you extremely
well.
Castel: But... the other half? I can barely say I've scratched
the surface.
Pup: You know, this is actually starting to sound like... a
d- date...
Castel: I hadn't thought of that, but it does fit.
Castel: Hmm... It sounds nice, though.
Pup: After all this, it does feel like a nice change of
pace, at least.
Pup: Is "dating" a patient against your code of conduct 
or something, though?
Pup: Or... doing... "date like" things?
Castel: I suspect my current condition would be a bigger 
deal breaker than that should I return to the 
academy.
Castel: If anything, I wonder when you'll choose if your 
talk of a "date" is a joke or sincere.
Pup: I...
Pup: Uh...
Castel: One more thing to answer in our experiments, 
then?
Castel: And... one more reason for us to simply sit back 
and enjoy the scientific process.
Pup: ...
Pup: Hah...
Pup: *Sigh*...
Pup: Sure. "Scientific process" it is, then.

Castel: 你在實驗什麼嗎？ 現在又不是我們兩個都不是女性。
Pup: 什麼？ 沒有！ 只是... 我不太喜歡... 有人看到我裸體...

或者至少，上次之後... Charlotte 訓了我... 訓了... 好久...
Castel: 知道了。
Castel: 總之，我已經意識到我們目前為止的實驗-
Pup: Castel。 還沒穿衣服。
Castel: 我不介意。 為了實驗，我相信-
Pup: 出去。
我大喊著，因為我的手被佔用了，所以我用臀部撞擊把 Castel 推出了門外。
*砰*...！
Castel: ...
被關在門外，Castel 摸了摸自己的胸部。
Castel: 嗯... 所以我們共同的處境還不足以允許那種自在感...

我可能需要稍後更深入地研究一下。
Pup: 嗯...

(如果我現在出去... Castel 可能會把我拉到一邊做更多那種實驗...)

passages.name: SP: CharlottxJackson C - Story
passages.content:
*Thump*
The sound of scampering paws jolted back to me.
*Thump*
And the sound of paws, once more.
.........
Pup: Thanks, boy. I think I'm gonna go harder this time.
Pup: Grrrhhhaaaaa!!!
I threw a rubber ball. It was one of Jakson's few 
toys that he hadn't managed to destroy.

Yet.
He liked rope-like textures, but those didn't last
long. Dolls and other toys were destroyed in 
seconds.
..........
*Thump*
The ball landed further away than the previous 
tosses.
However, for Jakson, it was only a few more hops.
For me, it was way more effort than it often
seemed to be worth, but...
Pup: Good boy!
I patted him on the head.

Before I could throw it again, a knight in black 
armor called me for duty.
Norde: It's your turn on the training schedule now.

...
Norde: Make sure to wash your hands of Jakson's drool.
Pup: Jakson, I need to leave you for a bit. I'll come back
soon, okay, boy?
Jakson: *Agitated whining*...
Norde: Is something the matter?
Pup: Jakson seems to have a bit more energy than 
usual...
Out of the corner of my eye, a distinct outfit of 
white and blue caught my attention.
Pup: Charlotte!
Charlotte: Eh, what? Did something happen?
Pup: Can you play fetch with Jakson while I train?
Pup: He... has a bit more energy today than usual.
Charlotte: I guess?
Charlotte: I just have to throw the ball and wait for him to 
bring it back, right? I can do that.
Pup: Perfect! Thanks!
Dropping Jakson's ball into Charlotte's hand, I 
trotted off to join Norde for training.
Charlotte: Okay, so... this ball...
Charlotte: ...has a lot more drool than I thought... 
Can I clean this up first?
Charlotte grabbed a nearby cloth and carefully 
patted down the moisture.
Jakson: *Anticipatory stare*...
Charlotte: There we go. Now, then... fetch!
Charlotte launched the ball forward as far as she
could. After a short bit, Jakson returned the ball.
Charlotte: Hey, good boy. You...
Charlotte: Ah... How does it have even more drool now?
Charlotte: *Sigh*... Well, I'm not wasting more cleaning cloth 
for that lost cause.
Charlotte: But... I do have an idea...
Charlotte: Pup just asked me to tire you out, right?
She looked around before settling her eyes on a 
nearby tree.
She chucked the ball into the tree. The ball 
bounced on it, hit the ground, and returned to 
Charlotte's hand.
Jakson: *Confused whine* ...?
Charlotte: What's the matter, boy? Can't catch this?
Charlotte repeated the movement over and over 
again, taunting Jakson more and more.
Jakson looked at the ball, waiting for his chance to
strike.
Jakson: *Leans into hunting position*

...

.........

...!
Suddenly, before the ball could bounce on the 
floor, Jakson had caught it.
Charlotte: Good job!
Jakson strolled over to Charlotte, ball in mouth.
Jakson: *Drools*
Charlotte: Okay... now drop the ball...
Jakson: *Stares in 'No take, only throw'*
Charlotte: ...
Charlotte: *Sigh*...
Charlotte robotically lowered her arm to take it from
him, as if to detach herself from the act.
Charlotte: Eww... eww... eww...  *Sigh*... There it is.
With the ball in hand, Charlotte chucked the ball 
as hard as she could, almost like she was trying
to spin the drool off of it.
She returned to bouncing the ball on the tree 
while changing the rhythm to make it harder for 
the dog to catch.
Pup: Hmmmmmm...! Nothing like a good exercise to 
stretch the muscles.
Pup: Jakson! Where are you, boy?
Charlotte: Shhh! He is sleeping!
Besides Charlotte, lay a big sleeping beast.
Pup: (A once mighty beast tamed by a beau-)
Pup: (...by a maide-)

...

(...by Charlotte.)
Jakson just snored away, none the wiser.
Pup: He's that tired out? How'd you manage it?
Charlotte: Oh, just a few throws here and there. Nothing too
fancy.
Charlotte: Do you want me to teach you how to train your own dog?
Pup: Haha... funny. I'm good.
Pup: Come on, Jakson. Time to get going.
I poked and petted my dog until he woke up, and 
he walked towards my tent.
Charlotte: Eh, not a bad way to spend an afternoon.
Charlotte: Zzz...
Charlotte: .........
Charlotte: Zzz...
Charlotte: .........
Charlotte: ...GAH!
In the middle of the night, a heavy weight 
thumped itself down onto Charlotte's stomach.
Charlotte: ...I- Is this what night terrors feel like...?
Charlotte squirmed around to free her hand, and 
through that was able to get a feel of what had 
landed on her.
Whatever brown and furry lump had landed on her.
Charlotte: Wait... this feels like...
Charlotte: Jakson...!?
Jakson: *Yaaawwnnnnniiinngggg whine* ...
Charlotte: D- Don't look at me like it's my fault that you woke
up!
Charlotte: What am I supposed to...
Charlotte: *Sigh*... fine... I'll share my bed with you 
tonight... but just for tonight, ok?
*Shuffle*...  *Slide*...
Charlotte: Hmm...?
*Shuffle*...  *Slide*...
Charlotte: W- Wait...! At this rate, I'm gonna faaallll...!?
Charlotte: ...

Okay. That's it...
Pup: Eh... what?
Charlotte: Dog.
Pup: What does that...?
Charlotte: DOG.

Your dog was in my tent. 
Made me fall. 
Take him now.
Pup: *Yawwnnn*... Sure.
Pup: Jakson... come on in, buddy.
Jakson: *Midnight energetic pants*
Charlotte carefully folded up a recently cleaned 
and dried dress.
Charlotte: Okay, done. Now time to head back to-
With a basket of clothes in her hands, Charlotte 
peeked around it to see what had bumped into 
her.
Charlotte: Oh, hey there Jakson. What do you have here...?
Jakson had a white and blue striped piece of 
clothing hanging from his snout.
It seems to have been heavily sniffed...
...and licked.
Charlotte: ...Why...?

Why... Why slobber over it?!
Charlotte: Pup...!

...
Charlotte: PUUPPP...!!!!!
Charlotte: Take care of your... your... your horny dog!
Pup: My...? "Horndog"...?
Charlotte: Just do it!
Charlotte left stomping the ground.
Pup: "Horndog"...
Pup: Sort of has a fun ring to it.
I looked over to Jakson, who had a strip of cloth 
still on him.
Pup: Ah... Underwear again?
Jakson: *Looking away*...
Pup: You gotta stop doing that, bud.
Jakson: *Feigning ignorance whine*...
Charlotte: Finally... a moment of peace while I enjoy my food.
Charlotte: ...I know that sound...
As Charlotte looked to her left, a brown sack of fur
sat down, heavily drooling over Charlotte's food.
Charlotte: Do you somehow know that this is one of my 
favorite foods amongst what we actually can get 
here?
No, you can't have it.
Charlotte took her plate slowly... 
and slowly stood up.
Jakson slowly stood up as well, paying close 
attention to the leaving plate.
Charlotte: ...
And she ran! With the brown fuzzball in a sprint 
not far behind.
Charlotte: What makes you think I was going to give you a 
piece in the first place?!
Jakson: *Hopeful bark*...!
As Charlotte was running, she identified a familiar
location.
Charlotte: Wait, that's it!
Charlotte found herself right in front of the tree 
from when she played ball with Jakson before.
She remembered that the tree had a few climbable
branches.
Charlotte: I will... not... relent...!
With only one hand available, she balanced her food 
and climbed the tree at the same time.
*Snap*...  *Snap*... *Snap*...
A few branches snapped as Charlotte clumsily 
climbed up the tree.
Before Jakson could catch up, Charlotte was sitting 
on a sturdy branch, looking from above as...
Charlotte: What's the matter, boy? I see trees are still your
weakness.
Charlotte: *Munch*... *Munch*... *Munch*...

I have to say... food after some exercise does taste
better.
Jakson: *Whine*...*Whine*...
Charlotte: *Slow munch*...
Charlotte: *Sigh*... Fine... Here, have a piece.
Jakson: *Excited bark*!
Charlotte: Ahhhh~
Charlotte: It was pretty good in the end, right Jakson?
Jakson: *Agreeable bark*
Charlotte: Now I just have to...
Charlotte looked at the broken branches 
on the ground.
She was looking straight down.
Charlotte: ...
Charlotte: I- Is it me, or is the height suddenly feel more...
dangerous...
Charlotte: Hey... Jakson... if I jump down... would you catch 
me?
Jakson: .........

*Whine*...?
Jakson left.
Charlotte: ...

Jakson...?
Charlotte: Jakson, I shared my food with you, you coward!
Charlotte: I'm not even heavy!

...
Charlotte: Jakson, come back here!

.......
Charlotte: ...P- Pup...?
Charlotte: Anyone?!

Help!

HEEELLLPPPP!!!!!
passages.content_zh:
*重擊*
爪子亂跑的聲音又傳回我耳中。
*重擊*
又是爪子的聲音。
…………
小狗：謝謝，孩子。我想這次我會更加努力。
小狗：咕嚕哈哈哈！ ！ ！
我丟了一個橡皮球。這是傑克森為數不多的幾個之一
他沒能毀掉的玩具。

然而。
他喜歡繩索般的紋理，但這些並沒有持續多久
長。洋娃娃等玩具被毀
秒。
…………
*重擊*
球落地的距離比前一個球更遠
拋擲。
然而，對傑克森來說，也不過是多了幾跳而已。
對我來說，這比平常要付出更多的努力
似乎值得，但是…
小狗：好孩子！
我拍拍他的頭。

在我再次投擲之前，一位黑衣騎士
裝甲召喚我去執行任務。
Norde：現在輪到你來訂定訓練計畫了。

…
Norde：一定要把手上的傑克森的口水洗乾淨。
Pup：傑克森，我需要離開你一會兒。我會回來的
很快，好嗎，孩子？
傑克森：*激動的抱怨*...
諾德：有什麼事嗎？
小狗：傑克森似乎比其他人更有活力一點。 
平常...
從我眼角的餘光中，我看到了一套獨特的服裝
白色和藍色吸引了我的注意。
小狗：夏洛特！
夏洛特：呃，什麼？發生什麼事了嗎？
小狗：我訓練的時候你能和傑克森玩接球遊戲嗎？
Pup：他……今天比平常更精力充沛一點。
夏洛特：我猜？
夏綠蒂：我只需要把球丟出去，等他來
把它帶回來，對嗎？我能做到。
小狗：完美！謝謝！
將傑克森的球丟到夏洛特的手中，我
小跑去加入諾德接受訓練。
夏洛特：好吧，那麼……這個球……
夏綠蒂：……口水比我想像的多很多…
我可以先把這個清理乾淨嗎？
夏洛特抓起附近的一塊布，小心翼翼地
拍掉水分。
傑克森：*期待的凝視*...
夏洛特：我們走吧。現在，那麼……拿來！
夏洛特將球向前射出盡可能遠的距離
可以。過了一會兒，傑克森回傳球。
夏洛特：嘿，好孩子。你...
夏洛特：啊……怎麼現在口水更多了？
夏綠蒂：*嘆氣*...好吧，我不會浪費更多的清潔

passages.name: SP: NordexCastel B - New Event
passages.content:
Norde: Faster!
Norde sprinted around a corner, with Castel lagging 
behind.
Castel: I am... *pant*... going as fast... *pant*... as I... 
can...!
Castel: You.... You may recall... My feet are tiny and not 
well equipped for-
Castel slammed into Norde’s back.
Castel: Oof...!
Norde: So, that’s it then.
Norde was staring at a cobblestone wall. 

A dead end.
Castel: What an astute observation.
A gang of shadowy thieves rounded the corner.
Rioter: We’ve got you cornered now, curs. Prepare to die!
Castel: Tsk...
Norde: ...
Earlier that day...
Norde: The contact is a nekolyn merchant from the 
Outlands.
Castel: Fascinating. It seems my hypothesis was correct...
Norde: Pardon...?
Castel: I speculated that, given your status, you’d have 
developed connections to ensure you could
acquire whatever the Crows needed.
Norde: Hmph...

Be that as it may, it’s not an option I like to rely on.

This region isn’t exactly known for locals with... 
tolerant attitudes. Therefore this merchant is 
somewhat “underground”.
Norde: Since it’s going to be a stealth operation anyway, 
we may as well see how some of your theories on
persuading people hash out.
Castel: Hypotheses can rarely be tested without risk. 

I accept.
Norde: Then the meeting time is dusk. And
the meeting point...
Later that night...
The duo donned their hoods as a mob of unruly 
townspeople rushed past.
Norde: Act casual, and don’t make any sudden moves.
Part of the mob broke off from the larger group 
and started heading towards them.
Rioter: Where are you two going? Don’t you know there’s 
a hunt going on?

...And what’s with those hoods? Are ya hidin’ 
somethin’?
Norde: We’re just on our way home. My sister, she’s... 
very sick.
Castel: You see the sickness has, uh... ruined my 
appearance. I’m self conscious about it, and my 
sibling here is commiserating.
The rioter stared at them suspiciously for a few 
tense moments.

.........

A group of guards surged out of a nearby alleyway.
Constable: I hereby command all miscreants to disperse!

You’re disturbing the public order.
Rioter: What? We just started the hunt. Old Eowyn said 
she saw one doing something devious just a heavy
minute ago!
Constable: Well, if someone gets a lead more than runnin’ 
around like a chick with its head cut off, I’ll let ya
know.
Til then, stop keeping all the good citizens up with 
your noise.

The moon may as well drop on down on us if you 
keep up that ruckus.
Rioter: Ah... Tsk, fine!
The lead rioter started to disperse the group.
Castel: That would be our cue to leave, no?
Ducking into a nearby alleyway...
Norde: That was a smart move. Good job.
Castel: Thank you, but...

Let’s just get this over with before they regroup.
Norde knocked on an inconspicuous door on the 
side of a nearby building.

Cat styled ears poked out the door first, and a 
young male nekolyn stuck his head out.
Nekolyn: Oi, you two need to get out of here!
Norde: We won’t take too long. We just need to make 
the pickup I had...
Nekolyn: Are you blind? Can’t see you see they’re staking me 
out?
Castel: “They” being...?
Nekolyn: *Sigh*... just the usual miscreant lot.
Norde: I think we met the ones you’re talking about.
Norde: They seemed violent. Are you in any danger?
Nekolyn: It’s fine. This happens every now and again. Just 
gotta hunker down. 

Tis what happens when I forget my
hat before goin’ out for the day...

Anyways... I need to keep on the downlow, so 
shoo. And you two be safe, too.
The door slammed shut.
Castel: Well, then... That ended splendidly. What now?
Norde: Hmm...
Castel: New hypothesis: you’ve gotten us hopelessly lost.
Norde: Not helping. 

Don’t do something unnecessary to 
draw attention to-
Norde: ...hm?
Norde’s words stopped themselves.

..........

A soft sound could be heard in the silent night.
Castel: What is...?
Castel moved towards it.
Norde: Wait... it...
Castel turned the corner, to see...
Sad Girl: *Sniff*...
A young girl sobbing quietly in the 
corner of the alley.
Norde: Castel, we need to prioritize-
Norde: Huh...?
Castel: Excuse me, miss. But you appear to be in a state of 
great distress and I...
Sad Girl: Eek! A ghost, now?! Don’t hurt me!
Castel: I- I’m no ghost. I’m a shade. A shade...! See?
Castel's robe, which was meant to hide him,
floated towards the ground.
Sad Girl: W- Where did...?!
A slight bump arose from the robe, and it scattered 
along before exiting as... a rodent.
Sad Girl: *Sniff*... You’re... a rat...?
Castel’s form re-emerged and the robe burst up 
into the air.
Norde: Ah...?!
...and Norde went chasing after it as the winds 
above pushed it away.
Castel: Er... a “rodent” would be more taxonomically 
correct. But essentially, yes.
Sad Girl: Then... why... do you look like that?
Something blocked out Castel’s sight.
Norde: You dropped your robe...
Castel: Eh...?
Sad Girl: And why does your friend have scales... and funny 
ears?
Norde: Mmm...
Norde: I’m a dragon.
Sad Girl: A- A dragon...!?
Castel: One that scares away the bad guys...!
Castel: As... As the same with I.

I am a being of magic, sent by the Goddess to 
protect lost little girls in Zened’s blighted night.
Sad Girl: R- Really...? Daddy says there are a lot of bad 
people in the town.

Wicked creatures who want to poison and kill and 
kidnap and maim and-
Castel: I can assure you we mean to do none of that...!
Castel: Consider us a shield against those beings that have 
broke their oath to the Goddess.
Sad Girl: ...*Sniff*...

You seem... nice.
Norde: ...
Norde: Where do you and your ‘Daddy’ live? We’ll guide 
you home safely.
Sad Girl: I... *sniff*... I think we live...
The click of the door opening was paralleled by 
Norde and Castel disappearing around the corner.
Sad Girl: Where did they...?
The girl’s surprise was cut off by the jubilation of 
a fatherly figure seeing her.
Sad Girl: Heheh~ Daddy!

You wouldn’t believe what happened! The 
Goddess sent me a miracle!
Rioter: There they are...!
Rioter: Get ‘em! They tried to abduct a young girl!
Castel: No, we...
A small, growing mob started to encircle the two.
Castel: Ideas...?
Norde: Don’t get caught in the first place.
Castel: *Sigh*... And leave that little girl to her fate?
Norde: No, it was the right move.

Those with the power to act have an obligation to 
act when the vulnerable are within arm’s reach.
Castel: Hmph. I’ll accept that.
Rioter: Everyone, on three...
Norde: Then it'll come to-
Norde: ...

Wait, is that... horse hooves...?
Rioter: Three, two... one...!
Constable: HOLD!
The constable burst into the scene on horseback, 
flanked by some of the village guard.
Castel: Ah... That can’t be good.
Constable: Put down your weapons!
Rioter: Yeah! Put down that axe and let us kill ya’ proper!
Constable: ...

I wasn’t talking about them, you stonehead.
Rioter: Heh...?! But one’s a savage lizard thing! And she’s... 
a... uh...
Castel: A SHADE, you dolt!
Rioter: W- Why are you stoppin’ us, constable? What, are 
you gonna charge US with some crime?!
Constable: How about disturbing the peace? Violating curfew?

Even possession of contraband, based on some of 
the weapons I see here.
Rioter: I... But... Why would you...?
After a few meager attempts at protest and a 
stern gaze from the constable, the mob finally 
submitted to the guards.
The constable trotted his horse over to the duo 
once the situation was well in hand.
Constable: You two holding up? Not gonna keel over, are ya?
Norde: We are well, all things considered.
Norde: But... I did not expect help after how you talked 
about us before.
Constable: Hmph... Some of y’all beastie sorts killed my wife a 
few years back.

But...

*Sigh*... There’s probably a good one or two of 
ya. Doin’ what you did and all...
Castel: We’re happy to be of service, but what–
Just then their eyes settled on the horse’s other 
occupant.
Young Girl: Hi, ghost lady! And hello dragon too~!
Norde and Castel exchanged a look of incredulity.
Constable: “Those with the power to act have an obligation to 
act when the vulnerable are within arm’s reach.”

Heh...

It’s good that lot was rowdy enough to hear from a 
mile away.
Young Girl: Did I do good, daddy?
Constable: Yes, dear.

Now let’s get you to bed before you get yourself 
into any more trouble.
Norde: So... we’re free to go, then?
Constable: Well, I would arrest you, too...

But I have a feeling the jails are going to be awfully 
full tonight.
The constable mounted his horse and trotted 
away.
Castel: Well, that was unexpected.
Norde: To say the least. But I suppose it worked out in 
the end.
Norde: Speaking of which, I owe you an apology.
Castel: What for?
Norde: You were right. In the end, we changed 
someone’s heart... if only slightly.
Norde: I can’t remember the last time I saw even a scrap 
of that sort of progress.
Castel: A good academic never refuses credit.
Castel: However, it's obvious that luck played a big role in 
this outcome.
Norde: True, but luck only created the opportunity.

Your determination to see this through 
was what made it possible.
Castel: ...
Norde: Hrm?
Castel: You know, it's funny. I was so sure that logic held 
the ultimate power to change hearts.

But in the end it was merely...
Norde: ...humanity?
The two looked over their non-homlyn forms.

Their two “non-human” forms.
Castel: Hmph.

Indeed!
passages.content_zh:
諾德：更快！
Norde 急速繞過轉角，Castel 落後
後面。
Castel：我...*氣喘*...走得跟我一樣快...*氣喘*...
可以……！
Castel：你……你可能還記得……我的腳很小，但不
裝備精良，適合-
卡斯特猛地撞到了諾德的背上。
卡斯特爾：哎喲……！
諾德：那麼，就這樣吧。
諾德盯著鵝卵石牆。 

死胡同。
Castel：多麼敏銳的觀察。
一群陰暗的盜賊出現在轉角處。
Rioter：我們現在已經把你逼到牆角了，臭小子。準備好受死吧！
卡斯特：咳…
諾德：…
那天早些時候...
Norde：聯絡人是一名 nekolyn 商人，來自
外域。
卡斯特：令人著迷。看來我的猜測是正確的…
諾德：請原諒……？
Castel：我推測，以你的身份，你會
建立聯繫以確保您能夠
獲取烏鴉需要的一切。
諾德：哼…

無論如何，這不是我喜歡依賴的選擇。

這個地區並不為當地人所熟知...
寬容的態度。所以這個商家是
有點「地下」。
Norde：既然這無論如何都是秘密行動，
我們不妨看看你的一些理論是如何
說服人們討論。
Castel：假設很少能在沒有風險的情況下得到檢驗。 

我接受。
Norde：那麼見面時間就是黃昏。並且
集合點...
那天晚上晚些時候...
兩人戴上兜帽，就像一群不守規矩的暴徒
鎮民紛紛衝了過去。
Norde：表現得隨意，不要做出任何突然的舉動。
部分暴民脫離了更大的群體
並開始朝他們走去。
Rioter：你們兩個要去哪裡？難道你不知道有
狩獵正在進行嗎？

……那些兜帽是怎麼回事？你躲起來了嗎
東西’？
Norde：我們正在回家的路上。我的妹妹，她是…
病得很重。
Castel：你看，疾病已經，呃…毀了我的生活
外觀。我對此很自覺，而且我的
這裡的兄弟表示同情。
暴徒疑惑地看了他們幾眼
緊張的時刻。

…………

一群守衛從附近的小巷湧了出來。
警員：我在此命令所有雜項

passages.name: SP: KaraxElliot C - Story
passages.content:
Pup: Hey, Kara...!
Crow: Lady Kara...!
Norde: Can you...
Other Crow: Wait, have you...?!
Kara: ...
Kara: *Sigh*...
Voices bombard Kara, and all she could do was try
to parse each one as they spoke.
Pup: It's sort of important...
Norde: We'll be off schedule if we don't...
Kara: Hmm...
Kara: *Clears throat*... 

If everyone could allow me to speak?
Kara: One at a time.
Pup: Well-
Kara: Not one at a time in asking. 

I have already heard each. 

One at a time in my answers.
Kara patted down her wardrobe and took a quick, 
deep breath.
Kara: Pup, the sword from training was collected and
accounted for. Check the storeroom.

Norde, the order was handed off to the carrier 
already. You'll need to go after him on horseback.

And you two will need to fix the sharpening edge. 
New ones would be hard to come by out here.
Pup: I...
Norde: Hmm...
Kara: Now, now. Let's not stand around here while work is to
be done.
Norde: Right.
Pup: Yeah, I need to check that. Thanks!
The circle surrounding Kara had dispersed.
Kara: *Exhale*...
But one more set of footsteps signaled another
approach.
Elliot: Lady Kara.
Kara: Hm...?
Kara spun towards the voice.

Elliot was there to meet it, though the 
face across was unexpected.
Kara: May I help you?
Elliot: ...

I was wondering where the tea preparation 
materials were kept.
Kara: ...the... tea...?
Kara: *Sigh*... Of course.
Kara took a deep breath.
Kara: They are...
...and explained the storage arrangement to Elliot.
Elliot: Thank you. That will be invaluable info.

...
Elliot: Might... you wish to join me?
Kara: I appreciate the offer, but I am quite busy.
Elliot: The blend I got my hands on is quite exquisite. It is 
a luxury in the east.
Kara: ...
Kara: Perhaps I can make time for one cup, then?
Elliot: That's lovely to hear.
Elliot: So, how long have you and Mr. DeClares been engaged?
Kara: Oh, the better part of a year, I believe.
Elliot: Do you have a date for the wedding?
Kara: Hmph. If the man would show his face around me 
more often, that could be arranged.
Kara: For now, I'm happy enough to let us pursue our 
goals.
Kara: *Giggle*... Having my string around his finger to 
lead me back to him is enough... for now.
Elliot: You sound like you have an understanding of each 
other.
Kara: Hmm... I wonder, at times.
Kara placed her cup down and poured a second.
Kara: How has he been treating you?

You said that you are a squire assisting him in his
auditing duties?
Elliot: Yes, I'll often visit Vaults and other Covenant sites.

I help trim off the excess of his work, and we "split
the load", as Mr. DeClares often says.
Kara: Then you must have quite the stories.

What sort of locations has Cainan been to recently?
What was his side of the work?
Elliot: Has he not told you?
Kara: Many a times. But I imagine there are details he
forgot, didn't include, or hasn't gotten the chance 
to tell me.
Elliot: Well, he recently went south to...
Elliot described their work schedule in detail. Kara
listened in with a calm face, but focused ears.
Elliot: ...and then, we'd meet back in Oadthine when done.
Kara: Very interesting...
She sat there and took a sip of tea as she 
pondered.
As she did, Elliot started to feel awkward in the
silence.
Elliot: Hmm...
.........
Kara: ...
Kara: It is exquisite, I might add.
Elliot: Huh?
Kara: The tea. It is as luxurious as you boasted.
Elliot: Ah... that?
Elliot: It is a blend from the east after all. I make an effort
to have one of several high end brands on hand.
Kara: It has a familiar scent...

Is this a blend from Nodhan?
Elliot: Yes, it is...
Kara: As good as it is, I would not rate it above the
Republic's blend from Rasmus.
Kara: Many things from there do tend to outpace their
competitors from the Emerald Empire.
Elliot: It can be quite difficult to get a hold of... with the
Crusades disrupting trade in the east and all...
Elliot: So, I try to acquire some tea bags of this brand 
when the opportunity appears.
Elliot: But yes, I also prefer blends from outside the 
Emerald Empire.

Aureria's traditions in the space are to be lauded, as
an example.
Kara: You won't hear about Aurerian tea in the west 
very often. Are you just a connoisseur, or...?
Elliot: I was born in and grew up in Aureria, yes. My family
has ties to the Covenant leadership there.
Kara: Hmm...
Kara: Well, for your knowledge, I did as well.
Elliot: You did... what?
Kara: I was born in Aureria, like you. I spent a good 
chunk of my formative years in Aunrein, as well.
Kara: It may be considered relatively recent that I took up
residence in the Kingdom proper.
Elliot: Ah, then is that how you met Sir DeClares?
Kara: Something along those lines.
Kara set her tea cup down.
Kara: Curiosity taunts me, though, on what it is like there
now.

When I dwell on the thought, it often feels like it 
has been several lifetimes since I could return.
Elliot: It has been a the better part of a year for me, but
maybe I can satiate that curiosity?
Elliot: If you were there as a child...
Elliot: Did you ever hear of any tall tales and myths about 
the city?

Like about the statue of Reign?
Kara: Hmm... You mean the headless one, yes?
Elliot: The very one.
Elliot: When I studied in Aunrein, rumors about it seemed 
to swirl about the student body.
Elliot: I... may have not been thoroughly involved in those
social going-ons at the time...
Elliot: But I imagine I can recall details enough to compare 
it to your experience.
Kara: *Giggle*... Oh, it would not be wise to treat me 
as so old.
Elliot: Ah, I didn't... I figured you meant that you were
around it as a child.
Elliot: It likely would have been the better part of a 
decade that our attendance differed...
Kara: I can understand the approach, yes.

Some days it feels like it has been more like
a century or two since I've been there.
Kara: In this case... 

Your memories were plenty.

Thank you.
Elliot: You're welcome...
Kara returned to her cup of tea and stared into it 
as she enveloped herself in the fragrance.
Kara: Ah, to think they haven't tried to fix that statue,
yet.
Elliot: I don't believe they'd want to mimic the original
creator's work.
Kara: Or can't.
Kara smiled softly as she continued to stare into 
the tea.
Kara: It is a wonder what memories a scent can unlock.
Kara: It isn't even from Aureria proper, but it has that
nostalgic tinge that floods your mind with 
moments from the past.
Elliot: It's hard to disagree. It feels like it fills my mind
with reasons to return home.
Kara: To return to my birthplace... Hmmm...
Elliot: And... memories of reasons not to.

For me, at least...

I haven't exactly fulfilled my obligation to my family
yet...
A pause silenced the conversation.
Elliot: Sorry, I shouldn't have...
Kara: No, you are not alone.
Kara: "Reasons to not return"...

I'm not sure I could finish the list if I tried to
start it.
Elliot: Hmm...
Kara: But...

To need a "reason to not"...
...means there is a "reason to", no?
Kara raised the tea glass, and beckoned for 
Elliot to do the same.
Elliot: I...
Elliot: ...
And the fragrance reached both of them 
once more.
Elliot: ...
Kara: Good will never come without the bad.

For our time here, one of our duties is to 
appreciate the good, I think.
Kara took a sip.
Elliot: ...
Elliot followed suit.
Elliot: Indeed.

Even this tea came from past the lines of the 
Crusades, after all.

Something exquisite... in the depths of whatever 
murk surrounds it...

It is worth pursuing.
passages.content_zh:
小犬: 嘿，卡拉...！
烏鴉: 卡拉大人...！
諾德: 你可以...
另一隻烏鴉: 等等，你已經...？！
卡拉: ...
卡拉: *嘆氣*...
聲音如潮水般湧向卡拉，她只能盡力
理解他們所說的每一句話。
小犬: 這有點重要...
諾德: 如果我們不...就會延誤行程...
卡拉: 嗯...
卡拉: *清了清喉嚨*...

如果大家能讓我說話？
卡拉: 一次一個。
小犬: 嗯-
卡拉: 不是一次一個地提問。

我已經聽到了每一個問題。

一次一個地回答。
卡拉拍了拍她的服裝，深吸了一口氣。
卡拉: 小犬，訓練用的劍已經被收走並
記錄在案了。去儲藏室檢查。

諾德，訂單已經交給了運輸員
了。你需要騎馬去追他。

你們兩個需要修理磨刀邊緣。
在這裡很難找到新的。
小犬: 我...
諾德: 嗯...
卡拉: 好啦，好啦。別站在這裡閒聊了，工作還沒
做完呢。
諾德: 好的。
小犬: 是啊，我需要去檢查一下。謝謝！
圍繞著卡拉的圈子散開了。
卡拉: *呼氣*...
但另一組腳步聲預示著另一個人的
靠近。
艾略特: 卡拉大人。
卡拉: 嗯...？
卡拉轉身面向聲音。

艾略特在那裡迎接她，儘管
對面的面孔出乎意料。
卡拉: 我能幫你嗎？
艾略特: ...

我想知道茶葉準備
材料放在哪裡。
卡拉: ...茶...？
卡拉: *嘆氣*... 當然。
卡拉深吸了一口氣。
卡拉: 它們在...
...並向艾略特解釋了儲藏安排。
艾略特: 謝謝你。這將是非常寶貴的信息。

...
艾略特: 或許... 你願意和我一起品嚐嗎？
卡拉: 我很感謝你的邀請，但我很忙。
艾略特: 我弄到的這種混合茶非常精緻。 在東方是一種
奢侈品。
卡拉: ...
卡拉: 也許我可以抽出時間喝一杯，可以嗎？
艾略特: 很高興聽到你這麼說。
艾略特: 那麼，你和德克萊爾先生訂婚多久了？
卡拉: 哦，我想，差不多一年了吧。
艾略特: 你們有婚禮日期嗎？
卡拉: 哼。 如果那個人能多在我面前露面

passages.name: SP- JudexCastel B - New Event
passages.content:
*Slurp*... *slurp*...
Jude: ...*Gulp*
*Slurp*... *slurp*...
Cook: So...

How'd you like it?
Jude: Hmm... It's thick and juicy... and it's very messy...

It splurges everywhere...
Jude: But...

...a touch...

...more spicy.
Sitting in the dining tent, Jude was trying out new
recipes he shared with the cook.
One was an eastern method of preparing skewered 
meat using spices.
Cook: Are you sure about it? We are a bit low on 
the stuff we'd need to make it for everyone.
Jude: Hmm... That's troublesome.
Jude: Though, the forest surrounding us probably has 
some forageable spice bases.
Jude pulled out some weird plants from a pouch.
Jude: If you dry these up and grind them, you should 
have a better outcome.
Cook: Eh... So these ain't gonna kill ya if you eat 'em, are
they?
Jude: Fair question.
Jude slipped one of the weird plants from the 
pouch and put it directly into his mouth without 
hesitation.
Jude: *Munch munch*...
Cook: H- Hey...
Jude: Hmmm...
Jude: They should be safe.
Cook: Wait! What would have happened if they weren't 
safe!? You could've died!
Jude: Hm? We always used to- ...Right.
Jude's words drifted off as he realized the cook
wouldn't understand.
Jude: How to put it...?

Look. These plants are veiny, oily and often come 
in groups of twelve.

If you don't see these characteristics in these 
plants, they might be toxic. But if you look out for 
these, you will be safe.
Jude: And to be extra sure...
Jude picked up another and plopped it 
into his mouth.
Jude: *Munch munch*...

The toxic ones are bitter.
Cook: You don't say...?
The cook took one for himself and lightly cut off a
small piece.
Cook: You sure know a lot about plants.
Jude: Some. Spices, mainly. But...
Jude: Anyways, I'll finish the skewer and go back to-
Castel: Mercenary! There you are!
The tent entry curtain flapped around 
as Castel rushed through it.
Castel: I finally have time to do some live experimenting.
Castel: And with you being SOO eager to prove me wrong 
last time... I'd assume you'd be just as eager to 
now as well.
Jude: I gave suggestions, not 'proofs'...
Jude: *Sigh*... semantics...
Jude: Could it wait? I was in the middle of something.
Castel: No time to wait! Time, my time, is scarce and fleeting.
Castel started pulling Jude by the hand 
to their mobile lab.
Jude: ...?!
Jude passed through the tent flap, only to see one
final sight as the curtains moved about.
Cook: Isn't this...?
Jude: My... skewer...
Cook: ...*Munch munch* ...

Oh! Oh!! Spicy!!
Castel pulled Jude just outside a tent.
Jude: No tent?
Castel: Alas, we won't be here long enough to justify 
putting it all up before we leave.
Jude: 'kay.
Castel hurried around their makeshift setup, 
grabbing heirlooms and components alike.
Jude: So, have you figured out how to cast faster?
Castel: Ah, did you actually remember?
Castel: I started an extensive look into historical records on
the topic from around the world.

The old Emerald Empire seemed to have found a 
way to cast without an incantation.
Castel: What is required is a complex technique that 
requires a mental model of all the spells 
beforehand.
To enable casting them all sequentially 
and simultaneously.
Jude: Is that how they did it? Then you don't need me.
Jude turned, but Castel's hand reached out and 
grabbed him.
Castel: Oh, no, no, no! You are very important to the 
success of the experiment.
Castel: As you see, all of this is theoretical knowledge... 
but we are missing the practical component.
Jude: *Sigh*...
Jude: Couldn't you have done it with rats... or raw meat?
Castel: Oh, so NOW you are not so sure about this, are 
you?

You were so sure this was going to work, are you
feeling the hypothetical cold feet?
Castel: Unless you want to literally have cold feet.
Jude: ...
Jude: ...Fine.
Jude pulled his sleeve up, and left his hand exposed
for Castel's casted magic.
Castel: Heheh... Get ready.
Castel: I won't let anything happen...

Nothing that we couldn't fix with Blue Magic, at 
least.
Jude: 'kay.
Castel started casting a lengthy spell.
Castel: Oh goddess, may the light be true and guide our
purpose...
The area grew colder and the aura near Castel 
grew darker as their ghosty hair strands began to 
float in the air.
After a minute passed, Castel shouted the
incantation words.
Castel: Eucrasia! Rime!
Jude's hand began to grow a thin layer of ice...
Jude: ...
Castel: ...
...but his hand did not crumble into pieces like the
game meat did before.
Jude: Looks pretty frozen to me.

...

Done?
Castel: ...
Jude: ...

Will it wear off soon?
Castel: ...
Castel: W- Wait... you... it... did you set this up
beforehand?!
Jude: Sure, I had form fitting ice hidden up my sleeve.
*Thunk thunk*...!
Jude tapped his hand on a nearby table. The table
resonated as if it was tapped by a solid piece of 
rock.
Jude stared at Castel with a deadpan expression.
Castel: A... a false hand? Maybe it didn't splinter the skin
because it wasn't really a hand?
Jude: Have you not seen me wield a sword? My 
technique would not work with a prosthetic.
Castel: Maybe you... maybe you... maybe you are... naturally
immune to damage? Like a lineage deviation...?
Jude: Can homlyns do that?
Castel approached Jude and flicked their finger
on Jude's forehead.
Jude: Ow.
Castel: ...

Was that acting? That could've been acting.
Jude: Didn't I just say "ow"?
Suddenly, Jude grabbed his pinky finger...
And snapped it.
Separating it from the rest of the body.
Jude: See. Bone and blood. Frozen blood, but blood.
Castel: ...?!

ARE YOU ACTUALLY BRAIN DEAD!?

W- Why did you snap your own finger!? This goes 
against all laws of safe experimentation!
Castel: I am unsure if canceling the spell will even reattach
your own finger! What would you do if that is the 
case, eh!?
Jude: You did offer assurances it could be fixed with your
procedure.
Castel: Of course I did! I am not some brute!

I do my experiments in a safe environment! Of 
course, I experimented with rats beforehand!
Jude: So... you lied?
Castel: I mean... no... but yes...
Castel: Experimentation is an in-depth process that requires
careful design, consideration, and iteration...
Castel: I am not like some mercenaries... I do not chase truth
on a hunch!
Jude: If that's how you feel. I don't group myself with 
other mercenaries, though.
Castel: Yeah... you are the one to think with their 
stomach...

Otherwise, you wouldn't snap your finger.
Jude: It'll be fine.

So long as we reattach it properly with blue magic 
when this magic is fading.
Castel: Yes, of course we want to reattach the finger...
Jude: ...
Castel: ...
Jude: ...

...So how long does the spell last?
Castel: I used enough power to sustain it for about 1 hour.
Jude: Right...

So... "Time is fleeting"...
Castel: I- I said as much because I am inundated with work 
and research!
Jude: Then I'm stuck here for an hour.
Jude: Alright. Any food?
Castel: *Sigh*... I suppose I have my lunch that I could 
share.
Castel stepped to open a pack stored to the side.
Jude: Thank you. Anything else I can help with?
Castel: Hmmm... Something you can help me with...
Castel: I suppose there are a few topics I could use a 
second set of eyes on...
Castel: Just for the finishing touches, of course. Polish is
needed for thorough research.
Jude: By the way... Does this mean I win the bet?
Castel: Bet? 

Oh... no...
Jude: I've heard of some magic based, gourmet cooking
techniques from the Covenant.

A worthy research topic, I'd say.

*Munch*... After all, what is cooking, "if not the
science of art"?
Castel: ..."Bartholomew, A theoretical view into the 
advances of culture."
Jude: *Munch*...
Jude: ...
Castel: Damn Bartholomew... that fat bastard...!
passages.content_zh:
*咕嚕咕嚕*... *咕嚕咕嚕*...
裘德：…*咕嚕咕嚕*
*咕嚕咕嚕*... *咕嚕咕嚕*...
庫克：那麼…

你覺得怎麼樣？
裘德：嗯……又厚又多汁……而且很亂……

真是到處揮霍啊…
裘德：但是…

...觸碰...

……更辣。
裘德坐在餐廳帳篷裡嘗試新產品
他與廚師分享了食譜。
一種是東方的串燒方法
使用香料的肉。
庫克：你確定嗎？我們有點低
我們需要為每個人製作的東西。
裘德：嗯……這很麻煩。
裘德：不過，我們周圍的森林可能有
一些可採食的香料基底。
裘德從袋子裡拿出一些奇怪的植物。
裘德：如果你把它們曬乾並磨碎，你應該
有更好的結果。
庫克：呃...所以如果你吃了它們，這些不會殺死你，是的
他們？
裘德：公平的問題。
裘德從屋子裡偷走了一株奇怪的植物。 
直接放進嘴裡，不用
猶豫。
裘德：*咀嚼咀嚼*...
庫克：嘿——嘿…
裘德：嗯…
裘德：他們應該是安全的。
庫克：等等！如果他們不這樣做的話會發生什麼
安全！ ？你可能已經死了！
裘德：嗯？我們總是習慣-...對。
當裘德意識到廚師時，他的話漸漸消失了
不會明白。
裘德：怎麼說呢…？

看。這些植物有脈絡、油膩，經常出現
十二人一組。

如果您在這些中沒有看到這些特徵
植物，它們可能有毒。但如果你留意
這些，你就會安全。
裘德：而且更確定的是…
裘德拿起另一個，然後把它扔到地上
到他嘴裡。
裘德：*咀嚼咀嚼*...

有毒的是苦的。
庫克：你不是說…？
廚師自己拿了一個，輕輕切下了一個
小塊。
庫克：你對植物確實了解很多。
裘德：有一些。主要是香料。但是...
裘德：不管怎樣，我會把烤肉串吃完然後回去——
卡斯特：僱傭兵！你在那裡！
帳篷入口的布簾隨風飄動
當卡斯特爾衝過它時。
Castel：我終於有時間做一些現場實驗了。
Castel：你非常渴望證明我錯了
上次...我假設你

passages.name: SP- RowanxFlynnC - New Event
passages.content:
Rowan: Hmm...
Rowan had only just settled down to his assigned
laundry chore when a sharp voice broke the 
morning's silence.
Reagyn: ...I understand that you want to assist with the
chores. I simply implied that your time is better 
used elsewhere.
Reagyn: Besides, it isn't as though doing laundry will take all
day for those assigned to it. You should-
Charlotte: ...I get that you want to help. I do, too, at times.
Just... they're gonna be mad if I let you.
Charlotte: I can imagine your court's faces if they learned you
washed some mercenary's undergarments. They'd-
Rowan: Greetings, my fair robins. How serendipitous it shall
be to join me today.

It will surely make the time fly with so many hands.
Flynn: Hello Rowan, you're here too huh?
Reagyn: Prince Alexei, I did not expect you there.
Flynn took the opportunity to sit amongst the 
various Crows picking through the mountains of 
clothing.
Reagyn's gaze flickered between the two, now 
seated and working while she still stood.
Reagyn: *Sigh* ... Unfortunately, I will not be joining you all 
with the laundry today.
Reagyn: I have a previous commitment to assist with
restructuring camp logistics and situational
optimization.
Charlotte: ...Rowan.
Flynn took the opportunity to sit amongst the 
various Crows picking through the mountains of 
clothing.
Her gaze flickered between the two, 
now seated and working while she still stood.
Charlotte: Don't blame me if the Kingdom nobles get upset 
over this.
Rowan: We'd happily keep your own participation in this
endeavor a secret in turn~
Charlotte: ...No.
She turned on her heel and departed. Rowan 
watched her leave with a wistful smile.
Rowan: What a beautiful succulent rose~
Rowan: So proud and imperious her stem bedecked in 
thorns, but with blossoms so full of velvet promise.
Rowan paused to see the effect of his wordcraft 
upon his audience.
...but saw Flynn's hands over ears, with a face 
wincing in disgust.
Flynn: Could you not use words like... SUCCULENT... 
when talking about my TWIN sister...?
Flynn: Could you not use words like... SUCCULENT... 
when talking about our group's benefactor...?
This drew some crude chuckling from the present 
Crows.
Rowan: Ah Flynn, I can assure you I hold her in the highest
regard.
Rowan: It is with such regard that I feel compelled to speak
on the beauty that I see.
Flynn: I'm not hearing this. I'm not hearing this.
Rowan: Relax my friend.
Rowan: Alas, I'll say no more for now if it makes you
uncomfortable.
Rowan: But remember that it is in our natures to 
appreciate, and to be appreciated.

Beauty is in the eye of the beholder, and it 
behooves one to reciprocate with what one has 
beheld... so that beauty may grow.
Flynn: ...
Flynn: Does all that flowery poetry ever work on anyone?
Rowan looked around the laundry crew with a 
private smile.
Rowan: More than you know, my dear to-be-lord Flynn...
The two shared a light chuckle, but Rowan's 
expression shifted when a certain Crow 
approached with a bundle of clothes.
Lady Crow: Ah...
Rowan: ...
The sudden tension between them could be cut 
with a knife as she dropped her load and left 
without a word.
Rowan: And mayhap it backfires more than I would
hope...at times...
Flynn: Huh...? What was that about?
Rowan: Ah, yes. This discussion. A fun one.
Rowan leaned back, clearing his throat.
Rowan: She was led to believe that I invited her to sleep 
with me...
Flynn: Is that deserving of that reaction?
Rowan: ...immediately after she iterated her great love for
her husband.
Flynn: ...

Did you?
Rowan: I wouldn't dare.
Rowan: No, I remarked on the beauty of her openly 
expressed love... but she took it quite differently.
Rowan: She's been cold to me ever since, and drew a lance 
on me when I tried to explain the mistake.
Flynn: Haha...
The awkward laugh, shared with the Crows about,
underscored a contemplative thread of thoughts in
Flynn's head.
Flynn: Hmm...
With that the group got back to the task at hand,
working through the mountainous piles of the 
Nightless Crow's laundry.
The repetition of the laundry tasks was soothing to
Flynn's nerves.
The exact hope Flynn had for this task.
Calming enough that, when done, Flynn stepped 
into the circle of chatting Crows from the chore 
group.
Crow: ...and then they just left it there!
The group laughed as Flynn sat down 
near Rowan.
Flynn: ...
Rowan: Speaking which, Flynn my dear friend...
Flynn: Ah, wait. Me?
Rowan: Why is it that you let others nag you so flagrantly?
Rowan: Is it not clear to them that you chose this chore to
avoid that voice in your ear?
Crow: Yeah, who'd pick this crap? Harbin over there only
changes his undershit when we got laundry day!
The mercenary held up a random pair of 
underwear, implying it was the stated article, and 
the group broke out in laughter once more.
Flynn: Haha... Is it... that obvious?
Rowan: Yes, I believe you should simply state as much.
Rowan: "Your itinerary is insufficient for my mental health!"
Crow: Hm. Verily.
With a sarcastic scoff, the other Crows pushed 
along to another topic, leaving the two to talk to 
each other.
Flynn: That'd require me disagreeing with the 
expectations on me... and the needs they create.
Rowan's eyebrow raised.
Flynn: She tends to be good at everything she does...
including my training schedule.
Flynn: Even if I muck that up.
Flynn: I've always followed that sort of schedule.
Flynn: Only way I can actually get better is to actually do
those tasks.
Flynn began folding a uniform, punctuating the 
steps with frustrated words.
Flynn: Add to that, I'm still more experienced in some 
things than those in camp.

I... shouldn't mess things up... here, at least.
Rowan nodded sympathetically. Inspecting a 
soldier's gambeson for damage before hanging 
it to dry.
Flynn: If I can't handle the simple work of a camp, how 
will I be able to handle being the lord of the Coslett 
family territory?
Flynn: Balancing the log books, coordinating flood relief,
securing borders, settling trade disputes, or
calculating the harvest tax?
Flynn punctuated each duty with an 
aggressively folded cloth slapped into 
its appropriate pile.
Rowan: ...
Rowan caught himself before pointing out that 
there was unlikely to be a harvest in the Coslett 
lands this season.
Rowan: ...
Flynn: Nobility... it's a responsibility to the people you
serve. A weight.. a... a...

If I make a mistake then a lot of other people could
suffer because of it.

I know it can be hard to understand for a-
Flynn paused, a gear no longer spinning.
Rowan: Dearest fiery one? Are you alright?
Flynn: Wait... I'm remembering now... your real name is...
Alexei, right? As in Prince Alexei?
Rowan: Rowan is my birth name. Alexei is the name given 
to me as imperial prince.
Flynn: And a Prince is someone... who is a noble of an entire
country... and... and...
Flynn: Aaahhh.........

Of course you already understand what I'm
blathering om about...

How have I even screwed up laundry duty...?
Flynn turned beat red within a heartbeat, face 
buried in clothes and away from sight.
Flynn: AAaahhaaAAAHHhhhaaHHaAhHHaaAHhhh...
Rowan slid to sit next to Flynn and tried to use a
gentle pat to comfort Flynn.
Rowan: Think nothing of it. This is what I asked of you all
when you joined. "Treat Rowan as Rowan".
Rowan: I am Rowan. Alexei is a mask I must wear at times,
but...

Here in this camp I am me, and all the trials and
tribulations of Nolvanus are frozen to me.
Rowan reached for his instrument.
Rowan: Ah, perhaps a tune is in order to brighten the 
mood.

I know just the one! A little tavern song I picked 
up by the shores of Lake Lagos.
Flynn: ...aaaaaaaaaaaaa..........
Rowan: *Clears throat*...
Rowan: There once was a prince with a heavy brow~
Rowan: Who'd fret o'er the morrow and troubles enow~
Rowan: He'd count every shadow and measure each night~
Rowan: But never a joy would his heart take to flight~
The song had gathered the gazes of the 
Crows once more...

...with looks ranging from contentment to 
exasperation.
Rowan: Feeling any better?
Flynn: No, if anything I think I might be feeling worse.

Where did you say you learned that monstrosity of 
a tune?
Rowan: Why, from a sailor on the shores of Lake Lagos.
Flynn: Are you sure you're really a bard?

Maybe they were pulling your leg, or were stone 
drunk when they taught you? Haha...
Rowan: Everyone's a critic.
Rowan: Well, if the jigs of Lake Lagos are too exotic to lift
the mood of your delicate Cartenan tastes, then 
there's only one thing to do...
...continue playing until we find something enticing 
to your ears, ah ha!
There was a cheer from the Crows.
And with that, Rowan launched into a second tune.

Rowan才剛開始做他被分配到的洗衣工作，一個尖銳的聲音就打破了早晨的寧靜。

人多手雜，時間肯定會過得很快。

passages.name: SP- ElliotxCastel C - New Event
passages.content:
Elliot: ...
Elliot: Good.
Another arrow slammed into the bullseye of the
target.
Elliot: ...

Focus...

...just...one...more...!
Elliot drew the string back and was about to fire...
Elliot: ...?!
Elliot turned, as rustling came from a bush behind 
the range.
Elliot: Who's there? A spy? Come out with your hands up!
There was more rustling from the bush as the 
figure tried to dart away.
Elliot: I warned you...!
W- Wait, it's me!
Elliot: ...?
Elliot lowered the bow.
With a swoosh, Castel transfigured out of the bush.
Castel: D- Don't shoot again!
Elliot: ...
Elliot: Goddess forbid... My apologies. I didn't realize it was
you.
Elliot: Could've sworn I saw a...
Castel shuffled out of the bushes and over towards
Elliot.
Castel: Haha... think... nothing of it?
Castel: Objectively speaking, the error was mine. I 
shouldn't have been running around in the bushes 
like that.
Elliot: I take it that it is because you're a shade?
Castel: True, but... How did you know that? Or more 
importantly why are you asking?
Elliot: Well, a person couldn't hide in bushes like that.
Elliot walked over towards the archery 
practice target.
Elliot: Only a small creature could manage it. And then 
you just appeared out of nowhere...
Elliot pulled the arrow from the target on the tree.
Elliot: I had my suspicions when we first met, but I didn't
know for sure until just now.
Castel: Excellent, for you to understand the nature of it so
quickly.
Castel: It seems like so few people do, even after 
explaining several times.
Elliot: Hmm... But perhaps I shouldn't have jumped to
conclusions, still.
Elliot: It was very uncouth of me to almost shoot an 
innocent maiden like that.
Castel: ...maiden?
Castel: Ah, yes. This isn't my original body... I should
explain.
As they walked, Castel recounted how their body 
changed and what they had learned of this thus 
far.
Elliot: So, you weren't always a shade? And not only that, but
you are also the famous Castel Balreig?
Elliot: I had assumed the first name as a coincidence.
The two talked as they walked.
Castel: "Famous" might be a overstatement by
a scale of degree...
Elliot: It does make sense, though. Shades may take the 
form of people and creatures, but they aren't 
known to talk.
Elliot: Quite interesting, indeed.
Castel: 'Interesting' how, if I may ask?
Elliot: The Covenant archives never contained myths with
talking shades in them.

They were always nothing more than enemies for 
the heroes of old.
Castel: I've read the same stories.
Castel: But that means you were educated by the 
Covenant too then?
Elliot: Oh yes. Historical myths and legends were my 
primary field of study.
Castel: ...heh...
Elliot: Did I say something humorous?
Castel: Not quite.
Castel: It's just that it seems like we both have a great 
deal of things in common.
Elliot: I had read papers of yours during my time studying,
Professor, but...
Elliot: We have different fields of study, do we not?
Castel: The focus of my thought was more on how we 
both can swap forms. A unique trait amongst our 
group.
Elliot: ...
Elliot fidgeted with his heirloom.
Castel: I... did not offend, did I? Apologies, if so.
Castel: Trust me, I know how strange it can be to change so
dramatically.
Elliot: I am not intending to complain.

Not that I have a right to do so towards you, given 
I am not fully removed from my original state like 
you are, Professor.
Castel: Speaking of such, I had a thought...
As the two entered camp, Castel led Elliot 
to his own tent.
Castel: If we're sharing secrets, I was wondering if you 
might indulge me with the mechanism behind your 
own?
Elliot: Well...
Elliot: I conduct gray magic via my heirloom.

In my case, it was passed down from an ancestor in 
my noble lineage.
Elliot: The imprints of prayers my ancestor placed upon it 
give me form and skill beyond my normal aptitude.
Castel: Gray magic? I've never seen it in person before.
Castel: Does that mean your form is that of your ancestor's?
Castel: It is quite an... enchanting form. One to be proud of!
Elliot: Ah, well...
Elliot: To avoid... naming names... my ancestor was not a
woman. He was in my lineage of grandfathers...

The form I take is... a mystery to my family.
Castel: That... Hmm...
Castel: Ideas come to mind.

But as I go through them, I am reminded that the
research on the topic of gray magic is limited.

The time required to see the process through is 
generational in the literal sense after all... let 
alone the rarity of heirlooms capable of it...
Elliot: Yes, it has been... not without speculation inside 
and outside my family.
Castel: Such is the nature of people when we've gaps to 
our knowledge.
Castel: All the more reason to offer you my services, no?
Elliot: Services...?
Castel: Research of course, my dear maiden.
Elliot raised an eyebrow, and Castel sauntered over 
to a pile of books.
Castel: In my studies for Pup and myself, I've delved deep 
into the academics of each magic.
Castel: Between our disciplines, our academics minds can 
come together to form a sum greater than their 
parts, no?
Elliot: Is that why you brought me here? Hmm...
Elliot: I agree. This matter is worth getting to the bottom 
of.

And who knows? We may even be able to assist 
you as well.
Castel: Then to the investigation we shall tread.

Would you be willing to compare notes on this 
sometime? Say... over dinner?
Castel: In this band we oeprate, it will be nice to spend 
some time with a fellow person of learning.
Elliot met Castel's eyes and smiled.
Elliot: Yes, I think it will.
Castel approached Elliot, getting closer.
Elliot: Thank you, I feel like...
Elliot: ...I can finally relax. It has been some time.
Castel: Hm...? Oh...
Castel: *Sigh*...
With that, Castel stepped back, returning 
to his prior place.
Elliot: Did I say something wrong?
Castel: N- No... It is just...
Castel: It comes to mind that...
Castel: Yes, it comes to mind that I have a place to be now.
Elliot: Then let's plan on continuing the conversation in 
my tent sometime.
Castel: I assume you could... change to the ancestor form 
when that time comes?
Elliot: Sure, but... do you think it'll be needed?
Castel: I- It can be difficult to predict such things. Better
safe than sorry?
Elliot: Hmm... Yes, I suppose so.
The sentence led to a silence.
One that crept into an awkward silence.
Castel: *Clears throat*... I shouldn't dawdle.
Elliot: Actually, a moment? I had a question.
Castel stopped with the tent flap half opened.
Elliot: It really isn't anything of consequence, but...
Elliot: Might I ask what you were doing in the bushes before?
Castel: ...?!
A flash of heat rose in Castel, who silently gave
thanks for shades not having the biology to enable
blushing.
Castel: I- I was just... trying to find ways to spend more time
in the more natural form of a shade.
Castel: For... science.
Castel: Yes. Indeed. For science.

...
Castel: I- I really must not be late!
Elliot: ...

...that was strange?
Elliot: But, okay. I look forward to it.
Elliot stretched to his quiver.
Elliot: Now...
He twirled the arrow in his fingers.
Elliot: ...where were we?
