passages.name: SP- CharlottexReagyn C - New Event
passages.content:
Bandit: Look 'er. We found some loot on that ol' lady, we 
did.
Another Bandit: We sure did, boss. We just had to... persuade her 
a bit.
He held a knife, waving it about, as the two rushed
from their crime into the shadows of the alleyway.
Bandit: Nothing a good ol' show of force can't beat, right?
Another Bandit: You're right on that boss.
Echoing Voice: A... show of force, you say?
Bandit: Are ya deaf? A show of force, I said.
Another Bandit: Yeah, a show of force he sa-

Gwahh...!
From the cover of the night, a hulking cluster of 
metal showed itself and quietly rushed the bandit 
into the dark of unconsciousness.
Then, as quickly as it appeared, it dipped into 
another shadow cast by the moon.
Bandit: Heh..?! Where did...

...

Show er'self, I say!

Ya with da police? What about the deal we 
struck?!
*Clink*... 

...*clink ... 

......*clink*......
.........
Slowly, the cluster of metal revealed itself to be a
person in plated armor, glistening with the light of
the moon.
Bandit: You er'... you er' the Armored Bandit, you er'...

You er' a bandit... just like us, you er'!
Bandit: GHAAA...!

Ya... knocked me out... ya did...
The glistening armored unit punched the bandit 
in his gut hard enough to knock him out for 
several hours.
And with that, it turned its head to the scene.
The armored unit took the stolen goods and put 
the sack over its shoulder.
Tatiana: I am not like you.

You stole from an old innocent woman to give to
yourself.

While I steal from corrupt nobles and their lackies to
give to the normal folk.
*Knock Knock*
The door opened.
Old Lady: Huh...?
She saw a sight illuminated by the candlelight from
within her home, and it showed a coin purse on 
her front porch.
Old Lady: This... purse...? I thought the bandits had taken it.
Tatiana: There we go...
She stretched out as she allowed herself to relax.
Tatiana: Mmm... Ah~

That should take care of those bandits. Hopefully, 
they never steal again.
Tatiana: Another win goes to THE Armored Bandit!
Elliot: Are you proud of yourself?
Appearing from around a corner, Elliot had 
ambushed Tatiana.
She stepped back in unease, for once cursed by 
the shadows instead of blessed.
Tatiana: ...Pretty much, yeah.
Elliot: Do you think you could do better?
Tatiana: Yeah, maybe I could've punched them both in one 
motion. Not like they were strong.
Elliot: That isn't... quite what I meant.
Elliot: You have powers, powers that can be used for 
good, and yet you use them recklessly.
Tatiana: Heh? Are you saying I should've let them steal from 
an old lady?
Elliot: No. More that... sneaking around and ambushing 
them... is uncouth.

Rather than relying on scare tactics, you should 
fight your enemies head on.
Tatiana: ...
Tatiana: *Sigh*...
Tatiana started walking past Elliot.
Tatiana: Very funny.

Lettin' people see my face and identity defeats 
a lot of the purpose of the Armored Bandit.
Elliot: I am not saying that you reveal your identity. I am
just saying to fight honestly.
Tatiana continued, and Elliot followed along as they
exited the area.
Elliot: You lurk in the shadows, yet you wear a gallant suit 
of armor.

The clanking of the armor would make it pretty 
obvious to anyone with competent skills of 
detection.
Would it not be better place yourself as example? 
In a setting all can see and learn from? Like a duel.
Tatiana: *Sigh*... where do I even start?
Elliot: But you could be... like a knight. An "Armored 
Knight", like the heroes from myths and legends of 
old.
Tatiana: First of all, 'Armored Knight' doesn't have the same
zing as Armored Bandit.
Tatiana: Second, it's not like I chose to be the "Armored
Bandit". They named me that way because of how 
I act.
The corrupt nobles were too proud of themselves 
to admit they were defeated by some random 
person they never heard of before.
But because I sneaked and ambushed them, they 
named me the Armored Bandit. I never chose that 
name.
Elliot: You still have the opportunity to be more than 
that. An example for people to see and strive 
towards.
Tatiana: Yeah, well, I'm here to help. Not play games and 
duel shit.
Tatiana: You underestimate how easy they make it when 
you're hidden. Add to that the fear factor from the 
legend, and it's easy pickings.
Tatiana: The frightful face of those snub bastards makes the 
job all the sweeter.
Elliot: Would it hurt to simply try, though?
Tatiana: Ya think I haven't tried a direct approach before?

Even without the fact that they can call
reinforcements, it can make things worse.
She looked back at Elliot, who seemed doubtful of 
her conclusion.
Tatiana: ...

It was... a small-time noble closing an orphanage
because the building was "too ugly".
Tatiana: I thought I taught him a lesson, but he was back at
harassing the orphanage a day later.
Tatiana: This shit doesn't work on noble blood unless you
actually strike fear into their hearts, ya know?
Elliot: ...
Tatiana: Besides, what's the problem with all this?

Isn't it good enough that the "Armored Bandit" is
helping people?

Why does it have to be in the middle of the day, or
honor-y and the like?
Elliot: ...
Elliot: Heroes are meant to inspire hope, not fear.

I... used to listen to stories about how the 
Armored Bandit would come and take me away if I 
didn't behave.
Tatiana: Heh, so you're one of them.

What, you scared of me or somethin'?
Elliot: My concern is that you just validate them.

You strike fear into the hearts of your victims... but
you also strike fear into the hearts of those you 
want to help.
Tatiana: Hmm...
Tatiana: BOO!
.........
Elliot: ...

As I was saying...
Elliot: Conserving hope is a very fragile endeavor.
Tatiana: Tsk. Common folk love the Armored Bandit, I'll have 
you know.
Elliot: For a time, perhaps.

The nobility is the original source for much of
culture. It trickles down, as it were.

With your actions, it is fertile soil to drive that
belief amongst even common folk.

If, for nobles, you are an uncouth evil thief, so will
the general opinion be in time.
Tatiana: I am NOT a dirty evil thief.
Elliot: I am not saying you are... but...
Tatiana: Tsk... Look. If you are not going to offer any REAL
solutions, then I'm not going to hear it.

Fighting in broad daylight would not be as effective,
and way more dangerous.

'Til that changes, just keep your own fears of the 
dark and the boogeymen to yourself.
Tatiana turned on her heel, and she walked away.
As she disappeared into a tent, Elliot was left
standing there.
Elliot: ...
Elliot stood still, breathing calmly.
Elliot: I am not afraid... 

...anymore.
passages.content_zh:
強盜：瞧瞧。我們在那老太太身上發現了一些戰利品
做到了。
另一個強盜：我們確實做到了，老闆。我們只需要...說服她
一點。
他拿著一把刀，揮舞著，兩人衝了上去。
從他們的犯罪行為中走入小巷的陰影之中。
強盜：沒有什麼是武力展示所無法擊敗的，對吧？
另一個強盜：你說得對。
迴響：你是說…展示武力？
強盜：你聾了嗎？展示武​​力，我說。
另一個強盜：是的，他展示了武力——

嘎嘎……！
從夜色的掩護中，一簇巨大的
金屬現身，悄悄衝向強盜
進入無意識的黑暗。
然後，隨著它的出現，它很快就陷入了
月亮投下的另一個陰影。
強盜：誒……？ ！哪裡...

…

展示一下自己吧，我說！

你和警察在一起嗎？我們的交易怎麼樣
被擊中了？ ！
*叮噹*...

....叮噹...

....*叮噹*......
…………
慢慢地，金屬簇顯露出來，它是一個
身披盔甲的人，閃爍著光芒
月亮。
強盜：你呃……你呃鐵甲強盜，你呃……

你呃是強盜……就像我們一樣，你呃！
強盜：啊啊啊……！

是的...把我擊倒了...是的...
閃閃發光的裝甲部隊猛擊強盜
在他的內心深處足以把他擊倒
幾個小時。
說完，它就轉頭看向了現場。
裝甲部隊拿走贓物並放置
麻袋扛在肩上。
塔蒂亞娜：我和你不一樣。

你偷了一個無辜的老婦人的東西給她
你自己。

當我從腐敗的貴族和他們的走狗那裡偷竊
送給普通老百姓。
*敲敲門*
門開了。
老太太：啊……？
她看到燭光照亮的景象
在她家裡，上面顯示了一個零錢包
她的前廊。
老太太：這個……錢包……？我以為強盜已經把它拿走了。
塔蒂亞娜：我們開始了…
她伸了個懶腰，讓自己放鬆。
塔蒂亞娜：嗯……啊~

應該可以解決那些強盜。希望，
他們再也不會偷東西了。
塔蒂亞娜：裝甲強盜又贏了！
艾爾

passages.name: SP- CharlottexReagyn C - New Event
passages.content:
Charlotte: *Clears throat*...
Charlotte: ...and for that reason, I believe that getting 
supplies from the northern town rather than the 
southern town would help our prospects more.
Charlotte paced back and forth as she spoke.
Charlotte: Hmm...
Charlotte: Well, that didn't come out so bad.
Charlotte: Maybe one more time, since no one else is here, yet...
Charlotte spoke in a low volume while moving,
presenting to an imaginary crowd.
She had arrived a bit earlier to the meeting place in
order to practice a bit.
Charlotte: Hm?
Reagyn: Ah! Apologies, I was told that the meeting was 
going to be at a later time.
Charlotte: It... is...?
Reagyn: Oh...
Reagyn: *Clears throat*...  
Apologies. I thought I was late. I...
assumed I'd be the first here.
Charlotte: Ah yeah, I'm just here practicing my oration a bit. 
Can only ever find the time in between stuff 
nowadays.
Reagyn took a seat, took out a bundle of notes, 
and starting to scan over them.
Charlotte: ...
Charlotte: So... how've you been handling it here?
Charlotte: I know from experience that there's a learning 
curve for working with mercenaries.
Reagyn: ...
Reagyn did a double take, looked at Charlotte, then 
at her notes, and then at Charlotte again.
Reagyn: Oh, ah... you were talking to me?
Reagyn: Hmm... it has been... workable, I guess.
Reagyn returned to her notes immediately after.
Charlotte: ...
Charlotte: So... the weather... always colder than you would
imagine, am I right?
Charlotte: I never get to wear what I want.
Without looking away from her notes, 
Reagyn responded.
Reagyn: I would recommend wearing an additional layer.
The echoes of the gentle breeze from outside 
filled the room once again.
Charlotte: ...

I guess... 

Mind if I just keep practicing?
Reagyn: It would give me time to go over the notes I prepared,
so that would be good. Please don't mind me.
Charlotte: *Clears throat*...
Charlotte: Yadda yadda, introductions, introductions...
Charlotte: As you all know, about 75% of our budget is going
towards weapon repair-
Reagyn: Closer to 78%.
Charlotte: ...I was rounding.
Reagyn: Understood.
Charlotte: ...

About 78% of our budget is going toward weapon 
repairs. However, we only manage to procure 50% 
of the material we need from-
Reagyn: Around 46%.
Charlotte: ...

...We only manage to procure ABOUT 46% of the
materials we need...
Charlotte paused and waited for a correction 
that never came.
Charlotte: ...from the enemies defeated. Therefore we need to get
some iron from nearby-
Reagyn: Plus coal.
Charlotte: Reagyn. You were reading your notes, weren't you?
Reagyn: It's no problem. I can multi-task to help with your
presentation.
Charlotte: ...but not help with anything fun...
Charlotte said in a low voice.
Reagyn: Hm? Did you say something?
Charlotte: Oh nothing. Just... 'thanks for the help'.
Reagyn: No need to worry, I'll make sure to not neglect my 
own notes review for the meeting.
Reagyn: Please don't mind it and continue.
Reagyn: I think you were about to talk about going to a 
nearby mining town.
Charlotte: ...Right.
Norde: ...Good, some people are actually on time.
Charlotte sighed in relief at the sight of another
person.
Charlotte: Oh, thank the goddess...
Norde: Has Pup come by?
Charlotte: No? Are we waiting on that?
Norde: Hmm... Can you give me the cost rundown as we wait?
Charlotte: Sure, I don't mind.
Charlotte gave Norde the rundown, which then 
turned into an actual meeting after a certain person 
did not show up.
Not naming who.
Reagyn paid close attention to what Charlotte was
saying, often referring to her notes before 
switching her attention back to Charlotte.
Norde and Reagyn asked a couple of questions at 
the end, to which Charlotte responded confidently.
Afterward, Norde and the rest of the Crows stood 
up and left, leaving only Reagyn and Charlotte, who 
were cleaning up.
Reagyn: Miss Charlotte... may I speak with you for a moment?
Charlotte: Sure, Reagyn, what's up?
Reagyn: I just wanted to congratulate you on the 
presentation, it was succinct and to the point.
Charlotte: Aw, thanks.
Charlotte: I made it so because a certain someone tends to 
doze off if the meeting is too long.

It took me a while to figure it out, so I'm glad you
think it went smoothly.
Reagyn: I did have... a few points of feedback, if you're open
to it.
Charlotte: Uh... I guess?
Charlotte: Lay 'em on me.

I'm sure my plans aren't perfectly refined, after all.
Reagyn: Thank you.
With the folder lowered, Reagyn looked Charlotte 
in the eyes.
Reagyn: First, the village you posed a trade with wants a
resource we lack an abundance of.
Charlotte: I figured we could shore up that supply by 
bartering as we move.

We have the advantage of not being in one place, 
after all.
Reagyn: That wasn't mentioned in the presentation. But
understood. I assume it was for brevity.
Charlotte: Something like that.
Reagyn: There was also the issue of the local village being 
out of the way and through more rough terrain.

That's a cost of both time and general resources.
Charlotte: Well, I assumed...
Reagyn: Assumptions can be fatal to an army, Miss Charlotte.
Charlotte stood there for a second, silent.
Charlotte: Uh... wait. You're acting like there's some crazy
assumption in there.
Charlotte: It's a forageable, too. If we forage as we move, 
then our supply is greater than a village's demand.
Reagyn: A valid point.
Reagyn: But... It'd be hard to imagine the troops agreeing 
to such given recent developments and the current 
mood.
Might it be a bit demeaning to be asked to 
forage each day as they move?
Charlotte: They're mercenaries, they already-
Reagyn: I think it is possible though, if someone can 
convince them. I can make an attempt.
Charlotte: Sure, you do that. Go talk to the... mercenary
"troops"...
Charlotte turned, exiting the tent.
Reagyn: Second...
Charlotte: Wonderful, you had more.
Reagyn: I recall some expedition research that concluded 
local coal deposits were low quality here.
Charlotte: Weren't you the one that brought up coal in 
the first place?
Reagyn: I just offered the info that it was in low supply, not
a specific suggestion on how to acquire it.
Charlotte: Well, then we can use green magic to refine it.
Reagyn: Isn't substance refinement a very intricate process 
for magi?

Will the magic users here have the patience for 
that? They're not nobles, but mercenaries.
Charlotte: Won't know until you try.
Reagyn: A bit speculative, but I suppose we can put a pin in
it.

Thirdly-
Charlotte: Hey.
Charlotte stopped walking and turned to Reagyn.
Charlotte: You know, if I didn't know better, I'd say you were
trying to insult me.
Charlotte: Do I know better?
Reagyn: I... What? Why would I ever do that? Lockhart is a
valued ally of the Kingdom, and you are of a 
respected station there.
Charlotte: ...

You know it's getting really hard to tell if you're
being condescending or not.
Reagyn: No, is this not the norm for a lady in your place?

Lockhart is known for being business first, so-
Charlotte: Eh? Are you insulting my people now?
Reagyn: I-
Reagyn: ...

Apologies, that was not my intent. I harbor no ill-
intent in my reference to Lockhart.
Reagyn: I... simply saw the need to correct some 
fundamental mistakes. For your position and 
responsibilities-
Charlotte: Okay, that's it-
Pup: H- Hey! Sorry that I'm late.
Pup: I was training, then ate before coming...

Then I felt sleepy, and...
Pup: Hm...?
Charlotte: ...
Reagyn: ...
Pup: Oh, sorry, Charlotte...
Pup: I didn't realize you were in the middle of one of 
your passionate, captivating speeches.
Charlotte: ...

Hmph.
Charlotte bumped into me a little as she stormed 
out of the area and into another tent.
Pup: Was I... Was I THAT late?
Reagyn: *Sigh*...

I only meant that her position like required many
advisers that did the same as I did.
Reagyn started to step in the opposite direction 
that Charlotte went.
Reagyn: Yes, yes you were THAT late.
And left.
Pup: I... Damn.
Pup: I always liked Charlotte's speeches.
passages.content_zh:
Charlotte: *清了清喉嚨*...
Charlotte: ...因此，我認為從北部城鎮而非南部城鎮獲取
補給，更有助於我們的發展前景。
夏洛特邊說邊來回踱步。
Charlotte: 嗯...
Charlotte: 喔，聽起來還不賴。
Charlotte: 或許可以再來一次，反正現在還沒有其他人...
夏洛特壓低音量，一邊走動一邊說話，
彷彿在向想像中的人群演講。
她提早抵達了會議地點，
以便稍微練習一下。
Charlotte: 嗯？
Reagyn: 啊！抱歉，我被告知會議會晚一點開始。
Charlotte: 是...嗎？
Reagyn: 喔...
Reagyn: *清了清喉嚨*...
抱歉。我以為我遲到了。我...
以為我會是第一個到的。
Charlotte: 啊，對啊，我只是在這裡練習一下我的演講技巧。
現在只能在零碎時間裡找時間練習了。
Reagyn坐下，拿出一疊筆記，
開始瀏覽。
Charlotte: ...
Charlotte: 所以...妳在這裡還習慣嗎？
Charlotte: 我根據經驗知道，和傭兵合作需要一個學習
曲線。
Reagyn: ...
Reagyn愣了一下，看了看夏洛特，然後
看了看她的筆記，又看了看夏洛特。
Reagyn: 喔，啊...妳是在跟我說話嗎？
Reagyn: 嗯...還算...可以應付，我想。
Reagyn立刻又回到她的筆記上。
Charlotte: ...
Charlotte: 所以...這裡的天氣...總是比妳想像的
還要冷，對吧？
Charlotte: 我永遠都不能穿我想穿的衣服。
Reagyn沒有抬頭看，
直接回應。
Reagyn: 我建議多穿一件。
從外面吹來的微風迴盪在
房間裡。
Charlotte: ...

我想...

我繼續練習，妳不介意吧？
Reagyn: 這樣我就可以有時間複習我準備的筆記，
所以這樣很好。請別在意我。
Charlotte: *清了清喉嚨*...
Charlotte: 嘰哩呱啦，介紹，介紹...
Charlotte: 如各位所知，我們預算的75%左右是...

passages.name: SP- ElliotxTatiana B - New Event
passages.content:
Tatiana: ...

Why am I paired up with you?
Elliot: I would say 'By the Goddess's will'.... 
but... Norde made the list.
Tatiana: Did you do something to piss Norde or the Goddess 
off?
Elliot: ...

Perhaps that is a question better pressed in 
your direction.
Tatiana: Oi. I was the one to ask.
Shopkeep: *Clears throat*

... 

Ehh... is that everything you are
going to get?
Elliot: Apologies for my associate. I do not believe she
intended to scare you.
Tatiana: Oi. You started it. You were too picky when 
choosing the vegetables.
Elliot: *Sigh*... Yes. That will be everything.
Shopkeep: Well... it's going to be...
A hefty price was uttered out of the shopkeeper's
mouth.
Elliot: That seems... a bit much for just a bunch of
vegetables.
Elliot: If it was because of my companion. She is sorry.
Tatiana: Oi.
Shopkeep: Oh! No no no... it's actually because of...
The shopkeeper lowered her voice and pulled in 
Elliot and Tatiana a bit.
Shopkeep: The local lord increased the taxes... again... making
breaking even harsher and harsher.
Elliot: The lord must be putting it to good use, right? Or
maybe the land was struck by a natural disaster
recently?
Shopkeep: Nah, not any famine or natural disasters. I can't say
I've seen any new public works projects start 
either. Just more and more taxes.
Don't know a soul that isn't struggling to get by
despite this having been a well off town since I was 
a lass.
Tatiana: Hmph. Sounds like typical noble behavior to me.
Elliot: Hmm...
As the two paid and then walked away from the 
stall, they glanced at one another.
Tatiana: ...
Elliot: ...
The two turned their backs to each other, 
parting ways.
Noble: 12001, 12002, 12003, 12004...

...and 12005 gold pieces from those poor and dirty
peasants.
Noble: Ugh... I really must wash my hands, though. Who 
knows what blight the poor put on these coins 
before relenting them...
Maids! Maids! Come here and wash my hands!
Soon after, a group of maids appeared from behind 
a very decorated door.
The leader of the maids carried a small sun-shaped
necklace around her neck.
The maids began to wash the hands of their lord.
All the while, the noble ogled his money, waiting 
for it to be cleansed of the "poverty odor" so he 
could, once again, caress it with all his attention.
Head Maid: ...S- Sir...

One of the goddess's teachings says...

"Those who only seek the shine of the coin, shall 
lose the light of the sun, cursed to live in the 
moon's shadow."
Noble: Pft! You suggest this coin is not mine to do as I 
wish?

I demand it because I have need of it. I deserve it.
He relaxed back in his chair.
Noble: Why, I would lose sleep without them! How would 
I be able to afford my wine? Or luxurious clothes?

How can an economy run without the money 
flowing to the providers, after all?

It would be a humanitarian crisis, as well! Are you
saying I should die of thirst!?

Or how about my horses, cows, and exotic birds? 
Would you rather I kill the animals?!
The head maid, with a shocked expression, took a 
step back and was at a loss for words
Noble: The alternative would be... Ugh... The poor do not 
make use of the coin.

I must make the world turn, woman.
Head Maid: I am just offering the teaching of the Goddess for 
your soul's salvation.

But I see you will have a wonderful time in this life.

Now... if you excuse me, sir. We will take our leave.
The maids funneled into the same candlelit 
hallway that they came from.
*Thump*
*Thump*
Noble: Hm? What were those sounds?
As the noble opened the door to his estate, two of 
his guards laid flat on the floor, unconscious.
Noble: There is no time for a nap. Wake up!
The noble tapped the guards with his feet, but 
they did not respond.
Noble: N- Now is not... Come on... I told you to wake up!
The noble's tap became a kick, but the guards 
still did not wake up.
With the moon shining over the patio, a lone figure
stood opposite to the noble.
The armored figure reflecting the light of the-
Noble: Guards! Guards! We are under attack!
The noble ran away from the door and shouted 
into his enormously wealthy mansion...
But all he could hear were the echoes of his 
shouts.
Noble: G- Guards...?
The deeper he went into his mansion, the more 
eerily quiet and darker it felt.
Noble: M- Maids...!?
The hallways that were normally adorned with
candlelight were dark and devoid of life.
Noble: Anyone...?
From the corner of his eyes, the noble could see a
long-haired, blonde woman, whose hair reflected 
the moonlight that shone through the window.
Noble: Wait can you tell me-
But as soon as the noble approached her, 
she vanished.
Noble: W- What is happening?!
The noble continued to walk through his mansion,
looking for any sign of light.
It was then that he saw a maid running into a lit 
room and closed the door immediately after.
Noble: Open up! It is your lord!
A sliding peephole smaller door opened within the
smaller door.
Head Maid: I am afraid we cannot do that, sir.

You have been tainted by the shadow of the 
moon. Of Zened!

Your avarice has cursed your domain and if we 
don't act, we will too shall suffer the 
consequences!
Noble: Shadow of the moon!? What sort of nonsense are 
you spouting?
Head Maid: I tried to warn you, sir! Your incessant seek for
wealth at the cost of others has doomed your oath 
to the Goddess!
She raised her hand, showing an intricately sun-
decorated lit candle aggressively pointing at the 
noble 
And waiving it as if trying to scare a wild animal.
Head Maid: May the light of the sun purify you!
Noble: Open up, or I will kick the door down. Myself!
With those words, she slammed the sliding smaller 
door shut, in the noble's nose.
Noble: W- When all of this is d- done, you are all f- fired
and-
The noble continued walking in his 
empty dead mansion.
Whatever life he could find were unconscious 
guards, or maids held up in a room with candles.
Noble: ...Maybe... if I lit a candle... I'll be safe... right?
With a flick of a match, the noble rose the lit candle
upwards.
Noble: See! I am not cursed by Zened!
*Swoosh*
???: Those who only seek the shine of the coin shall 
lose the light of the sun, cursed to live in the 
moon's shadow.
A feminine but stern voice echoed through the 
empty mansion, ringing the noble's ears 
multiple times.
???: Monsters shall look to kill you to steal your gold.
People, whom you trust, will backstab you.

You shall forever live in fear, as long as you seek 
the light of the coin.
Noble: B- But... what can I do!? Is it too late to change?
..........
The voice did not answer.
Tatiana was waiting outside, looking on with a 
menacing expression.
Still bothered by their previous interactions, Elliot's
words echoed in her mind about trying to be more
gallant-like.
Tatiana: I took care of all the guards. I can go for the noble
when he tries to flee.
Surely enough, the noble exited his mansion with a 
sack full of gold and valuables.
As Tatiana was preparing her speech, the noble 
dropped all his money to the ground in front of 
Tatiana.
Noble: I am sorry! Please don't curse me by the shadow of 
the moon! I can change!
The noble desperately crawled towards her as 
though seeking HER help.
Tatiana: The shadow... of the... what?
Noble: Here! Have all the gold I have accumulated! Surely 
this will make the Goddess forgive me!
Tatiana: Uhh... sure... and...  *Clears throat* ...
Tatiana: I hope you have learned your lesson foul doer... 
err... Don't ever be greedy again, or I will come 
back!
Noble: I have learned my lesson! Please, give me the light 
of the sun back!
Tatiana: The light of the...? 

Err... give away the money to the needy before 
the sunrise and your curse will disappear...?
Noble: I will do so! Thank you so much for a second 
chance!
Tatiana: That was... easier than expected.
Elliot: Agreed.
Elliot: Without the guards and with your imposing 
armored figure, the legend felt way more impactful.
Elliot stepped from the shadows of the mansion.
Tatiana: Legend...? Wait, you had a hand in all of this?
Elliot: It seems we struck at the same time.

I used the teachings of the Goddess, about how 
evil doers' light, like candle lights, get snuffed out 
due to Zened's, the moon's, influence.
Elliot raised an arrow along with a bow.
Elliot: I sneaked in and snuffed out all the candles.

Every time the noble tried to light a candle, I just
fired an arrow and snuffed it out from a distance.
Tatiana: Sneaking around? Didn't you tell me not to do 
that?
Elliot: Well... I tried do... something else instead. 

At first, at least.
Elliot: Bless the maids, but they did not pick up on my 
plan.
Tatiana: Hmph. So you used my approach.
Elliot: It was more a patchwork of my own intent
and your approach, in a sense. 

And it... may have worked better than I even 
anticipated my original plan to.
Tatiana: Haha...
Tatiana: Ah... well...
Tatiana: I guess just standing in front of the enemy can also 
be intimidating in its own right.
Tatiana: Especially if you got a heroic reputation like you 
keep gawking about.
The two turned towards each other.
.........
Elliot: ...
Tatiana: ...
passages.content_zh:
Tatiana: ...

我怎麼會跟你湊成一對？
Elliot: 我會說『這是女神的旨意』....
但是... 名單是諾德做的。
Tatiana: 你是不是做了什麼惹諾德或女神
不高興的事？
Elliot: ...

或許這個問題更適合問
妳。
Tatiana: 喂。是我先問的。
店主: *清了清喉嚨*

...

呃... 這些就是你
們要買的全部東西了嗎？
Elliot: 為我的同伴道歉。我不認為她
有意嚇到妳。
Tatiana: 喂。是你先開始的。你挑選
蔬菜的時候太挑剔了。
Elliot: *嘆氣*... 是的。這些就是全部了。
店主: 嗯... 總共是...
店主口中說出了一個
高昂的價格。
Elliot: 這價格... 對於只是一些

Elliot: 如果是因為我的同伴的關係。她很抱歉。

店主: 哦！不不不... 實際上是因為...
店主壓低了聲音，把
Elliot和Tatiana拉近了一些。
店主: 當地的領主增加了稅收... 又... 使得

Elliot: 領主一定會好好利用這些錢的，對吧？ 或者

passages.name: SP-Atticus x Tatiana C - New Event
passages.content:
Crow: *Pant*...  *pant*...
Atticus: Come now, is that all? I can see why I was asked to
help conduct combat training.
Crow: *Pant*... Knew you were some kinda old 
legend but...

I thought time would have made you easier to take 
on.
The Nightless Crow, nursing his wrist, leaned over 
to pick up his disarmed blade.
Another Crow: All that rock really doesn't slow you down at all?
Atticus: Best never to judge from appearances. That goes 
for everyday life and on the battlefield.
As he said so, he sheathed his own weapon.
Atticus: Hmm... Now. how about you lot train amongst
yourselves for a bit?

Think about your loss here and reflect on how 
to improve through that training.
Atticus: As this was a pair exercise. I suggest each of you 
perform reps until you've got it down to instinct.
Crow: R- Right.
All the Crows stood up straighter than before, 
like they were struck with a sense of authority 
they weren't used to.
Another Crow: Hey, you want to pair with me?
Crow: Oh thank the Goddess. That'd be easier than the 
old guy.
Another Crow: Pft. We'll see about that.
Atticus: Haha...
The Crows all started to pair up to work on the 
lessons Atticus had left with them.
Seeing enough 'defeat' in their eyes to motivate 
them, Atticus stepped aside.
With a slow and controlled motion, he sat down to 
watch over the group. 

He moved as though one could feel a creaking 
sensation with each inch he lowered.
As he did, he noticed someone watching him out 
of the corner of his eye.
Tatiana: Hmm...
Tatiana tilted her head as she saw to the 
maintenance of her own gear, looking on as 
Atticus lifted his stone arm towards his lap.
Her motion stopped for a second, but after a 
moment of consideration, she turned towards him.
Tatiana: ...Hey, mind if I join you?
With a creak, Atticus turned his head towards the
einlyn youth.
Atticus: Why, hello young miss.

Yes, it'd be no trouble to talk.
Tatiana nodded and causally made her way over.
Atticus: It was... Tatiana, correct? You've made a name for
yourself around the camp, from what I've heard.
Tatiana: Good. Means I don't need to introduce myself 
then, and saves us both some time!
She stepped across Atticus's vision and took
a seat on a nearby stump.
Tatiana: Kinda surprised about the whole...
She motioned towards Atticus's stone body.
Tatiana: Thought that was just part of the stories to claim 
how tough you were.

Not that... you actually were made of the stuff.
Atticus: A mix of both, I'd imagine.

Most tales about me pre-date this.
He let out a dry chuckle.
......
A silence set in, with Tatiana sneaking looks at
Atticus, as though she wanted to say something.
Tatiana: So... Those nobles and Covenant folk...

They pay you well, yeah?

Like... enough to make working with them as 
somethin' you can swallow?
Atticus: You may want to be more specific on your 
meaning.

I'm afraid you're catching this old man off-guard.
Tatiana: Oh, come on, you know what I mean.

You've dealt with them directly. How they treat 
non-homlyns and anyone without a golden pacifier.
Atticus: Hmm... if you must know. Yes, they pay well.

Enough so that it'd have been irresponsible for me 
to not have taken this position.
Tatiana: Okay, so it WAS a matter of money.

Guess that would make sense, at least. Lots of 
people have their price, after all.
Atticus: Hmm...
Atticus slowly raised up a finger.
Atticus: No care for the "why"? Why it would have been
"irresponsible" to not have taken the job?
Atticus: Though... thinking entirely in terms of coin...?
That would indeed be a very 'noble' perspective.
Tatiana: I... was getting to that.
Tatiana: Y- You'd think an old timer like you would've 
learned some patience.
Atticus: Haha...
Atticus looked on at Tatiana with a considerate and
warm smile.
Atticus: By all means, then.
Tatiana opened her mouth, about to talk but 
clearly caught off guard.
Tatiana: As... As I was going to say.

I can only assume the money was for something so
important you couldn't turn down the nobles' 
offer?
She looked away, with her face clearly annoyed 
and trying to hide her fluster.
Tatiana: Don't need to treat me like...
She mumbled beyond Atticus's hearing.
But she kept one eye open with it peeking towards
Atticus as though she tried to hold her tongue on
saying anything more.
Atticus: Right you are.
Atticus: There is rarely a point in life when all paths before
you are appealing in every aspect.
He reached down with his good arm, feeling and
fidgeting with his stone one opposite of it.
His gaze had lost its focus on Tatiana.
Atticus: One makes choices not for himself.

...
Atticus: A father makes choices not for himself.
His head raised, turning once more to 
the einlyn youth.
Atticus: A father makes choices for his family's chance to
flourish.
Tatiana: I... well...
Tatiana: ...I see what you mean.
Atticus: To be clear. I am proud of each decision I made.
Tatiana: ...
A silence lingered for a time.
Tatiana: I guess I can at the very least understand someone 
that can do that.
Atticus: I'm of the mind that we all will eventually face
choices like that.

I imagine you will in due time... or even already 
have perhaps.
Atticus pushed himself up. His movement was stiff 
as he pulled his right side along with the rest of 
him.
On his two feet, he stretched a little.
Atticus: With that, I must return to my duties.
Atticus: The mercenaries look like they've been getting a 
handle on that exercise I provided.
Atticus: ...
Atticus: Unless you had something more for me?
Tatiana: Ah, well...

Nah. No.

I wouldn't want to keep you here.

If anything I should get going myself.
Tatiana got to her feet as well, scuttling to the 
other side of the stump seat to keep her distance.
Atticus: Hmm...
Atticus: Don't be afraid to have a chat with this old soldier.
Atticus: I'm always willing to make a little time.
The two parted on slightly awkward terms.
Each to their own tasks.
Tatiana made her way to a different part 
of the camp.
Tatiana: Tsk, guy really went there.

Thought I'd get something out of that...

But...
Tatiana: *Sigh*... So that's why.

Family, eh?

...
Tatiana: Yeah, I guess everyone has their price. 
In one way or another.
With the training Crows...
Crow: What'd she want?
Atticus: That Tatiana girl?
Crow: Yeah. She's not the sort I'd think would talk to
someone hired by the Covenant.
Atticus: You think so?

Hmm... You know... It reminds me of my how my 
own children were at a point.
Atticus: I think... she's still working it out.
Crow: Working what out?
Atticus: What she wanted to ask me.

passages.name: SP-PupxJakson B - New Event
passages.content:
Pup: ...
Jakson: ...
Pup: ...
Jakson: ...
Pup: ...
Jakson: ...
Pup: ...!
I blinked.
Jakson: *Happy bark*!
Pup: Dammit...
I blinked rapidly.
My eyes stung from the staring contest.
Pup: Fine. Take the bedding. It's not like I haven't slept
on the ground before.
Jakson: *Happy bark*!
Norde: A messenger just came by.

They said that the bedding purchase was 
delivered successfully.
Pup: Perfect timing, Norde.
Norde: Mm... It isn't as though I can control when the
messenger arrives.
Norde: Of what i can control, though... I am surprised by 
the need for more bedding.
Norde: I could have sworn that the recent supply refresh
purchased enough to suit our current numbers...
Pup: Ah... well...
I looked over at Jakson while trying to not let 
Norde notice.
Pup: (He never counts Jakson in those, since he's a dog.)
Pup: Mistakes like that are bound to happen every once 
in a while, yeah?
Norde: ...
Norde: Regardless, the bedding needs to be picked up 
from the nearby town.
Pup: It's not here?
Norde: Like said, we simply received the delivery message.
Norde: It was delivered to the store, since we were 
passing this town on our way to our next 
destination.
So...
Norde: It's in your hands now.
With raised hands, I watched on as Norde made a 
bit of a exaggerated "cleaning my hands of this" 
motion.
...and as he walked away with his job done.
Pup: Tsk.
Pup: (Why not just send the bedding instead of a 
messenger?)
Jakson: *Confused whine*...?
Pup: Looks like we've got a mission to complete before 
the day's out.
Jakson: *Eager bark*!
After trekking to the nearby town, 
we had procured the admittedly 
mediocre sleeping cot.
Shopkeep: I know we don't have those normally in stock, 
but... you sure you want a cheap one like that?
Pup: It's okay. It's easy to carry and not too expensive 
to replace if we need to ditch it.
Shopkeep: ...

Should I ask?
Pup: Don't worry about it.
Tying it up like a backpack, I lifted it up.
And with that, we started on our way back to camp.
Pup: There we go. Let's head back, boy.
Jakson: *Happy pant*
Pup: (While we're here, maybe we should pick up some 
other supplies?)

(Aren't we running low on... uh... running low 
on...)
Pup: (What was it again? It was-)
Pup: ...?!
Jakson: *Bark*!
Pup: Grk!
Surprised and dazed, I jumped to my feet 
to see a horse and its rider galloping 
away from me.
Pup: Yeah! You run away! You- You..! *Sigh* ...Damn
that asshole. What, was he drunk or something?
I turned, only to see the sleeping cot snapped 
in two and off to my side.
Pup: ...
My body slumped down onto the ground.
Pup: I'll just...
Pup: I'll just sleep here.
Jakson approached me and started to lick my hand.
Jakson: *Confused whine*...?
Pup: I know I said it'd be cheap to replace, but we can't 
do it this soon...
Pup: ...
My weary eyes stared at the earth beneath
my buttocks.
Pup: The ground is same ground wherever you go, after 
all?

Why not embrace it for once in my-
Pup: ...?!
A heavy, furry weight plopped down on top of me.
Pup: J- Jakson...?

Hey, boy... please... get off?!

Sort of... hard to breath...
Jakson: *Panting*
.........
Pup: F- Fine! I'll get up and head back to camp! Is that
what you want to hear?
Jakson: *Happy bark*!
Pup: *Sigh*... I wasn't really going to sleep here, you
know?
Jakson: *Confused whine*...?
I gave him a few scratches, and he willingly obliged 
me to allow me to stand once more.
Pup: Hah...
I felt the cold of the night on my skin.
Getting to sleep would be a true challenge
for me this time.
Pup: ...
Pup: Ugh... 

(What spectacular timing for a cold night 
to hit...)
I couldn't do much else outside of shiver and pull 
the blanket up more.
.........
Pup: ...?
Or so I thought. The blanket pulled itself back.
Pup: (Wait, no... That doesn't make any sense...)
Jakson: ...
A certain brown fuzzball was sliding himself into the
blanket with me.
Jakson slid all the way to the top. He didn't do 
much else as he settled down into a sleeping 
position.
Pup: (That's... warm...)
The blanket didn't fit properly now, but I found
comfort in cuddling up with the teddy bear in front 
of me.
The living, breathing, slobbering teddy bear.
Pup: ...
Pup: ...
The night wore on and sleep started to take me.
Sleepy thoughts faded as my consciousness left me.
The sounds of existence blending into eternity.
And the darkness of it became absolute.
Every tick of a second carried on and on...
...until a final twinge of the thought burst from 
the rapidly disappearing crack of the mind.
Pup: (Doesn't this mean that the bed I left... for Jakson 
to use... is currently unoccupied...?)
Pup: ...?!
Pup: *Sigh*...
Pup: ...

店主：我知道我們通常沒有庫存，

小狗：沒關係。攜帶方便而且價格不會太貴

passages.name: SP- ElliotxTatiana C - New Event
passages.content:
Bandit: Look 'er. We found some loot on that ol' lady, we 
did.
Another Bandit: We sure did, boss. We just had to... persuade her 
a bit.
He held a knife, waving it about, as the two rushed
from their crime into the shadows of the alleyway.
Bandit: Nothing a good ol' show of force can't beat, right?
Another Bandit: You're right on that boss.
Echoing Voice: A... show of force, you say?
Bandit: Are ya deaf? A show of force, I said.
Another Bandit: Yeah, a show of force he sa-

Gwahh...!
From the cover of the night, a hulking cluster of 
metal showed itself and quietly rushed the bandit 
into the dark of unconsciousness.
Then, as quickly as it appeared, it dipped into 
another shadow cast by the moon.
Bandit: Heh..?! Where did...

...

Show er'self, I say!

Ya with da police? What about the deal we 
struck?!
*Clink*... 

...*clink ... 

......*clink*......
.........
Slowly, the cluster of metal revealed itself to be a
person in plated armor, glistening with the light of
the moon.
Bandit: You er'... you er' the Armored Bandit, you er'...

You er' a bandit... just like us, you er'!
Bandit: GHAAA...!

Ya... knocked me out... ya did...
The glistening armored unit punched the bandit 
in his gut hard enough to knock him out for 
several hours.
And with that, it turned its head to the scene.
The armored unit took the stolen goods and put 
the sack over its shoulder.
Tatiana: I am not like you.

You stole from an old innocent woman to give to
yourself.

While I steal from corrupt nobles and their lackies to
give to the normal folk.
*Knock Knock*
The door opened.
Old Lady: Huh...?
She saw a sight illuminated by the candlelight from
within her home, and it showed a coin purse on 
her front porch.
Old Lady: This... purse...? I thought the bandits had taken it.
Tatiana: There we go...
She stretched out as she allowed herself to relax.
Tatiana: Mmm... Ah~

That should take care of those bandits. Hopefully, 
they never steal again.
Tatiana: Another win goes to THE Armored Bandit!
Elliot: Are you proud of yourself?
Appearing from around a corner, Elliot had 
ambushed Tatiana.
She stepped back in unease, for once cursed by 
the shadows instead of blessed.
Tatiana: ...Pretty much, yeah.
Elliot: Do you think you could do better?
Tatiana: Yeah, maybe I could've punched them both in one 
motion. Not like they were strong.
Elliot: That isn't... quite what I meant.
Elliot: You have powers, powers that can be used for 
good, and yet you use them recklessly.
Tatiana: Heh? Are you saying I should've let them steal from 
an old lady?
Elliot: No. More that... sneaking around and ambushing 
them... is uncouth.

Rather than relying on scare tactics, you should 
fight your enemies head on.
Tatiana: ...
Tatiana: *Sigh*...
Tatiana started walking past Elliot.
Tatiana: Very funny.

Lettin' people see my face and identity defeats 
a lot of the purpose of the Armored Bandit.
Elliot: I am not saying that you reveal your identity. I am
just saying to fight honestly.
Tatiana continued, and Elliot followed along as they
exited the area.
Elliot: You lurk in the shadows, yet you wear a gallant suit 
of armor.

The clanking of the armor would make it pretty 
obvious to anyone with competent skills of 
detection.
Would it not be better place yourself as example? 
In a setting all can see and learn from? Like a duel.
Tatiana: *Sigh*... where do I even start?
Elliot: But you could be... like a knight. An "Armored 
Knight", like the heroes from myths and legends of 
old.
Tatiana: First of all, 'Armored Knight' doesn't have the same
zing as Armored Bandit.
Tatiana: Second, it's not like I chose to be the "Armored
Bandit". They named me that way because of how 
I act.
The corrupt nobles were too proud of themselves 
to admit they were defeated by some random 
person they never heard of before.
But because I sneaked and ambushed them, they 
named me the Armored Bandit. I never chose that 
name.
Elliot: You still have the opportunity to be more than 
that. An example for people to see and strive 
towards.
Tatiana: Yeah, well, I'm here to help. Not play games and 
duel shit.
Tatiana: You underestimate how easy they make it when 
you're hidden. Add to that the fear factor from the 
legend, and it's easy pickings.
Tatiana: The frightful face of those snub bastards makes the 
job all the sweeter.
Elliot: Would it hurt to simply try, though?
Tatiana: Ya think I haven't tried a direct approach before?

Even without the fact that they can call
reinforcements, it can make things worse.
She looked back at Elliot, who seemed doubtful of 
her conclusion.
Tatiana: ...

It was... a small-time noble closing an orphanage
because the building was "too ugly".
Tatiana: I thought I taught him a lesson, but he was back at
harassing the orphanage a day later.
Tatiana: This shit doesn't work on noble blood unless you
actually strike fear into their hearts, ya know?
Elliot: ...
Tatiana: Besides, what's the problem with all this?

Isn't it good enough that the "Armored Bandit" is
helping people?

Why does it have to be in the middle of the day, or
honor-y and the like?
Elliot: ...
Elliot: Heroes are meant to inspire hope, not fear.

I... used to listen to stories about how the 
Armored Bandit would come and take me away if I 
didn't behave.
Tatiana: Heh, so you're one of them.

What, you scared of me or somethin'?
Elliot: My concern is that you just validate them.

You strike fear into the hearts of your victims... but
you also strike fear into the hearts of those you 
want to help.
Tatiana: Hmm...
Tatiana: BOO!
.........
Elliot: ...

As I was saying...
Elliot: Conserving hope is a very fragile endeavor.
Tatiana: Tsk. Common folk love the Armored Bandit, I'll have 
you know.
Elliot: For a time, perhaps.

The nobility is the original source for much of
culture. It trickles down, as it were.

With your actions, it is fertile soil to drive that
belief amongst even common folk.

If, for nobles, you are an uncouth evil thief, so will
the general opinion be in time.
Tatiana: I am NOT a dirty evil thief.
Elliot: I am not saying you are... but...
Tatiana: Tsk... Look. If you are not going to offer any REAL
solutions, then I'm not going to hear it.

Fighting in broad daylight would not be as effective,
and way more dangerous.

'Til that changes, just keep your own fears of the 
dark and the boogeymen to yourself.
Tatiana turned on her heel, and she walked away.
As she disappeared into a tent, Elliot was left
standing there.
Elliot: ...
Elliot stood still, breathing calmly.
Elliot: I am not afraid... 

...anymore.
passages.content_zh:
強盜：瞧瞧。我們在那老太太身上發現了一些戰利品
做到了。
另一個強盜：我們確實做到了，老闆。我們只需要...說服她
一點。
他拿著一把刀，揮舞著，兩人衝了上去。
從他們的犯罪行為中走入小巷的陰影之中。
強盜：沒有什麼是武力展示所無法擊敗的，對吧？
另一個強盜：你說得對。
迴響：你是說…展示武力？
強盜：你聾了嗎？展示武​​力，我說。
另一個強盜：是的，他展示了武力——

嘎嘎……！
從夜色的掩護中，一簇巨大的
金屬現身，悄悄衝向強盜
進入無意識的黑暗。
然後，隨著它的出現，它很快就陷入了
月亮投下的另一個陰影。
強盜：誒……？ ！哪裡...

…

展示一下自己吧，我說！

你和警察在一起嗎？我們的交易怎麼樣
被擊中了？ ！
*叮噹*...

....叮噹...

....*叮噹*......
…………
慢慢地，金屬簇顯露出來，它是一個
身披盔甲的人，閃爍著光芒
月亮。
強盜：你呃……你呃鐵甲強盜，你呃……

你呃是強盜……就像我們一樣，你呃！
強盜：啊啊啊……！

是的...把我擊倒了...是的...
閃閃發光的裝甲部隊猛擊強盜
在他的內心深處足以把他擊倒
幾個小時。
說完，它就轉頭看向了現場。
裝甲部隊拿走贓物並放置
麻袋扛在肩上。
塔蒂亞娜：我和你不一樣。

你偷了一個無辜的老婦人的東西給她
你自己。

當我從腐敗的貴族和他們的走狗那裡偷竊
送給普通老百姓。
*敲敲門*
門開了。
老太太：啊……？
她看到燭光照亮的景象
在她家裡，上面顯示了一個零錢包
她的前廊。
老太太：這個……錢包……？我以為強盜已經把它拿走了。
塔蒂亞娜：我們開始了…
她伸了個懶腰，讓自己放鬆。
塔蒂亞娜：嗯……啊~

應該可以解決那些強盜。希望，
他們再也不會偷東西了。
塔蒂亞娜：裝甲強盜又贏了！
艾爾

passages.name: SP-Kara x Charlotte C - New Event
passages.content:
Kara ate across from Charlotte, her attire and poise
with regality not befitting the simple camp chair.
In contrast, Charlotte had a more shabby look 
about her.
Charlotte: I honestly didn't expect to see you again after I
graduated from Theodal.
Kara: A good surprise, I hope?
Charlotte: Yes! You always seemed so unapproachable there, 
but now that I'm an alumni, too...
Charlotte: ...I'm not so easily intimidated. I'd like to get to
know you better.
Kara: Of course. I look forward to it much the same.
Kara took a bite of her hard bread and salted pork,
chewed it, and put it down with a grimace.
Kara: Not exactly mansion food, is it?
Charlotte: Not so much.
Kara: I know of a delightful location in a nearby city
where we could acquire something better,
if you are so inclined?
My treat?
It was a market day, so they pushed through a 
crowd of townsfolk buying from the farmers.
The city smelled earthy and musky.
Kara: How are you adapting to life in a mercenary 
company? It must be a far cry from Lockhart's 
luxuries.
Charlotte: Eh. It's not as bad as what other nobles would 
have you believe.
Charlotte: In the end, it'll mean that I can lead all sorts, from
knights to mercenaries. No need to pamper me. All 
of you can rely on me.
Charlotte: Still... 

Yeah, the food has been the worst part.
They turned and hiked up a hill away from 
the river.
A breeze blew fresh air down the cobblestone street.
Kara: I'm glad to hear the trials of the road haven't been
too harsh. Is it tough for you, being away from
Lockhart?
Charlotte: I've been away from Lockhart before.
Charlotte: Am I so forgettable that you don't remember where we
met?
Kara: Of course not.
Kara: Simply... it's one thing to be away from home and 
know you can go back, another to know you 
cannot return.
Charlotte: ...
Charlotte: I'm taking Lockhart back.
Kara: I understand, but...
Charlotte: Oh, we're here.
Kara introduced them to the hostess, asked for 
a table, and they waited off to the side of 
the anteroom.
Charlotte: Anyway, we've only talked about me so far. How'd 
you end up as the queen's handmaiden?
Kara: Ah, that is a fanciful telling of it.

I attend court as my family's representative and
occasionally assist her majesty.

I am far from the only one, and I wouldn't classify
those activities as special.
As they talked, they were lead to a table.
After a short pause to peruse their menus - lots of
fish and fresh vegetables - they continued talking.
Charlotte: You're always like this.
Kara: Like what?
Charlotte: Never giving details. Mysterious and aloof.
Kara: I'm neither mysterious nor aloof... merely boring.
Charlotte: Now you're making fun of me.
Kara: What would you have me do, play truth or dare?
Charlotte: Good idea!
Kara: Charlotte...
Kara: Aren't we too old for that?
When their waitress came, Kara ordered sautéed 
trout with squash.
Charlotte asked for a tuna on salad with tomatoes,
peppers, and wild rice.
Charlotte: Are you afraaaaaaaaaaaid?
Kara: Charlotte, do I seem the sort to be influenced like so?
Charlotte: Yes.
Kara: ...
Charlotte: Truth or dare?
Kara: …

Truth.
Charlotte: Who did you have a crush on at Theodal?
Kara: You're presuming I had a crush during our
schooldays, then?
Charlotte: ...
Kara: *Sigh*...
Kara: Let's say, hypothetically, you were right.

Do you recall the previous student council 
president? A year ahead of me and had 
curly brown hair.
Charlotte: Oh... I think I vaguely remember.. We talked a few
times, but we only were in the school together for 
my first year.
Kara: Truly someone I looked up to and admired. A kind 
soul who had a thoughtful memory.
Kara: I always wondered if there was more to it, but I don't
think it was mutual even if so.
The waitress brought their food, which distracted 
them both for a bit.
Charlotte: So... you prefer... older partners?
Kara: ...
Kara: ...
Charlotte: W- What's that look?
Kara: You already took your turn.
Kara: Truth or dare?
Charlotte stabbed a cherry tomato with her fork,
and it squirted tomato juice onto the table.
Charlotte: ...
She hastily wiped it off with her napkin, giggling.
Charlotte: Well, maybe... Truth?
Kara: How did you feel about Alexei back during our school
days?
Charlotte: Alexei? You're talking about Rowan when he was...
normal?
Charlotte: Well, we were only friends, I think? He was a shy 
kid so he was easy to talk to, especially as a fellow 
heir.
...Why ask about him of all things?
Kara: All in the proper order, my dear Charlotte.

I didn't say "truth" for your next turn yet, 
after all.
Charlotte: Heh, you... 

Hmm...
Charlotte: Truth or dare?
Kara: Truth.
Charlotte: How did you and Cainan meet? He must have been
something special to catch your eye.
Kara: I'm afraid our story is more practical than romantic. I
met him in the course of my duties for her majesty.
Kara delicately sliced a piece of fish off, speared it
with her fork, and stared at it for a moment before
eating it primly.
Kara: We do pair well and work effectively together. His
Covenant connections are useful to both my family 
and Cartenan.
Likewise, my connections in Cartenan will help him 
as he curtails the misuse of the Oathbreakers.
Charlotte: So more like an arranged marriage?

Phooey. I'd hoped that you at least could marry for
love. He's how much older than you are?
Kara: Seventeen years, I believe. 

I don't mind.
Charlotte: Does he treat you well at least?
Kara: He treats me with respect. And, he is a pretty 
man, isn't he? More than a few women sighed 
when they heard of our engagement.
Charlotte: I guess that will have to do. I wanted there to be
more.
Kara: A love story for the ages?
Charlotte: Yes! You deserve that!
Kara: And you don't?
Charlotte: I do too!
Charlotte: Sure, I probably won't get that choice, but its still
fun to think about.
Kara: To marry for love - one of the few things you could
envy a commoner for.
Charlotte: Oh, if only they knew how hard we had it...
Kara: Indeed, it is but a tragedy.
Self deprecating and joking smiles on their faces, 
they moved to finish their food.
Kara asked for the check, and both of them 
cleaned their plates.
Charlotte: This feels just like being back in school. I always
appreciated when you invited me out.
Charlotte: Maybe we have time for a walk, too? Don't really 
feel like I want to head back to camp yet.
Kara: Do you know the area well enough to have a suggested
destination?
Charlotte: Actually...
She gestured in the direction opposite of the 
camp. Kara nodded and paid for their meal.
They strolled along a ridge that overlooked the city,
river, and surrounding farms.
Kara: I will say that I am flattered by your interest in my
life since school.
Charlotte: How could I not be? You always do everything so
effortlessly.
Charlotte: Even your hair is so sleek, shiny, and... stable!
Nothing like my own's tendency to become a 
wreck.
Kara: Your affinity for hats might have something to do 
with that.
Charlotte: Don't scorn my hats! Their style is better suited to
the future leader of a merchant republic than an
ostentatious crown.
Charlotte adjusted her beret and smoothed 
out her hair.
Charlotte: And don't think I didn't notice you trying to change
the topic from you to me.
Charlotte: You deserve more praise! Your eyes are so pretty, 
you have such excellent fashion and are so 
effortlessly elegant.
Kara: Saying as much in such succession makes each 
seem a little less sincere than the last...
Charlotte: I mean it, though. You're... like everything they say 
I should be to be Lockhart's heir.
Kara: Do you... wish to discuss that topic? I know it has
caused friction with your sister.
Kara: Do you... wish to discuss that topic? I know it has
caused friction within your family.
Charlotte: Ah... well, me not being a lot of people's first 
choice for the next leader isn't exactly a secret...

It'd... only cause trouble to talk about within my
family... even talking to my parents about it was...
Charlotte: Besides, it's other families that... well... 

Maybe... I shouldn't talk about it here either...
Charlotte: ...?
Kara reached to take Charlotte's hand, perhaps to 
pull her closer for a hug, but Charlotte stepped 
back.
Kara: Charlotte, you can talk to me about anything.
Charlotte: My home is conquered and that shitty wannabe 
fiancé was put in charge of Lockhart. At least 
you've got a decent one to look forward to.
It doesn't matter. This... this conversation doesn't
matter about heirs or whatever, it just needs to-
Charlotte flinched and looked down, hugging 
herself.
Charlotte: ...

I didn't mean to snap at you. I'm sorry.

...
Charlotte: We should get back.

Before the others figure out we've been 
eating real food, not mercenary rations.

Especially Pup and that dog.
Charlotte: We should get back.

Before the others figure out we've been 
eating real food, not mercenary rations.

Especially Pup.
Kara: I'm always available, if you need an ear to listen or a
shoulder to cry on.
Charlotte: Thanks...
Charlotte nodded stiffly and left.
Kara: ...
Kara sighed and wandered the city a bit more to 
gather her thoughts.
Eventually, she hunted down Rowan and pulled 
him away from the camp to a nearby location.
Kara: ...and that's how she left.
Kara: I tried to help, but I'm afraid I pushed her away
instead. You were friends with her in those 
schooldays, so...
Rowan: I don't know her as well as you think. We were 
friends, but since we met again, she's given me the 
cold shoulder.
Kara: You're still closer to her than I am.
Rowan: Am I? Was I? I do not recall being idolized during 
that time as you were.
Rowan: If anything strikes me as a potential way forward...
why not be that idol?
Kara: I have attempted to be a role model for her.
Rowan: What about a role model for opening up on your
feelings?
Rowan: I... as an open book that invites others to write 
within myself... see you as, my dear Kara...
Rowan: Well, even in our schooldays, I don't recall many a
time you talked about yourself candidly.
Kara: Hmm...
Rowan: Ah, even better yet, to talk on such a level as 
though equals?

Would it be the role of a lifetime for you, my 
dearest upperclassman.
Kara: ...Alexei.
Rowan: Ah, yeah, I'll seal my mouth shut for a time.
Kara: No... just...
Kara: Thank you.
Rowan: ...
Miming as though his mouth was sealed shut, 
Rowan smiled a sense of relief and to 
communicate his own gratitude.
The two parted to their tasks for the remainder of 
the day.
Rowan with an optimistic skip to his step.
And Kara, with a pensive look of worry on her own.
passages.content_zh:
卡拉坐在夏洛特對面用餐，她的服裝和姿態
帶著一種與簡樸的營地椅不相稱的貴氣。
相比之下，夏洛特看起來更為樸素。
夏洛特：老實說，我沒想到從席奧達爾畢業後還會再見到妳。
卡拉：希望是個驚喜？
夏洛特：是的！妳在那裡總是看起來那麼難以接近，
但現在我也是校友了...
夏洛特：...我沒那麼容易被嚇倒了。我想更了解妳。
卡拉：當然。我也同樣期待。
卡拉咬了一口她那硬邦邦的麵包和醃豬肉，
咀嚼後，皺著眉頭放了下來。
卡拉：這可不是豪宅裡的食物，對吧？
夏洛特：差遠了。
卡拉：我知道附近城市有個很棒的地方，
我們可以弄到更好的東西，
如果妳有興趣的話？
我請客？
那天是市集日，所以她們擠過一群向農民購買商品的
鎮民。
城市裡瀰漫著泥土和麝香的味道。
卡拉：妳適應傭兵公司的生活了嗎？
這一定和洛克哈特的奢華生活相去甚遠。
夏洛特：嗯。沒有其他貴族說的那麼糟。
夏洛特：最終，這意味著我可以領導各種人，從
騎士到傭兵。不需要特別照顧我。你們
都可以依靠我。
夏洛特：不過...

是啊，食物是最糟糕的部分。
她們轉身爬上遠離
河流的山丘。
微風將新鮮空氣吹向鵝卵石街道。
卡拉：很高興聽到旅途的考驗沒有太過嚴酷。
離開洛克哈特對妳來說很難嗎？
夏洛特：我以前也離開過洛克哈特。
夏洛特：我這麼容易被忘記嗎，妳不記得我們在哪裡
相遇了嗎？
卡拉：當然不是。
卡拉：只是...離開家鄉並
知道妳可以回去是一回事，知道妳
無法回去又是另一回事。
夏洛特：...
夏洛特：我要把洛克哈特奪回來。
卡拉：我明白，但是...
夏洛特：喔，我們到了。
卡拉向女主人介紹了她們，要了一張
桌子，然後她們在接待室的
一旁等候。
Ch

passages.name: SP-ReagynxCharlotte B - New Event
passages.content:
Reagyn: Due to our recent skirmish, we are down 27.2% of 
our supply of weapons.

If we want to be ready for our next encounter, we 
will need to supply the camp with 22 kg of iron, 10 
kg copper, 1100 grams of tin, and 60kg of wood...
...by a conservative calculation, at least.
Reagyn stepped further into the tent, flipping 
through the pages of a report.
Reagyn: Due to the state our weapons are at, I predict that
repairs will take two and a half weeks.

The number of skirmishes we are in outpace that, 
so we will need to rely on the local blacksmiths, or 
expedite the ones in camp.
Reagyn closed the report, and stood tall.
Reagyn: Furthermore, we-
Pup: Zzzzz....
Pup: ...!

W- What?
Pup: *Yawwwnnn*... Morning.
Reagyn: ...
Reagyn took a minute to take a breath and look 
around for the first time after entering the tent.
Expecting a full entourage of people, Reagyn had 
burst in dramatically and started explaining things.
However, the only person in the room was... me.
Reagyn: Pup... are you the only one in the room?
Pup: Eh...? Yeah... Why?
Reagyn: *Sigh*... I guess I can't really expect much outside
Her Majesty's courts...
I looked towards a magical time keeping device 
within the meeting tent.
Pup: Wait, isn't the meeting booked to start in 10 
minutes?
Reagyn: Correct, but arriving on time is the same thing as
arriving late.
Reagyn: You are on time... surprising, actually.
Pup: I'm just trying to avoid a repeat of last time.
Reagyn: ...

Then we are to not expecting anyone for another 
ten minutes, then.
Pup: Seems to be the case. Norde and everyone aren't 
always on time anyways.
Pup: So...
Pup: How was your day...?
Reagyn: If you don't mind, I believe I'll use those 10 
minutes to double check the math.
Pup: Oh... sure. That's a good thing to trust to you.
Pup: Well... back to my nap, I guess?
Reagyn: If we move... calculate that...
Charlotte: ...and we can-
Charlotte: Oh, you're already here.
Norde: As well as Pup, it seems.
Charlotte: Sort of figured we'd get here first... We're five
minutes early, even.
Pup: Heheh~
Charlotte: Hmm...
Reagyn: Don't mind me. I just arrived early to...
Reagyn's gaze turned up to the others.
Reagyn: ...Norde?

What brings you here, I thought it would only be
Charlotte, Pup, and myself today.
Norde: Charlotte insis-
Charlotte: I just wanted Norde to ask some questions on the topic.
Charlotte: I think those opinions would be... fruitful. Norde 
has a good way of putting these logistical 
questions.
Charlotte: Feel free to proceed as though it was just the 
three of us that you expected, though.
Charlotte said the words as she stepped 
towards one of the chairs to sit down.
Charlotte: Also...

Should we do something about... uhh...
Pup: ZZzzzz...
Norde: Pup will wake up with the noise.
Pup: ZZzzzz...
Norde: Maybe...
Reagyn: Regardless, this is likely a good time to start the
meeting.
Reagyn: And so, due to the current rate we found 
ourselves in skirmishes, we will need about 21.7 kg 
of iron and-
Charlotte: *Clears throat*...
Charlotte: If possible, how would that expand to battle strategy?
Reagyn: Hm? What do you mean?
Charlotte: Like those strategies that get trained into the 
Crows? Done so we can coordinate with each other 
when the fighting starts.
Reagyn: I imagine that would fall out of the scope of a
logistics meeting...?
Norde: She has a point.
Norde: The logistics are battlefield maneuvers as well.
Norde: Like these detours... they may invite more battles 
and more strategic considerations.
Reagyn: ...Perhaps.
Norde: The optimized math you have also assumes 
predictable market conditions.

It is actually rare that small villages work on market
rates. They leverage the situation to 
barter, typically.
Norde: Generally, smaller adjustments to our process are
better.
Norde: We can always take bigger swings later.
Reagyn: Ah... well...
Charlotte smirked, and she showed on her face 
that she saw it funny how the "all-knowing Reagyn" 
was being cornered by Norde's questioning.
Charlotte: Like maybe you could reforge the worn equipment? 
Or just reuse it, like using worn swords as lance 
tips.
Norde: Hmm... How much wood do we have?
Reagyn: Not that much... but if we convert it into lances... I
would need to recalculate...
Norde: Have you collected info on how much equipment 
we outright lose each battle, too? Like arrows.
Reagyn: Not... yet.
Charlotte: Tsk...
Charlotte felt a bit of a knot in her stomach...
One could call it guilt. However, her pride didn't
allow her to acknowledge that.
Charlotte: I think they said that we could re-use some 
arrows...
Charlotte: But it depends on the quality. Some arrowheads 
are just... bad...

Especially if we pick up ones the bandits 
used... sheesh.
Norde: Then what about-
Charlotte: The smiths have the ability to fix the chipped 
weapons, yes. It would take some time.

Especially if they are smelting the arrowheads 
into ingots to help the process.
Norde: But what about the wood? You said the arrows 
had minimal scavenge value, so how is our 
inventory?
Charlotte: Ah... I don't know-
Reagyn: We should have enough that we can create some 
emergency lances using the extra material from 
the arrowheads.
Norde: Then...
The meeting proceeded with the two taking
turns to answer Norde's thorough questioning.
Norde: I think that should cement our plan and allow us to
move forward.

Well done.

Now, if you'll excuse me.
Charlotte: *Sigh*... I thought he'd never run out of 
questions.
Reagyn: Indeed. That was very thorough, yet to the point...
Reagyn: But... Norde does not pull any punches, it seems?
Charlotte: Hah... once in a blue moon...
Charlotte: One time, Norde just straight up told me I was fat!
Reagyn: Were you eating extra portions, again?
Charlotte: H- Hey! That was one time.
Charlotte: It's not often we have delicacies from Lockhart
available...
Reagyn: Perhaps I am speaking out of line at this time.
Apologies.
Reagyn: Though... I wanted to say... thank you.
Charlotte: Hm? What for?
Reagyn: The information you had regarding the smithies was
useful.
Charlotte: Ah, yeah. A bit of a mercantile habit, I suppose.

I tend to ask about that sort of stuff when helping
with the supply runs.
Charlotte: But your understanding of math, numbers and your
knowledge of our supply is also a commendable skill.
Reagyn: It is the least I could do. As the younger sibling, I
must be prepared at all times... for both of us.
Reagyn: Next time, I will be better prepared. That was... I
should have been better prepared.
Reagyn: Perhaps I can join your discussions with the
blacksmiths?
Charlotte: Well, if the opportunity arises.
Charlotte: They're not exactly scheduled, so... maybe 
sometime this next week?
Reagyn: Next time, I will be better prepared. That was... I
should have been better prepared.
Reagyn: Perfect. I should have some time at
9:15!
Charlotte: Perhaps we can be a bit more... flexible on the
specific time...
Reagyn: Hmm... I should be available
between 8:30 and 9:30 tomorrow?
Charlotte: Ah... so early.
Charlotte: But it's a start I guess.
Pup: ...?!

10kg of lumber!
Pup: Oh, man...

Zzzzz...
passages.content_zh:
Reagyn: 由於我們最近的衝突，我們的武器供應量減少了 27.2%。

如果我們想為下一次遭遇做好準備，我們需要為營地提供 22 公斤的鐵、10 公斤的銅、1100 克的錫和 60 公斤的木材……
……至少保守估計是這樣。
Reagyn 更進一步走進帳篷，翻閱著一份報告。
Reagyn: 由於我們武器的現狀，我預計維修需要兩個半星期。

我們遭遇衝突的次數超過了這個時間，所以我們需要依賴當地的鐵匠，或者加快營地裡的鐵匠的速度。
Reagyn 合上報告，挺直了身子。
Reagyn: 此外，我們-
Pup: Zzzzz....
Pup: ...!

W- 什麼？
Pup: *Yawwwnnn*... 早安。
Reagyn: ...
Reagyn 花了一分鐘時間深吸一口氣，並在進入帳篷後第一次環顧四周。
Reagyn 期待著一個完整的隨行人員，戲劇性地衝進來並開始解釋事情。
然而，房間裡唯一的人是……我。
Reagyn: Pup... 房間裡只有你一個人嗎？
Pup: 欸...? 是啊... 怎麼了？
Reagyn: *嘆氣*... 我想我不能對陛下法庭之外的人期望太多...
我看向會議帳篷裡的一個魔法計時裝置。
Pup: 等等，會議不是預定在 10 分鐘後開始嗎？
Reagyn: 沒錯，但準時到達和遲到是一樣的。
Reagyn: 你很準時... 說實話，令人驚訝。
Pup: 我只是想避免重蹈覆轍。
Reagyn: ...

那麼我們就不指望在十分鐘內有其他人來了。
Pup: 看來是這樣。 Norde 和其他人反正也不總是準時。
Pup: 所以...
Pup: 你今天過得怎麼樣...?
Reagyn: 如果你不介意，我想我會用這 10 分鐘來仔細檢查一下數學。
Pup: 哦... 當然。 把這個信任交給你真是太好了。
Pup: 好吧... 我想我還是回去睡午覺吧？
Reagyn: 如果我們移動... 計算一下...
Charlotte: ...然後我們可以-
Charlotte: 哦，你已經在這裡了。
Norde: 還有 Pup，看來。
Charlotte: 大概猜到我們會得到

passages.name: SP-ReagynxCharlotte A - New Event
passages.content:
Charlotte: How dare you!
Off in the corner of the mess tent, there sat two
"noble" "ladies"... as one may call them.
Reagyn: *Sigh*... You are making a scene.
One of them was a redhead with a somewhat 
diplomatic and subdued attitude, hands crossed 
across a lap until an opening to speak arose.
Charlotte: Making a scene!? You are the one that called me a dirty
pig!
While on the other side of the table, there stood a
feisty blonde speaking with gusto aplenty.
Even though her voice was raised, and her 
emotions were rampant, her voice was smooth 
and eloquent.
Crow: They are at it again, aren't they?
Other Crow: Hopefully without a food fight this time...
And on the other side of the tent, stood two 
Crows tasked with preparing the food...
With hopes in their hearts...
...that it would be eaten. Not thrown.
A show. Via both its drama and its audience.
Crow: We are low on supplies as it is... And its those two
who have been managing the budget lately.
Other Crow: ...Hey, I bet you one gold Miss Charlotte starts it
this time.
Crow: Doesn't she always?
Reagyn: I did not say that!
Charlotte: I heard you. Loud and clear.
Reagyn: I said...!
Reagyn: *Sigh*... forget it.
Charlotte: Then you admit it?
Reagyn: Not in the context you are imagining...
Out on the sidelines, there entered an extra to this
conflict.
Pup: Uh... did I miss something?
Crow: The usual.
Other Crow: Think they'll almost collapse the tent again? Chicken
bones can get some velocity when whipped fast.
Crow: Is the dog around to catch it like last time?
Crow: Man, we had to move quickly.
Pup: While you two are cooking again, too. You're not 
adding something to the sauce, are you?
Other Crow: By the Goddess, no. I've heard them argue in other
tents at night, too.
Charlotte: That's it...
As she said the words, her hand hovered over the
remaining chicken bone from her meal.
Other Crow: Here comes the money shot...!
Crow: I didn't make the bet.
Charlotte: I am...
Charlotte: ...leaving.
...and she left the mess tent.
Reagyn: *Sigh*...
Other Crow: Tsk.
Pup: Hmm... Interesting.
Later that day, a meeting was arranged to 
discuss the mysteriously depleted food supply.
Charlotte: ...and therefore, I suggest approaching this village
due to their abundance of wheat.

Our recently gathered supply of legumes would be 
a good trade for it.
Reagyn was the first one to clap. Norde was 
second. And I... clapped last after realizing the 
meeting was over.
Reagyn: Well done, Miss Charlotte. Your analytics have
improved. No objections come to mind.

Your oration has improved with your confidence 
too.
Norde's ears twitched.
Norde: You did well, indeed. Now, if you'd excuse me. I 
must be on my way.
Pup: Hm?
As though with a newfound purpose, Norde exited 
the tent quickly.
Charlotte: Haha, yeah. Practice makes perfect, I guess?
Reagyn reacted with a small but warm smile.
Reagyn: ...
Charlotte: ...
Pup: ...
Reagyn: Then... any feedback you'd relay back to me?
Charlotte: Uh... You let me finish?
Charlotte: Which... might be better than barraging me with
questions, like I've done to others at times.
Reagyn: You were going out of your way for that?
Charlotte: Uh... No. Maybe. No... What was the question again?
Reagyn: ...If you had any feedback for me.
Charlotte: I gave the... incorrect answer, then?
Reagyn: ...

What of... outside the meetings? Do you have any
thoughts you'd like to share?
The two started back and forth on unimportant 
details like habits and logistical endeavors.
Pup: (Is this...?)
Pup: ...
Pup: (Well, this is subtle as a brick.)
Pup: Now, you two, don't you think you should be more 
open in this olive branch?
Pup: Charlotte, if you'd start.
Charlotte: What's that supposed to mean?
Pup: ...
I stared at her for a solid few seconds, then tilted 
my head slightly forward.
Pup: (Ah... fresh relationship drama~)
Pup: Now now, you two. Is this how "business partners" talk?
I leaned over unconsciously, with my arms on the 
table and hands to my mouth in excitement.
Charlotte: What's that supposed to mean?
Pup: ...
My fingers twiddles about as a soft smile rose into a
smirk.
Pup: (Ah... this dog and pony show.)
Pup: You two. It's obvious there's a problem here you 
both want to get the horse going on.
Pup: Why not just get on with it already?
Charlotte: What's that supposed to mean?
Pup: ...
I stared at her for a solid few seconds, then tilted 
my head slightly forward.
Charlotte: F- Fine...!
I led the two to sit across from each other, 
each a red tint to their cheeks.
Pup: *Clears throat*
Pup: Charlotte starts. Begin.
Charlotte: I...
Charlotte: Reagyn just... is always throwing compliments my way.
Charlotte: How well I do my job... How much I have improved...
Charlotte: It just gives me this... weird tight feeling.
Charlotte: Is it a backhanded compliment? Or... is it... Mmm...!
Charlotte began to do weird signs with her arms 
and hands. As if she was moving boxes from one 
side of the room to another.
Pup: Well that's... a reaction.
Pup: Reagyn, this is your time for a rebuttal. You're on 
the clock.
Reagyn: *Sigh*...
Reagyn: As Charlotte so mentioned, I have observed her 
growth into her role as an administrator and leader.

I only wish to be true and open on my honest 
feedback. That I admire what she has done.
Pup: So what is causing the problem?
Reagyn: Charlotte, in turn... is not... doing the same.
Pup: Same what?
Reagyn: Acknowledging my... m- my own growth across our 
time together.
Reagyn: It's growth of mine that I have her to thank for,
too...

I just was hoping for... a bit of... you know...?
Pup: Ah...
I turned my whole body to Charlotte.
Pup: Translation: Reagyn wants you - Charlotte - 
to give compliments.
Reagyn: I- I... Asking such a thing would be uncouth!
Leaning to Reagyn, I paused and then tilted my 
head towards her.
Pup: Am I wrong?
Reagyn: ...no.
Charlotte: But... I've said nice things before... right? I'm
pretty sure I did.
Pup: Maybe it didn't come across like that? Can you give an
example?
Charlotte: I- I...
Charlotte: *Clears throat*...

I like... your... analytical skills. It always feels
like...
Charlotte: ...like you always are right on point.
Reagyn: ...!
Charlotte's comment made Reagyn fume with 
grateful embarrassment.
Reagyn: I- I am glad that you think of me... as an asset...
Reagyn: I really appreciate your sense of honesty and
directness!
Reagyn: ...towards finding appropriate trade partners in our
travels.
Charlotte: I- I mean... is nothing compared to the way you 
speak. Its so eloquent and fancy...
Charlotte: ...whenever you describe your relationship about
getting nobles to help our cause.
Reagyn: Well, I love the way you stand stall and confident...
Reagyn: ...whenever we present the information that we have for
Pup and Norde to assess.
Charlotte: But it doesn't compare to the way you elegantly sway as
you walk...
Charlotte: ...whenever you are counting our weapon stock.
Reagyn: It's nothing special. At least compared to how you
bravely act...
Reagyn: ...whenever there is a rowdy complaint.
Pup: Aren't you two getting along better?
Pup: (Hoho~ Maybe I should get a snack for the show?)
Pup: Happy to see you two getting along better. I knew 
you just needed to talk.
Pup: (Maybe this is a good time for me to get back to 
my business and leave.)
Charlotte: ...
Reagyn: ...
Charlotte: I would love to be your partner...
Charlotte: ...in mercantile affairs.
Reagyn: Excuse me...?
Charlotte: Or... maybe not mercantile? Logistics? Trading
associate?
Reagyn turned away.
Reagyn: Are you...

...
...and turned back to Charlotte.
Reagyn: I would... love to be your trading partner.
Outside the tent, as I walked away...
Pup: (A rustling sound?)
As I stepped towards my goal, I could hear some
rumbling noises from the tent I just left.
Pup: (I... Maybe it's time for me to step away?)
Pup: (Let 'em figure out how bright this particular fire is
for themselves.)
Pup: (No, they wouldn't be fighting again, would they? 
After that?)
Pup: (There's no way... right?)
passages.content_zh:
夏洛特：你怎麼敢！
食堂帳篷的角落坐著兩個人
「貴族」「女士」……人們可以這樣稱呼她們。
Reagyn：*嘆氣*...你正在大吵大鬧。
其中一個是紅頭髮的，有點
外交和克制的態度，雙手交叉
跨了一圈，直到有說話的機會。
夏洛特：大吵大鬧！ ？你就是那個罵我骯髒的人
豬！
而在桌子的另一邊，站著一個
精力充沛的金髮女郎，說話充滿熱情。
儘管她的聲音提高了，而且她
情緒洶湧，聲音平緩
和雄辯。
Crow：他們又來了，不是嗎？
其他烏鴉：希望這次沒有食物大戰…
帳篷的另一邊，站著兩個
烏鴉的任務是準備食物...
他們心中充滿希望…
……它會被吃掉。沒有扔。
一場表演。透過它的戲劇和觀眾。
Crow：我們的供應量已經不足了……而且是那兩個
最近一直在管理預算的人。
另一隻烏鴉：……嘿，我跟你賭一金，夏綠蒂小姐開始了
這次。
烏鴉：她不總是這樣嗎？
雷金：我沒這麼說！
夏洛特：我聽到了。響亮清晰。
雷金：我說……！
Reagyn：*嘆氣*...算了。
夏洛特：那你承認了？
Reagyn：不是你想像的情況…
在場外，有一個額外的內容
衝突。
Pup：呃……我是不是錯過了什麼？
烏鴉：平常的樣子。
其他烏鴉：你認為他們會再次把帳篷推倒嗎？雞
快速鞭打時，骨頭可以獲得一定的速度。
烏鴉：狗會像上次那樣來抓它嗎？
Crow：夥計，我們得快點行動。
小狗：你們兩個又在煮飯的時候。你不是
在醬汁裡加點東西，是嗎？
其他烏鴉：女神發誓，不。我聽過他們在其他方面爭論過
晚上也搭帳篷。
夏洛特：就是這樣…
說這句話的時候，她的手懸在了
她吃飯時剩下的雞骨頭。
其他烏鴉：錢來了……！
Crow：我沒有打賭。
夏洛特：我是…
夏洛特：……離開。
……她把混亂拋在了一邊

passages.name: SP-Atticus x Tatiana B - New Event
passages.content:
Elliot: ...
Elliot stood there, hesitating a bit before the tent
flap.
Elliot: Excuse me, Castel? I received a message from 
you...
There were panicked sounds on the other side of 
the tent flap.
Castel: H- Hold on... for one moment... please...!
Elliot could hear a sound of shuffling, as though 
items were being hastily arranged.
Castel: And... perfect~
Elliot: ...
Castel: You may enter now.
Elliot pushed aside the tent flap, only to see...
Elliot: ...

Forgive me sir, but I don't understand what is
happening here.
There was a table set for two, with the rations of 
the day on them.
Castel: When we last spoke on the subject, I alluded to 
the possibility of discussing your... heirloom 
situation...
...over dinner.
Castel: Well, this is that opportunity.
Elliot: I see.
Elliot: Far be it for me to refuse such a gracious invitation.
Castel: Ah, your heirloom?
Castel looked at Elliot's body. 
The current form of it.
Elliot: Right. Our arrangement. Apologies.
There was a flash of light.
Elliot: As agreed.
Castel: That'll be much more conducive to studying it, 
thank you.
Without additional delay, the two sat at the table.
Castel: I hope you enjoy the libations. I find it difficult to
think on an empty stomach.
Elliot: I feel much the same.
Elliot: Though... the wine?
Castel: Ah, well... alcohol... s- stimulates the brain. It is
an established scientific fact.
Elliot: And the candles?
Castel: Well, how else does one expect to read, if they do 
not have adequate lighting?
Elliot seemed content with the answer. 

He went to take an initial bite of the food... 
only to pause...
Elliot: What of the rose petals?
Castel: That is just, eh... an effort of mine to counteract 
the smell of horses and sweat.
Castel: Mercenary camps can be so dirty, can't they?
A statement met by Elliot sniffing the air.
Elliot: But... they do not keep the horses on this side of
camp.
Elliot: And today is a rest day on the training schedule. 
Not even Pup is about.
Castel: Old habits... die hard...?
Elliot: I suppose so.
The pair ate and drank in silence for some time.
Elliot: So, when are we going to do it?
Castel choked on his food.
Elliot: And for that matter, how are we even going to do 
it?
Elliot: With us being so different and all. 

Our forms, I mean.
Coughing, Castel wiped his mouth.
Elliot: Are you okay?
Castel: Fine... I just wasn't expecting such a forward
question.
Castel blushed bright red.
Castel: Though I suppose I'm fine with skipping formalities 
if you are.
Castel: Fortunately, I've given this much thought.
Elliot: Formalities? I was merely speaking of your intent to
discuss my ancestor...?
Castel's eyes went wide.
Castel: Oh! That! Of course! Yes!

Not "do it", but-
Elliot: ...?
Castel: Well, never mind.
Castel: We're nearly done with the meal, so we can finish
and...
The two stepped to the research setup Castel had 
within the tent.
Castel: You see, I have been pondering this matter with 
your ancestor and your unexpected transformation.
Castel: Everything I have experienced recently, and 
throughout my professional experience, has made 
one thing clear.
The psychology of the individual who uses a 
heirloom is the most significant factor in how that 
heirloom expresses itself.
Castel: This is doubly true for the case of transformations,
and your situation uniquely involves both.
Castel walked over to a table with a few heirlooms 
laid out on it.
Castel: Specifically, the area of emotion. Attitudes. 
Feelings. Beliefs.
Castel: Therefore, I propose we discuss your inner 
thoughts on your transformation in greater detail.
Elliot: I see... that does make a certain degree of sense.
Elliot: However, I'm not certain where to begin.
Castel responded with a fidget motion as though 
touch his no longer relevant glasses.
Castel: Fair enough. Perhaps it would help if I speak about 
my own feelings first?
Elliot: I imagine that could help to see an example. Thank you.
Elliot: Then I suppose to start...

How do you feel about... being a shade? And a 
feminine presenting one at that?
Elliot: After all, it seems like you still identify as a man,
so doesn't that cause some friction?
Castel: Hrm... it does. Or perhaps it would be more 
accurate to say that it should?
Castel: I recognize most people would reasonably find the
situation somewhat distressing.
Castel: After all, I didn't ask for this. And given the chance,
I would much rather return to my old body.
Castel: However, I also view the situation with a sense of
detachment.
Elliot: As in, you don't view this body as... "your body"?
Castel: Correct. It is merely a chance for me to study a 
unique situation up close
Castel: One that has never been seen before, and one 
where one can come away from it with new 
scientific knowledge.
Elliot: I appreciate that you shared that. I think it helps 
me work through some of my thoughts.
Castel: Should you be willing to share, I am glad to listen.
Elliot: ...
Castel: Not that... you must...
Elliot: I suppose for me, it is the opposite.
Elliot: I am a man. I've been a man.
Elliot: But this form... it has been with me for years now. 
It would be a lie to say it feels removed from me.

Would I trade it to get rid of the shame of it? 
Remove it from my history?
Elliot: That? That I do not know.
Castel: "Shame"...? Because of the female form, or...?
Elliot: Shame of my failure to my family.

This is not the legendary ancestor I was destined 
to cloak myself within. To raise our lineage back to
prominence.
How many more generations until we reach that 
point...?

...
Elliot: With that all, I suppose that it is hard to deny that
the female form isn't a reminder of that guilt.
Castel: I see...
The two settled into a considerate silence.
Elliot: Do you see a path forward, now? Did what I 
provided help see the next steps?
Castel: The guilt and shame... could they be derived from
another ancestor?

Somehow strong feelings corrupt the access to the
familial history in the heirloom...?
Elliot: But those feelings weren't around until after I
first transformed?
Castel: True... true... maybe it can act as a starting point,
though?

Hmm...
Castel: You are absolutely sure it is the correct heirloom?
Elliot: Yes.
Castel: Then yes, my theories will have to act as a starting
point.
Castel: Have you ever had thoughts about being a woman 
before?
Elliot: What?
Castel: Before the first time you took this form.
Elliot: No.
Elliot: Or...  *sigh*...
Elliot: No.
Castel: Did you have any strong feeling or wants before 
that point?
Castel: I understand I am speculating from my theory, but 
if it is true then any source of 'deviating' influences 
may be relevant.
Elliot: I suppose... I wanted to feel more free.
Elliot: I was essentially a child at the time, barely on the
precipice of adulthood.
Elliot: A life of being raised to be my family's savior... and
a savior via another person's greatness over my 
own...
Castel: Yes, I imagine such feelings would increase even in
one's later teenage years.
Elliot: Indeed, it is not a rebellious phase I am proud of. 
Nor one I can take back.
