Castel: But do you feel more "free"?
Castel: In this form, I mean.
Elliot: I... suppose so?
Elliot: I feel more heroic. Confident. As if the rest of the
time, I'm only pretending.
Castel: That would imply any emotional influence would've still
made this the form of a hero, then?
Castel: And it is something to work with. I am happy I
stopped by that bookstore recently.
Castel gestured at a pile on his bed
containing a number of books.
Elliot: You wish for us to read those? Could two people 
get through that many in one evening?
Castel: Not if we simply check the appendices for anything
relating to your ancestor.
Castel: Even then, we only have to skim those sections for
mentions of anything related to the emotions 
you're experiencing.
Elliot: What would we be looking for?
Castel: Reasons you could subconsciously associate the 
heroic presence with a feminine form.
Elliot: As a potential corruptive influence, like you
mentioned...
Castel: And if without success, then we've eliminated one
avenue of inquiry.
Elliot: Indeed. Well, let's get started.
Castel: Hmm...
Castel's eyes scanned across the book's words 
made visible by the campfire's light.
Elliot: Have you found anything yet? I've yet to find 
anything myself.
Castel: *Yawn*... I am afraid nothing from me either.
Castel: And I was so sure this was the right way to 
investigate it...
Elliot: No, it is fine. As you said, it was worth a try.
Elliot: It is getting late. I think I should retire soon.
Castel: As should I...
Castel: Though consider me glad that we were able to 
share this time together.
Elliot: Indeed. It is rare to find another willing to delve
into the depths of Covenant myths.
Castel: Y- Yes, t- that's what I meant. Of course~!
Elliot: ...
Elliot: Haha, you can be humorously silly at times.
Elliot: Thank you, Castel. Despite our lack of concrete
results, I'm glad we talked.

It helped, in at least some ways.
Castel: Truly? Then I am most pleased with the outcome.
Elliot: In fact, I think I will continue reading some of these
titles and thinking on my feelings, as you 
suggested.
Elliot: Might I ask to return to your forum? You've 
managed to transport an impressive amount of 
literature.
Castel: Yes! Please do! And come speak with me in it, 
whenever you have the chance!
Castel: Erm, for science, of course.
Elliot: Yes, for science.
Elliot's relaxed laughter mixed with the hint of
nervousness from Castel's own.
Elliot: Goodnight, Castel.
Castel: Goodnight.
And so Elliot turned towards the tents while re-
entering his original form, leaving Castel with his
books and campfire.
Castel: *Sigh*... Too close. 

I feared that I had come on too strongly.
Castel: I think... I think Elliot didn't catch on to my...
advances...?
Castel: *Sigh*... I can hope.

I do not wish undue stress on her...
Castel: Not that I don't sincerely wish to assist...
Castel looked at the pile of books ominously.
Castel: ...

We can only take so many when we move next, 
so...
Castel: I suppose one more couldn't hurt...
passages.content_zh:
艾略特：…
艾略特站在那兒，在帳篷前猶豫了一下
襟翼。
艾略特：對不起，卡斯特爾？我收到一條來自
你...
另一邊傳來驚慌的聲音
帳篷門襟。
Castel：呼、等一下……等一下……拜託……！
艾略特聽見一陣拖曳的聲音，彷彿
物品正在匆忙的整理中。
Castel：而且…完美~
艾略特：…
Castel：你現在可以進去了。
艾略特掀開帳篷的門簾，卻看到…
艾略特：…

原諒我，先生，但我不明白什麼是
發生在這裡。
那裡擺了一張兩人桌，配給的食物是
他們的日子。
Castel：當我們上次談論這個話題時，我提到
討論你的...傳家寶的可能性
情況...
....晚餐時。
Castel：嗯，這就是機會。
艾略特：我明白了。
艾略特：我絕對不會拒絕如此盛情的邀約。
Castel：啊，你的傳家寶？
卡斯特看著艾略特的屍體。 
目前的形式。
艾略特：對。我們的安排。抱歉。
一道光芒閃過。
艾利歐特：按照約定。
Castel：這更有利於研究它，
謝謝。
沒有再耽擱，兩人就坐到了桌邊。
Castel：我希望你喜歡奠酒。我覺得很難
空腹思考。
艾略特：我也有同樣的感覺。
艾利歐特：不過……酒？
Castel：啊，嗯……酒精……刺激大腦。它是
既定的科學事實。
艾略特：蠟燭呢？
卡斯特：好吧，如果人們願意閱讀，他們還指望如何閱讀呢？ 
沒有足夠的照明？
艾略特似乎對這個答案很滿意。 

他去吃了第一口食物…
只能暫停...
艾略特：玫瑰花瓣呢？
Castel：那隻是，呃……我的努力來抵消
馬的氣味和汗水。
卡斯特：傭兵營地也可以這麼髒，不是嗎？
艾利歐特嗅著空氣聽到了這項聲明。
艾利歐特：但是……他們不把馬放在這邊
營地。
艾利歐特：今天是訓練計畫的休息日。 
就連小狗也不在意。
Castel：舊習慣……很難改掉……？

passages.name: SP-Atticus x Tatiana B - New Event
passages.content:
Atticus: ...
The old Guardian was making his rounds around 
the busy town as part of the Crows' journey 
across the lands.
Atticus: Let's see...
He peeked down at the list in his hands,
refamiliarizing himself with the goals of his 
mission.
Supplies, and some recon were the order of 
the day.
A good ways behind him was a light footed woman.
Tatiana: This should be a good distance to stay out of sight.
She whispered it to herself as she peeked around a
corner.
The young einlyn continued to whisper to herself 
as she tailed the old guardian.
Tatiana: Let's see what you're up to, old man, now that the
others' aren't around to keep an eye on you.
As she moved, she blended into crowds and 
jumped between various stalls, objects, and 
walls to keep herself out of line of sight.
All the while...
Atticus: ...
...keeping an eye on her target.
Shopkeep: Thank ya.
Atticus: No, I must thank you.
As the minutes turned to an hour, Atticus only 
seemed to perform the tasks given to him.
Tatiana: Really? He's truly just dutifully handling the list of
stuff?
Tatiana: *Sigh*... Maybe he's just used to following orders.
Like from the nobles he sold out to...
......
Tatiana: Wait...
It seemed that way... until the einlyn saw him start 
to go off the beaten path of his supposed task list.
She continued to track him, from an offshoot of 
the main market street, to the edges of the 
residential district...
...all the way into the doors of a comfy looking
bakery.
Tatiana: Interesting...
It wasn't long before he emerged back onto the 
street, the last of his free arm space full of 
aromatic freshly baked goods.
From there, still, he headed towards the outskirts 
of the town.
He came to a large cottage on the edge of the 
town's fields.
A number of children ran about, with some noticing 
as he approached the open door.
Director: Is that... you, Atticus?
Atticus: In the flesh.
Director: In a sense...

I heard you were making a living being as sturdy as
stone but...
He stared on with a nostalgic smile, tinted with a
pang of concern.
Alongside him, more children gathered, looking 
on in awe.
Atticus: It was a surprise to me, as well, at first. But I make
due.
Atticus: Here, before I forget. For the orphanage.
Director: So many years later and you still feel the need... 
Your donations will always be welcomed.

Can I invite you in for-
Then like a warhorn, a scream tore through the air.
Eyes turned to see children running in from some of 
the empty fields from around.
Child: H- Help! They took her!
The shrill cry for assistance raised the hairs on the
necks of all those who heard it.
Atticus: Who did? Please tell me anything you can about them.
Child: U- Uh... Like... leather armor stuff... with a patch?
Director: That sounds... a bit like what you wore before,
Atticus. All those years ago.
Atticus: Do they still operate in this area?

Hmmm...
Atticus: Everyone. Inside. Now.
He commanded gently. The Director said nothing 
to him, but quickly gathered up the young ones 
inside the orphanage.
And with that, he was off.
Tatiana: No... no no no...
Tatiana stealthily headed off herself, using the 
sparse trees and cottages of the area to stay out 
of sight.
Atticus: ...

Footprints?
Tatiana: ...is that laughin'?
Atticus jumped into a forest clearing, with Tatiana
stealthily setup in the brush.
Rouge Crusader: GAH! Quit squirming brat! Don't make us shut you 
up. You're worth more uninjured.
Vile Crusader: Listen to your elders, squirt. Don't wanna become
damaged goods, do ya?
Quiet Crusader: *Sigh*...
On their armor was emblazoned a crest of the 
Covenant. The badge of the crusader emblazoned 
across three chests.
Atticus: You lot! What in the Goddess's name are you doing?!
Atticus lowered his hand to his hilt, and the three
depraved crusaders turned to him.
Vile Crusader: Back off ol' man. We got this job. We'll deliver the,
uh... young miss.
Rouge Crusader: Wait, ain't that... one of the titled?
Vile Crusader: Really?
Rouge Crusader: Yeah, the Ashen Fox. Didn't think he'd be so...
actually ash colored, haha.
Vile Crusader: Tsk. He's half dead. Leave us to our work, old 
timer. We-
Orphan: H- Help...! I'm scar-
The child managed to wiggle their head free, but 
only long enough to get a few words out.
Atticus: You say you were given orders for... this? You'd make
that claim?
Rouge Crusader: Confidential. Even to your titled'ness.
Tatiana: Is he... is he actually talking with these kidnappers?
I should of known he couldn't be trusted.
Tatiana said quietly as she skirted around the outer
edge of the clearing.
She grew more and more sick to her stomach with 
each word she heard.
Her eyes threw daggers towards Atticus, but as 
she spun her head...
Tatiana: (Is... his stone arm moving...?)
It was a small semi-circle like pattern, over and 
over again.
Tatiana: (There's no way. Is that the same as in training 
during camp? A signal?)
He would go over them with the Crows between 
training sessions, when he recounted his lifetime 
of combat wisdom.
Tatiana: No... that's not for me. It could be for the other
crusaders for some plot.

...
She glanced again to the struggling girl. Air froze in
her throat in that moment.
Tatiana: *Inhale*...  *Exhale*...
Tatiana: Fine, ya old man.
Atticus: Members of Her Crusade would have no reason to 
hide their deeds or mission.

Do you think she would... look kindly upon this?
Vile Crusader: I'm sure she'd understand. We are her chosen, 
after all, heh.
He stepped forward, boastfully tapping on the 
crest he wore.
Rouge Crusader: You questionin' the Goddess's protection? Maybe 
you should head back to the way you came.
Atticus: ...
The stone man stayed firm.
His eyes shifted from the would be crusaders to 
their captive and further still to the seemingly 
empty path in the forest.
Atticus: *Exhale*...
Atticus: I think it is time... to go.
Tatiana: Aaaahhhh!!! GO!
Tatiana burst forth, assuming it was a call to action,
and left no time for prejudice.
Vile Crusader: W- What?! Where did-

Argh!
She sprung from behind and trees and downed the 
one of the three crusaders with one swipe of steel.
Quiet Crusader: ...?!
Quiet Crusader: Gk!  *Gurgle*...
He turned to see why his comrade had yelled,
but...

He was denied a word as Atticus swiftly struck at 
his throat, slitting it in a clean motion.
Two were down, one each by each of 
Tatiana and Atticus.
Atticus: ...!
Atticus turned to the final one, who was holding 
the orphan, and rushed him without hesitation.
Rouge Crusader: Don't you dare!
He turned his blade to the child.
Atticus: ...!
Rouge Crusader: I'm gonna-

Grhk?!
But before he could even think of acting, an axe 
ripped through his back.
Tatiana: Move, kid!
Orphan: U- Uh huh!
The child jumped to the side, and Tatiana finished 
her follow-through, driving the crusader face first 
into the mud.
Atticus: Here.
Atticus shield the young child, turning away from it.
Rouge Crusader: *Cough*...  *Sputter*... And...the Goddess... 
saw this... more worthy?
Tatiana: Shut up.
Tatiana raised her boot and stomped down onto 
the handle of her axe to drive it further in.
With a whimper of a final screech, the man went 
limp.
Tatiana: There. Did it.
Tatiana: You alright, kid?
She said, pulling the axe from the corpse's back.
Orphan: *Nods*
She tightly clung to Atticus, and he motioned 
Tatiana to start walking back with them.
Atticus: We've no business left here.
He wiped his blade, sheathing it, and taking the 
girl's hand to keep moving.
Even as he did, he glimpsed back and saw the 
fallen men. He wasn't sure if they were imposter 
crusaders or not.
Atticus: Tatiana. If you could.
The child's hand was moved to Tatiana's grip, and 
she led her away instead.
Atticus stepped back, and deftly sliced the crusader
emblems into nothing more than shredded fabric.
Atticus: ...
Tatiana: ...
Tatiana: So, they were part of your order thing, yeah?
The three exited the forest, and Tatiana didn't let 
her guard drop despite the event.
The thoughts jumped through her head as she saw 
the connections and parallels form.
Tatiana: I'm not stupid. I know your background. The 
people you kneel to.
Atticus: ...If they were... they are not any longer.
He leaned down, picking up the orphan and 
carrying her like she was his own daughter.
Atticus: Let's get you home, little miss.
His stride accelerated a gear, and Tatiana soon 
found herself separated from the two.
Tatiana: ...
Tatiana: *Sigh*...
Director: Oh thank the Goddess!
Orphan: *Sniiiiiffffff*...!
The children and orphanage director lovingly 
swarmed the former missing girl with hugs and 
comfort.
Director: And thank you, both of you!
Tatiana: Heh. No problem.
As heart-warming as the sight was to Tatiana, her 
mind lingered with a question for the man at her 
side.
Tatiana: So... how long did you know I was there?
Atticus: Oh, when was it...?
Atticus: Around when we left camp, I believe.
Tatiana: Ack...
Atticus: Well, I didn't know the who.
Atticus: I was only confident in the lack of hostile intent.
Atticus: Which, I think helping the young girl there is proof
of.
Tatiana: ...
Tatiana: *Sigh*...

I'm losing my touch, aren't I?
Atticus: No, I would say your approach was spot on, 
Tatiana. What I noticed were eyes upon me, 
something I'm quite attuned to.
Atticus: It's been... nary a day without such a stare.
Tatiana: Gah... I was just making sure some former crusader
wasn't plotting something nefarious.
Atticus: A nefarious former crusader?
Tatiana: Yeah? Whatever would drive someone to kneel to 
that lot...
Tatiana: And what are you complainin' about! After what just
happened.
Atticus: Haha... A fair thought.
Atticus: So, the results of your investigation?
Tatiana: Crusaders suck fucking ass.
Tatiana stood with a palpable show of 
determination.
A stance that stood defiantly... at least at first.
Tatiana: ...
Tatiana: Argh... I dunno. Maybe you're... one of the 
good ones.
Each word was slightly quieter than the one before.
Tatiana: But... that doesn't mean I'm lettin' you outta my
sight!
Atticus: Haha...
A relieved look washed across Atticus's face, 
stone and all.
Atticus: I thank you, Tatiana. Such is reassuring to hear.

I am not without my own doubts... 
or faults... after all...
Tatiana: *Sigh*... You got that right.
Atticus: I'll do my best to keep you on your toes, yes?
Tatiana: Hey...
Atticus simply chuckled as he stepped away, 
signaling the conclusion to their business here.
The two returned to camp, and they informed the 
town guard along that path.
Each stepped into camp, holding onto items from
the supply list that Atticus left with.
And a story to tell around the next campfire.
passages.content_zh:
阿蒂克斯：…
老守護者正在四處巡視
烏鴉隊旅程中繁忙的小鎮
跨越各個土地。
阿蒂克斯：讓我們看看…
他低頭看了一眼手中的清單，
重新熟悉自己的目標
使命。
補給品和一些偵察任務是
那天。
在他身後不遠的地方，有一個腳步輕盈的女人。
塔蒂亞娜：這應該是遠離視線的好距離。
她一邊低聲自言自語，一邊環顧四周。
角落。
年輕的艾琳繼續自言自語。 
當她跟蹤老守護者。
塔蒂亞娜：讓我們看看你在做什麼，老夥計，現在
其他人不在身邊監視你。
隨著她的移動，她融入了人群，
在各種攤位、物體之間跳躍
牆壁，以保持自己遠離視線。
一直以來...
阿蒂克斯：…
……密切注意她的目標。
店員：謝謝。
阿蒂克斯：不，我必須感謝你。
隨著分鐘變成一小時，阿迪克斯只
似乎正在執行交給他的任務。
塔蒂亞娜：真的嗎？他確實只是盡職盡責地處理名單
東西？
塔蒂亞娜：*嘆氣*...也許他只是習慣了服從命令。
就像他把貴族賣給了...
.....
塔蒂亞娜：等等…
看起來就是這樣……直到艾琳看到他開始
走出他假定的任務清單的老路。
她繼續追蹤他，從一個分支
主要市場街道，到邊緣
住宅區...
....一路走進舒適的大門
麵包店。
塔蒂亞娜：有趣…
沒多久，他又出現在了
在街上，他最後的自由手臂空間充滿了
芳香的新鮮烘焙食品。
從那裡，他仍然朝郊外走去。 
城鎮的。
他來到了山邊的一間大小屋。 
鎮上的田野。
有些孩子跑來跑去，有些注意到了
當他走近敞開的門。
導演：那是……你嗎，阿迪克斯？
阿蒂克斯：在肉體中。
導演：從某種意義上來說…

我聽說你正在謀生，就像
石頭但是...
他懷著懷舊的心情凝視著

passages.name: SP- CharlottexElliot C - New Event
passages.content:
Charlotte: Hmm...
As I approached the tent, I could hear a sound I 
didn't recognize.
Charlotte: ...

Hmmmmm...
Pup: Hm?
Charlotte: ...
Charlotte: HMMMM......!!!
Pup: C- Charlotte?
I stepped into the tent, only to find Charlotte in
front of a planning board.
They were boards that we setup to map out 
strategies or organize impending plans.
Charlotte: JonesBakerBellDaviesBrown...
Charlotte was staring intensely at it, mumbling
something.
Pup: You... okay...?
Charlotte: TaylorSmithJohnsonEvansHughes
Pup: (It's like... she's speaking another language...)
I took a step back towards the tent opening.
Pup: If you need anything... just... let me know...
And I left Charlotte to her devices.
Charlotte: ...

ARGGHHH!!!

How do you even do this without any of these 
guys on board?! Stupid oligarchies!
Charlotte threw her hands up, knocking the 
documents on the board off.
And also hitting...
Elliot: ...?
Elliot stumbled back after being hit in the face by
Charlotte's motion.
Charlotte: Oh... I'm sorry!
Elliot: It's... okay.
Elliot blinked a few times, shaking away the sting.
Elliot: Is something wrong?
Charlotte: Ah, nothing much.
Charlotte: ...Nothing that isn't of my own making 
at least.
Elliot: You were saying names before, right?
Elliot: Some of them sounded familiar. Are they from Lockhart?
Charlotte: Recognize them?
Elliot: Yes. Rare for them to come up, but they are 
distinct family names from that region, and I've 
seen them in the work I've helped audit before.
Charlotte: That'd make sense. They're merchants.
Charlotte: Specifically, ones that hold a grip over specific
industries in Lockhart.
Elliot: Your talk of "oligarchy" of the city?
Elliot: ...or was that rude?
Charlotte: Nah, we know the deal.
Charlotte: Speaking of which, I should clean them up here, too...
Charlotte leaned down, picking up the small stack 
of notes that was knocked off the board from 
before.
Elliot: Here, I can...
And so Elliot followed and grabbed a few of the 
sheets of paper himself.
Elliot: ...

Is that what you're trying to do here?
Elliot stared at papers and saw the names they 
were just talking about.
Charlotte: Yeah... Sort of not worth keeping a secret here.
Charlotte: Liberating Lockhart means a new power structure 
needs to be established.
Charlotte: For lots of reasons, but... in part cause I can't trust
this lot anymore.
Charlotte: The problem is that they are... invasive.

Every time I look it over, there's something else 
that sort of falls apart if I try to remove even half of
them.
Elliot: Why?
Charlotte: Because they're greedy assholes, but that doesn't 
mean they're incompetent.

There's too much you'd have to rebuild from 
scratch without them in each industry. Lockhart 
would fall apart.
Charlotte finished grabbing the papers, and 
stepped over to the board.
Elliot: Lockhart requires rebuilding anyways, though. 
Would it not be an excellent chance to 
restructure?
Charlotte: Yeah... but its hard to imagine the people would 
just embrace a significantly longer rebuilding 
process.
Charlotte pinned a name into the board, 
then another.
Elliot: Hmm... this does remind me of an old tale.
Elliot: Long ago, a small country led a revolution against 
the Emerald Empire, in the Covenant's name.

One famous for restructuring generations of kings 
into a collective rule by the merchants of the land.
Charlotte: Ah...
Elliot: That was Lockhart, no?
Charlotte: I saw that coming.
Charlotte: That's some niche knowledge to get your hands 
on.

But it was a different time. Half the world was rising
up against the Emerald Empire and their puppet 
kingdoms of the day.
Elliot: Hmm...
Elliot was left in thought.

As Charlotte ran out of names to pin, he 
handed the ones he picked up.
Charlotte: A fantastical time, touched by the light of the
Goddess...
Charlotte: I appreciate your help as a representative of the
Covenant, but we're not ordained by Her to retake 
the city and rebuild it.
Elliot: I didn't actually mean to refer to that.
Charlotte: ...?
Elliot: The revolution I refer to was one created by 
people. Led by leaders of innovation who were 
exploited by the previous regime.
A revolution led by the people. In the name of the
Goddess, yes, but that was just a rallying cry.
Elliot: The Covenant is not gone, nor is the Goddess.
Elliot: And moreso, nor are the people of Lockhart.
Charlotte: I...
Charlotte: It really is a nice story, but I can assure you I've
heard it before.
Elliot: Hmm...
Charlotte: Maybe we can talk about the story behind your 
own legend.
Elliot: ...?
Charlotte: You know, that lady you turn into.
Charlotte: Gray magic pulls from a memory of your ancestor, 
right?
Elliot: ...
Elliot tensed up.
Charlotte: Don't worry, there aren't weird rumors going 
about on you or anything.

I just have some common knowledge of
how it works from my education.
Elliot: ...
Elliot fidgeted with his fingers, trying to decide 
when to breathe next.
Charlotte: I mean...
Charlotte: ...?
Charlotte: Oh... sorry, I didn't mean it like that.
Elliot: ...?
Elliot's tenseness alleviated some in the confusion.

Despite Charlotte's confident words,
her meaning was lost to Elliot.
Charlotte: You don't need to worry. She does herself proud, 
your ancestor.
Charlotte: Very skilled, and very cute.
Elliot: ...?! What...?
Charlotte: Seriously, no need to worry about it. She reps you 
and your family well.
Charlotte passed by Elliot and exited the tent.
Elliot: ...That's not... what I... was... concerned about...
Elliot struggled to get out the words. Each one 
with a pause.
Elliot: But...
Elliot: But I suppose... yes, it is a... good form...
But as he reached the apex of the thought, 
Charlotte was already long gone.
Elliot: ...Miss Charlotte?
Elliot: *Pant*... *pant*...
Elliot arrived in Charlotte's location after rushing to
catch up.
Charlotte: Chasing after me, eh?
Elliot: *Pant*... Yes, but...
Elliot took a deep breath and regained his 
composure.
Elliot: I think you misunderstood me.
Charlotte: What's to misunderstand? Legends are inspiring and 
all, but they tend to dance around the details.
Elliot: The situation now was not without precedent.

Lockhart was a kingdom that prospered as a 
western hub of the old world.

But it threw away that prosperity and built 
something new.
Charlotte: ...
Elliot: What I mean to say...

Why can it not do so again?
Charlotte: But the details are still...
Elliot: ...also still there.

The Covenant is still there to act as a glue for the
people even in a transition to a new age.

Lockhart itself will not lose the international desire
for its services. It is too vital a port.
Elliot: The question is...
Elliot: Do you trust the people to rise to the occasion?
Charlotte: I...
Charlotte was left a bit speechless. Her next words
failed to form despite a few attempts.
Charlotte: I get what you're saying, but...

It's hard to take that risk on a whim, ya know?

Hmm...
Charlotte: Maybe if we could test it? I do come from a 
product development background in my family.
Elliot: Then you could test it, no?
Charlotte: Test what, though?
Elliot: I do suppose premise 1 of my concept was...
Elliot: That the Goddess can be the glue that keeps the 
people together. Elevates them.
Charlotte: Well... Hmmm...
Charlotte's wandering eye drifted, setting on a 
sight.
Charlotte: Hmm... Maybe that?
Pup: ...

RRAAAGGHH!!!!!
Pup: *Pant*...
I swung my sword as I continued my training.
Charlotte: Let's go go go!
And Charlotte stood there, organizing my training
session.
...for some reason.
Pup: How was that one?
Charlotte: Good.

And after your break...
As we prepped another set, Charlotte's words 
started to repeat a few phrases more often.
Even into the next set itself.
Charlotte: Is that supposed to impress the Goddess? You got 
to do your best for her!
Pup: *Pant*...  *pant*...
As I worked, Charlotte made a short note on a 
piece of paper.
Elliot: Improved?
Charlotte: Yup. Against the control, at least.
Charlotte: We'll have to do one against the motivation of food 
at some point.
Elliot: That is... surprisingly relevant for a revolutionary
city status.
Pup: *Pant*... That one good too?
Charlotte: Yes, and thank you again for letting me tag along.
Pup: No problem.
Pup: This might be a good place to sto-
Charlotte: Now for the next round!
Pup: Huh?!
Charlotte: That was just test #1, my dear darling Pup...
Pup: ...HUH?!
passages.content_zh:
Charlotte: 嗯...
當我靠近帳篷時，我聽到了一種我不認識的聲音。
Charlotte: ...

嗯嗯嗯嗯...
小狗: 嗯？
Charlotte: ...
Charlotte: 嗯嗯嗯嗯......！！！
小狗: 查- Charlotte？
我走進帳篷，只見 Charlotte 站在一個計畫板前。
那些是我們用來規劃策略或組織即將到來的計畫的板子。
Charlotte: JonesBakerBellDaviesBrown...
Charlotte 正專注地盯著它，喃喃自語。
小狗: 你... 還好嗎...？
Charlotte: TaylorSmithJohnsonEvansHughes
小狗: (感覺... 她在說另一種語言...)
我向帳篷的開口退了一步。
小狗: 如果你需要什麼... 就... 告訴我...
然後我讓 Charlotte 自己處理。
Charlotte: ...

啊啊啊啊！！！

沒有這些傢伙在船上，你到底要怎麼做？！ 愚蠢的寡頭政治！
Charlotte 舉起雙手，把板上的文件都撞掉了。
而且還打到了...
Elliot: ...？
Elliot 被 Charlotte 的動作打到臉後，踉蹌地退了幾步。
Charlotte: 喔... 對不起！
Elliot: 沒... 沒事。
Elliot 眨了幾下眼睛，甩開刺痛感。
Elliot: 發生什麼事了嗎？
Charlotte: 啊，沒什麼。
Charlotte: ...至少沒有什麼不是我自己造成的。
Elliot: 你之前在說名字，對吧？
Elliot: 其中一些聽起來很熟悉。 他們是來自 Lockhart 的人嗎？
Charlotte: 你認得他們？
Elliot: 是的。 他們很少出現，但他們是那個地區獨特的家族姓氏，而且我在我協助審計的工作中見過他們。
Charlotte: 那就說得通了。 他們是商人。
Charlotte: 具體來說，是那些控制 Lockhart 特定產業的人。
Elliot: 你說的城市的「寡頭政治」？
Elliot: ...還是我太失禮了？
Charlotte: 沒事，我們知道內情。
Charlotte: 說到這個，我也應該在這裡清理一下...
Charlotte 彎下腰，撿起之前從板上撞掉的一小疊筆記。
Elliot: 這裡，我可以...
於是 Elliot 跟著撿起幾張紙。
Elli

passages.name: SP- CharlottexElliot B - New Event
passages.content:
Elliot: ...and of course, the movement didn't end there in 
that revolution.
Charlotte: I never realized there was such a cultural shift
underwriting that.
Charlotte and Elliot were walking around the camp.
Lunch had been served, so the two moved 
together towards the line.
Charlotte: Huh...?
They reached that line and it proved to be 
particularly long today.
It extended out the camp's entryway.
Elliot: Even the traveling merchants are closer to the 
camp than us...
Charlotte: *Sigh*... It'll be what it is.
Charlotte: Maybe we can continue our conversation as we 
wait?
Elliot: I'd like that.
The two had become regular partners in such
revolutionary discussions.
Elliot's intrigue into myth and his Covenant 
education left him well equipped to have them.
And Charlotte's own experiences in government 
created a curious mind on such a topic. One she 
only served to gain from.
Elliot: From my understanding, Cartenan was the first to 
rise up against the Emerald Empire.
Charlotte: I guess it would've been easier when they had that
Oathbreaker to control the weather.
Elliot: The story goes that the revolution was led by an
uncorrupted soul.
Charlotte: Yeah... One of those they say are sent by the 
Goddess to lead humanity in times of strife...
Elliot: One with no Oath to break, yes.
Charlotte: You think it was just a story?
Elliot: Well...
Charlotte: Why else would they have kept it a secret?
Elliot: Perhaps a better question for Lady Kara. I am not 
one to question the Covenant's teachings.
Charlotte: Ah, I can get that. Given your position.
The line continued on, and the two began to pass 
a merchant group.
Charlotte: Hm?
Crow: Sir, I can't just-
City Planner: You can, and you will!
Crow: S- sir...
City Planner: Well, then I'll just have to-!
The man stepped forward towards the Crow like he 
was about to strike.
Elliot: ...!
Elliot: ...!
City Planner: Argh!
The man fell to the ground as Elliot's nimble moves
took him down, pinning and immobilizing him.
Elliot: Calm down.
City Planner: W- What are you doing? Unhand me... w- woman?!

You! You!
Elliot: I was not asking when I said to calm down.
City Planner: O- Ow ow ow!
Charlotte: We get another scam artist here?
Crow: Well, no.

He wanted to sell a picture of-
City Planner: YOU!
Elliot: ...Huh?
With what little flexibility the man had, he was
pointing at Elliot.
Specifically... Elliot in his gray magic form.
City Planner: You! You're the woman from the drawing!
Elliot: ...
The man furiously unfurled a piece of paper.
City Planner: Here!
Elliot: Hmm...
What sat before them was a drawing of what 
looked distinctly like Elliot's transformed form.
Charlotte: What is this? And who are you?
City Planner: I am a MASTER city planner, thank you very much.

And I am in town looking to sell some goods to 
fund...

Well... to fund some city planning.
Charlotte: I'm not in a patient mood.
City Planner: ...?!

Right... so I was part of an investment group to
redevelop an old historic city not far from here.

The problem is that it is overrun with bandits and
scavengers...
Charlotte: And why are you making this our problem?
City Planner: I- I just wanted to sell some of the relics! The
bandits are too stupid to know their value.
Crow: Ma'am, we don't... buy things like that, right?
Charlotte: Obviously.
City Planner: I can assure you it is worth money...!

It is actually a famous city from a revolutionary story
many have heard of! It pre-dates the Covenant!
Charlotte: We still aren't buying relics.
Elliot: ...Was that drawing one of the relics?
City Planner: Yes, of course. Likely someone who fought in that
revolution.
Elliot: ...
Charlotte: Well, that is cool. Your ancestor won a revolution.
Elliot: Hmm...
City Planner: Won?

No. 

It was a loss.

A... slaughter...
Elliot: ...

Where is this city?
A Paralogue has been unlocked!
passages.content_zh:
Elliot: ...而且當然，那場革命中的運動並未就此結束。
Charlotte: 我從未意識到那背後有如此巨大的文化轉變。
Charlotte 和 Elliot 在營地裡散步。
午餐已經供應，所以兩人一起走向隊伍。
Charlotte: 呃...?
他們走到隊伍前，發現今天的隊伍特別長。
隊伍延伸到了營地的入口處。
Elliot: 連旅行商人離營地都比我們近...
Charlotte: *嘆氣*... 就這樣吧。
Charlotte: 或許我們可以邊等邊繼續我們的談話？
Elliot: 我很樂意。
兩人已經成為這種革命性討論的固定夥伴。
Elliot 對神話的興趣和他所受的聖約教育，使他有充分的準備進行這些討論。
而 Charlotte 自己在政府中的經驗，也培養了她對這個話題的好奇心。她只會從中獲益。
Elliot: 根據我的理解，卡特南是第一個起來反抗翡翠帝國的人。
Charlotte: 我想當他們有那個破誓者來控制天氣時，會更容易吧。
Elliot: 故事是說，這場革命是由一個未被腐化的靈魂領導的。
Charlotte: 是啊... 他們說是由女神派來引導人類度過艱難時期的人...
Elliot: 一個沒有誓言可以打破的人，沒錯。
Charlotte: 你認為這只是一個故事嗎？
Elliot: 嗯...
Charlotte: 不然他們為什麼要保密呢？
Elliot: 或許問卡拉女士是個更好的問題。我不會質疑聖約的教義。
Charlotte: 啊，我能理解。鑑於你的立場。
隊伍繼續前進，兩人開始經過一群商人。
Charlotte: 嗯？
Crow: 先生，我不能就這樣-
City Planner: 你可以，而且你必須！
Crow: S- 先生...
City Planner: 好吧，那我只好-！
那人朝 Crow 走去，好像要打他一樣。
Elliot: ...！
Elliot: ...！
City Planner: 呃！
那人倒在地上，因為 Elliot 敏捷的動作將他擊倒，壓制並固定住他。
Elliot: 冷靜點。

passages.name: SP- ElliotxCastel B - New Event
passages.content:
Elliot: ...
Elliot stood there, hesitating a bit before the tent
flap.
Elliot: Excuse me, Castel? I received a message from 
you...
There were panicked sounds on the other side of 
the tent flap.
Castel: H- Hold on... for one moment... please...!
Elliot could hear a sound of shuffling, as though 
items were being hastily arranged.
Castel: And... perfect~
Elliot: ...
Castel: You may enter now.
Elliot pushed aside the tent flap, only to see...
Elliot: ...

Forgive me sir, but I don't understand what is
happening here.
There was a table set for two, with the rations of 
the day on them.
Castel: When we last spoke on the subject, I alluded to 
the possibility of discussing your... heirloom 
situation...
...over dinner.
Castel: Well, this is that opportunity.
Elliot: I see.
Elliot: Far be it for me to refuse such a gracious invitation.
Castel: Ah, your heirloom?
Castel looked at Elliot's body. 
The current form of it.
Elliot: Right. Our arrangement. Apologies.
There was a flash of light.
Elliot: As agreed.
Castel: That'll be much more conducive to studying it, 
thank you.
Without additional delay, the two sat at the table.
Castel: I hope you enjoy the libations. I find it difficult to
think on an empty stomach.
Elliot: I feel much the same.
Elliot: Though... the wine?
Castel: Ah, well... alcohol... s- stimulates the brain. It is
an established scientific fact.
Elliot: And the candles?
Castel: Well, how else does one expect to read, if they do 
not have adequate lighting?
Elliot seemed content with the answer. 

He went to take an initial bite of the food... 
only to pause...
Elliot: What of the rose petals?
Castel: That is just, eh... an effort of mine to counteract 
the smell of horses and sweat.
Castel: Mercenary camps can be so dirty, can't they?
A statement met by Elliot sniffing the air.
Elliot: But... they do not keep the horses on this side of
camp.
Elliot: And today is a rest day on the training schedule. 
Not even Pup is about.
Castel: Old habits... die hard...?
Elliot: I suppose so.
The pair ate and drank in silence for some time.
Elliot: So, when are we going to do it?
Castel choked on his food.
Elliot: And for that matter, how are we even going to do 
it?
Elliot: With us being so different and all. 

Our forms, I mean.
Coughing, Castel wiped his mouth.
Elliot: Are you okay?
Castel: Fine... I just wasn't expecting such a forward
question.
Castel blushed bright red.
Castel: Though I suppose I'm fine with skipping formalities 
if you are.
Castel: Fortunately, I've given this much thought.
Elliot: Formalities? I was merely speaking of your intent to
discuss my ancestor...?
Castel's eyes went wide.
Castel: Oh! That! Of course! Yes!

Not "do it", but-
Elliot: ...?
Castel: Well, never mind.
Castel: We're nearly done with the meal, so we can finish
and...
The two stepped to the research setup Castel had 
within the tent.
Castel: You see, I have been pondering this matter with 
your ancestor and your unexpected transformation.
Castel: Everything I have experienced recently, and 
throughout my professional experience, has made 
one thing clear.
The psychology of the individual who uses a 
heirloom is the most significant factor in how that 
heirloom expresses itself.
Castel: This is doubly true for the case of transformations,
and your situation uniquely involves both.
Castel walked over to a table with a few heirlooms 
laid out on it.
Castel: Specifically, the area of emotion. Attitudes. 
Feelings. Beliefs.
Castel: Therefore, I propose we discuss your inner 
thoughts on your transformation in greater detail.
Elliot: I see... that does make a certain degree of sense.
Elliot: However, I'm not certain where to begin.
Castel responded with a fidget motion as though 
touch his no longer relevant glasses.
Castel: Fair enough. Perhaps it would help if I speak about 
my own feelings first?
Elliot: I imagine that could help to see an example. Thank you.
Elliot: Then I suppose to start...

How do you feel about... being a shade? And a 
feminine presenting one at that?
Elliot: After all, it seems like you still identify as a man,
so doesn't that cause some friction?
Castel: Hrm... it does. Or perhaps it would be more 
accurate to say that it should?
Castel: I recognize most people would reasonably find the
situation somewhat distressing.
Castel: After all, I didn't ask for this. And given the chance,
I would much rather return to my old body.
Castel: However, I also view the situation with a sense of
detachment.
Elliot: As in, you don't view this body as... "your body"?
Castel: Correct. It is merely a chance for me to study a 
unique situation up close
Castel: One that has never been seen before, and one 
where one can come away from it with new 
scientific knowledge.
Elliot: I appreciate that you shared that. I think it helps 
me work through some of my thoughts.
Castel: Should you be willing to share, I am glad to listen.
Elliot: ...
Castel: Not that... you must...
Elliot: I suppose for me, it is the opposite.
Elliot: I am a man. I've been a man.
Elliot: But this form... it has been with me for years now. 
It would be a lie to say it feels removed from me.

Would I trade it to get rid of the shame of it? 
Remove it from my history?
Elliot: That? That I do not know.
Castel: "Shame"...? Because of the female form, or...?
Elliot: Shame of my failure to my family.

This is not the legendary ancestor I was destined 
to cloak myself within. To raise our lineage back to
prominence.
How many more generations until we reach that 
point...?

...
Elliot: With that all, I suppose that it is hard to deny that
the female form isn't a reminder of that guilt.
Castel: I see...
The two settled into a considerate silence.
Elliot: Do you see a path forward, now? Did what I 
provided help see the next steps?
Castel: The guilt and shame... could they be derived from
another ancestor?

Somehow strong feelings corrupt the access to the
familial history in the heirloom...?
Elliot: But those feelings weren't around until after I
first transformed?
Castel: True... true... maybe it can act as a starting point,
though?

Hmm...
Castel: You are absolutely sure it is the correct heirloom?
Elliot: Yes.
Castel: Then yes, my theories will have to act as a starting
point.
Castel: Have you ever had thoughts about being a woman 
before?
Elliot: What?
Castel: Before the first time you took this form.
Elliot: No.
Elliot: Or...  *sigh*...
Elliot: No.
Castel: Did you have any strong feeling or wants before 
that point?
Castel: I understand I am speculating from my theory, but 
if it is true then any source of 'deviating' influences 
may be relevant.
Elliot: I suppose... I wanted to feel more free.
Elliot: I was essentially a child at the time, barely on the
precipice of adulthood.
Elliot: A life of being raised to be my family's savior... and
a savior via another person's greatness over my 
own...
Castel: Yes, I imagine such feelings would increase even in
one's later teenage years.
Elliot: Indeed, it is not a rebellious phase I am proud of. 
Nor one I can take back.
Castel: But do you feel more "free"?
Castel: In this form, I mean.
Elliot: I... suppose so?
Elliot: I feel more heroic. Confident. As if the rest of the
time, I'm only pretending.
Castel: That would imply any emotional influence would've still
made this the form of a hero, then?
Castel: And it is something to work with. I am happy I
stopped by that bookstore recently.
Castel gestured at a pile on his bed
containing a number of books.
Elliot: You wish for us to read those? Could two people 
get through that many in one evening?
Castel: Not if we simply check the appendices for anything
relating to your ancestor.
Castel: Even then, we only have to skim those sections for
mentions of anything related to the emotions 
you're experiencing.
Elliot: What would we be looking for?
Castel: Reasons you could subconsciously associate the 
heroic presence with a feminine form.
Elliot: As a potential corruptive influence, like you
mentioned...
Castel: And if without success, then we've eliminated one
avenue of inquiry.
Elliot: Indeed. Well, let's get started.
Castel: Hmm...
Castel's eyes scanned across the book's words 
made visible by the campfire's light.
Elliot: Have you found anything yet? I've yet to find 
anything myself.
Castel: *Yawn*... I am afraid nothing from me either.
Castel: And I was so sure this was the right way to 
investigate it...
Elliot: No, it is fine. As you said, it was worth a try.
Elliot: It is getting late. I think I should retire soon.
Castel: As should I...
Castel: Though consider me glad that we were able to 
share this time together.
Elliot: Indeed. It is rare to find another willing to delve
into the depths of Covenant myths.
Castel: Y- Yes, t- that's what I meant. Of course~!
Elliot: ...
Elliot: Haha, you can be humorously silly at times.
Elliot: Thank you, Castel. Despite our lack of concrete
results, I'm glad we talked.

It helped, in at least some ways.
Castel: Truly? Then I am most pleased with the outcome.
Elliot: In fact, I think I will continue reading some of these
titles and thinking on my feelings, as you 
suggested.
Elliot: Might I ask to return to your forum? You've 
managed to transport an impressive amount of 
literature.
Castel: Yes! Please do! And come speak with me in it, 
whenever you have the chance!
Castel: Erm, for science, of course.
Elliot: Yes, for science.
Elliot's relaxed laughter mixed with the hint of
nervousness from Castel's own.
Elliot: Goodnight, Castel.
Castel: Goodnight.
And so Elliot turned towards the tents while re-
entering his original form, leaving Castel with his
books and campfire.
Castel: *Sigh*... Too close. 

I feared that I had come on too strongly.
Castel: I think... I think Elliot didn't catch on to my...
advances...?
Castel: *Sigh*... I can hope.

I do not wish undue stress on her...
Castel: Not that I don't sincerely wish to assist...
Castel looked at the pile of books ominously.
Castel: ...

We can only take so many when we move next, 
so...
Castel: I suppose one more couldn't hurt...
passages.content_zh:
艾略特：…
艾略特站在那兒，在帳篷前猶豫了一下
襟翼。
艾略特：對不起，卡斯特爾？我收到一條來自
你...
另一邊傳來驚慌的聲音
帳篷門襟。
Castel：呼、等一下……等一下……拜託……！
艾略特聽見一陣拖曳的聲音，彷彿
物品正在匆忙的整理中。
Castel：而且…完美~
艾略特：…
Castel：你現在可以進去了。
艾略特掀開帳篷的門簾，卻看到…
艾略特：…

原諒我，先生，但我不明白什麼是
發生在這裡。
那裡擺了一張兩人桌，配給的食物是
他們的日子。
Castel：當我們上次談論這個話題時，我提到
討論你的...傳家寶的可能性
情況...
....晚餐時。
Castel：嗯，這就是機會。
艾略特：我明白了。
艾略特：我絕對不會拒絕如此盛情的邀約。
Castel：啊，你的傳家寶？
卡斯特看著艾略特的屍體。 
目前的形式。
艾略特：對。我們的安排。抱歉。
一道光芒閃過。
艾利歐特：按照約定。
Castel：這更有利於研究它，
謝謝。
沒有再耽擱，兩人就坐到了桌邊。
Castel：我希望你喜歡奠酒。我覺得很難
空腹思考。
艾略特：我也有同樣的感覺。
艾利歐特：不過……酒？
Castel：啊，嗯……酒精……刺激大腦。它是
既定的科學事實。
艾略特：蠟燭呢？
卡斯特：好吧，如果人們願意閱讀，他們還指望如何閱讀呢？ 
沒有足夠的照明？
艾略特似乎對這個答案很滿意。 

他去吃了第一口食物…
只能暫停...
艾略特：玫瑰花瓣呢？
Castel：那隻是，呃……我的努力來抵消
馬的氣味和汗水。
卡斯特：傭兵營地也可以這麼髒，不是嗎？
艾利歐特嗅著空氣聽到了這項聲明。
艾利歐特：但是……他們不把馬放在這邊
營地。
艾利歐特：今天是訓練計畫的休息日。 
就連小狗也不在意。
Castel：舊習慣……很難改掉……？

passages.name: SP- RowanxFlynn B - New Event
passages.content:
Flynn: ...
Flynn found Rowan leaning against a supply wagon.

It was brought up from the village, and 
Rowan was idly tuning his lute.
In a short time, they would be loading it. So, the
laborers were gathering with Rowan and Flynn 
a part of their numbers.
Flynn: Rowan. Can I talk to you for a second?
Despite the chaos of the surrounding camp, Rowan 
seemed entirely in his own world.
He plucked soft notes that somehow rose above 
the din of barking orders and clanging steel.
Rowan: Flynn! Of course, my friend.

I was just practicing a new tune to soothe your 
weary soul.
Flynn: That's... actually what I wanted to talk about.

Could you... if it wouldn't be too much to ask... 
stop playing music for me?
Rowan: Stop?
Rowan tilted his head, his fingers halting mid-strum.
Rowan: Might I ask why?
Flynn: I know you're trying to help me...
Flynn: And I really do appreciate the effort.
Flynn: But... it's a little, err... embarrassing to have
you... s- serenading me whenever we hang out.
Rowan lowered his lute, his expression falling as he
gave Flynn an acknowledging nod.
Rowan: My deepest apologies, Flynn. I never meant to 
offend.
Flynn: H- Hey, I wouldn't go as far as to say you offended 
me!
Flynn: It's just... Well, I'm not sure how to explain it in
words.

Excessive maybe?
Rowan: I might have gotten caught up in the drama of 
playing musician to your troubles.
Rowan: Mayhap... like minstrels do for the kings and queens 
at court?
Rowan: Indeed, I simply have-
Rowan: Ah, no... I get ahead of myself again.

If my melodies are unwelcome, then I shall withhold
them.
Flynn: R- Rowan, I... didn't...
A bit flustered, Flynn took a seat on a nearby sack.
Flynn: I...

Mmm...
Starting and stopping a few times, Flynn tried to 
find the words to console a friend.
But Flynn got there, and calmly started again.
Flynn: Rowan... you've been to a lot of places in your
travels, right?

Is it common to have minstrels on hand to... 
"soothe the souls of troubled rulers"?
Rowan: Hm? Oh certainly.
Rowan: More often than not when you visit a court, you'll 
see their bard playing to all after the day concludes.
Flynn: My family had a few, even as a smaller noble family.

I'm not sure I'd say their performances were "soul
soothing", though.
Flynn: In fact, I'd say my father rather liked to be a little
riled up most of the time.

He said it kept him sharp and alert, and the bards
played music to match.
Rowan: Haha... mayhap he be a soul to reflect your sister's?
Flynn: Oh, certainly. Mother, too.
As the words left Flynn's mouth, a foreman from 
the town arrived.
With their contact at hand, the assigned Crows 
gathered around the wagon, ready to reload it.
Rowan and Flynn stepped into the gathering of 
workers, now distracted from their conversation 
by the job and their idling thoughts.
It was several minutes before Flynn spoke up again.
Flynn: You know... looking back...
Flynn: Mmmmrgh...!
Flynn breathed out, the huff of exertion winding 
the sentence's words.
Flynn: Looking back, I knew a lot of people who might 
have benefitted from a minstrel or two to soothe 
their soul.
Flynn: Not that they'd have ever admitted it...
Flynn: I think they liked the stress. Liked knowing that
success rested on their shoulders.
Rowan: But not fair Flynn, it seems?
Rowan grunted, dropping a box in the wagon.
Flynn: But maybe the good bard Rowan, yes?
Flynn: I don't think I've seen you just... listening to music. 
At least any that you weren't responsible for.
Rowan: Heh. Guilty as charged~
Rowan: But not for lack of want.
Rowan: I'm afraid if I weren't making music, these crows 
would live up to their dour namesake.
Flynn: So who soothes the soul of the poet then?
Rowan: Does my soul need soothing?
Their banter was interrupted by a particular female
mercenary dumping a box of supplies into the 
wagon.
Rowan: Ah...
Rowan hopped back in surprise, expecting to once 
again be on the receiving end of her icy glare...
Crow: ...
...but to his surprise she did no such thing, and her
icy demeanor was entirely absent as she left for 
other duties.
Rowan: ...
Rowan: I can hardly believe my eyes. She ignored me, not a
single death glare.

She must not have recognized me.
Flynn: Rowan, you're the most obvious man in camp.
Between loads, Rowan kept turning to look back 
at where the mercenary had disappeared to...
fruitlessly trying to puzzle out the change.
Flynn: Haha...
With the wagon reloaded, Rowan and Flynn began 
to make their way towards the camp for the 
mid day meal.
The two were on the path, when...
Abruptly, Rowan grabbed Flynn's hand.
Rowan: Over here!
Flynn: W- What's happening?
Rowan: You know how they say a picture is worth a 
thousand words?
Flynn: Sure.
Rowan: What if I told you that the picture is worthless...
Rowan: ...if you do not stop to appreciate it?
Rowan gestured grandly, and Flynn looked.
Below them was a town nestled in the valley, 
framed by softly falling snow.
Flynn: What am I supposed to be looking at? The village?
Rowan: Just outside of it. You see there in the trees?
Rowan closed the gap between the two, and he 
used his arm to guide Flynn's eyeline to the scene.
Flynn: Yeah, I see...
Rowan: An elderly couple, they're dancing together. Just 
the two of them.
Flynn: ...
Flynn: ...Cute.
As Flynn let the moment soak in, Rowan pulled out 
his loot.
Rowan: Absolutely wonderful~
Making some tentative strokes, Rowan's voice 
choked with emotion.
Rowan: This is everything Flynn, why I make music, why we
fight each day.
Rowan: Not for revenge, not for survival...
Rowan: But because our lives in this realm are as beautiful 
of the sun itself.

It is worth it to appreciate it.
The lute played deliberately in his hands, moved by 
the inspiration of the moment to create a melody 
caught in the wind.
Glints of tears amongst the light sculpted the 
emotion that Rowan gave with each note.
Rowan: And such is true... even if you have to steal the 
moments, or fight for the chance to cherish it 
one more time...
The two stood side by side appreciating the scene 
as the bard composed.
The busy camp forgotten behind them.
Flynn: ...
It was calming tune, but one where each note felt 
like a beat of a story.
At least, it felt that way to Flynn as Rowan reached
the final note.
Flynn: ...
Flynn: Thank you.
So the two sat back, and let the moment soak in 
for the time.
Flynn: Maybe we can make a deal, Rowan...

You help me to "steal" these worthwhile moments 
back periodically...

To help me see them, much like you've managed 
to...

Do that, and I'll let you play all the songs for me
that you want.
Rowan: ...
Rowan: Very well, if our lord does insist.
Rowan: Haha... I think I'd very much enjoy such an
arrangement.
Rowan strummed away on the lute once more.
And Flynn listened along.
At least, until someone from camp realized
they were missing, and dragged them back 
by their ears.
passages.content_zh:
弗林：…
弗林發現羅文靠在一輛補給車上。

它是從村子裡帶出來的，
羅文正悠閒地調著魯特琴。
很快，他們就會加載它。所以，
工人們與羅文和弗林聚集在一起
他們的數字的一部分。
弗林：羅文。我可以和你談談嗎？
儘管營地周圍一片混亂，羅文
似乎完全在他自己的世界裡。
他彈奏出柔和的音符，不知何故超越了
狗叫聲和鋼鐵叮噹聲。
羅文：弗林！當然，我的朋友。

我只是在練習一首新曲子來安撫你
疲憊的靈魂。
Flynn：這……其實是我想談的。

你能不能……如果這要求不過分的話……
停止為我播放音樂嗎？
羅文：停下來？
羅文歪著頭，手指在彈奏中停了下來。
羅文：我可以問為什麼嗎？
Flynn：我知道你想幫我...
Flynn：我真的很感謝你們的努力。
Flynn：但是……有點，呃……有點尷尬
每當我們出去玩時，你都會唱小夜曲給我聽。
羅文放下了魯特琴，他的表情沉了下來。
向弗林點頭致意。
羅文：我深表歉意，弗林。我從來沒想過
冒犯。
Flynn：H-嘿，我不會說你冒犯了
我！
Flynn：這只是......好吧，我不知道如何解釋它
的話。

也許太過分了？
羅文：我可能已經陷入了戲劇性的境地
為你的煩惱扮演音樂家。
羅文：也許…就像吟遊詩人為國王和王后所做的那樣
在法庭上？
羅文：確實，我只是──
羅文：啊，不……我又超前了。

如果我的旋律不受歡迎，那麼我將保留
他們。
Flynn：R- Rowan，我...沒有...
弗林有點慌亂，在附近的麻袋上坐下。
弗林：我…

嗯...
弗林開始和停止了幾次，試圖
找出安慰朋友的話。
但弗林到了那裡，並平靜地重新開始。
弗林：羅文……你一生中去過很多地方。
旅行，對嗎？

有吟遊詩人在場是很常見的嗎？ 
「撫慰陷入困境的統治者的靈魂」？
羅文：嗯？哦，證書

passages.name: SP-Pup x Mariel A - New Event
passages.content:
Footsteps blistered through the blades along the
ground.
Each blade of grass crinkled under the feet of the
passionate stride.
And as the steps rose to their horizon, so did their
view of the setting sun.
Mariel: And... here... it... is!
Mariel jumped with joy as she reached the peak of 
the local mountain.
Mariel: *Inhale*...  *Exhale*...
The crisp air was a relief as she took in the sight of
the sunset before her.
Mariel: Yeah... This'd work well.

Sis and Pup would love this place for a date.
Pup: For a... what?
Mariel: Ah...?!
Mariel jumped back a little, startled by my own
arrival.
Mariel: H- Hello...
Pup: Hm?
I turned to the sunset myself.
Pup: Wow... That's a sight.
Pup: I didn't expect to see that here of all places. We
picked a good place to camp this time.
Mariel: I know, right? It's so pretty.

The sort of place where memories are made~
Pup: Yeah...
I looked between Mariel and the sunset.
I did indeed feel a memory forming.
Mariel: We're not gonna be camping here forever, so... no 
time to waste.
Pup: Hm...?
Mariel: First things first.
Mariel: How'd it go...!?
Pup: How did... what go?
Mariel: You know? With Sis?
Pup: ...
Pup: (With Charlotte? I guess there was that inventory 
thing a while back.)
Pup: (Or the training thing...)
Pup: (Or the...!)
So many memories passed through my mind over 
the course of our journey.
Memories of... lots of meetings... and lots of 
requests and questions we never actually 
followed up on.
Pup: (So... much... unfinished... business...!)
Mariel: T- That bad...?
As I short circuited from a lifetime of small regrets
packed into one convenient journey...
...Mariel turned to the side, away from 
my prying ears.
Mariel: So the confession really went that poorly...?

I guess it is Sis... and... Pup... 
Awkwardness was a given...

But what to do now?
Mariel: Well, awkward doesn't mean she said no? How 
could either of them say no this far in...?!
Mariel spun back towards me.
Pup: I never... ordered... that new... training sword
set...!
Mariel: Pup!
Pup: Huh?!
I jumped a little as I snapped out of it.
Mariel: I understand it went poorly.
Pup: (Even Mariel realizes it!)
Mariel: But... this could be the perfect excuse to practice 
for the real deal!
Pup: ...
Pup: Huh...?
Mariel: We can go on test runs of the local spots.
Mariel: See the sights, try the food. Make a day of it, 
even.
Pup: ...

O- Okay...
Mariel: Perfect~ I'll let you know when we can start.
Mariel grabbed my hand, patting it gently in a
reassuring manner.
With that and a smile, it wasn't long before she 
began her descent down back to camp.
Pup: (Did... she just... ask me out...?)
Soon after...
...a day came where Mariel pulled me from my bed,
lights dancing about in my morning ridden vision.
Mariel: *Clears throat*...

Welcome, my young student Pup...
Mariel: ...to a fun day... of learning!
I blinked a few times as the sunlight peaked 
through the alleyways of the town.
Pup: (The town...?)
For the crack of dawn, the town was oddly busy.
People moved about and between each other like 
the market was at its height of activity.
Mariel: Apparently, there is a festival in this town for the
next few weeks.
Pup: Ah... okay.
Pup: (So they're setting up? At least for the day.)
Mariel: Come on, time for some research~)
Mariel grabbed my hand...
Pup: ...Sure...
...and pulled me along.
We walked through the market and talked to the 
locals.
Many of the stalls weren't open, but the locals 
were kind and inviting.
We assisted their setup on a few occasions, and in
return one kind stall owner offered us the first 
taste of the day.
Mariel: Tasty~
Pup: Yeah. It has that... fresh 'crisp' to it, while still
being soft.
I took another bite of the pretiola.
The heat of it was warm to the touch, and a steam 
rose from it in the cool morning air.
Pup: Mm~
Mariel: Your face...
Mariel giggled softly with me still distracted.
Pup: You know...
Pup: ...is this what you had in mind? Is this really a dat-
Mariel: Here.
Her hand reached up to mine...
Pup: ...?!
Mariel: There we go. You had some on your face.
Pup: T- Thanks...

...
Mariel: Oh sorry, did I interrupt you?
Pup: Did you?
Pup: I don't know, slipped the mind somehow, 
haha...ha...
Mariel: *Giggles*
We traversed the area more and more 
as the day went on.
Before long, the sun held high up in the sky and 
tilted again before long.
So, before the sun started to set, Mariel pulled us
towards a restaurant.
Mariel: Kara said this one was famous in the region. The 
sort you hear about in rumors and wives tales.
Pup: T- That sounds good?
Pup: ...

(What are the options on this menu... What's a...
"haggis"...?)
Mariel: ...and apparently that's when a hero returned,
returning home before passing away.

The Covenant stories say the tree over there grew 
from his grave...
Pup: ("Colcannon"? Is that even a real thing?)
Pup: (Wait, is Mariel talking about a story about a
hero...?)
I peeked over my menu.
Mariel: According to the store owner, they say the old 
hero watches over us as the tree even to this day.
Pup: I think I remember that story from when I was a 
kid. One where-
Waitress: You two ready to order?
Pup: Gah...!
Pup: I'll just... have a...
My eyes darted across the menu page.
Mariel: We'll have a slab of corned beef.
Pup: (There was beef hidden on this page somewhere...?!)
Mariel: I figure you want something more straightforward, 
yes?
Pup: My hero~
Mariel just giggled a little at my words, and the
waitress scribbled down the order.
Waitress: We'll have it right out.
Pup: This... is...
Pup: ...great!
Mariel: The texturing is wonderful. I didn't expect it.
Pup: It's so tender.
Pup: I'll have to thank Kara myself for the 
recommendation when we get back.
Satisfied, we two ate our fill and chatted away.
Mariel: Also, I had no idea you knew so much about old myths.
Pup: We used to be told them as bedtime stories when 
we were kids.
Pup: From what Rowan said, I think we were told the 
versions from the Emerald Empire...?

Ones from before the modern Covenant versions, 
at least.
Mariel: I had no idea those stories were prevalent back 
then.

That one you mentioned before sounded like an
early version of the one I mentioned earlier.
I looked over the tree that Mariel mentioned prior.
As I did, I put another piece of meat into my 
mouth and started chewing.
Pup: The tale of 'Arbova'.

A sentient tree... said to stand up and fight 
alongside the village in times of turmoil.
Mariel: It's so different than what they taught us at 
school. I wonder how the story diverted.
Pup: I wonder if that tree really is it? Or maybe the store
owner just likes it for marketing.
Mariel: I'm mostly happy there's no 'turmoil' to test that
theory.
Mariel: For all the strife we've seen, this village has avoided
being a part of it.
Pup: Yeah... that is nice to see.
And so both of us leaned back, relaxing in our
chairs...
...taking in...
...peace.
Mariel: The sun is going to set soon, I think.
Pup: Time to head back?
Mariel: One more item to check off the list.
Pup: ...?
It was not long...
And steps came again.
Ones that, as they strode along the grassy wild, so 
did their view of the setting sun.
Mariel: *Inhale*...  *Exhale*...
The crisp air was a relief as she took in the sight of
the sunset before her.
Pup: This place again, then? With this sunset...
I said it quietly, as the chill of the night started to
settle on my skin.
And I could simply... smile.
Pup: It's... pretty.
Stepping over to one of the rocks, I sat down and
Mariel followed me.
Mariel: It is.
So we sat there.
And enjoyed the moment.
Mariel: I'm happy this went well today. I'm sure it'll be 
great research for you.
Pup: ...research?
Mariel: Mhm. You and Charlotte will have a lovely date, I'm
sure.
Pup: ...

What?
Mariel: I sort of wish I could see the date for myself.
Mariel: But...  *giggle*... I'll just have to ask Sis about it
afterwards.
Pup: ...

(Oh.)
I wasn't even sure what to say.
I had been pulled along so much this day that I 
hadn't had a real chance to think through what 
was happening.
Just... what my instinct told me.
What I was sort of hoping was really happening.
Mariel: Maybe we should start heading back?
Pup: ...

I figured you already saw it.
Mariel: Saw what?
Pup: The...
Pup: The... date...
Mariel: I...
Mariel: That's... a funny joke?
Mariel: Haha... Ha...
Pup: I had fun.
Mariel: You don't need to joke around with me, you know?
Pup: ...
I wasn't sure if I regretted saying it.
It was too much to process.
As I squirmed internally, Mariel fidgeted next to 
me with her fingers.
Mariel: You shouldn't joke around...

...when...
Mariel: ...when people might take you seriously...

...and get their hopes up.
Pup: ...!
Pup: ...do I look like I'd be funny enough to tell a joke at
a time like this?
Mariel: *Giggle*... Maybe... 

...with that funny face of yours.
Pup: ...?!
Pup: How would you know...
Pup: ...with that cute face of yours?
Mariel: *Giggle*
Mariel: I guess that's one thing we have in common.
Mariel's head lowered to rest on my shoulder.
And my head rested atop of her own.
Slowly...
...our hands intertwined.
And we watched the sun set.
passages.content_zh:
腳步聲沿著刀刃穿過
地面。
每片草葉在腳下都皺巴巴的
激情的步伐。
當台階上升到他們的地平線時，他們的
夕陽的景色。
Mariel：還有……這裡……它……是！
瑪麗埃爾到達頂峰時高興得跳了起來
當地的山。
瑪麗埃爾：*吸氣*...*呼氣*...
當她看到眼前的景象時，清新的空氣讓她鬆了一口氣。
她面前的夕陽。
Mariel：是的...這會很有效。

姐姐和小狗會喜歡這個地方約會。
Pup：為了……什麼？
瑪莉艾爾：啊……？ ！
瑪麗埃爾被我自己嚇了一跳，向後退了一點
到達。
瑪麗埃爾：哈——你好…
小狗：嗯？
我自己也轉向了夕陽。
小狗：哇...那真是個景象。
Pup：我沒想到會在這裡看到這個。我們
這次露營選了一個好地方。
瑪麗埃爾：我知道，對吧？真是太漂亮了。

那種留下回憶的地方~
小狗：是啊...
我看著瑪麗埃爾和夕陽。
我確實感覺到記憶正在形成。
Mariel：我們不會永遠在這裡露營，所以...不
浪費時間。
小狗：嗯……？
瑪麗埃爾：首先要做的事情。
瑪麗埃爾：怎麼樣……！ ？
Pup：怎麼……發生了什麼事？
瑪麗埃爾：你知道嗎？和姐姐一起？
小狗：…
小狗：（和夏洛特？我猜有那個庫存
前段時間的事情。 ）
Pup：（或是訓練的事情…）
小狗：（或者是……！）
太多的回憶從我的腦海中掠過
我們的旅程的過程。
回憶……很多會議……還有很多
我們實際上從未提出過請求和問題
跟進了。
Pup：（這麼多……很多……未完成的……事……！）
瑪莉埃爾：那、那麼糟嗎……？
當我從我一生的小遺憾中短路
打包成一趟便捷的旅程...
……馬裡爾轉向一邊，遠離
我愛探聽的耳朵
瑪莉埃爾：所以告白真的那麼糟嗎…？

我猜是姐姐……還有……小狗……
尷尬是理所當然的…

但現在該怎麼辦呢？
瑪麗埃爾：嗯，尷尬並不代表她拒絕了？如何
到目前為止，他們中的任何一個人都可以說不嗎？ ！
瑪麗埃爾轉身面向我。
Pup：我從來沒有…訂過…那把新的…訓練劍
設定

passages.name: SP - Pup x Norde A - New Event
passages.content:
Norde: *Pant*... *pant*...
Pup: *Pant*... *pant*...
Crow: Heh.
Other Crow: Backed into a corner, eh?
Crow: More like backed into a back.
Norde: ...
Pup: (They're not wrong...)
I peeked behind me to see Norde there.
We had, in fact, both retreated and found 
ourselves back to back and on the defensive.
Pup: You assume this isn't part of my strategy.
Flicking my sword up, I pointed it at the Crow 
that I was training with.
Pup: (Not that I'm actually faring that well.)
Norde: ...
Pup: (Norde isn't exactly doing so well either...)
Norde had been training with the other Crow.
I didn't get to observe since I was also sparring, 
but what little I saw seemed rough.
Slow reactions and just being a step behind...
Pup: (Maybe more importantly...)
Norde: ...!
Pup: (...Norde never said anything to me.)
Crow: C'mon little pup, you can do better than that.
Pup: You won't be saying that after I've won your dinner.
Crow: (Dammit! Again.)
I stepped back, trying to regain my balance 
as I did.
Pup: (He keeps doing that stutter step... I feel like I
normally read those well, but this time...)
Pup: ...

(Normally Norde would...)
Me eyes peeked to my side.
Norde: Rrragh...!
Other Crow: Haha! Fuck, that was actually close to my head.
Norde: Stay focused.
Other Crow: Really? Sure that's the quip you want to end this on?
Norde: ...End this on?
Other Crow: Heh.
Norde: ...
Norde's weapon had flown up, landing well away 
from the two training combatants.
Other Crow: Heh. First time for everything.

I win.
Norde: ...
Pup: (Norde...?)
Crow: Stay focused!
He lunged towards me.
Pup: ...!
And with that...
...we tied.
Pup: *Sigh*... I'm starved.
All four of us re-entered camp under the 
setting sun.
Crow: So I got that extra dinner I won, yeah? Wanna 
trade me some of your stash of jerky for half of it?
Other Crow: I guess... I am pretty hungry today.
Crow: Really?! I can trade the entire thing.
Other Crow: This is all assuming that they'll believe either of us
actually beat Norde.
The two chuckled on as they continued to the 
dining tent.
In contrast, Norde had stopped.
Pup: Not heading to the dining tent?
Norde: ...I lost my dinner in the battle.
Pup: Oh...

(I know they kept talking about it, but... I guess it
hadn't set in...)
Norde: *Inhale*...

*Exhale*...
Pup: Are you okay?
Norde: Everyone loses fights.
Norde turned and started towards the 
sleeping tents.
Pup: No, not because of that.
And then Norde stopped.
Norde: Hm?
Pup: You've lost fights before, even if not all that often.
Pup: What you haven't done before is...
Pup: ...not correct me.
Norde: What?
Pup: My training partner was doing a stutter step that I
wasn't reacting to correctly.
Pup: I managed a draw because I eventually figured out 
it was an issue with my balance being frontloaded.

At least... in comparison to when I last trained
against that approach.
Norde: You... had that problem...?
Pup: Yep, and I wouldn't normally be the first to notice,
either.

You would.
Norde: ...
Norde: Maybe, then.
Pup: Norde.
Pup: I challenge you to a duel.
My sword extended out towards Norde.
Pup: Winner gets my dinner.
Norde: ...
Pup: ...
Charlotte: ...

Go!
Pup: ...
Norde: ...
Pup: (3...)

(2...)

(1...!)
We both jumped back after our steel met.
Norde: You're slow.
Pup: We did JUST finish training.
Pup: (Though the same can be said of Norde.)
Norde: Stay focused.
Pup: Oh, I am.
I tightened my grip.
Pup: (Now... If I want to do this, then I need to...)
I breathed in.
Pup: Go!
I rushed forward blindly, each step getting longer 
into a gallop.
Pup: You're slow...!
Norde: ...?
Norde... stepped to the side at the last second.
Norde: Hmph.
With an axe raised...
...down it went!
Pup: ...?!
But I kept barreling forward, tripping into a roll
before bouncing back to my feet half a dozen feet 
from Norde.
Norde: ...?!
Pup: Don't... let your guard down...!
I wound up big and slow, being just a few long 
paces away from making a large swing.
Norde: ...?
But I shifted my weight and grip.
...and unleashed a flurry of fast strikes!
Pup: Hiya! Hiya! Hiya! ...Hiya!
Norde: ...
Norde met my steel and stepped back, offering 
space to adjust angles for each blow.
I rushed forward with a long step and a long follow
through swing.
Pup: Try this!
Norde: ...?
Norde... held their ground and met my 
steel with steel.
Norde: Hmph.
...before spinning their grip and pushing my center 
of gravity to the side.
Pup: Ah...?!
I fell to the side, catching myself in a roll that left
me outside of Norde's range.
Pup: *Sigh*...
Pup: ...
I stuck my sword into the ground at a low angle.
Pup: ...!
Kicking the hilt of my sword into the ground and 
up, it boosted up a large clump of dirt.
Norde: ...?!
I grabbed it, and...
...threw it!
Norde: ...!?
Norde started to twitch.
Pup: Gotcha.
I stepped forward to go for the strike, and Norde
seemed to be raising their weapon to react to the 
dirt instead of my weapon.
Norde: ...
Norde: ...
But grabbed the clump instead!
Pup: ...?!
...pushing it back at my own strike, then ducking 
under the collision.
Norde: ...
It was then that a clear opening was visible 
to Norde.
Pup: ...?!
Norde struck at my grip, knocking the sword out of 
my hand.
And soon I saw Norde's weapon pointing at me.
Pup: Well done.
Norde: You were sloppy.
Pup: I suppose I was. But that routine works on the 
typical mercenary.
Norde: I'm not your average mercenary.
Pup: Exactly.
Pup: You saw through it immediately.

I came at you like a beast, and you fought back like
man. Like a tactician.
Norde: What are you...?
Pup: I know this change has put you on edge.
Pup: Trust me, I know what it's like. Those doubts don't
just disappear when you want them to.
Pup: But you're not a beast. You're Norde.

Skilled and clever enough to see that chance to 
repel my strong and quick attacks just like that.

Most of the Crows wouldn't have figured it out that
quickly.

You need to adapt, but you're still you.

Norde. Stalwart of the Nightless Crows, and my 
brother.
Pup: You saw through it immediately.

I came at you in basically every way I could, and 
you still repelled them all.
Norde: What are you...?
Pup: I know this change has put you on edge.
Pup: Trust me, I know what it's like. Those doubts don't
just disappear when you want them to.
Pup: But even as a woman, you're still you, Norde. Your
strengths were not only in your muscles.

I needed to learn how to fight more deliberately. 
Each step being more considered and tactical to 
the little details.
Pup: But look at you... the change fits you like a glove.
You didn't need to learn anything, just adapt.
Pup: Don't let the learning curve fool you, you're still
you.

Norde. Stalwart of the Nightless Crows, and my 
family.
Norde: ...
Norde: ...

*Exhale*...

I know. I know...
Norde's breathing calmed, as though the stress was
dissipating ever so slowly.
Pup: ...
Pup: ...
Norde: ...
Norde had fallen to the ground.
Pup: ...
With myself standing tall.
Pup: You didn't think I'd let you win just because I was
teaching you a lesson, did you?
Pup: Heheh~
Charlotte: No.

Norde won.
Pup: Huh? Charlotte?
Charlotte: Yup, still here.
Charlotte: ...and still being the duel judge, as requested by 
you two...
Pup: I...!

...
Pup: *Sigh*... fuck.
I slumped down, falling down onto my butt much 
like Norde had.
Norde: ...Hah...
Norde: Hahahahaha...
Pup: What's so funny? You won.
Norde: It's just... when you were standing there... I... saw 
a glimpse of Ivan.
Pup: ...?
Norde: I can't count the amount of times Ivan's training 
left me on the ground as he lectured me.

It was...
Norde: ...nostalgic. If just for a moment.
Pup: ...
Pup: Alright.
I slowly stood up.
And extended my hand out to help Norde up.
Pup: I'll be your 'Ivan' for you.

And you, for me.
Norde: ...
Pup: If we can't live up to him, then we can lead the 
Crows together.

Each of us making up for each other's 
shortcomings. Making each other better 
at what we do.
Norde: ...
Norde: Maybe.
Norde took my hand, and soon we were both 
on our feet.
Pup: That's about as close to as a 'yes' as I can get, isn't
it?
Norde: Just please try and keep up.
Norde: I'll be taking that dinner now.
Norde started to turn towards the path back 
to camp.
Pup: Hey!
And I chased after, as we got into a friendly sibling
feud once more.
.........
Charlotte: ...

Those two are idiots.
passages.content_zh:
諾德：*喘*... *喘*...
小狼：*喘*... *喘*...
鴉： 呵呵。
另一隻鴉： 被逼到角落了，嗯？
鴉： 更像是被逼到背靠背。
諾德： ...
小狼：（他們說的沒錯...）
我偷瞄了一下身後，諾德在那裡。
事實上，我們都撤退了，發現
自己背靠背，處於防禦狀態。
小狼： 你以為這不是我的策略的一部分。
我彈起劍，指向正在與我訓練的鴉。
小狼：（並不是說我真的表現得很好。）
諾德： ...
小狼：（諾德的狀況也沒好到哪裡去...）
諾德一直在和另一隻鴉訓練。
我沒能觀察到，因為我也在練習，
但看到的一點點似乎很粗糙。
反應遲緩，總是慢一步...
小狼：（也許更重要的是...）
諾德： ...！
小狼：（...諾德從來沒對我說過什麼。）
鴉： 來吧小狼崽，你可以做得更好。
小狼： 當我贏了你的晚餐後，你就不會這麼說了。
鴉：（可惡！又來了。）
我退後一步，試圖恢復平衡。
小狼：（他一直做那個小碎步... 我覺得我
通常能很好地判斷出來，但這次...）
小狼： ...

（通常諾德會...）
我的眼睛瞥向一旁。
諾德： 吼啊啊啊...！
另一隻鴉： 哈哈！靠，差點就打到我的頭了。
諾德： 保持專注。
另一隻鴉： 真的？你確定這是你想用來結束這一切的俏皮話？
諾德： ...結束這一切？
另一隻鴉： 呵呵。
諾德： ...
諾德的武器飛了起來，落在離兩個訓練戰士很遠的地方。
另一隻鴉： 呵呵。 凡事都有第一次。

我贏了。
諾德： ...
小狼：（諾德...？）
鴉： 保持專注！
他朝我猛撲過來。
小狼： ...！
就這樣...
...我們打平了。
小狼： *嘆氣*... 我餓死了。
我們四個人在夕陽下重新進入營地。
鴉： 所以我贏了那份額外的晚餐，對吧？ 想用你藏的一些肉乾換我一半嗎？
另一隻鴉： 我想... 我今天確實很餓。
鴉： 真的？！ 我可以全部換給你。
另一隻鴉： 這一切都假設他們會相信我們其中任何一個
真的打敗了諾德。
兩人笑了起來。

passages.name: SP-Rowan x Charlott A - New Event
passages.content:
It was a windy day.
The mountains of Cartenan and Nolvanus looked 
down and into the distance.
Onto a simple camp out and down below.
A simple day within the Nightless Crows camp.
With Crows themselves lined up to eat.
A steaming soup to coax the hungry men and 
women to the call of lunch...
Crow: ...think they got some of that high grade beef for 
the stew this time?
Other Crow: Hmm... *Sniff*...  *sniff*...

Nah, smells like chicken.
Crow: Really? Must have some nice spices this time cause 
that ain't a smell I remember.
Other Crow: Could be worse.
Crow: Mmm... *Stomach growls*...
Other Crow: ...or you could just be hungry.
Crow: ...maybe...
Other Crow: *Sigh*... We've not been able to get much high 
quality stuff since Lockhart got invaded.

Not like trade from the east is prosperous either,
given the constant war the Empire and Republic 
have got going.
Crow: What I'd give to get a t-bone steak sometime 
soon...

Heh, though maybe all we needed to do was help 
liberate Lockhart all proper like.

No more military occupation now, so the food 
flows~
Other Crow: Maybe..

Or... also maybe...

...those two...
Charlotte: ...
Rowan: ...
Other Crow: Who knows with those two?
Crow: You mean... cuz they keep fightin'?
Other Crow: More that it seems to be getting worse... They're 
more at each other's throats than ever.

And now that we actually revolutionized ol' 
Lockhart...

Those two are in line to influence what the Empire 
and Lockhart will be in the future yeah?
Crow: Argh... You're right...

...I just want my beef...
Other Crow: Well... W-
The Crows felt an ominous feeling wrap around 
their shoulders.
Rowan: Ye of little faith. You will have your beef, my good
man.
Crow: R- Really?!
Other Crow: How much of that did you hear?
Rowan: Do not fret.
Rowan: Dear Charlotte and I are not at such dire odds. It
is... more...
Rowan: Yes, it is more like when we were in school.

Like the two lovebirds of a schoolyard, performing 
an awkward courting dance~
Crow: Wait... really...?
Other Crow: So you're saying...

Have you... like... with her...?
Another feeling fell onto the Crow's shoulder...
Charlotte: Like what... "with her"...?
Other Crow: N- Nothing...!
Charlotte: And you.
Charlotte stared daggers at Rowan, and the two 
Crows backed away.
Charlotte: Why are you spreading rumors, now?
Rowan: Have you seen the company morale? It is the least 
I can do.
Charlotte: At MY expense?
Rowan: Perish the thought. To think we two to be 
intermingled is but a flowering conception 
of the mind~
Charlotte: *Sigh*... You weren't like this in school.
Charlotte: Did something hit you on the head or something?
Rowan: Heheh~ So I am now the 'Alexei' you knew from school?
Charlotte: I...!
Charlotte: Don't take that as a compliment! The current you is 
a downgrade from that sweet innocent boy.
Rowan: Indeed, I am but a man now~
Charlotte: A 'man'?
Charlotte: And they expect you to help re-establish the 
Empire...

Imagine how you'll fair if you can't defuse a tense
situation without a joke.
Rowan: Indeed, a thought to be had.
The two continued on, bickering a bit more as the 
two Crows watched on.
Crow: They're at it again...
Other Crow: So much for getting us some beef.
Charlotte: "Emperor of a No Man's Land", right?
Rowan: You do not need to phrase it as such.
Crow: ...
Other Crow: ...
The two watched on as the argument raised to a 
fever pitch.
Both sides appeared sincerely irritated, even the 
ever calm Rowan.
Rowan: We shall simply see, then, shall we not?
Charlotte: Indeed... We will see.
Each of them turned on their heels...
...and walked away.
.........
Crow: I feel like it's been happening more frequently, to 
be honest.
Other Crow: Maybe. Maybe not.
.........
Crow: Is a bit quieter now, at least.
Other Crow: Duh. They stormed off and away from here.
.........
Crow: I could really go for some chicken stew right about
now.
Other Crow: Goddess I could, too...
Charlotte: What does that even mean?

Your birth mother isn't even from the Empire!
Rowan: She could make a wonderful empress.
Rowan: Her homemade meals alone could bring the 
Empire together!
.........
Charlotte: What are you on about?

Cats are clearly best.
Rowan: How can one say that, in this camp of all places...!?

It is to invite tragedy in a place most dog oriented.
.........
...........................
Rowan: ...

That was my pudding.
Charlotte: ...

I paid for it.
.........
...........................
Charlotte: ...
Charlotte: You're such an idiot.
Rowan: Haha... That's my charm though.
And the calming wind blew across the hillside.
As Rowan's hand landed on Charlotte's head, 
patting it softly.
Crow: Mmm~
The Nightless Crow took a bite of the bread, then
dunked it back into the soup for the next bite.
Other Crow: This actually is better than normal.
Crow: Yeah, some spices they added that just work.
The two sat towards the exterior of the camp, and
watched the nearby sea as the sun set over it.
Other Crow: Yeah, we didn't have this last time we had chicken 
in the stew.

Maybe...
Crow: Maybe what?
Other Crow: I wonder if liberating Lockhart opened up a spice
warehouse or somethin'.
Crow: Ah~ Then maybe things will get a bit better on the food
front.
Other Crow: Maybe, maybe...

Makes you wonder how the whole region will fair 
when we've seen this to the finish line though.
Crow: If it tastes anything like this, then it'll 
be fan-tast-ic~
Other Crow: Eh. With the Charlotte girl and the imperial prince in
charge, though?

It'll effect more than just food supplies if they 
argue 24/7.
Crow: Heh. Who knows...

Maybe they get off on it?
Other Crow: ...
Crow: ...

H- Hey... I was joking.
Other Crow: Y- Yeah, of course, haha...

You had my mind racing there for a second.
Crow: Yeah, as if.
So the two laughed on.
Nervously, and unsure if they had discovered 
something they shouldn't have.
A secret that, in its worst case...
...was worth keeping in exchange for some tasty 
soup and bread.
passages.content_zh:
那是個颳風的日子。
卡特南和諾凡努斯山脈
俯瞰著遠方。
俯瞰著下方簡樸的營地。
無夜鴉營地中平凡的一天。
烏鴉們排隊等著吃飯。
熱騰騰的湯引誘著飢腸轆轆的男人和
女人們前來享用午餐...
烏鴉：...你們覺得這次的燉湯裡有高級牛肉嗎？
其他烏鴉：嗯... *嗅*... *嗅*...

不，聞起來像雞肉。
烏鴉：真的嗎？這次一定加了不錯的香料，因為
這味道我沒印象。
其他烏鴉：可能更糟。
烏鴉：嗯... *肚子咕嚕叫*...
其他烏鴉：...或者你只是餓了。
烏鴉：...也許吧...
其他烏鴉：*嘆氣*... 自從洛克哈特被入侵後，我們就
沒辦法弄到太多高品質的東西了。

來自東方的貿易也不景氣，
畢竟帝國和共和國之間
持續不斷地在打仗。
烏鴉：我真想在不久的將來吃到一塊丁骨牛排...

呵呵，不過也許我們只需要好好地
解放洛克哈特就行了。

現在沒有軍事佔領了，所以食物
就會源源不絕了～
其他烏鴉：也許吧...

或者... 也可能...

...那兩個人...
夏洛特：...
羅文：...
其他烏鴉：誰知道他們兩個在想什麼？
烏鴉：你是說... 因為他們一直在吵架？
其他烏鴉：更糟的是，情況似乎越來越嚴重... 他們
比以往任何時候都更水火不容。

而且現在我們實際上已經徹底改造了
洛克哈特...

他們兩個將會影響帝國
和洛克哈特未來的走向，對吧？
烏鴉：唉... 你說得對...

...我只是想要我的牛肉...
其他烏鴉：嗯... 呃-
烏鴉們感到一股不祥的感覺籠罩在
他們的肩上。
羅文：你們這些沒信心的人。你們會吃到牛肉的，我的好
夥伴。
烏鴉：真- 真的嗎？！
其他烏鴉：你聽到了多少？
羅文：別擔心。
羅文：我和親愛的夏洛特並沒有處於如此糟糕的境地。這
更像是...
羅文：是的，更像是我們在學校的時候。

就像校園裡的兩隻愛情鳥，跳著
笨拙的求愛舞～
烏鴉：等等... 真的嗎？

passages.name: SP- JenxEvexMacy C - New Event
passages.content:
Jenny: Mmmgghhh...
Macy: Hmm...?
Eve: Uuuugggnnnhhh...
Macy: Hmmm.
Jenny: Hrrrgghh...
Macy: Almost there...

Hold on a second...

Hrrrn!
Eve: I... can't hold on any longer!
Jenny: Aaahhh!
As two others were trying to clean a high shelf...
...a lonely redhead "priestess" was lying down on a
couch, trying to read a book to no avail.
Jenny: I'm so BORED!!!
Macy: O- Ouch...
Eve: H- Hey...

You're... kinda... heavy...!
Besides the bored priest, a maid and a farmer were 
down on the floor after an unsuccessful attempt at 
cleaning noted high shelf.
The modest-sized maid weighed upon the farmer's
existing... plateau.
Macy: You know, this would be easier if you helped us...
Macy said the words carefully, as she raised herself
from the floor.
Eve: Let her rest.
Eve followed, returning herself to her feet after the
stumble.
Eve: I am sure she is tired of doing... whatever she has
been doing... right?
Macy: What are you doing... exactly?
Jenny: I am trying to see if there are any good stories.
Jenny: Where are the stories of dragons and knights? Of
wizards defeating evil demons?
Macy: Is that like... a bard thing in an age like this? Did
you ask Rowan for a song or two?
Jenny: Eww...
Jenny: Last time I tried, he started flirting with me.
Jenny: ...as if I were a girl...
Macy: Are you... not?
Jenny: L- Long story...
Eve: Haha... I've been there.
Jenny: Where I am from, stories about the past and future 
are abundant.
Jenny: Stories of spaceships, dragons, and even a few 
about dragons in space!
Eve: That sounds... familiar.
Jenny: Even still, we have this sort of... I guess you all
would call it a magic item?
Jenny: They're called video games. They show all sorts of
fantastic sights from fictional worlds.

You could even interact with them!
Macy: Wait... are you not from this world?
Jenny: N- No... why?
Macy: I also... came from another world.
Macy: Actually, we had something called video games 
there, too.
Eve: Me too! We had stuff called that in the world I was
born.
Macy: ...
Each of them continued on explaining their version 
of "video games" to each other.
Jenny: Ah... so is the different world we all come from... 
the same world?
Eve: Well, this is my third. I got teleported to one and
then... I guess here?

I might need a dimensional passport...
Jenny: Are those a real thing?!
Macy: Where I come from, you can get a planetary 
passport now that they're colonizing Mars.
Macy: Not "dimensional" passports though.
Eve: O- Oh, right! Mars... colonization... I might not 
watch the news enough since I don't remember
that...
Eve: That said, I was... exaggerating a bit.
Eve: No dimensional passport in reality, hehe.
Jenny: Wait, Mars is being COLONIZED?!
Jenny: Last I checked, there were rovers on the planet...
Jenny: I think one of them even sang "Happy Birthday" to
itself.
Jenny raised her hand to her mouth as she 
giggled a bit in excitement.
Jenny: It sounds like the next decade will be a lot of fun!
Jenny: The 2020s will thankfully bring us closer to a Mars
colony, and nothing bad will happen!
Macy: Hmmm... Should I tell her?
Eve: Don't you dare.
Jenny: Huh? What's happening?
Macy: Uhh... nothing... just... uhh... stay indoors.
Eve: And get used to wearing a mask if you go back to your
world.
Jenny: Like a... fox mask from the Japanese carnivals?
Macy: S- Sure...
Macy: Anyways...!
Macy: You two liked games? What sort?
Eve: Oh! I actually like strategy games! I am playing 
a game in the Water Emblem saga!

Or... was, at least.
Jenny: Strategy games? I don't know... I feel that
micromanaging an army might feel a bit tedious...
Jenny: This weapon breaks, that unit is hurt, oh Jenny, 
heal me! Jenny, unlock that chest!

Oh no, I am seeing sexy visions in the cursed 
dungeon~

Just because I-
Jenny: I mean the tactician is not involved in active
combat... It doesn't mean I like micromanaging 
people!
Eve: I just... like the idea of having a large group of
friends.
Eve: Especially in the newest entries, you can pair up
different kinds of people.
Eve: Like the human and the succubus, or the human 
and the slime girl...

...or the human and the vampire, or the human 
and the cow girl, or the...
Macy: Seems like that might take a while.

Jenny, since you seem to have such an... 
interesting opinion on strategy games, what games 
do you like to play, or used to?
Jenny: Oh! I like this franchise called Final Flight! They are
on their 15th entry at the moment.
Macy: I think they were on the 20th over in my time?
Jenny: I like stories where a small group of people 
overcome some god or demon king with the power 
of friendship.
Macy: Oh, I know those. They sort of come across as
unrealistic to me.
Macy: Why is that group of people tasked to defeat the 
evil program?

I mean, sure, they have the powers to defeat the 
evil program, but why does it have to be THEM, 
you know?
Jenny: Did you not just answer your own question?
Jenny: The hero has the power to save people. 
Therefore, the responsibility of helping them!
Jenny: Imagine you had the power to save someone, but chose
not to?
Macy: *Sigh*... I guess you have a point... At least I wish
they would give me...
Macy: I mean... the hero... give them some sort of 
thanks.
Macy: Monetary gifts would be appreciated.

Especially if the hero had to buy stuff from a person
named after the concept of greed...
Eve: ...and a human and a mermaid, and a human and 
an elf, and a human and a fox girl...
Jenny: What about you? What games did you used to play?
Macy: Oh, I was not much of a "gamer"...

I just casually played a farming Sim called Moondew
Canyon. Very chill.
Eve: ...and the human and the whole village...
Eve: Wait, did you say farming simulator? That sounds
tiring...
Macy: What do you mean? It's super chill.
Macy: You just wake up, water your plants, say hi to your
neighbor, and go to sleep.
